【选项】A) 以偏概全 The body continues to act as if the sleeper were awake只描述了patients with conditions like sleepwalking, in which the sleeper engages in the kind of physical movement that does not normally occur during sleep这一梦游异常情况；原文明示 这并非常态。 B) 无中生有 The neural activity of the brain will become intensified借neural(神经的) virtual reality中的 neural 一词造形似干扰；原文只说大脑重演活动，从未说神经活动“变得更 强烈”。 C) 过度推断 The brain behaves as if it were playing a virtual reality video game把原文比喻 what one psychologist calls a neural(神经的) virtual reality扩写为“在玩虚拟现实电 子游戏”，添加了 game 这一无中生有的设定。 D) ✓ 正确 the brain replays ↔The brain once again experiences the patterns of activity it experienced during waking hours ↔ the learning activities of the day 预判核心“大脑再次经历白天的活动”，The brain once again experiences the learning activities of the day在“再次”“经历”“白天活动”三处均精确等值。 我们睡觉时大脑在做什么? A) 它系统化白天收集的所有数据。 B) 它用新数据替换旧信息。 C) 它处理和吸收新获得的数据。 D) 它对信息进行分类并将其放入不同的文件中。

questions.q: What does the brain do while we are sleeping?
options: It systematizes all the data collected during the day.
It substitutes old information with new data.
It processes and absorbs newly acquired data.
It classifies information and places it in different files.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What does the brain do while we are sleeping是 what does X do 句式，问大脑在 做什么这一客观行为。

【拆句】What does the brain do while we are sleeping? 主句 What does the brain do 是疑问 句，while we are sleeping 是时间状语从句，sleeping 是现在分词。无陷阱。

【定位】This shows that while our bodies are at rest, our brains are drawing what's important from the information and events we've recently encountered, then integrating that data into the vast store of what we already know. 这表明，当我们的身体休息时，大脑在从最近接触到的信息和事件中提取重要内容，然后把 这些数据整合进我们已有的庞大知识库中。 53. What does the brain do while we are sleeping? A) It systematizes all the data collected during the day. B) It substitutes old information with new data. C) It processes and absorbs newly acquired data. D) It classifies information and places it in different files.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 It systematizes all the data collected during the day把原文what's important（重要 的部分）擅自扩大为 all the data（全部数据），与原文“筛取重要”相矛盾。 B) 与原文相反 It substitutes old information with new data说“用新数据替代旧信息”，与定位句 integrating that data into the vast store of what we already know恰好相反——原 文是把新数据“整合进”已有知识，并非“替换掉”已有知识。 C) ✓ 正确 drawing what's important from the information and events we've recently encountered ↔ It processes and absorbs newly acquired data the information and events we've recently encountered ↔newly acquired data 预判核心“提取+整合新信息”，It processes and absorbs newly acquired data两个谓 语动词精确对应定位句的两个动名词，是最贴合的同义替换。 D) 无中生有 It classifies information and places it in different files中的 classifies（分类）+ places…in different files（放入不同文件）在原文中找不到对应；原文只说“提取重要 +整合进已有知识库”，没有“分门别类放进不同档案”这一层动作。 Robert Stickgold 对增强学习有什么建议? A) 白天学习后小睡一会儿。 B) 睡前熬夜到很晚。 C) 做任何事情的梦。 D) 思考梦到这些材料的可能性。

questions.q: What does Robert Stickgold suggest about enhancing learning?
options: Having a little sleep after studying in the day.
Staying up late before going to bed.
Having a dream about anything.
Thinking about the odds of dreaming about the material.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What does Robert Stickgold suggest about enhancing learning问某人具体建议什 么，是事实型问题。

【拆句】What does Robert Stickgold suggest about enhancing learning? 主干 What does Robert Stickgold suggest，about enhancing learning 介词短语作 suggest 的状语，限 定话题范围。enhancing 是动名词。无陷阱。

【定位】Robert Stickgold, one of the Harvard researchers, suggests that studying right before bedtime or taking a nap following a study session in the afternoon might increase the odds of dreaming about the material. 哈佛研究人员之一的 Robert Stickgold 建议：临睡前学习，或者在下午学习之后小睡一会 儿，可能会增加梦到所学内容的几率。 54. What does Robert Stickgold suggest about enhancing learning? A) Having a little sleep after studying in the day. B) Staying up late before going to bed. C) Having a dream about anything. D) Thinking about the odds of dreaming about the material.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 taking a nap following a study session in the afternoon ↔ Having a little sleep after studying in the day Stickgold 的建议含两条，其中“下午学完后小睡”一条与Having a little sleep after studying in the day逐词对位；选项不必复述全部建议，只要属于建议之一即正确。 B) 偷换概念 Staying up late before going to bed（睡前熬夜）与原文studying right before bedtime（临睡前学习）方向完全不同——原文建议的是睡前“学习”，不是“熬夜”。 C) 以偏概全 Having a dream about anything说“做关于任何事的梦”，而原文dreaming about the material强调“梦到所学的材料”——选项把对象 the material 扩大成 anything，与原意 不符。 D) 张冠李戴 Thinking about the odds of dreaming about the material借用原文最后一句Think about that as your head hits the pillow tonight并改造为“去想梦到材料的几率”，但 原文这句是给读者的提醒，不是 Stickgold 的“增强学习”建议；同时把 odds 这一名词强 行说成 Stickgold 建议的“做法”。 从文章中可以推断出关于做梦的什么信息? A) 我们可以通过做梦来增强学习。 B) 做梦能提高你的语言能力。 C) 所有梦游者在睡觉时都会做出舞蹈动作。 D) 学习后小睡可以帮助你找到穿过迷宫的路。

questions.q: What can be inferred about dreaming from the passage?
options: We may enhance our learning through dreaming.
Dreaming improves your language ability.
All sleepwalkers perform dance moves when they are sleeping.
Taking a nap after learning can help you find the way through the maze.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What can be inferred about dreaming from the passage中 inferred 显式宣告本题 问“从全文可推出”，不是问字面陈述。

【拆句】What can be inferred about dreaming from the passage? 主干是 What can be inferred，be inferred 是被动语态（情态动词 can+be+过去分词），about dreaming 与 from the passage 都是介词短语作状语，分别限定推断对象和推断依据来源。被动结构提 示考生关注“可被推出来的内容”，而非原文字面说法。 55. What can be inferred about dreaming from the passage? A) We may enhance our learning through dreaming. B) Dreaming improves your language ability. C) All sleepwalkers perform dance moves when they are sleeping. D) Taking a nap after learning can help you find the way through the maze.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 dreaming is an essential part of understanding, organizing and retaining what we learn ↔ We may enhance our learning through dreaming college students who dreamed about a computer maze(迷宫) task they had learned showed a 10- fold improvement in their ability to find their way through the maze compared with participants who did not dream about the task ↔We may enhance our learning through dreaming 全文研究结论、机制、实验、建议四层证据全部指向“做梦有助于学习”，We may enhance our learning through dreaming恰好是这条主线的一步合理外推，且情态动 词 may 留出合理余地，最稳。 B) 以偏概全 Dreaming improves your language ability只对应原文括号里举的语言例证we're "getting" a foreign language once we begin dreaming in it，不能覆盖迷宫实验、 Stickgold 建议等其他区间；且原文用 popular notion（流行观念）描述此说法，并非 作者断言。 C) 以偏概全 All sleepwalkers perform dance moves when they are sleeping把原文one female patient on the tape performs the dance moves she learned earlier中“某位女患者” 扩大为“所有梦游者”，把单一例证拔到全称命题。 D) 强加因果 Taking a nap after learning can help you find the way through the maze强行把第 四段哈佛迷宫实验与第五段 Stickgold 的小睡建议拼成因果关系——原文中两者只是分 别论证“做梦助学”这一更大主线，并未明示“学完小睡就能走出迷宫”。

items.title: 2020年9月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2020年9月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Americans spend billions of dollars each year trying to change our weight with diets, gym memberships and plastic surgery.

P2 Trying to live up to the images of "perfect" models and movie heroes has a dark side: anxiety and depression, as well as unhealthy strategies for weight loss or muscle gain. It also has a financial cost. Having an eating disorder boosts annual health care costs by nearly US $2,000 per person.

P3 Why is there both external and internal pressure to look "perfect"? One reason is that society rewards people who are thin and healthy looking. Researchers have shown that body mass index is related to wages and income. Especially for women, there is a clear penalty at work for being overweight or obese. Some studies have also found an impact for men, though a less noticeable one.

P4 While the research literature is clear that labor market success is partly based on how employers and customers perceive your body image, no one had explored the other side of the question. Does a person's own perception of body image matter to earnings and other indicators of success in the workplace?

P5 Our recently published study answered this question by tracking a large national random sample of Americans over a critical time period when bodies change from teenage shape into adult form and when people build their identities.

P6 As in other research, women in our sample tend to over-perceive their weight—they think they're heavier than they are—while men tend to under-perceive theirs.

P7 We found no relationship between the average person's self-perception of weight and labor market outcomes, although self-perceived weight can influence self-esteem(自尊心), mental health and health behaviors.

P8 While the continued gender penalty in the labor market is frustrating, our finding that misperceived weight does not harm workers is more heartening.

P9 Since employers' perception of weight is what matters in the labor market, changing discrimination laws to include body type as a category would also help. Michigan is the only state that prohibits discrimination on the basis of weight and height. We believe expanding such protections would make the labor market more fair and efficient.

questions.q: What does the author say may have an adverse impact on people?
options: Undergoing plastic surgeries in pursuit of beauty.
Imitating the lifestyles of heroes and role models.
Striving to achieve perfection regardless of financial cost.
Attempting to meet society's expectation of appearance.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say may have an adverse impact on people? 用 What 直 问作者所述的某种不利影响，是对原文事实信息的复述，不要求推理。

【拆句】What does the author say may have an adverse impact on people? 主干其实是 What may have an adverse impact on people（什么会对人产生不利影响），中间的 the author say 是插入说明「作者所说的」。考生若把 say 误当作主干动词，就会读不通；记 住「主语+情态动词 have+宾语」才是句子骨架。

【定位】Trying to live up to the images of "perfect" models and movie heroes has a dark side: anxiety and depression, as well as unhealthy strategies for weight loss or muscle gain. 努力达到「完美」模特和电影英雄的形象是有阴暗面的：焦虑、抑郁，以及不健康的减肥或 增肌方式。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Undergoing plastic surgeries in pursuit of beauty（为了美而整形）只是 plastic surgery 在引子段被列举的现象之一，原文没说「整形」本身有 dark side，而是说「试 图迎合完美形象」才有。 B) 偷换概念 Imitating the lifestyles of heroes and role models 偷偷把原文的 images（形象、外 貌）替换成 lifestyles（生活方式），与原文 images of "perfect" models and movie heroes 强调的是「外貌形象」而非生活方式不符。 C) 无中生有 Striving to achieve perfection regardless of financial cost 的 regardless of financial cost（不计经济成本）在原文里没有依据；It also has a financial cost 只是说 「同时也产生经济成本」，并非「不计成本」。 D) ✓ 正确 Trying to live up to the images of "perfect" models and movie heroes ↔ Attempting to meet society's expectation of appearance Attempting to meet society's expectation of appearance 恰好把预判「迎合社会对 外貌期待」逐字呈现，正中。 研究人员对人们的收入有什么发现? A) 它们与人们的社会地位密切相关。 B) 它们与人们的体重和体型有关。 47. What have researchers found out about people's earnings? A) They are closely related to people's social status. B) They have to do with people's body weight and shape. C) They seem to matter much less to men than to women. D) They may not be equal to people's contributions. C) 它们对男性的重要性似乎远低于对女性的重要性。 D) 它们可能与人们的贡献不相称。

questions.q: What have researchers found out about people's earnings?
options: They are closely related to people's social status.
They have to do with people's body weight and shape.
They seem to matter much less to men than to women.
They may not be equal to people's contributions.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What have researchers found out about people's earnings? 问研究者「发现了什 么」，定位到结论句直接复述即可。

【拆句】What have researchers found out about people's earnings? 现在完成时强调「已经研 究并得出结论」，主干是 What have researchers found out（研究者发现了什么）， about people's earnings 是话题限定。结构平直，无陷阱。

【定位】Researchers have shown that body mass index is related to wages and income. 研究者已证明，身体质量指数（即体型胖瘦的衡量指标）与薪资和收入相关。

【选项】A) 无中生有 They are closely related to people's social status 的 social status（社会地位）在原 文从未出现，原文只谈体重/体型与收入的关系。 B) ✓ 正确 body mass index is related to wages and income ↔ They have to do with people's body weight and shape They have to do with people's body weight and shape 把定位句逐成分等值改写， 是与预判最贴合的一项。 C) 答非所问 They seem to matter much less to men than to women 把比较关系错置在「收入」 上，原文说的是「体重对女性收入的惩罚比男性明显」，而非「收入对男性意义更 小」。题目问的是研究者发现的关于收入的事，而非男女对收入的看重程度。 D) 无中生有 They may not be equal to people's contributions（收入可能与贡献不匹配）涉及的 「贡献」概念在原文完全不存在。 作者最近的研究关注什么? A) 关于职场竞争力指标的先前文献。 B) 在劳动力市场追求成功中最重要的特质。 C) 身体形象的自我认知是否影响职场成功。 D) 老板对身体形象的认知如何影响员工的晋升。

questions.q: What does the author's recent study focus on?
options: Previous literature on indicators of competitiveness in the workplace.
Traits that matter most in one's pursuit of success in the labor market.
Whether self-perception of body image impacts one's workplace success.
How bosses' perception of body image impacts employees' advancement.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author's recent study focus on? 直问研究焦点，需要在原文找到明 确指明研究问题的句子。 48. What does the author's recent study focus on? A) Previous literature on indicators of competitiveness in the workplace. B) Traits that matter most in one's pursuit of success in the labor market. C) Whether self-perception of body image impacts one's workplace success. D) How bosses' perception of body image impacts employees' advancement.

【拆句】What does the author's recent study focus on? 主干 What does the study focus on （研究关注什么），author's recent 是修饰 study 的两个前置定语。结构清晰，无难点。

【定位】Does a person's own perception of body image matter to earnings and other indicators of success in the workplace? Our recently published study answered this question by tracking a large national random sample of Americans over a critical time period when bodies change from teenage shape into adult form and when people build their identities. 一个人自己对身体形象的感知是否影响其收入和其他职场成功指标？我们最近发表的研究通 过追踪一批庞大的全国随机样本回答了这个问题——这些样本横跨人从青少年体型变成成年 体型、并开始建立自我认同的关键时期。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Previous literature on indicators of competitiveness in the workplace 写的是「前 人文献」，但原文明确说「前人文献清楚雇主感知会影响职场成功，无人探究问题的另 一面」——前人文献是背景而非作者研究焦点。 B) 无中生有 Traits that matter most in one's pursuit of success in the labor market 的 Traits （特质）一词原文未出现；原文讨论的是「自我感知」这一具体维度，而非泛泛的 「特质」。 C) ✓ 正确 Does a person's own perception of body image matter to earnings and other indicators of success in the workplace? ↔Whether self-perception of body image impacts one's workplace success Whether self-perception of body image impacts one's workplace success 把 P4 的 疑问句逐成分改写，预判一对就中。 D) 与原文相反 How bosses' perception of body image impacts employees' advancement 的 bosses' perception（雇主的感知）恰恰是原文 how employers and customers perceive your body image 这条已被前人研究透、作者明确表态「另一面没人探讨」的 方向。作者研究焦点正是其对立面。 作者最近的研究有什么发现? A) 超重实际上对员工的整体福祉并没有太大损害。 B) 人们在职场中不会因对体重的错误自我认知而受到不利影响。 C) 自尊有助于对抗职场中的性别不平等。 D) 性别不平等继续使许多女性员工感到沮丧。 49. What is the finding of the author's recent research? A) Being overweight actually does not do much harm to the overall well-being of employees. B) People are not adversely affected in the workplace by false self-perception of body weight. C) Self-esteem helps to combat gender inequality in the workplace. D) Gender inequality continues to frustrate a lot of female employees.

questions.q: What is the finding of the author's recent research?
options: Being overweight actually does not do much harm to the overall well-being of employees.
People are not adversely affected in the workplace by false self-perception of body weight.
Self-esteem helps to combat gender inequality in the workplace.
Gender inequality continues to frustrate a lot of female employees.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the finding of the author's recent research? 问研究结论本身，是对原文 We found... 句的同义复述。

【拆句】What is the finding of the author's recent research? 主干 What is the finding（结果是 什么），of the author's recent research 是后置定语限定 finding 的来源。无难点。

【定位】We found no relationship between the average person's self-perception of weight and labor market outcomes, although self-perceived weight can influence self-esteem(自尊心), mental health and health behaviors. 我们发现普通人对自身体重的感知与劳动力市场结果之间没有关系，尽管自我感知的体重确 实会影响自尊心、心理健康和健康行为。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Being overweight actually does not do much harm to the overall well-being of employees 把研究主语从「自我感知体重」换成「真实超重」；原文研究的是 self- perception（自我感知），不是 actual overweight；且原文从未说真实超重「不损 害」员工，P3 反而明确女性超重在职场上有 clear penalty。 B) ✓ 正确 no relationship between the average person's self-perception of weight and labor market outcomes ↔ People are not adversely affected in the workplace by false self-perception of body weight People are not adversely affected in the workplace by false self-perception of body weight 是对 P7 结论句的标准被动改写，与预判完全一致。 C) 与原文相反 Self-esteem helps to combat gender inequality in the workplace 说「自尊心帮助 对抗性别不平等」，与原文 self-perceived weight can influence self-esteem（自我 感知体重影响自尊）方向完全相反，且原文没说自尊能对抗性别不平等。 D) 答非所问 Gender inequality continues to frustrate a lot of female employees 对应的是 the continued gender penalty in the labor market is frustrating 那句情绪表态，并非作 者本次研究的核心发现；题干问 finding（研究结论），不是问情绪感受。 作者认为什么有助于改善劳动力市场的状况? A) 禁止基于员工身体形象的歧视。 B) 扩大对女性反性别歧视的保护。 50. What does the author think would help improve the condition in the labor market? A) Banning discrimination on the basis of employees' body image. B) Expanding protection of women against gender discrimination. C) Helping employees change their own perception of beauty. D) Excluding body shape as a category in the labor contract. C) 帮助员工改变自己对美的认知。 D) 在劳动合同中排除体型作为一个类别。

questions.q: What does the author think would help improve the condition in the labor market?
options: Banning discrimination on the basis of employees' body image.
Expanding protection of women against gender discrimination.
Helping employees change their own perception of beauty.
Excluding body shape as a category in the labor contract.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author think would help improve the condition in the labor market? 问作者认为什么能改善现状，对应原文末段的明确主张句。

【拆句】What does the author think would help improve the condition in the labor market? 主干 What would help improve the condition（什么能帮助改善现状），the author think 插入说明「作者认为」，in the labor market 限定改善对象。结构稍长但平直，提醒 考生把 the author think 当插入语处理即可。

【定位】Since employers' perception of weight is what matters in the labor market, changing discrimination laws to include body type as a category would also help. Michigan is the only state that prohibits discrimination on the basis of weight and height. We believe expanding such protections would make the labor market more fair and efficient. 既然在劳动力市场中真正起作用的是雇主对体重的感知，那么修改反歧视法、把体型也列入 受保护类别就会有所帮助。密歇根州是唯一以法律禁止基于体重和身高进行歧视的州。我们 相信扩大此类保护会让劳动力市场更公平、更高效。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 changing discrimination laws to include body type as a category ↔ Banning discrimination on the basis of employees' body image Michigan is the only state that prohibits discrimination on the basis of weight and height ↔ Banning discrimination on the basis of employees' body image Banning discrimination on the basis of employees' body image 把 P9 的法律建议 浓缩为一句，预判对比即中。 B) 偷换概念 Expanding protection of women against gender discrimination 把保护对象偷偷换 成「女性免受性别歧视」，但原文末段主张扩大的是「基于体型的反歧视保护」（body type），不是性别歧视保护；P8 提到 gender penalty 但作者紧接着说 our finding... is more heartening，并未把性别保护作为主推方案。 C) 与原文相反 Helping employees change their own perception of beauty 主张「帮助员工改变自 我审美感知」；但原文 Since employers' perception of weight is what matters in the labor market 明确表态「起作用的是雇主感知」，作者要改的是法律环境而不是员 工自我感知。 D) 与原文相反 Excluding body shape as a category in the labor contract 写的是「把体型排除在劳 动合同范畴之外」，与原文 include body type as a category 中 include（纳入）形成 Excluding（排除）的反义对立，完全反向。

items.title: 2020年9月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2020年9月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 The work-life balance is dead. By this, I'm not advocating that you should give up your pursuit of having a fulfilling career and a thriving personal life, and I'm definitely not saying that you have to give up one to have the other. I also acknowledge that we have a work-life problem, but I'm arguing that the concept of balance has never been helpful, because it's too limiting. You see, our language makes a difference, and how we refer to things matters because it affects our thinking and therefore our actions.

P2 At the minimum, most of us work because we want to be able to support ourselves, our families, and the people around us. In the ideal world, we're all doing work that we're proud of and that provides meaning and purpose to us. But even if your job doesn't give you shivers of joy each new day, working is a part of what each of us does and the contribution we make to society. When you separate work and life, it's a little bit harder to make that connection. But when you think of work as part of a full life and a complete experience, it becomes easier to see that success in one aspect often supports another.

P3 Losing your balance and falling isn't pleasant. A goal to balance suggests that things could quickly get off balance, and that causes terrible outcomes. It's more constructive to think of solutions that continue to evolve over shifts in life and work. Rather than falling or failing, you may have good days or better days or not-so-good days. These variations are normal, and it's more useful to think of life as something that is ever evolving and changing, rather than a high-risk enterprise where things could go wrong with one misstep.

P4 How we talk to ourselves matters, and how we talk about issues makes a difference. Let's bury "work-life balance" and think bigger and better about work-life fulfillment to do a little less balancing and a lot more living.

questions.q: What does the author suggest by saying "The work-life balance is dead"?
options: The hope of achieving a thriving life is impossible to realize.
The pursuit of a fulfilling career involves personal sacrifice.
The imbalance between work and life simply doesn't exist anymore
The concept of work-life balance contributes little to a fulfilling life.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干用 What does the author suggest by saying 的句式，直接询问作者说这句话想表达 什么，是典型的句意理解题。

【拆句】主干是 What does the author suggest，by 引导的方式状语 by saying "The work-life balance is dead" 修饰 suggest，引号内是宾语从句的内容，整体平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What does the author suggest by saying "The work-life balance is dead"? A) The hope of achieving a thriving life is impossible to realize. B) The pursuit of a fulfilling career involves personal sacrifice. C) The imbalance between work and life simply doesn't exist anymore D) The concept of work-life balance contributes little to a fulfilling life.

【定位】The work-life balance is dead. By this, I'm not advocating that you should give up your pursuit of having a fulfilling career and a thriving personal life, and I'm definitely not saying that you have to give up one to have the other. I also acknowledge that we have a work- life problem, but I'm arguing that the concept of balance has never been helpful, because it's too limiting. 「工作-生活平衡」这个说法已经死了。我说这话不是劝你放弃追求充实的事业和蓬勃的私 人生活，更不是说你必须放弃其一才能拥有另一个。我承认我们确实存在工作-生活问题， 但我主张「平衡」这个概念从来都没什么用，因为它把人框得太死。

【选项】A) 把对「概念」的否定偷换成对「目标」的否定 选项说「实现充实人生的希望根本不可能实现」，而作者明确否认了这种解读：I'm not advocating that you should give up your pursuit of having a fulfilling career and a thriving personal life——他根本没说目标做不到，只说「平衡」这个词不好用。 B) 无中生有 选项说追求充实事业需要「个人牺牲」，文中通篇没讨论过 sacrifice 或牺牲——作者只 是要换掉 balance 的提法，没说追求事业要牺牲生活。 C) 与原文相反 选项说工作和生活的失衡现象不再存在了，作者却紧接着承认 I also acknowledge that we have a work-life problem——他承认问题真实存在，只是反对 balance 这个概 念，与选项正相反。 D) ✓ 正确 the concept of balance has never been helpful ↔ The concept of work-life balance contributes little to a fulfilling life a fulfilling career and a thriving personal life ↔a fulfilling life The concept of work-life balance contributes little to a fulfilling life 用「贡献甚 微」换「从来没帮助」、用「充实人生」概括「事业加私生活」，正是定位句 the concept of balance has never been helpful 的同义改写。 作者关于我们使用语言说了什么? A) 它影响我们的思维和行为方式。 B) 它随着时间的流逝而变化。 C) 它反映了我们如何沟通。 D) 它因人而异。

questions.q: What does the author say about our use of language?
options: It impacts how we think and behave.
It changes with the passage of time.
It reflects how we communicate.
It differs from person to person.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say about our use of language 直接问作者关于某具体对象 的明确表述，要求复述原文观点。 52. What does the author say about our use of language? A) It impacts how we think and behave. B) It changes with the passage of time. C) It reflects how we communicate. D) It differs from person to person.

【拆句】主干 What does the author say，about 介词短语 about our use of language 限定 say 的内容范围，句式简单。

【定位】You see, our language makes a difference, and how we refer to things matters because it affects our thinking and therefore our actions. 你看，我们的语言会造成不同，我们如何称呼事物很重要，因为它影响我们的思维，进而影 响我们的行动。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 it affects our thinking and therefore our actions ↔It impacts how we think and behave It impacts how we think and behave 同时覆盖「思维」和「行动」两个语义点，与定 位句中的因果链完全对应，是定位句的最简同义改写。 B) 无中生有 选项说语言「随时间推移而变化」，原文谈的是语言对思维的影响，从未讨论语言本身 的历时演变。 C) 偷换概念 选项说语言「反映」我们如何沟通，定位句说语言「影响」思维和行动——reflect（反 映）和 affect（影响）方向相反：一个是被动镜像，一个是主动塑造。 D) 无中生有 选项说语言「因人而异」，原文谈的是语言对所有人的共同效应（影响思维与行动）， 完全没讨论个体差异。 作者说在理想世界中我们做什么? A) 我们做改善家人和朋友生活的工作。 B) 我们做每天都给我们带来快乐的工作。 C) 我们做对社会有贡献的有意义的工作。 D) 我们做充分发挥我们能力的高要求工作。

questions.q: What does the author say we do in an ideal world?
options: We do work that betters the lives of our families and friends.
We do work that gives us bursts of joy each new day.
We do meaningful work that contributes to society.
We do demanding work that brings our capacity into full play.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say we do in an ideal world 限定在 ideal world 这一条件下 询问具体做法，是单点细节复述。

【拆句】主干 What does the author say we do，we do 是宾语从句省略 that，in an ideal world 是地点状语；句式直白。 53. What does the author say we do in an ideal world? A) We do work that betters the lives of our families and friends. B) We do work that gives us bursts of joy each new day. C) We do meaningful work that contributes to society. D) We do demanding work that brings our capacity into full play.

【定位】In the ideal world, we're all doing work that we're proud of and that provides meaning and purpose to us. But even if your job doesn't give you shivers of joy each new day, working is a part of what each of us does and the contribution we make to society. 在理想世界里，我们都在做让自己自豪、能为我们提供意义与目的的工作。但即便你的工作 不会让你每天都因喜悦而颤抖，工作仍是我们每个人所做的事情之一，是我们对社会做出的 贡献。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 选项说工作让「家人与朋友」的生活变得更好，原文说的是 the contribution we make to society——贡献对象是「社会」，不是「家人与朋友」；且 support … our families, and the people around us 是讲「养活」，不是「理想世界中的工作 内容」。 B) 与原文相反 原文 even if your job doesn't give you shivers of joy each new day 用 even if 引导 让步：即便工作不带来 shivers of joy，工作也仍是贡献——意味着作者承认「很多人的 工作并不带来 shivers of joy」，选项却把「带来 shivers of joy」说成「理想世界的状 态」，与原文意图相反。 C) ✓ 正确 provides meaning and purpose to us ↔meaningful work the contribution we make to society ↔contributes to society We do meaningful work that contributes to society 同时打中「有意义的工作」和 「对社会有贡献」两个语义点，与定位句两层并列对应。 D) 无中生有 选项说「做让我们能力全开的高难度工作」，原文谈的是工作的「意义、目的、对社会 贡献」，从未涉及工作难度或能力发挥维度。 作者关于生活说了什么? A) 它是循环的。 B) 它是动态的。 C) 它是充实的。 D) 它是有风险的。

questions.q: What does the author say about life?
options: It is cyclical.
It is dynamic.
It is fulfilling.
It is risky.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about life 与第 52 题同款句式，问作者对 life 这个对象的明确 陈述。

【拆句】What does the author say about life 一句话主谓宾齐全，无从句、无否定，无陷阱。 54. What does the author say about life? A) It is cyclical. B) It is dynamic. C) It is fulfilling. D) It is risky.

【定位】These variations are normal, and it's more useful to think of life as something that is ever evolving and changing, rather than a high-risk enterprise where things could go wrong with one misstep. 这些变化都是正常的，把人生看作不断演变、不断变化的事物，比把它看成「一步错就全盘 崩」的高风险事业更有益。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 选项说生活是「循环往复」的，原文说的是「不断演变与变化」——演变是单向推进， 循环是周期回到原点，两者方向不同。 B) ✓ 正确 ever evolving and changing ↔It is dynamic These variations are normal ↔It is dynamic It is dynamic 用「动态的」一词总括了原文 ever evolving、changing、variations 等 同一语义场词汇，符合作者对 life 的定性。 C) 张冠李戴 选项说生活是「充实的」——但原文 provides meaning and purpose 修饰的是 work，不是 life；本题问的是作者对 life 的看法。 D) 与原文相反 选项说生活是「有风险的」，但原文 rather than a high-risk enterprise where things could go wrong with one misstep 中的 rather than（而不是）正是要否定「高风 险」这种看法——作者主张的恰恰是 life 不是 high-risk。 作者建议我们做什么? A) 让生活尽可能简单。 B) 用更简单的方式谈论平衡。 C) 以一种新的方式平衡生活和工作。 D) 追求更充实的生活。

questions.q: What does the author advise us to do?
options: Make life as simple as possible.
Talk about balance in simpler terms.
Balance life and work in a new way.
Strive for a more fulfilling life.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author advise us to do 不指向某段细节，而问作者贯穿全文给读者的最终 主张，落在末段总结句，本质是主旨或态度类问题。

【拆句】What does the author advise us to do，主干 the author advise us，to do 是不定式宾 语补足语，结构平直。 55. What does the author advise us to do? A) Make life as simple as possible. B) Talk about balance in simpler terms. C) Balance life and work in a new way. D) Strive for a more fulfilling life.

【选项】A) 无中生有 选项说让生活「尽可能简单」，原文从未谈过 simple 或 simplicity——作者主张的是 「更宏大美好的 fulfillment」，与「简化」无关。 B) 以偏概全 选项把作者的呼吁缩到「用更简单的措辞谈论 balance」，但作者主张的是「抛弃 balance、转向 fulfillment」，不是「换种说法继续谈 balance」。 C) 与原文相反 选项说「用新方式平衡工作与生活」，但作者末段明确 Let's bury "work-life balance"——要埋葬 balance，而不是用新方式继续 balance。 D) ✓ 正确 think bigger and better about work-life fulfillment ↔Strive for a more fulfilling life a lot more living ↔a more fulfilling life Strive for a more fulfilling life 用 strive for 对接末段 think bigger and better about，用 a more fulfilling life 对接 work-life fulfillment 加 a lot more living—— 选项准确覆盖全文呼吁的两个核心词 fulfillment 与 living。

items.title: 2020年9月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2020年9月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 When was cleaning a crime? When you're doing it to create art, obviously. A number of street artists around the world have started expressing themselves through a practice known as reverse graffiti(涂鸦). They find dirty surfaces and paint them with images or messages using cleaning brushes or pressure hoses(高压水管). Either way, it's the same principle: the image is made by cleaning away the dirt. Each artist has their own individual style but all artists share a common aim: to draw attention to the pollution in our cities. The UK's Paul Curtis, better known as Moose, operates around Leeds and London and has been commissioned by a number of companies to make reverse graffiti advertisements.

P2 Brazilian artist, Alexandre Orion, turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting in 2006 by getting rid of the dirt. Made up of a series of white skulls(颅骨), the painting reminds drivers of the effect their pollution is having on the planet. "Every motorist sits in the comfort of their car, but they don't give any consideration to the price their comfort has for the environment and consequently for themselves," says Orion.

P3 The anti-pollution message of the reverse graffiti artists confuses city authorities since the main argument against graffiti is that it spoils the appearance of both types of property: public and private. This was what Leeds City Council said about Moose's work: "Leeds residents want to live in clean and attractive neighbourhoods. We view this kind of advertising as environmental damage and will take strong action against it." Moose was ordered to "clean up his act." How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again?

P4 As for the Brazilian artist's work, the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with. They had no other option but to clean the tunnel—but only the parts Alexandre had already cleaned. The artist merely continued his campaign on the other side. The city officials then decided to take drastic action. They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo.

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti?
options: It uses paint to create anti-pollution images.
It creates a lot of trouble for local residents.
It causes lots of distraction to drivers.
It turns dirty walls into artistic works.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti? 问的是关于这个概念 的客观信息，答案应该是对原文某句的同义转述，不需要推断

【拆句】题干 What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti? 是 What 引导的特殊 疑问句，主干 we learn，from the passage 是状语，about reverse graffiti 修饰 learn 的 内容；无从句、无否定、无比较，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱 46. What do we learn from the passage about reverse graffiti? A) It uses paint to create anti-pollution images. B) It creates a lot of trouble for local residents. C) It causes lots of distraction to drivers. D) It turns dirty walls into artistic works.

【定位】They find dirty surfaces and paint them with images or messages using cleaning brushes or pressure hoses. Either way, it's the same principle: the image is made by cleaning away the dirt. 他们找到脏污的表面，用清洁刷或高压水管在上面「画」出图像或讯息。无论哪种方式，原 理都一样：图像是通过清除脏污而形成的。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 uses paint to create anti-pollution images 把原文的核心做法说反了——反向涂鸦恰 恰不用颜料，而是清除污渍 B) 无中生有 creates a lot of trouble for local residents 文中无对应描述；麻烦的是市议会的执法 逻辑，居民层面文中只提到他们 want to live in clean and attractive neighbourhoods，并未说反向涂鸦给居民带来麻烦 C) 张冠李戴 原文提到的是 Made up of a series of white skulls(颅骨), the painting reminds drivers of the effect their pollution is having on the planet——是提醒司机，而非 分散司机注意力；且这是 Orion 一人的做法，并非反向涂鸦的普遍特征 D) ✓ 正确 the image is made by cleaning away the dirt ↔turns dirty walls into artistic works 预判要的是「在脏面上靠清洁形成图像」，turns dirty walls into artistic works 正是这 层意思的同义改写 反向涂鸦艺术家试图做什么? A) 宣传他们的艺术追求。 B) 美化城市环境。 C) 提高公众对环境污染的意识。 D) 表达他们对地方政府的不满。

questions.q: What do reverse graffiti artists try to do?
options: Publicise their artistic pursuit.
Beautify the city environment.
Raise public awareness of environmental pollution.
Express their dissatisfaction with local governments.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do reverse graffiti artists try to do? 问群体共同意图，原文必有明文交代，仅 需找出该明文即可

【拆句】题干 What do reverse graffiti artists try to do? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主语 reverse graffiti artists，谓语 try to do；try to do 是固定结构，表示「试图、致力于做某 事」；句法平直，无陷阱 47. What do reverse graffiti artists try to do? A) Publicise their artistic pursuit. B) Beautify the city environment. C) Raise public awareness of environmental pollution. D) Express their dissatisfaction with local governments.

【定位】Each artist has their own individual style but all artists share a common aim: to draw attention to the pollution in our cities. 每个艺术家都有自己独特的风格，但所有艺术家都拥有一个共同的目标：唤起人们对城市污 染的关注。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Publicise their artistic pursuit 把原文中的「让公众关注城市污染」偷换成「宣传他们 自己的艺术追求」——原文 a common aim 是污染议题，不是他们个人艺术名声 B) 无中生有 Beautify the city environment 文中无对应；尽管反向涂鸦的产物确实清洁了表面，但 艺术家自陈的目的是「让人关注污染」，而非「美化城市」 C) ✓ 正确 to draw attention to the pollution in our cities ↔ Raise public awareness of environmental pollution 预判要的是「让公众关注污染」，Raise public awareness of environmental pollution 是其标准同义改写 D) 过度推断 Express their dissatisfaction with local governments 把作者在第三段对市议会的暗 讽错当成全体反向涂鸦艺术家的目的；原文意图句仅指向污染议题，并未把矛头对准 政府 关于巴西艺术家Alexandre Orion我们了解到什么? A) 他擅长绘制白色骷髅。 B) 他选择隧道来进行涂鸦艺术创作。 C) 他建议禁止所有污染汽车。 D) 他喜欢进行创意艺术创作。

questions.q: What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion?
options: He was good at painting white skulls.
He chose tunnels to do his graffiti art.
He suggested banning all polluting cars.
He was fond of doing creative artworks.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion? 问的是该人物的客观情 况，属于以人为锚的细节题

【拆句】题干 What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion? 主干 we learn，about 后跟同位语结构「Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion」，前者是身份、后者是姓名；结构清 晰，无陷阱 48. What do we learn about Brazilian artist Alexandre Orion? A) He was good at painting white skulls. B) He chose tunnels to do his graffiti art. C) He suggested banning all polluting cars. D) He was fond of doing creative artworks.

【定位】Brazilian artist, Alexandre Orion, turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting in 2006 by getting rid of the dirt. 巴西艺术家亚历山大·奥利安在 2006 年通过清除污渍，把圣保罗的一条交通隧道变成了一幅 令人惊叹的壁画。

【选项】A) 过度推断 was good at painting white skulls 把原文中作品的视觉成分 a series of white skulls 误说成「擅长画白颅骨」；原文从未评价他的技能水平，颅骨也只是这一幅作品的具体 内容，并非他的招牌技能 B) ✓ 正确 turned one of Sao Paulo's transport tunnels into an amazing wall painting ↔ chose tunnels to do his graffiti art 预判要的是「他选了隧道做反向涂鸦」，chose tunnels to do his graffiti art 正是这层 客观事实的同义改写 C) 无中生有 suggested banning all polluting cars 文中无对应；Orion 的原话仅是批评驾驶者不顾 环境代价 they don't give any consideration to the price their comfort has for the environment，并未提出禁止任何污染车辆的建议 D) 以偏概全 was fond of doing creative artworks 把原文一次具体的隧道清洁创作扩大成「热衷于 做创意艺术品」这一普遍性格描述；原文 P2 只提到一次具体行动与一次发言，未对其 性格倾向作概括评价 作者对Leeds市议会的决定暗示了什么? A) 它简直荒谬。 B) 它是明智的。 C) 它相当出人意料。 D) 它相当合理。

questions.q: What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision?
options: It is simply absurd.
It is well-informed.
It is rather unexpected.
It is quite sensible.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision? 中 imply 是推 断题的标志词，问作者对市议会决定的隐含态度

【拆句】题干 What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision? 是 What 引导 的特殊疑问句，主语 the author，谓语 imply，about 引导对象状语；imply 一词把本题定 性为推断题，是关键信号 49. What does the author imply about Leeds City Council's decision? A) It is simply absurd. B) It is well-informed. C) It is rather unexpected. D) It is quite sensible.

【定位】Moose was ordered to "clean up his act." How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again? 穆斯被勒令「整改其行为」。他该怎么做呢：把他已经清洁过的所有地方再弄脏一遍？

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 How was he supposed to do this: by making all property he had cleaned dirty again? ↔ simply absurd 预判要的是「作者觉得这决定荒诞」，simply absurd 是该态度的最直接形容词替换 B) 与原文相反 well-informed（消息灵通、了解情况）是正面评价，与作者用归谬反问表达的否定态度 方向相反 C) 偷换概念 rather unexpected 把作者的「不合理、说不通」误写成「出乎意料」；原文并未表达 「我没想到他们会这么决定」，而是表达「这决定本身就站不住脚」 D) 与原文相反 quite sensible（相当明智）是正面评价，作者用归谬反问明显否定这一决定，方向相反 Sao Paulo市政官员如何处理Alexandre Orion的反向涂鸦? A) 他们让他清洁Sao Paulo所有的隧道。 B) 他们采取严厉措施禁止所有反向涂鸦。 C) 他们指控他污染城市隧道。 D) 他们使他无法进行艺术创作。

questions.q: How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti?
options: They made him clean all the tunnels in Sao Paulo.
They took drastic action to ban all reverse graffiti.
They charged him with polluting tunnels in the city.
They made it impossible for him to practice his art.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti? 问官 方采取了什么客观行动，原文必有明文，按细节题处理

【拆句】题干 How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti? 是 How 引导的特殊疑问句，handle 意为「处理、应对」；主体是官方，宾语是艺术家的作 品；结构清晰，无陷阱

【定位】The city officials then decided to take drastic action. They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo. 市政官员随后决定采取激烈手段。他们不仅清洁了那条隧道，还清洁了圣保罗的每一条 隧道。 50. How did Sao Paulo city officials handle Alexandre Orion's reverse graffiti? A) They made him clean all the tunnels in Sao Paulo. B) They took drastic action to ban all reverse graffiti. C) They charged him with polluting tunnels in the city. D) They made it impossible for him to practice his art.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 made him clean all the tunnels 把清洁主体偷换成艺术家本人；原文 They not only cleaned the whole tunnel 明确主语是 they（官方），不是艺术家 B) 过度推断 ban all reverse graffiti 把官方动作上升为「禁止反向涂鸦」的法规层面；原文 the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with 明确说找不 到罪名，因此他们没有也无法颁布禁令，只是用清洁的方式釜底抽薪 C) 与原文相反 charged him with polluting tunnels 与原文明文 the authorities were annoyed but could find nothing to charge him with 直接矛盾——原文说「找不到罪名可控告」， 选项却说「以污染隧道为罪起诉了他」 D) ✓ 正确 They not only cleaned the whole tunnel but every tunnel in Sao Paulo ↔ made it impossible for him to practice his art The city officials then decided to take drastic action ↔ made it impossible for him to practice his art 预判要的是「让艺术家无法继续创作」，made it impossible for him to practice his art 正是该后果的客观表述；反向涂鸦的前提是脏面，官方清光所有脏面即从根本上让他 无法操作

items.title: 2020年9月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2020年9月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 The practice of paying children an allowance became popular in America about 100 years ago. Nowadays, American kids on average receive about $800 per year in allowance. But the vast majority of American parents who pay allowance tie it to the completion of housework. Although many parents believe that paying an allowance for completing chores benefits their children, a range of experts expressed concern that tying allowance very closely to chores may not be ideal. In fact, the way chores work in many households worldwide points to another way.

P2 Suniya Luthar, a psychologist, is against paying kids for chores. Luthar is not opposed to giving allowances, but she thinks it's important to establish that chores are done not because they will lead to payment, but because they keep the household running. Luthar's suggested approach to allowance is compatible with that of writer Ron Lieber, who advises that allowances be used as a means of showing children how to save, give, and spend on things they care about. Kids should do chores, he writes, "for the same reason adults do, because the chores need to be done, and not with the expectation of compensation."

P3 This argument has its critics, but considering the way chores are undertaken around the world may change people's thinking. Professor David Lancy of Utah State University has studied how families around the world handle chores. At about 18 months of age, Lancy says, most children become eager to help their parents, and in many cultures, they begin helping with housework at that age. They begin with very simple tasks, but their responsibilities gradually increase. And they do these tasks without payment. Lancy contrasts this with what happens in America. "We deny our children's bids to help until they are 6 or 7 years old," Lancy says, "when many have lost the desire to help and then try to motivate them with payment. The solution to this problem is not to try to use money as an incentive to do housework, but to get children involved in housework much earlier, when they actually want to do it."

questions.q: What do some experts think about paying children for doing chores?
options: It may benefit children in more ways than one.
It may help children learn the worth of labor.
It may not turn out to be the best thing to do.
It may not be accepted by low-income parents.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do some experts think about paying children for doing chores? 直接问"某 些专家怎么看",指向原文里一处明确观点句,属于客观转述类细节。 51. What do some experts think about paying children for doing chores? A) It may benefit children in more ways than one. B) It may help children learn the worth of labor. C) It may not turn out to be the best thing to do. D) It may not be accepted by low-income parents.

【拆句】题干 What do some experts think about paying children for doing chores? 是一个 wh- 疑问句,主干是 What do some experts think,后接介词短语 about paying children for doing chores 作 think 的对象,paying 是动名词、doing 是动名词作介词 for 的宾语;结 构平铺直叙、无陷阱。

【定位】Although many parents believe that paying an allowance for completing chores benefits their children, a range of experts expressed concern that tying allowance very closely to chores may not be ideal. 尽管许多父母认为按完成家务发零花钱对孩子有益,一批专家却表达了担忧,认为把零花钱与 家务紧密挂钩可能并非理想做法。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 It may benefit children in more ways than one 说"给孩子付钱做家务在不止一方面对 孩子有益",正是原文 many parents believe that paying an allowance for completing chores benefits their children 中父母的观点,而非专家的观点;父母与专家 在原文里立场相反,这一项把"父母信念"安到了"专家观点"头上。 B) 无中生有 It may help children learn the worth of labor 说付钱能让孩子学到"劳动的价值",原文 从未在专家口中出现 worth of labor 或近义表达,属于凭常识脑补。 C) ✓ 正确 may not be ideal ↔may not turn out to be the best thing to do tying allowance very closely to chores ↔paying children for doing chores 选项 It may not turn out to be the best thing to do 与预判"未必是最好的做法"语义 完全吻合,情态词 may 和否定 not 都对齐,故锁定为答案。 D) 无中生有 It may not be accepted by low-income parents 说低收入父母可能不接受,原文通篇 没有讨论 low-income parents 这一群体,纯属节外生枝。 根据Suniya Luthar的观点,做家务将帮助孩子学会____。 A) 分担家庭责任 B) 认识工作的价值 C) 培养独立精神 D) 自己管理家庭事务

questions.q: According to Suniya Luthar, doing chores will help children learn to ____.
options: share family responsibilities
appreciate the value of work
cultivate the spirit of independence
manage domestic affairs themselves
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 According to Suniya Luthar, doing chores will help children learn to ____. 用 According to + 人名指明出处,要求补全她的观点细节。 52. According to Suniya Luthar, doing chores will help children learn to ____. A) share family responsibilities B) appreciate the value of work C) cultivate the spirit of independence D) manage domestic affairs themselves

【拆句】题干 According to Suniya Luthar, doing chores will help children learn to ____. 主干是 doing chores will help children learn to ____,doing chores 是动名词作主语,help sb. learn to do 是固定结构,空位接动词原形;结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。

【定位】Luthar is not opposed to giving allowances, but she thinks it's important to establish that chores are done not because they will lead to payment, but because they keep the household running. Luthar 并不反对给零花钱,但她认为重要的是要明确:做家务不是因为家务会带来报酬,而是因 为家务能让家庭正常运转。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 they keep the household running ↔share family responsibilities 选项 share family responsibilities 与预判"为家庭运转分担一份力"的语义吻合,核心都 是"为家庭"而非"为钱"或"为自身"。 B) 无中生有 appreciate the value of work 与 Q51 中的 learn the worth of labor 几乎同款,都是原 文未出现的"劳动价值"口号,Luthar 强调的是"为家庭运转"而非"劳动的价值"。 C) 偷换概念 cultivate the spirit of independence(培养独立精神)是常见的家务教育口号,但 Luthar 通篇没有谈 independence,她谈的是 household running(家庭运转),把焦点从"家庭"挪 到了"个人独立"。 D) 过度推断 manage domestic affairs themselves 说孩子自己"管家务",反身代词 themselves 强 调"独自",原文只说让家庭运转,从未要求孩子独立"打理家务",且年龄段也对不上。 Ron Lieber认为给孩子零花钱的目标应该是什么? A) 帮助加强家庭纽带。 B) 教他们如何管理金钱。 C) 激励他们做更多家务。 D) 表达父母对他们帮助的感激。

questions.q: What does Ron Lieber think should be the goal of giving children allowances?
options: To help to strengthen family ties.
To teach them how to manage money.
To motivate them to do more housework.
To show parents' appreciation of their help.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does Ron Lieber think should be the goal of giving children allowances? 直接问 Lieber 认为发零花钱的目的是什么,原文必有对应观点。

【拆句】题干 What does Ron Lieber think should be the goal of giving children allowances? 是宾语从句嵌入疑问句的结构:What 实际是宾语从句 What should be the goal of giving children allowances 中的主语,Ron Lieber think 是插入语,giving children allowances 是 动名词短语作 of 的宾语;结构稍复杂但无陷阱。 53. What does Ron Lieber think should be the goal of giving children allowances? A) To help to strengthen family ties. B) To teach them how to manage money. C) To motivate them to do more housework. D) To show parents' appreciation of their help.

【定位】Luthar's suggested approach to allowance is compatible with that of writer Ron Lieber, who advises that allowances be used as a means of showing children how to save, give, and spend on things they care about. Luthar 的零花钱主张与作家 Ron Lieber 的主张一致,Lieber 建议把零花钱用作教孩子如何 储蓄、给予以及在他们在意的事情上花钱的手段。

【选项】A) 无中生有 To help to strengthen family ties 说零花钱能加强家庭纽带,family ties(家庭纽带)在原 文中无任何对应表述。 B) ✓ 正确 showing children how to save, give, and spend on things they care about ↔ To teach them how to manage money 选项 To teach them how to manage money 把 save/give/spend 三者上位化为 manage money,与预判"教孩子理财"完全吻合。 C) 与原文相反 To motivate them to do more housework 说零花钱用来"激励孩子多做家务",正是 Lieber 与 Luthar 共同反对的观点(原文末引文 not with the expectation of compensation),把他立场完全反转。 D) 偷换概念 To show parents' appreciation of their help 说零花钱是为表达父母对孩子帮助的感 谢,Lieber 谈的是"教孩子"而非"父母表达感激",方向完全错位。 David Lancy对18个月大的孩子有什么看法? A) 他们有帮助做家务的天生本能。 B) 他们太小了,不应该为自己做的事要钱。 C) 他们应该学会理解家庭责任。 D) 他们需要一点激励才能参与家务劳动。

questions.q: What does David Lancy say about 18-month-olds?
options: They have a natural instinct to help around the house.
They are too young to request money for what they do.
They should learn to understand family responsibilities.
They need a little incentive to get involved in housework.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does David Lancy say about 18-month-olds? 直接问 Lancy 关于 18 个月孩 子说了什么,原文必有出处。

【拆句】题干 What does David Lancy say about 18-month-olds? 是 wh- 疑问句,主干是 What does David Lancy say,about 18-month-olds 是介词短语作 say 的对象状语,18-month- olds 是带连字符的复合名词,意为"18 个月大的孩子";结构平铺直叙。 54. What does David Lancy say about 18-month-olds? A) They have a natural instinct to help around the house. B) They are too young to request money for what they do. C) They should learn to understand family responsibilities. D) They need a little incentive to get involved in housework.

【定位】At about 18 months of age, Lancy says, most children become eager to help their parents, and in many cultures, they begin helping with housework at that age. Lancy 说,大约 18 个月大时,大多数孩子就变得渴望帮父母,在许多文化中,他们就是从这个年 龄开始参与家务的。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 become eager to help their parents ↔have a natural instinct to help around the house 选项 They have a natural instinct to help around the house 与预判"自发想帮父母做 家务"完全吻合,natural instinct 把 eager 的强度感与自发性都吃下来了。 B) 无中生有 They are too young to request money for what they do 说他们太小不会要钱,too young to 是"太……以至于不能"结构,原文从未谈 18 个月孩子是否"要钱",纯属脑补。 C) 偷换概念 They should learn to understand family responsibilities 用 should 提出应然主张,但 原文 Lancy 是在描述 18 个月孩子"已经渴望帮忙"这一事实,而非主张他们"应该去理解家 庭责任";动作主体也被悄悄换成了"教孩子去理解"。 D) 与原文相反 They need a little incentive to get involved in housework 说他们需要"一点激励"才 参与家务,这恰是 Lancy 反对的观点;原文明确说他们 become eager to help,根本不需 要外在 incentive,而文末 Lancy 又直接说 not to try to use money as an incentive。 David Lancy建议美国家长做什么? A) 在做家务方面为孩子树立好榜样。 B) 让孩子无偿做家务。 C) 教孩子如何做家务。 D) 接受孩子早期的帮忙意愿。

questions.q: What does David Lancy advise American parents to do?
options: Set a good example for children in doing housework.
Make children do housework without compensation.
Teach children how to do housework.
Accept children's early bids to help.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does David Lancy advise American parents to do? 问 Lancy 给美国父母的 建议,原文末尾必有明示建议句。

【拆句】题干 What does David Lancy advise American parents to do? 是 wh- 疑问句,主干是 What does David Lancy advise,advise sb. to do sth. 是固定结构,American parents 是 advise 的宾语,to do 是不定式作宾补;What 实指 to do 后省去的动词宾语;结构平铺直叙。

【定位】The solution to this problem is not to try to use money as an incentive to do housework, but to get children involved in housework much earlier, when they actually want to do it. 对这个问题的解决办法,不是用钱当作做家务的激励,而是让孩子在他们真的想做家务的更早 年龄就参与进来。 55. What does David Lancy advise American parents to do? A) Set a good example for children in doing housework. B) Make children do housework without compensation. C) Teach children how to do housework. D) Accept children's early bids to help.

【选项】A) 无中生有 Set a good example for children in doing housework 说父母要做榜样,原文从未谈 set a good example/role model 类内容,Lancy 谈的是"时机"而非"示范"。 B) 以偏概全 Make children do housework without compensation 说要让孩子无偿做家 务;without compensation 虽呼应了 Lieber 的 not with the expectation of compensation,但 Lancy 的核心建议不是"无偿",而是"趁早"(timing),把重点偏移到了"是 否给钱"上。 C) 偷换概念 Teach children how to do housework 说教孩子"怎么做家务"的技能,原文重点是"何时 让他们做"(timing)而非"如何教他们做"(skill);两者方向不同。 D) ✓ 正确 We deny our children's bids to help ↔Accept children's early bids to help get children involved in housework much earlier, when they actually want to do it ↔ Accept children's early bids to help 选项 Accept children's early bids to help 把 deny → accept 反义对换,early、bids to help 原词保留,与预判"趁早接住孩子主动"完全吻合。

items.title: 2020年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Three children in every classroom have a diagnosable mental health condition. Half of these are behavioural disorders, while one third are emotional disorders such as stress, anxiety and depression, which often become outwardly apparent through self-harm. There was an astonishing 52 percent jump in hospital admissions for children and young people who had harmed themselves between 2009 and 2015.

P2 Schools and teachers have consistently reported the scale of the problem since 2009. Last year, over half of teachers reported that more of their pupils experience mental health problems than in the past. But teachers also consistently report how ill-equipped they feel to meet pupils' mental health needs,

P3 Part of the reason for the increased pressure on schools is that there are now fewer 'early intervention(干预)' and low-level mental health services based in the community. Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services, despite strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line.

P4 The only way to break the pressures on both mental health services and schools is to reinvest in early intervention services inside schools.

P5 There are strong arguments for why schools are best placed to provide mental health services. Schools see young people more than any other service, which gives them a unique ability to get to hard- to-reach children and young people and build meaningful relationships with them over time. Recent studies have shown that children and young people largely prefer to see a counsellor in school rather than in an outside environment. Young people have reported that for low-level conditions such as stress and anxiety, a clinical setting can sometimes be daunting(令人却步的).

P6 There are already examples of innovative schools which combine mental health and wellbeing provision with a strong academic curriculum. This will, though, require a huge cultural shift. Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders must be brave enough to make the leap towards reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services.

questions.q: What are teachers complaining about?
options: There are too many students requiring special attention.
They are under too much stress counselling needy students.
Schools are inadequately equipped to implement any intervention.
They lack the necessary resources to address pupils' mental problems.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What are teachers complaining about? 用 what 直接问一个客观事实，没有 infer/suggest/imply 之类的推断信号词。 46. What are teachers complaining about? A) There are too many students requiring special attention. B) They are under too much stress counselling needy students. C) Schools are inadequately equipped to implement any intervention. D) They lack the necessary resources to address pupils' mental problems.

【拆句】题干 What are teachers complaining about? 是现在进行时的特殊疑问句，主语 teachers、谓语 are complaining about，介词 about 后被前置疑问词 what 取代，无从 句、无否定，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。

【定位】But teachers also consistently report how ill-equipped they feel to meet pupils' mental health needs, and often cite a lack of training, expertise and support from the National Health Service(英国国家医疗服务体系). 但是教师们也一贯反映自己在应对学生心理健康需求时装备多么不足，并经常列举培训、专 业能力和来自英国国家医疗服务体系支持的缺乏。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 There are too many students requiring special attention. 把抱怨内容偷换成学生数 量过多，但原文 a lack of training, expertise and support 抱怨的是教师自身资源不 足，并未说学生人数太多。 B) 偷换概念 They are under too much stress counselling needy students. 把抱怨内容换成教师 承受过大压力，但原文 how ill-equipped they feel 抱怨的是装备不足，不是工作压 力大。 C) 以偏概全 Schools are inadequately equipped to implement any intervention. 用 any intervention（任何干预）把范围放大；原文只说教师在应对心理需求上装备不足，并 未说学校不能实施任何干预。 D) ✓ 正确 a lack of training, expertise and support ↔lack the necessary resources to meet pupils' mental health needs ↔to address pupils' mental problems 预判的两个语义点（缺资源、为了应对学生心理问题）都精确落在 They lack the necessary resources to address pupils' mental problems. 里，故锁定。 从文章中我们对英国社区卫生服务了解到什么? A) 由于预算削减,它们已经恶化。 B) 它们为当地居民的日常生活提供便利。 C) 它们在帮助精神病患者方面被证明无效。 D) 它们为当地居民提供预防性护理。

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about community health services in Britain?
options: They have deteriorated due to budget cuts.
They facilitate local residents' everyday lives.
They prove ineffective in helping mental patients.
They cover preventative care for the local resident.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about community health services in Britain? 中 learn from the passage 是定向取信息，不是推断，问的是文中已陈述的事实。 47. What do we learn from the passage about community health services in Britain? A) They have deteriorated due to budget cuts. B) They facilitate local residents' everyday lives. C) They prove ineffective in helping mental patients. D) They cover preventative care for the local resident.

【拆句】题干结构为 What + do we learn + from the passage + about + community health services in Britain；about 短语限定要问的对象，in Britain 进一步限定地域。理解时 把 What do we learn 视作信息询问的固定外壳，重心放在 about 后面那串名词短语，无 陷阱。

【定位】Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services, despite strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line. 自 2010 年以来对地方财政预算的削减导致了这些服务的大幅衰退，尽管有强有力的证据证 明它们在预防后续危机方面的有效性。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Cuts to local authority budgets since 2010 have resulted in a significant decline of these services ↔They have deteriorated due to budget cuts. a significant decline of these services ↔They have deteriorated 预判的两个要点（衰退 + 预算削减为因）都精确落在 They have deteriorated due to budget cuts.，且因果方向一致，故锁定。 B) 无中生有 They facilitate local residents' everyday lives. 说社区服务便利居民日常生活，但原文 从未谈到对日常生活的便利，只谈预算与衰退。 C) 与原文相反 They prove ineffective in helping mental patients. 说服务被证明无效，但原文 strong evidence of their effectiveness in preventing crises further down the line 明确说有强证据证明其有效——正反相反。 D) 偷换概念 They cover preventative care for the local resident. 看似呼应 preventing crises， 但 preventative care 通常指预防性医疗保健，与原文 preventing crises further down the line（预防后续危机）不是一回事；且本题问的是文章对社区服务的描述要 点，原文重点是衰退，不是预防覆盖。 作者建议将心理健康服务设置在哪里? A) 在家里。 B) 在学校。 C) 在医院。 D) 在社区。

questions.q: Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed?
options: At home.
At school.
In hospitals.
In communities.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed? 用 where 直 问地点，配 suggest 提示要找作者明确写出的建议位置，仍是文章里已有的事实陈述。 48. Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed? A) At home. B) At school. C) In hospitals. D) In communities.

【拆句】题干 Where does the author suggest mental health services be placed? 表层是特殊疑 问句，深层是 suggest + that 从句的虚拟语气结构——从句省略了 that，谓语用 (should) be placed 的原形被动，should 被省略。基础薄弱考生易把 be placed 误读成时态错误， 其实是 suggest 后建议性虚拟。

【定位】The only way to break the pressures on both mental health services and schools is to reinvest in early intervention services inside schools. 打破心理健康服务和学校双方压力的唯一办法是把早期干预服务重新投入到学校之内。

【选项】A) 无中生有 At home. 在家中提供，原文 inside schools 与 Schools see young people more than any other service 反复强调学校，从未提到在家中提供心理服务。 B) ✓ 正确 inside schools ↔At school. 预判要求的地点是学校内部，四个选项里只有 At school. 对应，故锁定。 C) 与原文相反 In hospitals. 与原文 a clinical setting can sometimes be daunting 的态度相反—— 作者把医院/诊所环境视为令人却步的，反对在医院里提供低强度服务。 D) 张冠李戴 In communities. 看似呼应 low-level mental health services based in the community，但作者讲的是社区服务因预算削减已衰退（Cuts to local authority budgets… have resulted in a significant decline），主张方向已转向学校内部，不是 继续放在社区。 我们从最近的研究中了解到什么? A) 学生更愿意依靠同龄人来缓解压力和焦虑。 B) 年轻人热衷于建立有意义的关系。 C) 学生在学校寻求咨询时感到更自在。 D) 年轻人从各种户外活动中受益。

questions.q: What do we learn from the recent studies?
options: Students prefer to rely on peers to relieve stress and anxiety.
Young people are keen on building meaningful relationships.
Students are more comfortable seeking counselling in school.
Young people benefit from various kinds of outdoor activities.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the recent studies? 与第 47 题同句型，问的是研究直接给出的 结论，不需要跨句推断。

【拆句】题干 What do we learn from the recent studies? 与第 47 题同构，只是把 the passage 换成 the recent studies，结构无陷阱。 49. What do we learn from the recent studies? A) Students prefer to rely on peers to relieve stress and anxiety. B) Young people are keen on building meaningful relationships. C) Students are more comfortable seeking counselling in school. D) Young people benefit from various kinds of outdoor activities.

【定位】Recent studies have shown that children and young people largely prefer to see a counsellor in school rather than in an outside environment. 近期研究表明，儿童和年轻人在很大程度上更愿意在学校里见心理咨询师，而不愿在校外环 境中见。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Students prefer to rely on peers to relieve stress and anxiety. 称学生倾向于靠同 龄人缓解压力焦虑，但研究结论是关于咨询地点（校内 vs 校外），从未谈到同伴这一 路径。 B) 张冠李戴 Young people are keen on building meaningful relationships. 与 build meaningful relationships with them over time 关键词重合，但原文中这句话的主语 是 Schools/them（即提供方），不是青少年自己；且本题问 recent studies 的结论， 而不是这句一般性描述。 C) ✓ 正确 prefer to see a counsellor in school ↔more comfortable seeking counselling in school children and young people ↔Students 预判的两个要点（学生群体 + 校内更愿）都精确落在 Students are more comfortable seeking counselling in school.，故锁定。 D) 无中生有 Young people benefit from various kinds of outdoor activities. 谈户外活动的益 处，原文未出现 outdoor activities 这一概念。 作者所说的文化转变(第6段第2行)是什么意思? A) 学校学术课程的简化。 B) 家长参与学校的决策制定。 C) 教师对心理健康态度的转变。 D) 对学校概念的转变。

questions.q: What does the author mean by a cultural shift (Line 2, Para. 6)?
options: Simplification of schools' academic curriculums.
Parents' involvement in schools' policy-making.
A change in teachers' attitudes to mental health.
A change in the conception of what schools are.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author mean by a cultural shift 用 What does … mean by … 这一 固定句型直问引文含义，是典型的词义句意题。

【拆句】题干 What does the author mean by a cultural shift 是特殊疑问句，主干为 What does the author mean，介词短语 by a cultural shift 引出被询问的短语，注意 mean by 在此 是固定搭配（凭 X 意指什么），后跟括号注明的行号定位。 50. What does the author mean by a cultural shift (Line 2, Para. 6)? A) Simplification of schools' academic curriculums. B) Parents' involvement in schools' policy-making. C) A change in teachers' attitudes to mental health. D) A change in the conception of what schools are.

【定位】Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders must be brave enough to make the leap towards reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services. 政界、决策者、采购者和校领导必须有足够的勇气，迈出那一步，把学校重新想象成既提供 健康服务、也提供教育服务的场所。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Simplification of schools' academic curriculums. 简化学术课程，原文 combine mental health and wellbeing provision with a strong academic curriculum 强调学 术课程要保持坚实，不是简化。 B) 无中生有 Parents' involvement in schools' policy-making. 家长参与学校决策——原文呼吁的 参与者是 Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders，并不包含 家长，且谈的不是决策参与而是学校角色重塑。 C) 以偏概全 A change in teachers' attitudes to mental health. 把转变的范围缩窄到教师态度，但 原文 Politicians, policymakers, commissioners and school leaders 列出的转变主体 不是教师，而是政界、决策者、采购者和校领导——主体错位、范围缩小。 D) ✓ 正确 reimagining schools as providers of health as well as education services ↔ A change in the conception of what schools are. 预判的核心（重新定义学校是什么）与 D 的措辞一对一对齐，且 D 的 conception 一词 正好对应 cultural shift 中的 cultural（观念层面的）。

items.title: 2020年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Picture this: You're at a movie theater food stand loading up on snacks. You have a choice of a small, medium or large soda. The small is $3.50 and the large is $5.50. It's a tough decision: The small size may not last you through the whole movie, but $5.50 for some sugary drink seems ridiculous. But there's a third option, a medium soda for $5.25. Medium may be the perfect amount of soda for you, but the large is only a quarter more. If you're like most people, you end up buying the large (and taking a bathroom break midshow).

P2 If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one. In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy(诱饵), making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small.

P3 I have written about this peculiarity in human nature before with my friend Dan Ariely, who studied this phenomenon extensively after noticing pricing for subscriptions(订阅) to The Economist. The digital subscription was $59, the print subscription was $125, and the print plus digital subscription was also $125. No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription when you could get digital as well for the same price, so why was it even an option? Ariely ran an experiment and found that when only the two "real" choices were offered, more people chose the less-expensive digital subscription. But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option.

P4 Brain scientists call this effect "asymmetric dominance" and it means that people gravitate toward the choice nearest a clearly inferior option. Marketing professors call it the decoy effect, which is certainly easier to remember. Lucky for consumers, almost no one in the business community understands it.

P5 The decoy effect works because of the way our brains assign value when making choices. Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices. If more options are introduced, the value equation changes.

questions.q: Why does the author ask us to imagine buying food in the movie theater?
options: To illustrate people's peculiar shopping behavior.
To illustrate the increasing variety of snacks there.
To show how hard it can be to choose a drink there.
To show how popular snacks are among movie fans.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author ask us to imagine buying food问的是作者为什么设置这个例子， 不是问例子本身说了什么，属于例证目的题。

【拆句】Why does the author ask us to imagine buying food in the movie theater?是一个why 引导的特殊疑问句，主干为Why does the author ask us，to imagine buying food是ask 的宾语补足语，in the movie theater作地点状语修饰imagine。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. Why does the author ask us to imagine buying food in the movie theater? A) To illustrate people's peculiar shopping behavior. B) To illustrate the increasing variety of snacks there. C) To show how hard it can be to choose a drink there. D) To show how popular snacks are among movie fans.

【定位】If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one. In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small. 如果你在想谁会去买中杯可乐，答案是几乎没人。事实上，营销部门很可能是故意把中杯定 价为诱饵，让你更倾向于买大杯而不是小杯。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small ↔people's peculiar shopping behavior Picture this: You're at a movie theater food stand ↔To illustrate 预判到答案是"展示异常购物行为"，选项里只有To illustrate people's peculiar shopping behavior同时覆盖illustrate（举例目的）和peculiar shopping behavior （异常购物行为），与预判完全吻合。 B) 无中生有 the increasing variety of snacks说的是零食"种类的增多"，但原文从头到尾只谈大中小 三种可乐的定价心理，根本没有讨论零食种类多寡。 C) 偷换概念 how hard it can be to choose a drink说的是"选饮料有多难"。原文It's a tough decision确实承认决定难，但这只是引出诱饵效应的铺垫，作者的真正意图不是讲选择 之难，而是讲选择被操纵；选项把铺垫当成目的，是偷换。 D) 无中生有 how popular snacks are among movie fans说的是"零食在影迷中多受欢迎"，原文完 全没有谈零食的受欢迎程度，也没把读者定义为movie fans。 中杯汽水为什么这样定价? A) 为了吸引更多顾客购买它。 B) 为了显示价格与分量相匹配。 C) 为了确保顾客饮用适量的汽水。 D) 为了让顾客相信他们得到了实惠。

questions.q: Why is the medium soda priced the way it is?
options: To attract more customers to buy it.
To show the price matches the amount.
To ensure customers drink the right amount of soda.
To make customers believe they are getting a bargain.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why is the medium soda priced the way it is问的是文中已明示的因果，是对原文具体信 息的再现，属于细节题。

【拆句】Why is the medium soda priced the way it is?主干为被动结构the medium soda is priced，the way it is是方式状语从句简写（=in the way that it is priced），整体问的 是"为何如此定价"。考生需读懂被动语态，把priced还原成"被定价"。 52. Why is the medium soda priced the way it is? A) To attract more customers to buy it. B) To show the price matches the amount. C) To ensure customers drink the right amount of soda. D) To make customers believe they are getting a bargain.

【定位】In fact, there's a good chance the marketing department purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small. 事实上，营销部门很可能是故意把中杯定价为诱饵，让你更倾向于买大杯而不是小杯。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 To attract more customers to buy it说的是"吸引更多顾客来买中杯"，但If you're wondering who would buy the medium soda, the answer is almost no one明确告 诉我们中杯定价的目的恰恰不是为了卖中杯本身。 B) 无中生有 To show the price matches the amount说的是"展示价格与分量相符"，但原文从未声 称中杯价格合理，反而暗示这种定价是营销操纵。 C) 偷换概念 To ensure customers drink the right amount of soda说的是"确保顾客喝合适的量"， 体现的是关怀消费者健康的善意动机；原文中营销部门的动机是purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy，即操纵性的，与善意正相反。 D) ✓ 正确 purposely priced the medium soda as a decoy, making you more likely to buy the large soda rather than the small ↔To make customers believe they are getting a bargain Medium may be the perfect amount of soda for you, but the large is only a quarter more ↔ getting a bargain 预判答案是"让顾客觉得大杯划算/占便宜"，make customers believe they are getting a bargain里getting a bargain正是"占便宜"的标准说法，与预判精准匹配。 我们从Dan Ariely的实验中了解到什么? A) 价格较低的商品吸引更多顾客。 B) The Economist的促销策略有效。 C) The Economist的印刷版最终卖得最好。 D) 更多读者选择数字版而非印刷版。

questions.q: What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment?
options: Lower-priced goods attract more customers.
The Economist's promotional strategy works.
The Economist's print edition turns out to sell the best.
More readers choose the digital over the print edition.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment问的是实验本身揭示了什么客观事实， 是对原文的转述，属细节题。

【拆句】What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment?是what引导的特殊疑问句，主干为we learn，from Dan Ariely's experiment为状语。结构直白，无陷阱。 53. What do we learn from Dan Ariely's experiment? A) Lower-priced goods attract more customers. B) The Economist's promotional strategy works. C) The Economist's print edition turns out to sell the best. D) More readers choose the digital over the print edition.

【定位】Ariely ran an experiment and found that when only the two "real" choices were offered, more people chose the less-expensive digital subscription. But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option. Ariely做了一个实验发现：只提供两个"真实"选项时，更多人选了便宜的纯数字订阅。但加 入那个糟糕的选项后，人们更倾向于选更贵的纸质加数字组合订阅。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Lower-priced goods attract more customers说的是"低价商品吸引更多顾客"。原文 在加诱饵后的结果恰是"更多人选了更贵的"，并非低价更受欢迎；实验的核心是揭示诱 饵效应，不是廉价致胜。 B) ✓ 正确 the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option ↔The Economist's promotional strategy works 预判答案是"实验证明诱饵策略有效"，The Economist's promotional strategy works 里works即"奏效、起作用"，与预判中"有效"匹配；且promotional strategy恰好概括了 The Economist的特殊定价做法。 C) 与原文相反 The Economist's print edition turns out to sell the best说的是"纯纸质版卖得最 好"，但原文No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription when you could get digital as well for the same price明确指出几乎没人单买纸质版——它 根本不是最好卖的，而是诱饵本身。 D) 以偏概全 More readers choose the digital over the print edition说的是"更多读者选数字版而 非纸质版"。这只在But之前的场景（只有两个真实选项时）成立，But之后the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option改变了这个结果——而题问的是从整个实验中学到了什么，应 当看But之后的发现。 添加"劣选项"是为了什么目的? A) 为了迎合某些顾客的特殊需求。 B) 为了帮助顾客做出更理性的选择。 C) 为了诱使顾客购买价格更高的商品。 D) 为了给顾客提供更多样化的商品。

questions.q: For what purpose is "the bad option" (Line 7, Para. 3) added?
options: To cater to the peculiar needs of some customers.
To help customers to make more rational choices.
To trap customers into buying the more pricey item.
To provide customers with a greater variety of goods.
questions.explain:
【判型】For what purpose is "the bad option" added问的是文中明示的添加目的，是对原文信息 的客观转述，归为细节题。

【拆句】For what purpose is "the bad option" (Line 7, Para. 3) added?是被动疑问句，For what purpose是疑问短语前置，主语是the bad option，谓语是is added。括号内的Line 7, Para. 3是位置提示，不算原文成分。

【定位】But the addition of the bad option made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option. 但加入那个糟糕的选项使得人们更倾向于选择更贵的"纸质加数字"组合订阅。

【选项】A) 无中生有 To cater to the peculiar needs of some customers说的是"迎合某些顾客的特殊需 求"，但原文中加入诱饵的目的是营销操纵，不是为了满足顾客的任何需求；原文里No one in their right mind would buy the print subscription更直接说明没人需要这个 选项。 B) 与原文相反 To help customers to make more rational choices说的是"帮助顾客作出更理性的选 择"，但原文加入诱饵恰恰让顾客作出了非理性的选择——选了更贵的而非更便宜的；选 项把操纵动机说成助人为乐，方向反了。 C) ✓ 正确 made people much more likely to choose the more expensive print plus digital option ↔ To trap customers into buying the more pricey item the more expensive print plus digital option ↔the more pricey item 预判答案为"使顾客买更贵的"，To trap customers into buying the more pricey item 里trap...into精准对应"诱饵"的负面操纵色彩，more pricey精准对应more expensive， 与预判完全匹配。 D) 偷换概念 To provide customers with a greater variety of goods说的是"为顾客提供更多种类的 商品"。原文中加诱饵不是为了丰富选项种类，而是为了利用对比心理把顾客推向最贵的 那个选项。 根据文章,我们如何评估商品的价值? A) 通过考虑它的实用性。 B) 通过将它与其他选择进行比较。 C) 通过将它的质量纳入考量。 D) 通过检查它的价值等式。

questions.q: How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?
options: By considering its usefulness.
By comparing it with other choices.
By taking its quality into account.
By examining its value equation.
questions.explain:
【判型】How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?末尾 according to the passage显式要求从文本中找答案，属细节题。

【拆句】How do we assess the value of a commodity, according to the passage?主干是How do we assess the value，of a commodity是修饰value的后置定语，according to the passage是插入语，表示信息来源。结构清晰。

【定位】Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices. 价值几乎从不是绝对的；而是说，我们是相对于自己拥有的其他选项来决定一个物品的 价值。

【选项】A) 无中生有 By considering its usefulness说的是"考虑其用处"，但原文Value is almost never absolute; rather, we decide an object's value relative to our other choices明确指出 价值是相对的，从未提到用处这个独立维度。 B) ✓ 正确 we decide an object's value relative to our other choices ↔ By comparing it with other choices decide an object's value ↔assess the value 预判答案为"相对于其他选项"，By comparing it with other choices的 comparing...with正是"相对"的动作化表达，与预判完全匹配。 C) 无中生有 By taking its quality into account说的是"将其质量纳入考量"，原文从头到尾未谈商品 质量；这是常识维度而非原文维度。 D) 偷换概念 By examining its value equation说的是"通过检视其价值等式"。原文If more options are introduced, the value equation changes里的value equation是对评估过程的命 名，不是用来评估的工具；选项把名词搬来制造熟悉，但用错了角色。

items.title: 2020年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Boredom has, paradoxically, become quite interesting to academics lately. In early May, London's Boring Conference celebrated seven years of delighting in dullness. At this event, people flocked to talks about weather, traffic jams and vending-machine sounds, among other sleep-inducing topics.

P2 What, exactly, is everybody studying? One widely accepted psychological definition of boredom is "the distasteful experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity." But how can you quantify a person's boredom level and compare it with someone else's? In 1986, psychologists introduced the Boredom Proneness Scale, designed to measure an individual's overall tendency to feel bored. By contrast, the Multidimensional State Boredom Scale, developed in 2008, measures a person's feelings of boredom in a given situation.

P3 Boredom has been linked to behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling. In fact, many of us would choose pain over boredom. One team of psychologists discovered that two-thirds of men and a quarter of women would rather self- administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes. Researching this phenomenon, another team asked volunteers to watch boring, sad, or neutral films, during which they could self-administer electric shocks. The bored volunteers shocked themselves more and harder than the sad or neutral ones did.

P4 But boredom isn't all bad. By encouraging self-reflection and daydreaming, it can spur creativity. An early study gave participants abundant time to complete problem-solving and word-association exercises. Once all the obvious answers were exhausted, participants gave more and more inventive answers to combat boredom. A British study took these findings one step further, asking subjects to complete a creative challenge (coming up with a list of alternative uses for a household item). One group of subjects did a boring activity first, while the others went straight to the creative task. Those whose boredom pumps had been primed were more productive.

P5 In our always-connected world, boredom may be a hard-to-define state, but it is a fertile one. Watch paint dry or water boil, or at least put away your smartphone for a while, and you might unlock your next big idea.

questions.q: When are people likely to experience boredom, according to an accepted psychological definition?
options: When they don't have the chance to do what they want.
When they don't enjoy the materials they are studying.
When they experience something unpleasant.
When they engage in some routine activities.
questions.explain:
【判型】When are people likely to experience boredom, according to an accepted psychological definition?是 When 引导的事实型疑问句，且明确以according to an accepted psychological definition限定信息来源，答案应是原文定义句的客观转述。

【拆句】题干主干是 When are people likely to experience boredom，主句问的是「时间/情 境」；后置介词短语according to an accepted psychological definition为状语，限定答 案来源必须是「公认的心理学定义」，不是作者本人观点或常识。

【定位】One widely accepted psychological definition of boredom is "the distasteful experience of wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity." 无聊在心理学上一个被广为接受的定义是「想去从事一项令人满足的活动，却无法去做时的 那种不快体验」。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 wanting, but being unable, to engage in satisfying activity ↔ don't have the chance to do what they want When they don't have the chance to do what they want.把原文定义句的两个核心成 分「有意愿」与「被阻止」一一保留，且未添加任何原文未给出的限定，是定义句的最 忠实改写。 B) 无中生有 When they don't enjoy the materials they are studying.把场景限定到「学习材 料」，但原文定义未提学习场景，纯属添油加醋。 C) 偷换概念 When they experience something unpleasant.把原文里的「不快体验」拿出来当条 件，可原文 distasteful experience 描述的是无聊本身（结果），不是触发无聊的条 件，因果倒置。 D) 与原文相反 When they engage in some routine activities.把无聊触发条件描述为「在做日常 活动」，可原文定义明确强调「想做却做不成」，主体是「未能从事」而非「正在 从事」。 作者认为无聊会导致什么? A) 决心。 B) 专注。 C) 精神退化。 D) 有害行为。

questions.q: What does the author say boredom can lead to?
options: Determination.
Concentration.
Mental deterioration.
Harmful conduct.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say boredom can lead to?是 What 引导的事实问句，问的是「无 聊会导致什么」，是对原文具体陈述的转述。

【拆句】句子主干 What ... boredom can lead to，是宾语前置的特殊疑问句；what 是 lead to 的 宾语，问的是「后果」。句中嵌入does the author say并非考点，仅说明信息来源是作者 陈述，结构无陷阱。

【定位】Boredom has been linked to behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling. 无聊与多种行为问题相关，包括驾驶时心不在焉、不动脑子地乱吃东西、过量饮酒以及嗜赌 成瘾。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Determination.意为「决心」，原文从未提到无聊会让人变得有决心；整段讨论的全是 负面后果，与正向心理品质毫无关联。 B) 与原文相反 Concentration.意为「专注」，与原文inattentive driving描述的「分心驾驶」恰好相 反；无聊导致的是注意力涣散，不是专注。 C) 过度推断 Mental deterioration.意为「精神/智力衰退」，是把原文里的具体行为问题进一步推到 「精神层面退化」的程度，原文未提任何精神疾病或认知衰退后果。 D) ✓ 正确 behavior issues including inattentive driving, mindless snacking, excessive drinking, and addictive gambling ↔Harmful conduct. Harmful conduct.既保留了 behavior=conduct 的词汇对应，又用 harmful 准确概括 了那四个具体后果的共同属性，是对原文罗列最贴切的总括式改写。 一组心理学家在实验中有什么发现? A) 志愿者更愿意看一部乏味的电影,而不是独自坐着思考。 B) 许多志愿者选择伤害自己,而不是忍受无聊。 C) 男性志愿者比女性更能抵御无聊的影响。 D) 许多志愿者无法忍受超过十五分钟的无聊。

questions.q: What is the finding of one team of psychologists in their experiment?
options: Volunteers prefer watching a boring movie to sitting alone deliberating.
Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom.
Male volunteers are more immune to the effects of boredom than females.
Many volunteers are unable to resist boredom longer than fifteen minutes.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the finding of one team of psychologists in their experiment?问的是具体实验 的结论事实，需回到该实验描述句做同义比对，属典型细节题。 48. What is the finding of one team of psychologists in their experiment? A) Volunteers prefer watching a boring movie to sitting alone deliberating. B) Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom. C) Male volunteers are more immune to the effects of boredom than females. D) Many volunteers are unable to resist boredom longer than fifteen minutes.

【拆句】主干 What is the finding，主系表结构；of one team of psychologists 修饰 finding，in their experiment 进一步限定研究情境。三层修饰只是把范围限到「那个团队那次实验的结 论」，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】One team of psychologists discovered that two-thirds of men and a quarter of women would rather self-administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes. 一组心理学家发现，三分之二的男性与四分之一的女性宁愿对自己施加电击，也不愿独自静 坐沉思 15 分钟。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Volunteers prefer watching a boring movie to sitting alone deliberating.把后文另 一项实验「看无聊片时电击自己」（another team asked volunteers to watch boring, sad, or neutral films）的实验对象混进来——这是另一团队的研究，对应另一 题的结论，不是本题考的实验。 B) ✓ 正确 would rather self-administer electric shocks than sit alone with their thoughts for 15 minutes ↔ Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom.
