Many volunteers choose to hurt themselves rather than endure boredom.既保留 了原文比较结构两端的方向，又把具体动作恰当上位化，是对实验发现的最忠实概括。 C) 与原文相反 Male volunteers are more immune to the effects of boredom than females.把男女 比例的差异解读成「男性更能抗无聊」，可原文是「三分之二男性 vs 四分之一女性都选 择了电击」——男性选择电击的比例反而更高，意味着男性更难忍无聊，结论方向完全 相反。 D) 过度推断 Many volunteers are unable to resist boredom longer than fifteen minutes.把 15 分钟当成志愿者能忍耐的上限，可原文只是说「实验设定独坐 15 分钟」，并未测出志愿 者的耐受阈值——结论从实验时长推到「忍耐极限」，多迈了一步。 作者为什么说无聊并非全是坏事? A) 它刺激记忆。 B) 它为放松提供了时间。 C) 它可能促进创造性思维。 D) 它可能促进自主学习。

questions.q: Why does the author say boredom isn't all bad?
options: It stimulates memorization.
It allows time for relaxation.
It may promote creative thinking.
It may facilitate independent learning.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author say boredom isn't all bad?问作者给出的理由，原文转折句后必紧 跟解释，答案是该解释句的转述。 49. Why does the author say boredom isn't all bad? A) It stimulates memorization. B) It allows time for relaxation. C) It may promote creative thinking. D) It may facilitate independent learning.

【拆句】句首 Why 引出原因；主谓 does the author say 套着宾语从句 boredom isn't all bad。从 句用 isn't all bad（部分否定）而非 isn't bad，表示「并非完全是坏事」，暗示后面一定有 正面意义的展开。

【定位】But boredom isn't all bad. By encouraging self-reflection and daydreaming, it can spur creativity. 但无聊也并非全是坏事。通过促进自省与遐想，它能激发创造力。

【选项】A) 无中生有 It stimulates memorization.说无聊会刺激记忆，但原文谈的是 self-reflection、 daydreaming、creativity，全程没有 memory/memorization 这一概念。 B) 偷换概念 It allows time for relaxation.把无聊的好处概括为「有时间放松」，可原文明确说的是 促进自省与遐想进而激发创造力，重点是「创造产出」而非「身心放松」。 C) ✓ 正确 it can spur creativity ↔It may promote creative thinking. It may promote creative thinking.两端的动词（spur→promote）和名词 （creativity→creative thinking）都做了精准的同义替换，且未引入任何超出原文的限 定，是理由句的最忠实改写。 D) 过度推断 It may facilitate independent learning.把好处推到「促进自主学习」，但原文谈的是 创造力，而非学习或独立学习；从「自我反思」推到「独立学习」多走了一步。 作者建议人们在面对具有挑战性的问题时应该做什么? A) 停止闲散,放眼大局。 B) 解锁自己的智能手机。 C) 环顾四周寻找刺激。 D) 允许自己有一些时间感到无聊。

questions.q: What does the author suggest one do when faced with a challenging problem?
options: Stop idling and think big.
Unlock one's smartphone.
Look around oneself for stimulation.
Allow oneself some time to be bored.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest one do when faced with a challenging problem?问的 是作者给出的具体行动建议，是原文建议句的客观转述，未要求推断。

【拆句】主干 What does the author suggest one do，其中 one do 是 suggest 后省略 that 与 should 的虚拟语气从句；when faced with a challenging problem 是过去分词作时间状 语，相当于 when one is faced with ...，意为「当面对难题时」。 50. What does the author suggest one do when faced with a challenging problem? A) Stop idling and think big. B) Unlock one's smartphone. C) Look around oneself for stimulation. D) Allow oneself some time to be bored.

【定位】Watch paint dry or water boil, or at least put away your smartphone for a while, and you might unlock your next big idea. 看油漆变干，看水烧开，或者至少先把手机放下一会儿，你就可能解开下一个大点子。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Stop idling and think big.让人停止闲散、去想大事，可原文恰恰建议你 idle 一会儿 （看油漆干、看水开就是 idling）——方向完全相反。 B) 与原文相反 Unlock one's smartphone.让人解锁手机，可原文建议的是put away your smartphone，即放下手机；动作方向完全相反。 C) 与原文相反 Look around oneself for stimulation.让人四处寻找刺激，可原文建议恰好是减少刺激 （看油漆、看水开都是极低刺激场景，放下手机是切断刺激源）——方向相反。 D) ✓ 正确 Watch paint dry or water boil, or at least put away your smartphone for a while ↔ Allow oneself some time to be bored. Allow oneself some time to be bored.既呼应了尾段「主动放空」的具体动作，又与 全文「无聊能激发创造力」的主旨完全对齐，是对建议句最贴切的上位概括。

items.title: 2020年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo get a lot of attention from environmentalists, and it is easy to see why. South America and sub-Saharan Africa are experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale: every year almost 5 million hectares are lost. But forests are also changing in rich Western countries. They are growing larger, both in the sense that they occupy more land and that the trees in them are bigger. What is going on?

P2 Forests are spreading in almost all Western countries, with the fastest growth in places that historically had rather few trees. In 1990 28% of Spain was forested; now the proportion is 37%. In both Greece and Italy, the growth was from 26% to 32% over the same period. Forests are gradually taking more land in America and Australia. Perhaps most astonishing is the trend in Ireland. Roughly 1% of that country was forested when it became independent in 1922. Now forests cover 11% of the land, and the government wants to push the proportion to 18% by the 2040s.

P3 Two things are fertilising this growth. The first is the abandonment of farmland, especially in high, dry places where nothing grows terribly well. When farmers give up trying to earn a living from farming or herding, trees simply move in. The second is government policy and subsidy. Throughout history, governments have protected and promoted forests for diverse reasons, ranging from the need for wooden warships to a desire to promote suburban house-building. Nowadays forests are increasingly welcome because they suck in carbon pollution from the air. The justifications change, the desire for more trees remains constant.

P4 The greening of the West does not delight everyone. Farmers complain that land is being taken out of use by generously subsidised tree plantations. Parts of Spain and Portugal suffer from terrible forest fires. Others simply dislike the appearance of forests planted in neat rows. They will have to get used to the trees, however. The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere.

questions.q: What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays?
options: Rich countries are stripping poor ones of their resources.
Forests are fast shrinking in many developing countries.
Forests are eating away the fertile farmland worldwide.
Rich countries are doing little to address deforestation.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays? 是直接的特殊疑问句，问的 是一个具体事实，不含 infer、suggest、imply，也不问全篇主旨。

【拆句】题干 What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays? 是现在进行时的特殊疑 问句，主语是疑问代词 What，谓语 is catching 带宾语 environmentalists' attention，时 间状语 nowadays 在句末。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays? A) Rich countries are stripping poor ones of their resources. B) Forests are fast shrinking in many developing countries. C) Forests are eating away the fertile farmland worldwide. D) Rich countries are doing little to address deforestation.

【定位】Forests in countries like Brazil and the Congo get a lot of attention from environmentalists, and it is easy to see why. South America and sub-Saharan Africa are experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale: every year almost 5 million hectares are lost. 巴西、刚果这些国家的森林正得到环保人士的大量关注，原因不难看出。南美和撒哈拉以南 非洲正以巨大规模经历森林砍伐：每年几乎损失 500 万公顷。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只指出环保人士关注发展中地区的森林消失，并没说 Rich countries are stripping poor ones of their resources，这是套用国际关系常见话术编造出的内容。 B) ✓ 正确 Brazil and the Congo ↔many developing countries experiencing deforestation on an enormous scale ↔fast shrinking 预判说「发展中地区森林大规模消失」，Forests are fast shrinking in many developing countries. 在主语、动词、地域限定三处都与原文等值，是定位句的同义 替换。 C) 与原文相反 原文讲的是森林正在消失，选项却说 Forests are eating away the fertile farmland worldwide——森林在侵蚀农田，主客体关系恰好颠倒；首段也未提及 worldwide farmland 被吞噬。 D) 答非所问 题干问的是 What is catching environmentalists' attention nowadays?——环保人士 关注的是什么，而 Rich countries are doing little to address deforestation 是对富国 不作为的指责，原文首段并没有这一指控。 哪些国家的森林增长最快? A) 那些新近获得独立的国家。 B) 那些对木材需求最大的国家。 C) 那些过去森林覆盖率最低的国家。 D) 那些提供巨额政府补贴的国家。

questions.q: Which countries have the fastest forest growth?
options: Those that have newly achieved independence.
Those that have the greatest demand for timber.
Those that used to have the lowest forest coverage.
Those that provide enormous government subsidies.
questions.explain:
【判型】Which countries have the fastest forest growth? 直接问「哪些国家」，是对原文具体信 息的客观提取。

【拆句】题干 Which countries have the fastest forest growth? 是 Which 引导的特殊疑问句， Which countries 作主语，have 作谓语，宾语 the fastest forest growth。结构简单。 52. Which countries have the fastest forest growth? A) Those that have newly achieved independence. B) Those that have the greatest demand for timber. C) Those that used to have the lowest forest coverage. D) Those that provide enormous government subsidies.

【定位】Forests are spreading in almost all Western countries, with the fastest growth in places that historically had rather few trees. 几乎所有西方国家的森林都在扩展，其中增长最快的地方是那些历史上树木相当稀少的 国家。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 原文只用 Ireland 作为戏剧性案例（1922 年独立时 1%、现在 11%），并未说「森林增 长最快的是新近独立的国家」这一普遍规律，Those that have newly achieved independence. 是把单一举例拔高为通则。 B) 无中生有 the greatest demand for timber 在 P2 全段从未出现，森林增长最快的原因被原文限 定为「历史上树少」，而非木材需求。 C) ✓ 正确 historically had rather few trees ↔used to have the lowest forest coverage 预判说「历史上树木很少的国家」，Those that used to have the lowest forest coverage. 把「过去树少」换说成「过去森林覆盖率最低」，二者完全同义，因此 锁定。 D) 张冠李戴 enormous government subsidies 对应的是 P3 提到的 government policy and subsidy，那讨论的是「促进森林增长的因素」，不是 Q52 所问的「哪国增长最快」， 跨段错位。 历史上是什么促进了森林增长? A) 政府的倡导。 B) 木材用作燃料。 C) 有利的气候。 D) 环保运动。

questions.q: What has encouraged forest growth historically?
options: The government's advocacy.
The use of wood for fuel.
The favourable climate.
The green movement.
questions.explain:
【判型】What has encouraged forest growth historically? 问的是历史上具体促进森林增长的因 素，是对文中事实的提取，不要求多步推理。

【拆句】题干 What has encouraged forest growth historically? 是现在完成时特殊疑问句，What 作主语，has encouraged 作谓语，forest growth 作宾语，historically 是时间状语。现在 完成时强调「从过去延续到现在」的累积效应。

【定位】Throughout history, governments have protected and promoted forests for diverse reasons, ranging from the need for wooden warships to a desire to promote suburban house-building. 纵观历史，政府出于各种理由保护并推动森林的扩张，从制造木质战舰的需要，到希望促进 郊区住宅建设。 53. What has encouraged forest growth historically? A) The government's advocacy. B) The use of wood for fuel. C) The favourable climate. D) The green movement.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 governments have protected and promoted forests ↔The government's advocacy 预判说「历史上是政府保护并推动了森林」，The government's advocacy. 用名词形式 精准对应原文动词短语 promoted。 B) 偷换概念 原文虽提到 the need for wooden warships，但 warships 是用木材造战舰，并非烧木 头做燃料；The use of wood for fuel 偷换了用途。 C) 无中生有 原文讲历史上促进森林的是政府政策，没有提到 favourable climate 这一自然因素；这 是套用常识编造。 D) 张冠李戴 The green movement 属于近现代环保运动，对应原文 Nowadays 这一时间段，而题 干限定的是 historically 历史范围，时段不匹配。 是什么导致我们对森林的渴望日益增加? A) 它们独特的景观之美。 B) 它们作为果园的用途。 C) 它们改善空气质量的能力。 D) 它们稳定的建筑材料供应。

questions.q: What accounts for our increasing desire for forests?
options: Their unique scenic beauty.
Their use as fruit plantations.
Their capability of improving air quality.
Their stable supply of building materials.
questions.explain:
【判型】What accounts for our increasing desire for forests? 用 account for 直接问原因，对应 文中应有明确的因果句，属于事实信息提取。

【拆句】题干 What accounts for our increasing desire for forests? 中 account for 是固定短语， 意为「解释、是…的原因」。基础薄弱考生易把它误读成「算作」，须当心；除此之外句式 简单。

【定位】Nowadays forests are increasingly welcome because they suck in carbon pollution from the air. 如今森林越来越受欢迎，因为它们能吸走空气中的碳污染。 54. What accounts for our increasing desire for forests? A) Their unique scenic beauty. B) Their use as fruit plantations. C) Their capability of improving air quality. D) Their stable supply of building materials.

【选项】A) 无中生有 unique scenic beauty 在 P3 中并不存在；末段反而说 Others simply dislike the appearance of forests planted in neat rows，强调有人对景观不满，把「景观美」作 为渴求理由完全是无中生有。 B) 无中生有 use as fruit plantations 在 P3 全段未出现，原文用 plantations 是泛指「种植园」， 与水果无关。 C) ✓ 正确 suck in carbon pollution from the air ↔capability of improving air quality 预判说「森林能净化空气」，Their capability of improving air quality. 是这一句的标 准学术化转述，因此锁定。 D) 张冠李戴 supply of building materials 对应原文 wooden warships 与 suburban house- building，但那都是 Throughout history 段提及的历史理由，不是 Q54 所问的「如今 越发渴求」的理由。 作者对造林前景得出了什么结论? A) 撒哈拉以南非洲的沙漠将逐渐减少。 B) 它将在人们生活中发挥越来越重要的作用。 C) 发展中国家的森林破坏将迅速放缓。 D) 发达国家和发展中国家正朝着相反的方向发展。

questions.q: What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation?
options: Deserts in sub-Saharan Africa will diminish gradually.
It will play a more and more important role in people's lives.
Forest destruction in the developing world will quickly slow down.
Developed and developing countries are moving in opposite directions.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation? 问的是作者对整 体前景的结论，覆盖全文走向，不可由单一定位句直接拿到。

【拆句】题干 What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation? 是宾语从句 结构的特殊疑问句，What 是 conclude 的宾语，about the prospects of forestation 是 conclude 的状语，限定结论的话题对象。 55. What does the author conclude about the prospects of forestation? A) Deserts in sub-Saharan Africa will diminish gradually. B) It will play a more and more important role in people's lives. C) Forest destruction in the developing world will quickly slow down. D) Developed and developing countries are moving in opposite directions.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Deserts in sub-Saharan Africa will diminish gradually. 蹭了 sub-Saharan Africa 这 一地名，但话题对象从「森林」被偷换为「沙漠」，原文从未讨论沙漠消长。 B) 过度推断 It will play a more and more important role in people's lives. 是抒情式价值判断， 与原文末句「两条趋势同样不可阻挡」的冷静对照不匹配；原文从未把森林作用提升到 「在人们生活中越发重要」的层面。 C) 与原文相反 原文末句明说 The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere——他处毁林同样不可阻挡，而 Forest destruction in the developing world will quickly slow down. 却说「很快放缓」，方向相反。 D) ✓ 正确 The growth of Western forests seems almost as unstoppable as deforestation elsewhere ↔ moving in opposite directions But forests are also changing in rich Western countries. They are growing larger ↔Developed South America and sub-Saharan Africa ↔developing Developed and developing countries are moving in opposite directions. 同时容纳 了全文「造林与毁林」两条主线，与末句并置结构完美对齐，是唯一覆盖全文且不与任 何区间冲突的选项。

items.title: 2020年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 A growing number of U.S. bike riders are attracted to electric bikes for convenience, health benefits and their fun factor. Although ebikes first appeared in the 90s, cheaper options and longer-lasting batteries are breathing new life into the concept.

P2 Established bike companies and startups are embracing ebikes to meet demand. About 34 million ebikes were sold worldwide last year, according to data from eCycleElectric Consultants. Most were sold in Europe and China, where the bikes already have exploded in popularity. Recently, the U.S. market has grown to 263,000 bikes, a 25% gain from the prior year.

P3 The industry is benefiting from improved batteries as suppliers over the years developed technology for laptops, smartphones and electric cars. In 2004, the price of batteries used on ebikes fell, spurring European sales.

P4 But lower cost options are emerging, too. This month, three U.S. bikeshare companies, Motivate, LimeBike and Spin, announced electric bicycles will be added to their fleets. New York-based Jump Bikes is already operating an electric bikeshare in Washington, D.C., and is launching in San Francisco Thursday. Rides cost $2 for 30 minutes.

P5 The system works like existing dockless bikeshare systems, where riders unlock bikes through a smartphone app. "This is the beginning of a long-term shift away from regular pedal(踏板) to electric bikes," said Jump Bikes CEO Ryan Rzepecki. "When people first jump on an ebike, their face lights up. It's exciting and joyful in a way that you don't get from a regular bike."

P6 Two years ago, CEO Chris Cocalis of Pivot Cycles, which sells high-end mountain bikes, found that U.S. bike shops weren't interested in stocking ebikes. Some retailers warned Cocalis that they'd drop the brand if it came out with an electric bike.

P7 Now that sales are taking off, the vast majority of bike dealers are asking Cocalis when he'll make an ebike available. "There's tremendous opportunity to get a generation of people for whom suffering isn't their thing," Cocalis said. "Ebike riders get the enjoyable part of cycling without the massive suffering of climbing huge hills."

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about ebikes?
options: Their health benefits and fun values outweigh their cost.
They did not catch public attention in the United States until the 1990s.
They did not become popular until the emergence of improved batteries.
Their widespread use is attributable to people's environmental awareness.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about ebikes? 没有 infer/imply/mainly about， 问的是文中陈述的客观信息，四个选项各对应一处事实，属于综合性细节判断。 46. What do we learn from the passage about ebikes? A) Their health benefits and fun values outweigh their cost. B) They did not catch public attention in the United States until the 1990s. C) They did not become popular until the emergence of improved batteries. D) Their widespread use is attributable to people's environmental awareness.

【拆句】What do we learn from the passage about ebikes? 是常规疑问句：主干是 What do we learn，about ebikes 是介词短语限定话题，from the passage 提示答题范围在通篇，无 陷阱结构。

【定位】Although ebikes first appeared in the 90s, cheaper options and longer-lasting batteries are breathing new life into the concept. 尽管电动自行车早在 90 年代就出现了，但更便宜的款式和更耐用的电池正在为这个概念注 入新的生命力。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文只说 convenience, health benefits and their fun factor 是吸引人骑电动车的 几个并列原因，并没有把「健康与乐趣」与「成本」放在一起比，更没说「前者超过 后者」。 B) 偷换概念 原文 ebikes first appeared in the 90s 是说「90 年代才首次出现」，没有「在那之前 美国人不知道、之后才关注」的意思；而 They did not catch public attention in the United States until the 1990s. 把「出现」偷换成了「引起公众关注」。 C) ✓ 正确 Although ebikes first appeared in the 90s, cheaper options and longer-lasting batteries are breathing new life into the concept. ↔They did not become popular until the emergence of improved batteries. 预判的「电池变好才流行」与 They did not become popular until the emergence of improved batteries. 的「直到电池改良才流行」语义完全一致；首段又用 The industry is benefiting from improved batteries 强化「电池→产业受益」的因果，可 二次确认。 D) 无中生有 全文只字未提 environmental awareness（环保意识），原文给出的流行原因是 convenience, health benefits and their fun factor 与电池改进，没有任何句子把「环 保」列为推动因素。 是什么在世纪之初促成了欧洲电动自行车销量的增长? A) 自行车制造技术的更新。 B) 电动自行车电池价格的下降。 C) 短途出行方式的改变。 D) 制造电动汽车成本的上升。

questions.q: What brought about the boost in ebike sales in Europe at the beginning of the century?
options: Updated technology of bike manufacture.
The falling prices of ebike batteries.
Changed fashion in short-distance travel.
The rising costs for making electric cars.
questions.explain:
【判型】What brought about the boost in ebike sales in Europe at the beginning of the century? 是 What brought about 句式，问引起某事件的具体原因，是一道指向明确的因 果细节题。

【拆句】What brought about the boost in ebike sales in Europe at the beginning of the century? 主干是 What brought about the boost，in ebike sales 修饰 boost，in Europe 与 at the beginning of the century 是两个并列状语，分别给出地点与时间，结构 清晰、无陷阱。

【定位】In 2004, the price of batteries used on ebikes fell, spurring European sales. 2004 年，用于电动自行车的电池价格下降，促使欧洲销量大增。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文谈的是 The industry is benefiting from improved batteries as suppliers over the years developed technology for laptops, smartphones and electric cars.—— 技术进步发生在电池领域（且来自笔记本、手机、电动汽车），不是 bike manufacture （自行车制造）。 B) ✓ 正确 In 2004, the price of batteries used on ebikes fell, spurring European sales. ↔ The falling prices of ebike batteries. 预判「电池价格下降」与 The falling prices of ebike batteries. 完全一致；spurring 这个分词正好把「价格下降」与「欧洲销量」用因果绑在一起，无需推理。 C) 无中生有 原文从未提及 short-distance travel（短途出行）这个概念，更未把它和欧洲销量增长 挂钩；考生若凭「电动车=城市短途」的常识硬选，就掉进无中生有陷阱。 D) 偷换概念 原文只说电池技术是从 laptops, smartphones and electric cars 这些领域延伸过来 的，并没说「电动汽车制造成本上升」导致电动自行车在欧洲热销；选项把不相关的两 件事强行拼接。 根据Ryan Rzepecki的说法,自行车行业的前景如何? A) 将有更多资金投入到自行车电池研究中。 B) 电动自行车的销量将增加。 C) 该行业将从电动自行车共享中获益。 D) 该行业将对人们的日常生活产生影响。

questions.q: What is the prospect of the bike industry according to Ryan Rzepecki?
options: More will be invested in bike battery research.
The sales of ebikes will increase.
It will profit from ebike sharing.
It will make a difference in people's daily lives.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the prospect of the bike industry according to Ryan Rzepecki? 用 according to + 人名，问的是他对前景的具体看法，答案应在他的原话里直接拿到，是定向细节题。

【拆句】What is the prospect of the bike industry according to Ryan Rzepecki? 是简单疑问 句：主干 What is the prospect，of the bike industry 修饰 prospect，according to Ryan Rzepecki 限定信息源，无陷阱。

【定位】This is the beginning of a long-term shift away from regular pedal(踏板) to electric bikes. 这是从普通脚踏自行车向电动自行车长期转变的开端。

【选项】A) 无中生有 CEO 原话谈的是「骑行体验」和「长期转向」，与「投资电池研究」无关；原文第 3 段 提到电池技术从其他行业受益，但从未说会加大对电池研究的投入。 B) ✓ 正确 This is the beginning of a long-term shift away from regular pedal(踏板) to electric bikes. ↔ The sales of ebikes will increase. 预判的「销量会持续增长」与 The sales of ebikes will increase. 在语义上一致；且第 2 段已铺垫 the U.S. market has grown to 263,000 bikes, a 25% gain from the prior year，这种「长期转向」在 CEO 嘴里说出，结合销量背景，必然指向「销量上升」。 C) 偷换概念 原文确实在 P4 P5 介绍了 Jump Bikes 等公司的共享业务，但 CEO 的原话谈的是「骑 行体验与长期转向」，没有说整个产业会「靠共享盈利」。 D) 过度推断 CEO 原话只说「是一次长期转向的开端」，并未上升到「改变人们日常生活」的层级； 考生若把「长期转向」凭印象拔高，就会过度推断。 是什么阻止了Chris Cocalis更早开发电动自行车? A) 零售商拒绝经营电动自行车。 B) 传统自行车带来的高额利润。 C) 用户对骑行电动自行车风险的担忧。 D) 他专注于销售昂贵的山地自行车。

questions.q: What prevented Chris Cocalis from developing ebikes sooner?
options: Retailers' refusal to deal in ebikes.
High profits from conventional bikes.
Users' concern about risks of ebike riding.
His focus on selling costly mountain bikes.
questions.explain:
【判型】What prevented Chris Cocalis from developing ebikes sooner? 问的是阻碍发生在过去 的具体事实，需要在原文找到对应的客观陈述，属典型细节题。 49. What prevented Chris Cocalis from developing ebikes sooner? A) Retailers' refusal to deal in ebikes. B) High profits from conventional bikes. C) Users' concern about risks of ebike riding. D) His focus on selling costly mountain bikes.

【拆句】What prevented Chris Cocalis from developing ebikes sooner? 主干是 What prevented Chris Cocalis，from developing ebikes sooner 是 prevent sb from doing sth 的固定搭配，意为「阻止他更早开发电动车」；考生若没掌握这个搭配，容易把 prevent ... from 理解反，需特别留意。

【定位】Two years ago, CEO Chris Cocalis of Pivot Cycles, which sells high-end mountain bikes, found that U.S. bike shops weren't interested in stocking ebikes. Some retailers warned Cocalis that they'd drop the brand if it came out with an electric bike. 两年前，主营高端山地车的 Pivot Cycles 公司 CEO Chris Cocalis 发现，美国的自行车商 店并没有兴趣进电动自行车。一些零售商警告 Cocalis，如果他出电动车，他们就停售他的 品牌。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Some retailers warned Cocalis that they'd drop the brand if it came out with an electric bike. ↔ Retailers' refusal to deal in ebikes. 预判的「零售商不愿进货+威胁停售」与 Retailers' refusal to deal in ebikes. 完全等 值；refusal to deal in（拒绝经营）是 weren't interested in stocking + warned ... they'd drop the brand 的概括。 B) 无中生有 原文只说 Pivot Cycles, which sells high-end mountain bikes，介绍公司业务，未提 及「传统车带来高利润」或他舍不得放弃高利润；考生凭「高端=高利润」的常识硬补， 是无中生有。 C) 无中生有 全文从未提到 risk of ebike riding（电动车骑行风险）或 users' concern（用户担 忧）；阻碍来自零售商，而不是用户的安全顾虑。 D) 偷换概念 Pivot Cycles, which sells high-end mountain bikes 只是介绍公司业务的非限制性定 语从句，是背景；并不是「他专注卖高端山地车」导致他没做电动车——阻碍来自零售 商，不来自他自己。 是什么让Chris Cocalis相信电动自行车销售有更大的机会? A) 电动自行车价格的进一步降低。 B) 公众对健康的关注。 C) 对登山运动日益增长的兴趣。 D) 年轻一代对舒适骑行的追求。

questions.q: What makes Chris Cocalis believe there is a greater opportunity for ebike sales?
options: The further lowering of ebike prices.
The public's concern for their health.
The increasing interest in mountain climbing.
The younger generation's pursuit of comfortable riding.
questions.explain:
【判型】What makes Chris Cocalis believe there is a greater opportunity for ebike sales? 问的 是导致他形成某观点的具体理由，答案应在他原话里给出，属于定向细节题。

【拆句】What makes Chris Cocalis believe there is a greater opportunity for ebike sales? 主干 What makes Chris Cocalis believe ...，make sb do sth 表「使某人……」，believe 后接 that 从句（that 省略），从句主干是 there is a greater opportunity，for ebike sales 修 饰 opportunity；结构层级清晰，但 make sb believe 后接长从句，基础薄弱考生可能把 believe 误当成名词，需提醒。

【定位】There's tremendous opportunity to get a generation of people for whom suffering isn't their thing. Ebike riders get the enjoyable part of cycling without the massive suffering of climbing huge hills. 存在一个巨大的机会，能争取到一整代不愿吃苦的人。骑电动车的人可以享受骑行的乐趣， 而不必承受爬大坡那种痛苦折磨。

【选项】A) 答非所问 电动车价格下降在 cheaper options 与 the price of batteries used on ebikes fell 中 出现过，但 Cocalis 在 P7 谈到机会时，理由是「一代人不愿吃苦」，与价格无关。 B) 答非所问 health benefits 确实是电动车整体吸引力之一，但 Cocalis 在 P7 谈机会时，给出的理 由是「不愿吃苦」，与公众健康关注无关。 C) 与原文相反 原文 without the massive suffering of climbing huge hills 说的是骑电动车可以免去 爬坡的折磨——也就是说人们想避开爬坡，而不是对爬山兴趣上升。 D) ✓ 正确 There's tremendous opportunity to get a generation of people for whom suffering isn't their thing. ↔The younger generation's pursuit of comfortable riding. 预判的「新一代不愿吃苦、追求舒适」与 The younger generation's pursuit of comfortable riding. 完全对应；原话两句一起构成完整因果：「有一代人不愿吃苦」+ 「电动车让骑行享受而不痛苦」——这正是他看到机会的依据。

items.title: 2020年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2020年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 The terms "global warming" and "climate change" are used by many, seemingly interchangeably. But do they really mean the same thing?

P2 Scientists shaped the history of the terms while attempting to accurately describe how humans continue to alter the planet. Later, political strategists adopted the terms to influence public opinion.

P3 In 1975, geochemist Wallace Broecker introduced the term "climate change" in an article published by Science. In 1979, a National Academy of Sciences report used the term "global warming" to define increases in the Earth's average surface temperature, while "climate change" more broadly referred to the numerous effects of this increase, such as sea-level rise and ocean acidification(酸化).

P4 During the following decades, some industrialists and politicians launched a campaign to sow doubt in the minds of the American public about the ability of fossil-fuel use, deforestation and other human activities to influence the planet's climate.

P5 Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt. For example, the language and polls expert Frank Luntz wrote a memo encouraging the use of "climate change" because the phrase sounded less scary than "global warming," reported the Guardian.

P6 However, Luntz's recommendation wasn't necessary. A Google Ngram Viewer chart shows that by 1993 climate change was already more commonly used in books than global warming. By the end of the next decade both words were used more frequently, and climate change was used nearly twice as often as global warming.

P7 NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes to the planet caused by increasing amounts of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.

P8 The debate isn't new. A century ago, chemist Svante Arrhenius started one of the first debates over the potential for humans to influence the planet's climate. Arrhenius calculated the capability of carbon dioxide to trap heat in the Earth's atmosphere, but other chemists disagreed. Some argued that humans weren't producing enough greenhouse gases, while others claimed the effects would be tiny. Now, of course, we know that whatever you call it, human behavior is warming the planet, with grave consequences ahead.

questions.q: Why did politicians use the two terms "global warming" and "climate change"?
options: To sway public opinion of the impact of human activities on Earth.
To more accurately describe the consequences of human activities.
To win more popular votes in their campaign activities.
To assure the public of the safety of existing industries.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did politicians use the two terms 问的是政客使用这两个词的具体原因，属对文中明 示原因的事实性提问。

【拆句】题干 Why did politicians use the two terms "global warming" and "climate change"? 主干是 "Why did politicians use the two terms"，引号里的两个术语只是 the two terms 的同位补充，句式平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Later, political strategists adopted the terms to influence public opinion. 后来，政治策略家们采用这些术语，是为了影响公众舆论。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 to influence public opinion ↔To sway public opinion how humans continue to alter the planet ↔the impact of human activities on Earth 把 to influence public opinion 改成 To sway public opinion 再叠加上文 "how humans alter the planet" 的名词化转述，正好等价于 To sway public opinion of the impact of human activities on Earth.。 B) 张冠李戴 To more accurately describe the consequences of human activities. 这是 Scientists shaped the history of the terms while attempting to accurately describe how humans continue to alter the planet. 里科学家的目的，被错配到政客 头上。 C) 无中生有 To win more popular votes in their campaign activities. 文章只字未提选举或拉票； launched a campaign 中的 campaign 指"运动"而非"竞选活动"。 D) 与原文相反 To assure the public of the safety of existing industries. 与原文相反——launched a campaign to sow doubt 表明政客是制造怀疑、并非给公众吃定心丸。 在美国国家科学院报告中使用的"气候变化"一词与"全球变暖"的不同之处在于_________。 A) 听起来不那么模糊 B) 看起来更科学 C) 涵盖更多现象 D) 更接近现实

questions.q: As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global
options: it sounds less vague
it looks more scientific
it covers more phenomena
it is much closer to reality
questions.explain:
【判型】As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________. 问的是该报告里两词的具体差异，属事实层 提问。 52. As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________. A) it sounds less vague B) it looks more scientific C) it covers more phenomena D) it is much closer to reality

【拆句】题干 As used in a National Academy of Sciences report, the term "climate change" differs from "global warming" in that_________. 是个待补全的陈述句，主干 "the term climate change differs from global warming in that ..."，As 引导的状语限定范围；空格 由 in that 引导的从句填，选项即从句内容。

【定位】In 1979, a National Academy of Sciences report used the term "global warming" to define increases in the Earth's average surface temperature, while "climate change" more broadly referred to the numerous effects of this increase, such as sea-level rise and ocean acidification(酸化). 1979 年，美国国家科学院的一份报告用 global warming 这个术语来指地球地表平均温度 的上升，而 climate change 则更广泛地指这一升温带来的诸多影响，例如海平面上升和海 洋酸化。

【选项】A) 答非所问 it sounds less vague 谈的是"听起来更不含糊"，可这个报告本身比较的是两术语的指代 范围，不是听感；听感是 P5 里 Luntz 的话题，与本题报告无关。 B) 无中生有 it looks more scientific 谈"显得更科学"，原文从未比较两术语的科学性观感，纯属 编造。 C) ✓ 正确 more broadly referred to the numerous effects ↔it covers more phenomena 预判已经定调"climate change 范围更宽"，四个选项里只有 it covers more phenomena 直接讲范围差异，与定位句中 more broadly + numerous effects 一一 对位。 D) 无中生有 it is much closer to reality 说"更贴近现实"，原文并未在该报告中比较两术语谁更接近 实际，是无中生有。 20世纪末的实业家采取了什么手段来误导美国人? A) 编造的调查结果。 B) 虚假的研究发现。 C) 雇用气候专家。 D) 刻意选择措辞。

questions.q: What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans?
options: Made-up survey results.
False research findings.
Hired climate experts.
Deliberate choice of words.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans? 问的是实业家采取的具体手段，属对文中明示信息的事实性提问。 53. What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans? A) Made-up survey results. B) False research findings. C) Hired climate experts. D) Deliberate choice of words.

【拆句】题干 What did industrialists of the late 20th century resort to in order to mislead Americans? 主干 "What did industrialists resort to"，of the late 20th century 修饰 industrialists，in order to mislead Americans 是目的状语；resort to 意为"诉诸于"，是 高频四级词组。

【定位】Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt. For example, the language and polls expert Frank Luntz wrote a memo encouraging the use of "climate change" because the phrase sounded less scary than "global warming," reported the Guardian. 用词起到了关键作用，造就了那种怀疑。例如，语言与民调专家 Frank Luntz 写了一份备忘 录，建议使用 climate change，因为它听起来不像 global warming 那么吓人——《卫 报》报道。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Made-up survey results. 说"伪造调查结果"，原文只字未提调查造假，纯属编造。 B) 无中生有 False research findings. 说"虚假的研究发现"，原文从未提及实业家发布假研究，只提 了使用词汇上的策略。 C) 张冠李戴 Hired climate experts. 把 the language and polls expert Frank Luntz 的身份错置 ——Luntz 是语言与民调专家，并非气候专家，且原文未说他被实业家雇佣。 D) ✓ 正确 Word use played a critical role in developing that doubt. ↔Deliberate choice of words. 预判已明确"在用词上做手脚"，四个选项里只有 Deliberate choice of words. 谈选词， 其他三个分别引到调查、研究、专家，都不是文中点出的手段。 NASA为什么选择"气候变化"这个术语? A) 为了获得更多资金。 B) 为了更精确。 C) 出于政治需要。 D) 为了避免争论。

questions.q: Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"?
options: To obtain more funds.
For greater precision.
For political needs.
To avoid debate.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"? 是 Why 提问，问 NASA 选这个术 语的原因，原文必有直接对应句。

【拆句】题干 Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"? 是简单疑问句，主干 "Why did NASA choose the term"，引号短语作 choose 的宾语，句式无陷阱。 54. Why did NASA choose the term "climate change"? A) To obtain more funds. B) For greater precision. C) For political needs. D) To avoid debate.

【定位】NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes to the planet caused by increasing amounts of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere. 美国国家航空航天局之所以使用 climate change 这个术语，是因为它能更准确地反映由大 气中温室气体增加所引发的地球范围广泛的变化。

【选项】A) 无中生有 To obtain more funds. 谈"获取更多资金"，原文从未提及 NASA 的预算或经费问题。 B) ✓ 正确 more accurately reflects ↔For greater precision 预判已经给出"为了更准确"这个核心，四个选项里只有 For greater precision 谈精准 度，其他三个引到资金、政治、避免争论，都没在 P7 中出现过。 C) 张冠李戴 For political needs. 谈"出于政治需要"，这是 political strategists 与 industrialists and politicians 的动机，而非 NASA 的；NASA 的选词理由是科学准确性。 D) 无中生有 To avoid debate. 说"为了避免争论"，原文 P7 只字未提 NASA 想回避争论；P8 反而表 明争论一直存在、不可回避。 作者的最终结论是什么? A) 全球变暖是更准确的术语。 B) 术语的准确性在科学中很重要。 C) 人类活动对地球有严重影响。 D) 政治干扰严肃的科学辩论。

questions.q: What is the author's final conclusion?
options: Global warming is the more accurate term.
Accuracy of terminology matters in science.
Human activities have serious effects on Earth.
Politics interferes with serious scientific debate.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the author's final conclusion? 问的是作者的最终结论，是对全文中心的提问，不 靠某一句的细节解决。

【拆句】题干 What is the author's final conclusion? 是 What is 句型，主干极简，author's final 是 conclusion 的双层修饰，提示找全文末尾的总结表态。 55. What is the author's final conclusion? A) Global warming is the more accurate term. B) Accuracy of terminology matters in science. C) Human activities have serious effects on Earth. D) Politics interferes with serious scientific debate.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Global warming is the more accurate term. 说 global warming 更准确，恰好和 NASA used the term "climate change" because it more accurately reflects the wide range of changes 与 whatever you call it 的立场相反。 B) 以偏概全 Accuracy of terminology matters in science. 把"术语精确度"当作全文主旨，但这只 是 P3、P7 这两个局部所谈，作者在末段已明确越过术语之争，落点在"人类影响"。 C) ✓ 正确 human behavior is warming the planet, with grave consequences ahead ↔ Human activities have serious effects on Earth. Human activities have serious effects on Earth. 既概括了 P8 末句的核心判断，也 覆盖前文 P3 提到的海平面上升、海洋酸化等具体后果，是唯一兼顾主线与全文铺垫的 选项。 D) 以偏概全 Politics interferes with serious scientific debate. 说"政治干预严肃科学辩论"，这只是 P4\~P5 局部话题，且原文未给出"干预了严肃科学辩论"这样的明确价值判断，更不是作 者最终结论。

items.title: 2021年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2021年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Educators and business leaders have more in common than it may seem. Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future. Technology companies have an interest in developing a workforce with the STEM (science, technology, engineering and math) skills needed to grow the company and advance the industry. How can they work together to achieve these goals? Play may be the answer.

P2 Focusing on STEM skills is important, but the reality is that STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities. This combination is proving to be the best way to prepare today's children to be the makers and builders of tomorrow. That is why technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good, old-fashioned play.

P3 In fact many experts argue that the most important 21st-century skills aren't related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity; skills like imagination, problem-finding and problem- solving, teamwork, optimism, patience and the ability to experiment and take risks. These are skills acquired when kids tinker(鼓捣小玩意). High-tech industries such as NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory have found that their best overall problem solvers were master tinkerers in their youth.

P4 There are cognitive( 认知的) benefits of doing things the way we did as children—building something, tearing it down, then building it up again. Research shows that given 15 minutes of free play, four- and five-year-olds will spend a third of this time engaged in spatial, mathematical, and architectural activities. This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry.

P5 If play and building are critical to 21st-century skill development, that's really good news for two reasons: Children are born builders, makers, and creators, so fostering(培养) 21st-century skills may be as simple as giving kids room to play, tinker and try things out, even as they grow older. Secondly, it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills. This is especially important for under- resourced schools and communities. Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important "maker" skills. And anyone, anywhere, can do it.

questions.q: What does the author say about educators?
options: They seek advice from technology companies to achieve teaching goals.
They have been successful in preparing the workforce for companies.
They help students acquire the skills needed for their future success.
They partner with technology companies to enhance teaching efficiency.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say about educators 问的是作者对教育者说了什么客观陈 述，没有 infer/imply/mainly about，是定位 + 转述型细节题。 46. What does the author say about educators? A) They seek advice from technology companies to achieve teaching goals. B) They have been successful in preparing the workforce for companies. C) They help students acquire the skills needed for their future success. D) They partner with technology companies to enhance teaching efficiency.

【拆句】What does the author say about educators 主干是 "the author say what about educators" 的疑问倒装，about 后面跟话题对象，结构简单、无陷阱。

【定位】Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future. 教师想让学生为成功的未来做好准备。

【选项】A) 无中生有 They seek advice from technology companies to achieve teaching goals 说教师向 科技公司寻求建议，原文只说双方有共同点 Educators and business leaders have more in common than it may seem，并没有任何「教师向公司讨教」的方向性陈述。 B) 与原文相反 They have been successful in preparing the workforce for companies 用现在完成 时说教师已经成功地把劳动力交付给公司，原文只说 Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future——是 want to 的愿望，不是已实现的成果。 C) ✓ 正确 Teachers want to prepare students for a successful future ↔ They help students acquire the skills needed for their future success 预判要求「准备 + 未来 + 学生」三要素齐全，They help students acquire the skills needed for their future success 把三个要素一一对应，无新增也无遗漏，是定位句的 标准同义替换。 D) 偷换概念 They partner with technology companies to enhance teaching efficiency 说教师与 公司合作以提升教学效率，原文虽然提到 technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good, old-fashioned play，但目的是把游戏带回课堂，不是 「提升教学效率」。 根据作者的观点,教育工作者如何才能更好地培养学生的STEM技能? A) 通过将它们与传统的、富有启发性的活动相结合。 B) 通过邀请企业领导者帮助设计课程。 C) 通过增强学生批判性思考的能力。 D) 通过向学生展示最好的学习方式是通过玩耍。

questions.q: How can educators better develop students' STEM skills, according to the author?
options: By blending them with traditional, stimulating activities.
By inviting business leaders to help design curriculums.
By enhancing students' ability to think in a critical way.
By showing students the best way to learn is through play.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 How can educators better develop students' STEM skills 问的是具体方法，需要回 原文找一句明确的「办法」陈述，属于方法型细节题。 47. How can educators better develop students' STEM skills, according to the author? A) By blending them with traditional, stimulating activities. B) By inviting business leaders to help design curriculums. C) By enhancing students' ability to think in a critical way. D) By showing students the best way to learn is through play.

【拆句】How can educators better develop students' STEM skills, according to the author： 主干 educators develop STEM skills，better 是副词修饰 develop，according to the author 是插入语，整句问的是方法，结构简单。

【定位】Focusing on STEM skills is important, but the reality is that STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities. 关注 STEM 技能很重要，但事实是，只有当 STEM 技能与传统的、动手的创造性活动相结 合时，这些技能才能得到强化，也才更具相关性。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 STEM skills are enhanced and more relevant when combined with traditional, hands-on creative activities ↔By blending them with traditional, stimulating activities 预判的三要素「结合 + 传统 + 动手/创意」，By blending them with traditional, stimulating activities 命中「结合」「传统」两项硬词，「动手创意」被合理上位化为 stimulating，整体语义等值。 B) 无中生有 By inviting business leaders to help design curriculums 说请商业领袖来帮忙设计课 程，原文只说商业领袖与教师有共同利益、且科技公司与教师合作把游戏带回来 technology companies are partnering with educators to bring back good, old- fashioned play，没有任何「商业领袖设计课程」的说法。 C) 偷换概念 By enhancing students' ability to think in a critical way 把方法说成「增强批判性思 维」，但原文里 the most important 21st-century skills aren't related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity 列出的是 creativity、 imagination、problem-solving，并没有 critical thinking 这一项。 D) 过度推断 By showing students the best way to learn is through play 说告诉学生学习的最佳 方式是玩，原文虽然反复肯定 play 的价值 Play may be the answer，但用 may 表推 测，且没有把 play 表述为 the best way to learn，属于对原文力度的放大。 儿童如何获得21世纪所需的技能? A) 通过参与涉及特定技术的活动。 B) 通过摆弄物品来自行解决问题。 C) 通过熟悉高科技设备。 D) 通过团队合作掌握基本原理。

questions.q: How do children acquire the skills needed for the 21st century?
options: By engaging in activities involving specific technologies.
By playing with things to solve problems on their own.
By familiarizing themselves with high-tech gadgets.
By mastering basic principles through teamwork.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 How do children acquire the skills needed for the 21st century 是 How + 一般疑 问，问获得方式，定位 → 同义替换即可，不需要主旨级归纳。

【拆句】How do children acquire the skills needed for the 21st century：主干 children acquire the skills，needed for the 21st century 是过去分词后置定语修饰 skills，等价于 the skills which are needed for the 21st century。

【定位】These are skills acquired when kids tinker. 这些（21 世纪所需的）能力，正是孩子们在鼓捣小玩意时获得的。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 By engaging in activities involving specific technologies 说通过涉及具体技术的活 动来获得能力，但 the most important 21st-century skills aren't related to specific technologies or subject matter, but to creativity 明确说不是关联于 specific technologies，选项与原文方向相反。 B) ✓ 正确 These are skills acquired when kids tinker ↔ By playing with things to solve problems on their own 预判核心「自己动手 + 鼓捣 / 玩耍」在 By playing with things to solve problems on their own 中以 playing with things + on their own 完整复现，并把要获得的能力具 体化为 solve problems，与同段的 problem-solving 完全一致。 C) 与原文相反 By familiarizing themselves with high-tech gadgets 说让孩子熟悉高科技装置，但 it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills 明确说培养这些 技能并不需要 21 世纪的高科技。 D) 张冠李戴 By mastering basic principles through teamwork 把方式说成「通过团队合作掌握基 本原理」，原文同段列出的能力清单 skills like imagination, problem-finding and problem-solving, teamwork, optimism, patience and the ability to experiment and take risks 里虽然出现 teamwork，但 teamwork 是要获得的能力之一，不是获得 能力的途径，且 basic principles 出现在第四段说的是数学几何，与 21 世纪技能不是同 一回事。 我们可以做些什么来帮助儿童学习数学和几何的基础知识? A) 尽早激发他们的兴趣。 B) 花更多时间与他们一起玩游戏。 C) 鼓励他们动手制作东西。 D) 允许他们自由摆弄计算器。 49. What can we do to help children learn the basics of math and geometry? A) Stimulate their interest as early as possible. B) Spend more time playing games with them. C) Encourage them to make things with hands. D) Allow them to tinker freely with calculators.

questions.q: What can we do to help children learn the basics of math and geometry?
options: Stimulate their interest as early as possible.
Spend more time playing games with them.
Encourage them to make things with hands.
Allow them to tinker freely with calculators.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What can we do to help children learn the basics of math and geometry 问的是 建议性做法，回原文找一句明确的做法陈述即可，属于方法型细节题。

【拆句】What can we do to help children learn the basics of math and geometry：主干 we do what，to help 是目的状语，help children learn 是 help sb. do 结构，learn the basics of math and geometry 是 help 的宾补，无难点。

【定位】This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry. 这种游戏——尤其是搭积木——能帮助孩子发现并掌握数学和几何中的关键原理。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Stimulate their interest as early as possible 说要尽早激发兴趣，原文虽提到 four- and five-year-olds Research shows that given 15 minutes of free play, four- and five-year-olds will spend a third of this time engaged in spatial, mathematical, and architectural activities，但并没有提出「激发兴趣」这一做法，更没有「越早越 好」的表态。 B) 偷换概念 Spend more time playing games with them 说大人花更多时间陪孩子玩游戏，原文 的关键是「孩子自己搭建」 This type of play—especially with building blocks— helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry，并未 要求大人陪玩，更没说 more time 这一程度。 C) ✓ 正确 This type of play—especially with building blocks—helps children discover and develop key principles in math and geometry ↔Encourage them to make things with hands 预判核心「动手 + 搭建/制作」，Encourage them to make things with hands 同时 命中 make（建造/制作）与 with hands（动手），无新增信息，是 building blocks 的 合理上位概括。 D) 与原文相反 Allow them to tinker freely with calculators 把鼓捣的对象换成计算器，原文却强调 building blocks 这类纯动手物件；且 it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills 已经否定了高科技工具的必要性，calculators 属于反向。 作者建议条件不利的学校和社区做什么? A) 培训学生成为创造者以满足未来市场需求。 B) 利用现有资源培养学生的创造性技能。 C) 让学生参与具有挑战性的任务以培养他们的创造力。 D) 与企业合作改善他们的教学设施。

questions.q: What does the author advise disadvantaged schools and communities to do?
options: Train students to be makers to meet future market demands.
Develop students' creative skills with the resources available.
Engage students with challenging tasks to foster their creativity.
Work together with companies to improve their teaching facilities.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author advise disadvantaged schools and communities to do 是 定向问作者建议，需要找一句明确针对弱势学校的建议句，是定位型细节题，不需要全篇 归纳。

【拆句】What does the author advise disadvantaged schools and communities to do：主干 the author advise sb. to do sth.，advise sb. to do 是固定搭配，disadvantaged ... communities 整体作 advise 的宾语，结构清晰。

【定位】This is especially important for under-resourced schools and communities. Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important "maker" skills. 这一点对于资源匮乏的学校和社区尤为重要。拿手边任何能找到的材料动手鼓捣，就是激发 这些重要「制造者」能力的一种简单办法。 50. What does the author advise disadvantaged schools and communities to do? A) Train students to be makers to meet future market demands. B) Develop students' creative skills with the resources available. C) Engage students with challenging tasks to foster their creativity. D) Work together with companies to improve their teaching facilities.

【选项】A) 无中生有 Train students to be makers to meet future market demands 把目的设为「满足未 来市场需求」，原文里反复说的是培养 maker / creator 等能力 Children are born builders, makers, and creators，从未出现 market demands 这类商业目的。 B) ✓ 正确 Taking whatever materials are handy and tinkering with them is a simple way to engage those important "maker" skills ↔Develop students' creative skills with the resources available it doesn't take 21st-century technology to foster 21st-century skills ↔ Develop students' creative skills with the resources available 预判的「现有/手边资源 + 创造性能力」，Develop students' creative skills with the resources available 同时命中 with the resources available（现有资源）与 creative skills（创造性能力），两项语义点齐全且力度匹配。 C) 与原文相反 Engage students with challenging tasks to foster their creativity 说让学生做有挑 战性的任务，原文却强调 fostering 21st-century skills may be as simple as giving kids room to play, tinker and try things out，用的是 as simple as，方向是「越简单 越好」。 D) 张冠李戴 Work together with companies to improve their teaching facilities 说与公司合作改 善教学设施，原文虽然在首段提到 Educators and business leaders have more in common than it may seem，但末段给资源匮乏地区的建议只是用手边材料鼓捣，从 未提到「与公司合作改善设施」。

items.title: 2021年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2021年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Being an information technology, or IT, worker is not a job I envy. They are the ones who, right in the middle of a critical meeting, are expected to instantly fix the projector that's no longer working. They have to tolerate the bad tempers of colleagues frustrated at the number of times they've had to call the help desk for the same issue. They are also the ones who know there are systems that are more powerful, reliable and faster, but their employer simply will not put up the funds to buy them.

P2 According to a recent survey, employees who have a job reliant on IT support consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction. Through no fault of their own, they can suddenly find their productivity deteriorating or quality control non-existent. And there's little they can do about it.

P3 The experience of using IT penetrates almost the entire work field. It has become a crucial part of employees' overall work experience. When IT is operating as it should, employee self-confidence swells. Their job satisfaction, too, can surge when well-functioning machines relieve them of dull tasks or repetitive processes. But if there's one thing that triggers widespread employee frustration, it's an IT transformation project gone wrong, where swollen expectations have been popped and a long list of promised efficiencies has been reversed. This occurs when business leaders implement IT initiatives with little consideration of how those changes will impact the end user.

P4 Which is why managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees, and exert substantial effort in ensuring their IT team eliminates programming errors and application crashes. Adequate and timely IT support should also be available to enable users to cope with technological issues at work. More importantly, IT practitioners need to understand what employees experience mentally when they use IT.

P5 Therefore, businesses need to set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees' work, rather than adjust their work to fit in with the company's IT limitations.

questions.q: What does the author say about working in IT?
options: It is envied by many.
It does not appeal to him.
It is financially rewarding.
It does not match his abilities.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about working in IT? 用 what 引导，问作者对某一具体对象 的明确表态，属于带主观色彩的细节题，而不是 infer/imply。

【拆句】题干是简单疑问句，主干为 What does the author say about working in IT?，about 引 出话题，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Being an information technology, or IT, worker is not a job I envy. 成为一名信息技术（即 IT）工作者，不是一份我会羡慕的工作。 51. What does the author say about working in IT? A) It is envied by many. B) It does not appeal to him. C) It is financially rewarding. D) It does not match his abilities.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 It is envied by many. 把作者 not a job I envy 的态度改成"很多人羡慕"，方向完全相 反，且原文也没说"很多人羡慕"。 B) ✓ 正确 not a job I envy ↔does not appeal to him 预判"作者不羡慕 IT 工作"与 It does not appeal to him. 同义；其余选项与作者表态相 反或与文意无关。 C) 无中生有 It is financially rewarding. 称 IT 工作"经济回报丰厚"，但全文从未谈及薪资或金钱收 益，纯属编造。 D) 偷换概念 It does not match his abilities. 说 IT 工作"与他的能力不匹配"，原文只说作者不羡 慕、并描述 IT 工作辛苦，从未涉及作者本人的能力是否够格。 最近一项针对工作依赖IT支持的员工的调查有何发现? A) IT有助于提高生产力。 B) IT有助于改善质量控制。 C) 许多员工对IT深感沮丧。 D) 大多数员工在工作中严重依赖IT。

questions.q: What is the finding of a recent survey on employees who have a job reliant on IT support?
options: IT helps boost productivity.
IT helps improve quality control.
Many employees are deeply frustrated by IT.
Most employees rely heavily on IT in their work.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the finding of a recent survey 直接问一项调查的发现，是对原文具体信息的复 述，属于细节题。

【拆句】主干 What is the finding of a recent survey on employees，on 引出调查对象、who 从 句进一步限定。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】According to a recent survey, employees who have a job reliant on IT support consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction. 根据一项最新调查，工作依赖 IT 支持的员工把 IT 视为工作不满的主要来源。 52. What is the finding of a recent survey on employees who have a job reliant on IT support? A) IT helps boost productivity. B) IT helps improve quality control. C) Many employees are deeply frustrated by IT. D) Most employees rely heavily on IT in their work.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 IT helps boost productivity. 说 IT 提升生产力，与原文 their productivity deteriorating（生产力下降）完全相反。 B) 与原文相反 IT helps improve quality control. 说 IT 改善质量控制，但原文是 quality control non-existent，质控"不复存在"，方向反转。 C) ✓ 正确 consider IT a major source of job dissatisfaction ↔ Many employees are deeply frustrated by IT 预判"员工对 IT 极度不满"与 Many employees are deeply frustrated by IT. 完全吻 合；其他三项要么把 IT 说成正面作用，要么扯到使用频率，均偏离结论。 D) 答非所问 Most employees rely heavily on IT in their work. 说"大多数员工严重依赖 IT"，但题 干问的是调查的 finding，而原文 finding 是"员工不满"，不是"员工依赖"；"依赖"只是 调查对象的限定条件，不是调查结论。 据说当IT正常运行时会发生什么? A) 员工的工作效率会大幅提升。 B) 员工变得更加依赖机器。 C) 不再有任何枯燥或重复性的任务。 D) 员工对自己的工作变得更有信心。

questions.q: What is said to happen when IT is functioning properly?
options: There is a big boost in employees' work efficiency.
Employees become more dependent on machines.
There are no longer any boring or repetitive tasks.
Employees become more confident in their work.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is said to happen when IT is functioning properly? 问在某条件下会发生什么具体 结果，是原文已有陈述的复述题，属细节题。

【拆句】题干主干 What is said to happen，when 从句修饰 happen，is said 是被动语态，弱化 作者主观色彩，照常按客观细节处理。

【定位】When IT is operating as it should, employee self-confidence swells. 当 IT 像它本应那样运转时，员工的自信心便会膨胀。 53. What is said to happen when IT is functioning properly? A) There is a big boost in employees' work efficiency. B) Employees become more dependent on machines. C) There are no longer any boring or repetitive tasks. D) Employees become more confident in their work.

【选项】A) 过度推断 There is a big boost in employees' work efficiency. 把答案换成"工作效率大幅提 升"，原文只说自信和工作满意度上升，并未在 IT 正常运转时给出"效率大幅提升"的结 论；"a big boost"也属于原文未表达的程度夸大。 B) 偷换概念 Employees become more dependent on machines. 说员工"更依赖机器"，原文谈的 是 IT 正常时员工"自信增强"，未涉及依赖加深；"依赖加深"通常是负面评价，与本段 IT 正常时的正向描述也不符。 C) 过度推断 原文 well-functioning machines relieve them of dull tasks or repetitive processes 说机器"减轻"枯燥重复任务，There are no longer any boring or repetitive tasks. 却 说"不再有任何"重复任务，把"缓解"夸大为"彻底消除"。 D) ✓ 正确 employee self-confidence swells ↔Employees become more confident in their work 预判"员工自信增强"与 Employees become more confident in their work. 几乎逐字 同义；其余选项不是过度推断就是与原文相反。 企业领导者在实施新的IT举措之前应该做什么? A) 考虑客户的各种期望。 B) 列出承诺要实现的各项效率提升。 C) 评估培训员工的高昂成本。 D) 考虑对员工可能产生的影响。

questions.q: What should business leaders do before implementing new IT initiatives?
options: Consider the various expectations of their customers.
Draw up a list of the efficiencies to be promised.
Assess the swollen cost of training the employees.
Think about the possible effects on their employees.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should business leaders do before implementing new IT initiatives? 问"应当做 什么"，对应原文里直接给出建议/批评的句子，是细节题。

【拆句】主干 What should business leaders do，before 引导时间状语 before implementing new IT initiatives，implementing 是动名词作介词宾语。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Which is why managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees, and exert substantial effort in ensuring their IT team eliminates programming errors and application crashes. 正因如此，管理者应当意识到 IT 用户体验对员工有多大影响，并下大力气确保 IT 团队消除 程序错误与应用崩溃。 54. What should business leaders do before implementing new IT initiatives? A) Consider the various expectations of their customers. B) Draw up a list of the efficiencies to be promised. C) Assess the swollen cost of training the employees. D) Think about the possible effects on their employees.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Consider the various expectations of their customers. 把考虑对象从员工换成"客 户"，但全文从未谈及 customers，关注点始终是 employees/end user。 B) 与原文相反 Draw up a list of the efficiencies to be promised. 把"承诺的效率"列成清单，原文恰 恰批评 a long list of promised efficiencies has been reversed，即"承诺过的效率被 打回原形"，是失败之处而非应做之事。 C) 无中生有 Assess the swollen cost of training the employees. 借用 swollen expectations have been popped 中的 swollen 拼出"激增的培训成本"，但原文 swollen 形容的是 expectations（被吹胀的预期），从未提培训成本。 D) ✓ 正确 with little consideration of how those changes will impact the end user ↔ Think about the possible effects on their employees managers should appreciate just how influential the IT user experience is to their employees ↔ Think about the possible effects on their employees 预判"先考虑对员工的影响"和 Think about the possible effects on their employees. 高度吻合；A/B/C 要么换错对象，要么偏离核心动作。 企业如何帮助改善员工使用IT的体验? A) 通过设计适合他们需求的系统。 B) 通过确保他们的心理健康状况良好。 C) 通过调整他们的工作以适应IT系统。 D) 通过为他们提供定期的在职培训。

questions.q: How can a business help improve its employees' experience in using IT?
options: By designing systems that suit their needs.
By ensuring that their mental health is sound.
By adjusting their work to suit the IT system.
By offering them regular in-service training.
questions.explain:
【判型】How can a business help improve its employees' experience in using IT? 问公司具体 如何改善，对应原文给出的具体做法句，属细节题。

【拆句】主干 How can a business help improve its employees' experience，in using IT 是后置 介词短语修饰 experience。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Therefore, businesses need to set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees' work, rather than adjust their work to fit in with the company's IT limitations. 因此，企业需要这样搭建其 IT 基础设施：使其设计去适配员工的工作，而不是让员工调整 工作去迁就公司的 IT 局限。 55. How can a business help improve its employees' experience in using IT? A) By designing systems that suit their needs. B) By ensuring that their mental health is sound. C) By adjusting their work to suit the IT system. D) By offering them regular in-service training.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 set up their IT infrastructure so that it is designed to fit in with their employees' work ↔ By designing systems that suit their needs 预判"IT 去适配员工"严丝合缝对应 By designing systems that suit their needs.； B/C/D 要么扯心理健康、要么取了 rather than 后的反向做法、要么属于无中生有的 培训。 B) 偷换概念 By ensuring that their mental health is sound. 借用 what employees experience mentally when they use IT 里的 mentally 拼出"确保心理健康"，但原文是"理解员工使 用 IT 时的心理体验"，不是"维护员工心理健康"，且这一点也不是末段给出的总对策。 C) 与原文相反 By adjusting their work to suit the IT system. 把 rather than 后的反面做法 adjust their work to fit in with the company's IT limitations 当成对策，方向完全反转。 D) 无中生有 By offering them regular in-service training. 提到"定期在职培训"，全文从未谈及培 训这件事，纯属新概念。

items.title: 2021年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2021年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Sugar shocked. That describes the reaction of many Americans this week following revelations that, 50 years ago, the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists for research that shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat.

P2 What might surprise consumers is just how many present-day nutrition studies are still funded by the food industry. Nutrition scholar Marion Nestle of New York University spent a year informally tracking industry-funded studies on food. "Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest," Nestle tells us. Other systematic reviews support her conclusions.

P3 For instance, studies funded by Welch Foods—the brand behind Welch's 100% Grape Juice— found that drinking Concord grape juice daily may boost brain function. Another, funded by Quaker Oats, concluded, as a Daily Mail story put it, that "hot oatmeal(燕麦粥) breakfast keeps you full for longer."

P4 Last year, The New York Times revealed how Coca-Cola was funding well-known scientists and organizations promoting a message that, in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink. Coca-Cola also released data detailing its funding of several medical institutions and associations between 2010 and 2015.

P5 "It's certainly a problem that so much research in nutrition and health is funded by industry," says Bonnie Liebman, director of nutrition at the Center for Science in the Public Interest. "When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for." And what it pays for is often a pro- industry finding.

P6 Given this environment, consumers should be skeptical(怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science and ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed. "Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence," Liebman says, pointing to the official government Dietary Guidelines, which are based on reviews of hundreds of studies.

P7 "And that expert advice remains pretty simple," says Nestle. "We know what healthy diets are— lots of vegetables, not too much junk food, balanced calories. Everything else is really difficult to do experimentally."

questions.q: What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago?
options: They raised public awareness of the possible causes of heart disease.
They turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat.
They placed the sugar industry in the spotlight with their new findings.
They conducted large-scale research on the role of sugar in people's health.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago? 问的是过去某个具体行为，答案应是定位 段对该行为的客观陈述。

【拆句】What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago? 是 what 引导的一般疑问句，主语 Harvard scientists，时间状语 50 years ago，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Sugar shocked. That describes the reaction of many Americans this week following revelations that, 50 years ago, the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists for research that shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat. 糖业震惊。这描述了本周许多美国人在得知一桩内幕后的反应——50 年前，糖业出钱请哈 佛科学家做研究，把心脏病的责任焦点从糖身上挪开，狠狠地压在了膳食脂肪头上。 46. What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago? A) They raised public awareness of the possible causes of heart disease. B) They turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat. C) They placed the sugar industry in the spotlight with their new findings. D) They conducted large-scale research on the role of sugar in people's health.

【选项】A) 无中生有 raised public awareness of the possible causes of heart disease 说哈佛科学家"提高 了公众对心脏病病因的认知"，但原文只说他们"转移焦点"，从未提及"提高认知"，且行 为方向相反——是误导而非启蒙。 B) ✓ 正确 shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat ↔turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat 预判内容"把心脏病矛头从糖转向脂肪"与 turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat 在框架、对象、方向上完全重合，即同义替换型正确项。 C) 与原文相反 placed the sugar industry in the spotlight with their new findings 说研究让"糖 业"成为焦点，与原文 put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat 恰恰相 反——焦点是脂肪而非糖业。 D) 无中生有 conducted large-scale research on the role of sugar in people's health 强调"大规 模"研究，但原文未提及研究规模，只说糖业出钱资助；且研究内容不是"糖与健康的作 用"而是"转移焦点"。 Marion Nestle对当今营养学研究有何看法? A) 这些研究花了她整整一年时间来追踪和分析。 B) 它们大多基于系统性综述。 C) 它们依赖于食品行业的资助。 D) 几乎所有研究都服务于资助方的目的。

questions.q: What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies?
options: They took her a full year to track and analyze.
Most of them are based on systematic reviews.
They depend on funding from the food industries.
Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies? 直接索取一个人对 一事的具体说法，答案应是文中该人原话的转述。

【拆句】What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies? 主干 What...does Marion Nestle say，about 引出宾语补足语限定 say 的内容范围；句法直白。

【定位】"Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest," Nestle tells us. Nestle 告诉我们："在近 170 项研究里，约 90% 的结果都偏向了资助方的利益。" 47. What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies? A) They took her a full year to track and analyze. B) Most of them are based on systematic reviews. C) They depend on funding from the food industries. D) Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders.

【选项】A) 答非所问 They took her a full year to track and analyze 说"研究花了她一整年追踪"，对应原文 spent a year informally tracking，但这是关于 Nestle 的研究方法，不是她 对"present-day nutrition studies"本身的看法，答非所问。 B) 张冠李戴 Most of them are based on systematic reviews 把"systematic reviews"安 到"present-day nutrition studies"头上，但原文 Other systematic reviews support her conclusions 是说"其他系统性综述支持 Nestle 的结论"，systematic reviews 是支 持她的工具，不是被她评论的研究的本质。 C) 偷换概念 They depend on funding from the food industries 说"研究依赖食品业资助"，是"资 金来源"层面的事实，而原文 Nestle 强调的是"研究结论偏向资助方"——把"结论偏 袒"偷换成了"资金依赖"。两者层面不同。 D) ✓ 正确 Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest ↔ Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders 预判"九成研究服务资助方利益"与 Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders 在数量级、动作、对象三层全部对齐，是教科书级同义替换正确项。 可口可乐资助的研究声称什么? A) 运动对健康的重要性超过饮食。 B) 选择吃什么和喝什么是控制体重的关键。 C) 饮用可口可乐不会导致体重增加。 D) 食品行业在对抗肥胖方面发挥着重要作用。

questions.q: What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim?
options: Exercise is more important to good health than diet.
Choosing what to eat and drink is key to weight control.
Drinking Coca-Cola does not contribute to weight gain.
The food industry plays a major role in fighting obesity.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim? 问被可口可乐资助的研究主张了什么，答案 是文中明示的论断。

【拆句】What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim? 主语 Coca-Cola-funded studies 是"名词- funded 复合形容词+名词"结构，意为"被可口可乐资助的研究"；句意直白。

【定位】Last year, The New York Times revealed how Coca-Cola was funding well-known scientists and organizations promoting a message that, in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink. 去年《纽约时报》披露，可口可乐资助知名科学家和组织，宣扬这样一种主张：在对抗体重 增长的战斗中，人们应更看重运动，而不是吃了什么、喝了什么。 48. What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim? A) Exercise is more important to good health than diet. B) Choosing what to eat and drink is key to weight control. C) Drinking Coca-Cola does not contribute to weight gain. D) The food industry plays a major role in fighting obesity.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink ↔Exercise is more important to good health than diet 预判"重运动而轻饮食"与 Exercise is more important to good health than diet 的"运 动比饮食更重要"严格等价；定位句的 more/less 平行结构本身就是隐性比较。 B) 与原文相反 Choosing what to eat and drink is key to weight control 说"吃喝选择是控重关键"， 与原文 less to what they eat and drink"少在乎吃喝"完全相反——可口可乐研究恰恰 要弱化饮食责任。 C) 无中生有 Drinking Coca-Cola does not contribute to weight gain 凭空捏造一句"喝可乐不会 增重"，原文从未出现此论断；可口可乐资助研究只是"转移注意力"到运动，并未直接为 可乐本身辩护。 D) 偷换概念 The food industry plays a major role in fighting obesity 说"食品业在抗肥胖中起重 要作用"，看似与原文相关，但原文是说"可口可乐资助研究让人忽视饮食"，并未把食品 业塑造为"抗肥胖功臣"；把"产业操纵议程"偷换成了"产业贡献抗肥胖"。 Liebman对行业资助的研究有何看法? A) 它只关注营养和健康。 B) 它在消费者中造成困惑。 C) 它很少产生客观的研究结果。 D) 它违背公共利益。

questions.q: What does Liebman say about industry-funded research?
options: It simply focuses on nutrition and health.
It causes confusion among consumers.
It rarely results in objective findings.
It runs counter to the public interest.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Liebman say about industry-funded research? 同 Q47 同款句式，仍是细节 题，定位到 Liebman 引语即可。

【拆句】What does Liebman say about industry-funded research? 结构同 Q47；industry- funded 是"名词-过去分词"复合形容词，表被动"被产业资助的"。

【定位】"When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for." And what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding. "当食品业出钱做研究时，它常常能买到自己想要的结论。"而它想买的，往往是一个对产业 有利的结果。 49. What does Liebman say about industry-funded research? A) It simply focuses on nutrition and health. B) It causes confusion among consumers. C) It rarely results in objective findings. D) It runs counter to the public interest.

【选项】A) 答非所问 It simply focuses on nutrition and health 只说研究"聚焦营养健康"，是话题描述，未 触及 Liebman 对"业内资助偏袒"的核心评价；属答非所问。 B) 无中生有 It causes confusion among consumers 说"造成消费者困惑"，原文 P5 Liebman 谈的 是"研究结论偏袒产业"，未提及消费者困惑这一后果——"困惑"是后文（P6）作者建议 引出的语境，但不是 Liebman 的直接评价。 C) ✓ 正确 what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding ↔It rarely results in objective findings When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for ↔ It rarely results in objective findings 预判"买到的多是偏袒产业的结论"与 It rarely results in objective findings 是同一事实 的正反描述：常偏袒=极少客观。 D) 过度推断 It runs counter to the public interest 跨越"研究偏袒产业"直接推到"与公众利益对 立"——这是合理但过度的引申。原文只说结论亲产业，没有明示"对立于公众利益"， 且 Liebman 所在机构名 Center for Science in the Public Interest 是机构名而非她的 论断。 作者对消费者的建议是什么? A) 在决定吃什么时遵循自己的直觉。 B) 对饮食专家的建议持怀疑态度。 C) 忽略新闻推送中的无关信息。 D) 对新的营养学研究发现要三思而后行。

questions.q: What is the author's advice to consumers?
options: Follow their intuition in deciding what to eat.
Be doubtful of diet experts' recommendations.
Ignore irrelevant information on their news feed.
Think twice about new nutrition research findings.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the author's advice to consumers? 问的是一项具体行动建议，答案是文末作者 明示的劝告，仍属细节题（非笼统主旨）。

【拆句】What is the author's advice to consumers? What is 主系表结构，主语 the author's advice，介词短语 to consumers 修饰 advice 表对象；无难点。

【定位】Given this environment, consumers should be skeptical(怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science and ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed. 鉴于这种环境，消费者读到营养科学的最新发现时应当保持怀疑，并对新闻推送里冒出来的 最新研究置之不理。 50. What is the author's advice to consumers? A) Follow their intuition in deciding what to eat. B) Be doubtful of diet experts' recommendations. C) Ignore irrelevant information on their news feed. D) Think twice about new nutrition research findings.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Follow their intuition in deciding what to eat 让消费者"凭直觉决定吃什么"，与原文 末段 Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence（依赖审过全部证据 的健康专家）方向相反——作者要的是依赖权威而非凭直觉。 B) 与原文相反 Be doubtful of diet experts' recommendations 让消费者"怀疑膳食专家的建议"，但 原文恰恰相反 Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence——要怀疑 的是"业内出资的最新研究"，不是"健康专家"。 C) 偷换概念 Ignore irrelevant information on their news feed 让消费者"忽略新闻推送里的无关信 息"，但原文 ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed 让消费者忽略 的是"新闻推送里冒出的最新研究"——把"最新研究"偷换成"无关信息"，对象被偷偷扩大 并改性质。 D) ✓ 正确 consumers should be skeptical(怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science ↔ Think twice about new nutrition research findings 预判"对新研究保持怀疑"与 Think twice about new nutrition research findings 在态 度（怀疑↔三思）与对象（最新营养发现↔新营养研究结论）两层都对齐。

items.title: 2021年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2021年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder. The goal was to reach the top, accumulate wealth and retire to a life of ease. My father is a successful senior executive. In 35 years, he worked for only three companies.

P2 When I started my career, things were already different. If you weren't changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren't getting ahead in your career. But back then, if you were a consultant or freelancer(自由职业者), people would wonder what was wrong with you. They would assume you had problems getting a job.

P3 Today, consulting or freelancing for five businesses at the same time is a badge of honor. It shows how valuable an individual is. Many companies now look to these "ultimate professionals" to solve problems their full-time teams can't. Or they save money by hiring "top-tier(顶尖的) experts" only for particular projects.

P4 Working at home or in cafes, starting businesses of their own, and even launching business ventures that eventually may fail, all indicate "initiative," "creativity," and "adaptability," which are desirable qualities in today's workplace. Most important, there is a growing recognition that people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients.

P5 Who are these people? They are artists, writers, programmers, providers of office services and career advice. What's needed now is a marketplace platform specifically designed to bring freelancers and clients together. Such platforms then become a place to feature the most experienced, professional, and creative talent. This is where they conduct business, where a sense of community reinforces the culture and values of the gig economy( 零工经济), and where success is rewarded with good reviews that encourage more business.

P6 Slowly but surely, these platforms create a bridge between traditional enterprises and this emerging economy. Perhaps more important, as the global economy continues to be disrupted by technology and other massive change, the gig economy will itself become an engine of economic and social transformation.

questions.q: What does the author use the example of his father to illustrate?
options: How long people took to reach the top of their career.
How people accumulated wealth in his father's time.
How people viewed success in his father's time.
How long people usually stayed in a company.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What does the author use the example of his father to illustrate?里use the example...to illustrate是例证目的题的标志句式。 51. What does the author use the example of his father to illustrate? A) How long people took to reach the top of their career. B) How people accumulated wealth in his father's time. C) How people viewed success in his father's time. D) How long people usually stayed in a company.

【拆句】What does the author use the example of his father to illustrate?主干是What does the author use...to illustrate，宾语the example of his father插在use和to illustrate之 间，可还原为The author uses the example of his father to illustrate what？句子结构清 晰，无陷阱。

【定位】Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder. The goal was to reach the top, accumulate wealth and retire to a life of ease. My father is a successful senior executive. In 35 years, he worked for only three companies. 成功曾经被定义为能在一家公司长期任职、并沿企业晋升阶梯向上攀升。其目标是登上顶 峰、积累财富、退休享福。我父亲是一位成功的高级主管。35年里他只为三家公司工作过。

【选项】A) 把例子局部细节当成例证目的=以偏概全 A项How long people took to reach the top of their career.只截取了例子里"长期任 职"这层片面信息，且"花多久到顶"是文中未直接给出的时间细节。 B) 拎走并列项里的一个=以偏概全 B项How people accumulated wealth in his father's time.把原文里accumulate wealth截出来做主旨，但accumulate wealth只是论点中目标的一个并列项，并非例子 要说明的核心。 C) ✓ 正确 Success was once defined as being able to stay at a company for a long time and move up the corporate ladder. ↔How people viewed success in his father's time. C项把"父辈时代人们如何看待成功"完整对应原文论点句的语义，例子（35年三家公司） 正是这个看法的证据。 D) 把例子字面=目的，是答非所问 D项How long people usually stayed in a company.几乎是父亲例子（he worked for only three companies 35年）的复述，问的是"例子表面讲了啥"，而题问的是"例子用 来证明啥"。 当作者开始他的职业生涯时,为什么人们经常换工作? A) 这在当时被认为是一种时尚。 B) 这是一种在职业生涯中晋升的方式。 C) 这是对不断变化的就业市场的回应。 D) 长期保住一份工作很困难。

questions.q: Why did people often change jobs when the author started his career?
options: It was considered a fashion at that time.
It was a way to advance in their career.
It was a response to the changing job market.
It was difficult to keep a job for long.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did people often change jobs when the author started his career?问的是当时换 工作背后的具体原因，答案能在原文里找到对应表述。 52. Why did people often change jobs when the author started his career? A) It was considered a fashion at that time. B) It was a way to advance in their career. C) It was a response to the changing job market. D) It was difficult to keep a job for long.

【拆句】Why did people often change jobs when the author started his career?主干Why did people change jobs，后接when引导的时间状语从句，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】If you weren't changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren't getting ahead in your career. 如果你没在每三四年换一次公司，那你的职业基本就没在前进。

【选项】A) 无中生有 A项It was considered a fashion at that time.里的fashion（流行风尚）在原文中无任 何对应表述，作者强调的是"不换就升不上去"的功利动因，而非流行潮流。 B) ✓ 正确 If you weren't changing companies every three or four years, you simply weren't getting ahead in your career. ↔It was a way to advance in their career. 从预判"换工作是为了职业前进"出发，B项直接以a way to advance in their career对 位，完全覆盖定位句的正面含义。 C) 偷换概念 C项It was a response to the changing job market.把换工作说成是对"职场变化"的被 动响应，原文给出的是主动追求职业前进的内在动因，逻辑方向相反。 D) 与原文相反 D项It was difficult to keep a job for long.说当时"很难长期保住一份工作"，原文说的 是"如果想前进就得自己换"，并非工作保不住；D项把主动换岗读成被动失业。 关于现在同时为几家企业工作的人,作者说了什么? A) 他们常被视为最宝贵的人才。 B) 他们能够更充分地发挥自己的潜力。 C) 他们能够掌控自己的生活和工作日程。 D) 他们为自己是杰出的问题解决者而感到自豪。

questions.q: What does the author say about people now working for several businesses at the same time?
options: They are often regarded as most treasured talents.
They are able to bring their potential into fuller play.
They have control over their life and work schedules.
They feel proud of being outstanding problem solvers.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about people now working for several businesses at the same time?问的是作者对该群体的具体评价，原文应有直接陈述。

【拆句】What does the author say about people now working for several businesses at the same time?主干What does the author say about people，working for several businesses at the same time是people的现在分词后置定语；now是时间副词，把范围限 定在当下。 53. What does the author say about people now working for several businesses at the same time? A) They are often regarded as most treasured talents. B) They are able to bring their potential into fuller play. C) They have control over their life and work schedules. D) They feel proud of being outstanding problem solvers.

【定位】Today, consulting or freelancing for five businesses at the same time is a badge of honor. It shows how valuable an individual is. 如今，同时为五家公司做咨询或自由职业是一种荣誉徽章，它显示一个人有多么有价值。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 It shows how valuable an individual is. ↔ They are often regarded as most treasured talents. a badge of honor ↔are often regarded as 从预判出发，A项把badge of honor+how valuable汇总成most treasured talents， 最贴合作者对这群人的评价。 B) 张冠李戴（错段拼接） B项They are able to bring their potential into fuller play.说他们"能把潜力发 挥得更充分"，原文未在53题的定位段说这件事，潜力发挥要到P4再讨论focused and productive。 C) 过度推断 C项They have control over their life and work schedules.说他们"掌控自己的生活和 工作日程"，原文虽提到为多家公司打工，但没说他们对日程有控制权——这层引申是读 者的主观联想。 D) 偷换概念（叙述视角+部分原因） D项They feel proud of being outstanding problem solvers.说他们"为自己作为解决 问题者而自豪"，原文里badge of honor是社会对他们的视角，不是他们自己feel proud；problem solvers也只是企业聘他们的部分原因。 企业现在认识到了什么? A) 谁能够轻松地解决问题。 B) 人们如何能更加专注和高效。 C) 什么样的人能为它们做出更多贡献。 D) 为什么有些人对工作更有热情。

questions.q: What have businesses come to recognize now?
options: Who is capable of solving problems with ease.
How people can be more focused and productive.
What kind of people can contribute more to them.
Why some people are more passionate about work.
questions.explain:
【判型】What have businesses come to recognize now?问当下企业认识到了什么，是问事实细 节，不是推断。

【拆句】What have businesses come to recognize now?现在完成时have come to recognize表 示从过去到现在累积形成的认识，now强调当下状态，结构无陷阱。 54. What have businesses come to recognize now? A) Who is capable of solving problems with ease. B) How people can be more focused and productive. C) What kind of people can contribute more to them. D) Why some people are more passionate about work.

【定位】Most important, there is a growing recognition that people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients. 最重要的是，人们越来越认识到：那些工作与休息平衡、并从事自己所热爱之事的人，更专 注、更高产，能给客户带来更大的价值。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴+偷换程度 A项Who is capable of solving problems with ease.里solving problems with ease （轻松解决问题）来自solve problems their full-time teams can't，但P3说的是"解决 全职团队搞不定的问题"，并非"轻松"，且和"现在认识到的"语境不符。 B) 答非所问（偷换疑问词） B项How people can be more focused and productive.问的是"如何变得更专注高 产"，而原文给的是"哪类人更专注高产"，疑问词错位，且companies的认知对象是人， 不是方法。 C) ✓ 正确 people who balance work and play, and who work at what they are passionate about, are more focused and productive, delivering greater value to their clients ↔What kind of people can contribute more to them. 原文that从句的真正主语是people who...，整句重心是这类人能为客户贡献更多价值； C项的"What kind of people can contribute more to them"精准对位该重心。 D) 答非所问+偷换重心 D项Why some people are more passionate about work.问"为什么有些人对工作更 热情"，但原文里passionate只是描述这类人的特征之一，并未解释"原因"，且重心是其 价值，不是热情的成因。 关于零工经济,作者说了什么? A) 它可能迫使企业改革其商业实践。 B) 它可能很快取代传统的经济模式。 C) 它将在全球范围内推动技术进步。 D) 它将带来彻底的经济和社会变革。

questions.q: What does the author say about the gig economy?
options: It may force companies to reform their business practice.
It may soon replace the traditional economic model.
It will drive technological progress on a global scale.
It will bring about radical economic and social changes.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about the gig economy?问的是作者对零工经济的具体陈述； 答案直接在原文有对应句而非需要推断。

【拆句】What does the author say about the gig economy?结构简单：主干What does the author say，about the gig economy是介词短语修饰say，无陷阱。 55. What does the author say about the gig economy? A) It may force companies to reform their business practice. B) It may soon replace the traditional economic model. C) It will drive technological progress on a global scale. D) It will bring about radical economic and social changes.
