【选项】A) ✓ 正确 complex and dynamic ↔varied and complicated are increasingly ↔are getting more the issues facing today's world ↔It faces problems It faces problems that are getting more varied and complicated 把定位句的主语、 谓语、表语三处都做了同义替换，没增没减，符合「正确项=定位句同义替换」的范式。 B) 偷换概念 requires new approaches that extend beyond traditional ways of thinking 只是说 「需要超越传统思路」，并未说「已经摒弃了传统思路」，把 require beyond 偷换为 done away with。 C) 过度推断 原文只说 issues 变得 complex and dynamic，并没有说世界「正在经历根本性、深刻 变化」这种更强的程度判断。 D) 偷换概念 原文 may spark this type of innovation 只是说成长型思维可能「催生」创新，并未说 世界「正在见证各种创新」；选项把对未来潜能的描述偷换为对当下现象的事实陈述。 O'Keefe教授在他早期的研究中发现了什么? A) 人们的兴趣往往随年龄而变化。 B) 人们的兴趣决定了他们的思维模式。 C) 人们对兴趣的本质存在分歧。 D) 不同年龄的人有不同的思维模式。

questions.q: What did Professor O'Keefe find in his earlier studies?
options: People's interests tend to change with age.
People's interests determine their mindsets.
People are divided about the nature of interest.
People of different ages have different mindsets.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did Professor O'Keefe find in his earlier studies? 直问「发现了什么」，要的是原 文已陈述的事实，不是推断。

【拆句】What did Professor O'Keefe find in his earlier studies? 是 What 引导的疑问句，主 语 Professor O'Keefe，谓语 find，介词短语 in his earlier studies 锁定时间范围；结构 清晰。 52. What did Professor O'Keefe find in his earlier studies? A) People's interests tend to change with age. B) People's interests determine their mindsets. C) People are divided about the nature of interest. D) People of different ages have different mindsets.

【定位】Professor O'Keefe established in earlier studies that people hold different beliefs about the nature of interest. 奥基夫教授在早期研究中确立：人们对「兴趣的本质」持有不同的看法。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文谈的是不同人对兴趣本质的不同看法，没有任何句子涉及「兴趣随年龄变化」这一 时间维度。 B) 与原文相反 原文 Those with a growth mindset of interest tend to believe that interests can be developed 是先有 mindset、再决定对 interest 的看法；选项却说 interests determine mindsets，主从颠倒。 C) ✓ 正确 hold different beliefs ↔are divided about the nature of interest ↔about the nature of interest people ↔People People are divided about the nature of interest 与定位句结构几乎一一对应，只把 hold different beliefs 改写为 are divided，正是「正确项=定位句同义替换」的范式。 D) 无中生有 原文区分人群依据是「思维倾向」（growth vs fixed），与年龄毫无关系；选项凭空引 入 ages 维度。 O'Keefe教授最近研究的重点是什么? A) 如何消除文科和理科学科之间的界限。 B) 创建计算经济学等新学科的可行性有多大。 C) 文科和理科学生如何看待这两种兴趣思维模式。 D) 兴趣的成长型思维模式如何有助于跨学科思维。

questions.q: What is the focus of Professor O'Keefe's recent research?
options: How boundaries can be removed between arts and science disciplines.
How feasible it is to create new disciplines like computational economics.
How students in arts and sciences view the two types of mindset of interest.
How a growth mindset of interest can contribute to cross-disciplinary thinking.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the focus of Professor O'Keefe's recent research? 直问焦点，对应原文的目的 句，仍属定位题而非推断题。

【拆句】What is the focus of Professor O'Keefe's recent research? 是 What 引导的疑问句， 主干 the focus is what，of 短语层层修饰：of ... recent research 限定焦点的归属；结构 清晰。

【定位】Building on these findings, the latest research examined how a growth mindset of interest can boost integrative thinking across the traditional disciplinary boundaries of arts and sciences. 在前述发现的基础上，最新研究考察了「兴趣的成长型思维倾向」如何促进跨越文理传统学 科边界的整合性思维。 53. What is the focus of Professor O'Keefe's recent research? A) How boundaries can be removed between arts and science disciplines. B) How feasible it is to create new disciplines like computational economics. C) How students in arts and sciences view the two types of mindset of interest. D) How a growth mindset of interest can contribute to cross-disciplinary thinking.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文是研究「成长型思维如何促进跨学科思维」，并不是研究「学科边界如何被去 除」；boundaries 一词被借用，但研究对象偷换。 B) 偷换概念 原文只是用 computational economics 一词举例佐证研究结论，并未把「创建这种新 学科是否可行」当作研究焦点。 C) 偷换概念 研究的是成长型思维对跨学科思维的促进作用，不是「文理学生如何看待两种思维」； 主体与对象都被偷换。 D) ✓ 正确 a growth mindset of interest can boost ↔a growth mindset of interest can contribute to integrative thinking across the traditional disciplinary boundaries ↔ cross-disciplinary thinking how ... can boost ↔How ... can contribute to How a growth mindset of interest can contribute to cross-disciplinary thinking 把 boost 换成 contribute to、把 integrative ... across boundaries 浓缩为 cross- disciplinary thinking，主语与从句结构原样保留。 作者想用智能手机的例子说明什么? A) 跨学科研究需要高科技产品。 B) 改进的技术催生了广受欢迎的产品。 C) 制造创新产品需要多学科知识。 D) 高科技产品可以促进人们的综合思维。

questions.q: What does the author want to illustrate with the example of smartphones?
options: Hi-tech products are needed in interdisciplinary research.
Improved technology gives birth to highly popular products.
Making innovative products needs multidisciplinary knowledge.
Hi-tech products can boost people's integrative thinking.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author want to illustrate with the example of smartphones? 同时出现 example 与 illustrate，明牌例证目的题。

【拆句】What does the author want to illustrate with the example of smartphones? What 疑 问句，谓语 want to illustrate（不定式作宾语），with 短语 with the example of smartphones 指明所用的例子；结构清晰。

【定位】Take smartphones for example. You need not only computer science and engineering knowledge, but also an understanding of psychology and visual design to create a better product. 以智能手机为例：你不仅需要计算机科学与工程学的知识，还需要心理学与视觉设计方面的 理解，才能造出更好的产品。 54. What does the author want to illustrate with the example of smartphones? A) Hi-tech products are needed in interdisciplinary research. B) Improved technology gives birth to highly popular products. C) Making innovative products needs multidisciplinary knowledge. D) Hi-tech products can boost people's integrative thinking.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文是举智能手机说明「制造好产品需要多学科」，不是说「跨学科研究需要高科技产 品」；主客体倒置。 B) 偷换概念 原文重点在「需要多种知识」，不在「技术进步催生了热门产品」；选项偷换了论证 目的。 C) ✓ 正确 not only computer science and engineering knowledge, but also an understanding of psychology and visual design ↔multidisciplinary knowledge to create a better product ↔Making innovative products You need ↔needs Making innovative products needs multidisciplinary knowledge 把例子里四类知识 整体收束为 multidisciplinary knowledge，把 to create a better product 转写为主语 Making innovative products，整句保留 need 关系。 D) 与原文相反 原文是「需要整合思维 → 造出好产品」，选项却说「高科技产品 → 推动整合思维」， 把例子的目的反过来当因。 作者对求职者有什么建议? A) 学习实用技能。 B) 拓宽他们的兴趣。 C) 在疫情中保持安全。 D) 了解他们的紧迫问题。

questions.q: What is the author's suggestion to those who are seeking employment?
options: Learning practical skills.
Broadening their interests.
Staying safe in the pandemic.
Knowing their pressing issues.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the author's suggestion to those who are seeking employment? 直问作者的 建议是什么，对应原文具体语句，不是宏观主旨。

【拆句】What is the author's suggestion to those who are seeking employment? What 疑问 句，主干 the author's suggestion is what；to those 是介宾短语，who are seeking employment 是限定 those 的定语从句；结构清晰。

【定位】Having a growth mindset of interest can help job seekers expand their interests and become more adaptable to different fields, and take the initiative to learn new skills. 拥有兴趣的成长型思维，能帮助求职者拓展兴趣、对不同领域更具适应力，并主动学习新 技能。 55. What is the author's suggestion to those who are seeking employment? A) Learning practical skills. B) Broadening their interests. C) Staying safe in the pandemic. D) Knowing their pressing issues.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文 take the initiative to learn new skills 强调「主动学新技能」，重心在 take the initiative；选项掐头去尾只留 learning skills 还加上原文没有的 practical 限定词。 B) ✓ 正确 expand their interests ↔Broadening their interests their interests ↔their interests Broadening their interests 只是把 expand their interests 改写为 Broadening their interests 的动名词形式，与原文建议三件事中的第一件完全对应；选项虽只覆盖三件事 中的一件，但其他选项无一对得上，B 仍是唯一合规答案。 C) 无中生有 原文只把疫情列为背景说明就业压力大，从未给出「在疫情中保持安全」这条建议；属 于借背景词造选项。 D) 偷换概念 This is a pressing issue 是作者用来说明问题紧迫性的描述，不是给求职者的建议；选 项把背景描述偷换成建议对象。

items.title: 2022年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2022年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Online classes began to be popularized just a few decades ago. They are advertised as a way for adults to finish their education and students to learn the material at their own pace—it is far more compatible for people with busy schedules.

P2 But after being enrolled in an online course last fall semester, I came to realize online classes were merely a means to fulfil course requirements.

P3 First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material.

P4 As online courses tend to have more than 100 students, most of the assignments are short and simple. They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students.

P5 Perhaps the biggest disadvantage of taking an online class is the absence of face-to-face interaction between the teacher and their students. Live sessions are infrequent and are often scheduled during the middle of the day when students have to attend other classes or work. The office hours of the professor may also be during inconvenient times for many students as well. Most interaction with the professor has to be through email which is often impersonal. It is nearly impossible for students to build a relationship with their professor.

P6 There is also little interaction amongst students. It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers.

P7 Online classes also require either a computer or laptop and a reliable internet connection. Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage.

P8 Offering online classes certainly helps students who would otherwise not be able to attend classroom sessions. However, they fail to provide a genuine education with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking. We need restructured online classes in which students can have a learning experience that will actually provide quality education.

questions.q: What does the author say about students enrolled in online classes?
options: They can access course materials easily.
They are unmotivated to learn.
They can learn at their own pace.
They rarely fulfil the course requirements.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about students enrolled in online classes? 在问「就上网课 的学生这件事，作者具体说了什么」，是对单一陈述的事实核对。 46. What does the author say about students enrolled in online classes? A) They can access course materials easily. B) They are unmotivated to learn. C) They can learn at their own pace. D) They rarely fulfil the course requirements.

【拆句】题干主干是 What does the author say about X，标准的 say about 双宾结构，关于 X 的 对象是 students enrolled in online classes，其中 enrolled in online classes 是过去分 词短语作 students 的后置定语，等于 students who are enrolled in online classes，无 陷阱。

【定位】First of all, students lack the desire to learn, and they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade rather than genuinely engage with the course material. 首先，学生缺乏学习的欲望，他们只是完成作业以拿到及格分数，而不是真正与课程内容打 交道。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴：宣传方观点≠作者观点 They can access course materials easily. 取自 P1 对网课的宣传性描述，并非作者本 人就「学生」给出的评价，问的是作者对学生说了什么，不是对网课说了什么。 B) ✓ 正确 lack the desire to learn ↔unmotivated to learn 预判要找「学生没有学习动力」的表达，四个选项里只有 They are unmotivated to learn. 直接对应 lack the desire to learn，故锁定。 C) 张冠李戴：照抄被驳斥的卖点 They can learn at their own pace. 原句正是 learn the material at their own pace 的 近乎照抄，是作者列为反驳对象的卖点，不是作者对学生的论断。 D) 与原文相反：rarely 类否定词反转事实 They rarely fulfil the course requirements. 说学生很少完成课程要求，但 they simply complete their assignments to receive credit for a passing grade 明示他们 恰恰会完成作业、只是为拿学分，方向相反。 作者如何看待在线课程作业? A) 它们被设计得便于批改。 B) 它们旨在促进互动。 C) 它们基于容易获取的材料。 D) 它们是为了适应学生的需求而布置的。

questions.q: What does the author think of online course assignments?
options: They are made convenient to mark.
They are meant to facilitate interaction.
They are based on easily accessible material.
They are given to accommodate students' needs.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think of online course assignments? 指向作者对某一具体事物的 判断句，仍属细节核对。

【拆句】主干 What does the author think of X，think of 在此意为「认为…如何」，相当于 What is the author’s opinion of X，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 47. What does the author think of online course assignments? A) They are made convenient to mark. B) They are meant to facilitate interaction. C) They are based on easily accessible material. D) They are given to accommodate students' needs.

【定位】They are not designed for students to interact with the material in depth but designed to be graded easily to accommodate such a large number of students. 这些作业的设计不是为了让学生深入与材料互动，而是为了便于打分，以应对如此庞大的学 生群体。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 designed to be graded easily ↔made convenient to mark 预判锁定「便于打分」的语义，仅 They are made convenient to mark. 直接对应；其 他选项要么扯到互动，要么扯到材料/学生需求，不在 designed to 的目的范围。 B) 与原文相反：not…but… 的前半句反着用 They are meant to facilitate interaction. 把作业说成「促进互动」，但 not designed for students to interact with the material in depth 明确否定了「互动」目的。 C) 无中生有：制造原文未提及的属性 They are based on easily accessible material. 说作业基于「容易获取的材料」，原文 P4 没有任何句子谈论材料的获取难易，凭空捏造。 D) 偷换概念：动词宾语被替换 They are given to accommodate students' needs. 把 accommodate 的对象从原文 to accommodate such a large number of students 中的「大量学生（人数）」偷换 成「学生的需求」，目的指向被改。 作者说在线课程的一个缺点是什么? A) 它们经常被安排在不规律的时间。 B) 它们使得教授的办公室难以接近得多。 C) 它们往往会增加教授回复学生邮件的负担。 D) 它们几乎不为学生提供相互建立关系的机会。

questions.q: What does the author say is one disadvantage of online classes?
options: They are frequently scheduled at irregular times.
They make professors' offices much less accessible.
They tend to increase professors' burden of responding to students' emails.
They provide little chance for students to build relationships with each other
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say is one disadvantage of online classes? 中 one disadvantage 是单数，明示只问其中一个具体缺点，是定点取信息的细节题。

【拆句】题干主干 What does the author say is one disadvantage of online classes，say 后是 省略 that 的宾语从句 (that) one disadvantage of online classes is what，what 提前 到句首形成疑问，需注意「what 在从句里实为表语」这一点，否则容易把 say 误读成不 及物。

【定位】There is also little interaction amongst students. It can be harder for students to create study groups and form relationships with their peers. 学生之间的互动也很少。要想组建学习小组、和同伴建立关系会更难。 48. What does the author say is one disadvantage of online classes? A) They are frequently scheduled at irregular times. B) They make professors' offices much less accessible. C) They tend to increase professors' burden of responding to students' emails. D) They provide little chance for students to build relationships with each other

【选项】A) 偷换概念 + 与原文相反 They are frequently scheduled at irregular times. 说直播课「频繁地」被安排在不规 律时间，原文 Live sessions are infrequent 恰恰说直播课很少，且原文谈的是「时间冲 突」而非「时间不规律」。 B) 偷换概念：时间不便 ≠ 空间不可达 They make professors' offices much less accessible. 把焦点放在「办公室更不可 达」，但 The office hours of the professor may also be during inconvenient times 只说「办公时间不便」，没有说办公室不可达，accessible 与 convenient times 不是 同义。 C) 无中生有：从一个事实派生未提及的后果 They tend to increase professors' burden of responding to students' emails. 谈 教授回邮件「负担加重」，原文 Most interaction with the professor has to be through email which is often impersonal 只说邮件互动「冷冰冰」，并未提教授 负担。 D) ✓ 正确 form relationships with their peers ↔students to build relationships with each other It can be harder for students to create study groups ↔provide little chance 预判核心是「学生 + 学生之间难建立关系」，They provide little chance for students to build relationships with each other 在主体、动作、方向上全部命中。 如果课程转到线上可能会出现什么问题? A) 更多学生可能会发现容易缺课。 B) 教师会担心网络连接不佳。 C) 一些学生参加课程可能会有困难。 D) 资源有限的学校将处于不利地位。

questions.q: What problem may arise if classes go online?
options: More students may find it easy to be absent from them.
Teachers will worry about poor internet connections.
Some students may have difficulty attending them.
Schools with limited resources will be at a disadvantage.
questions.explain:
【判型】What problem may arise if classes go online? 问「在网课条件下会出现什么问题」，问 的是文中已写明的某一具体后果，不需要推论。

【拆句】主干 What problem may arise，后接 if 条件状语从句 if classes go online，arise 为不及 物动词「出现」，结构清晰；注意 go online 这个搭配指「转为线上」，不要望文生义译作 「上网」。

【定位】Not all students have access to these types of resources, whether it is for financial or other reasons, and some students can be put at a disadvantage. 并非所有学生都能用上这些资源，无论是出于经济还是其他原因，有些学生因此可能处于不 利地位。 49. What problem may arise if classes go online? A) More students may find it easy to be absent from them. B) Teachers will worry about poor internet connections. C) Some students may have difficulty attending them. D) Schools with limited resources will be at a disadvantage.

【选项】A) 无中生有：把后果嫁接到主观行为 More students may find it easy to be absent from them. 谈学生「更容易缺席」， 原文从未谈学生主观逃课难易，凭空添加。 B) 张冠李戴：替换受影响主体 Teachers will worry about poor internet connections. 把网络问题的担忧者换成 teachers，原文 P7 通篇是 students 受影响，无任何关于教师担忧的描述。 C) ✓ 正确 Not all students have access to these types of resources ↔ Some students may have difficulty attending them some students can be put at a disadvantage ↔may have difficulty 预判核心「部分学生上不了网课」，选项 Some students may have difficulty attending them 主体、动作、可能性三要素与原文一一对位。 D) 张冠李戴：把人替换成机构 Schools with limited resources will be at a disadvantage. 把 at a disadvantage 的主体换成 schools，但 some students can be put at a disadvantage 明确主语 是 students。 作者认为什么构成了真正教育的关键部分? A) 获取有用的知识。 B) 在校园进行实际生活技能的训练。 C) 发展学生的个性。 D) 培养分析思维能力。

questions.q: What does the author think constitutes a key part of genuine education?
options: Acquisition of useful knowledge.
Training of real-life skills on campus.
Development of students' personalities.
Cultivation of analytical thinking ability.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think constitutes a key part of genuine education? 仍是问作者 明示的具体内容，文末已直接点出，无需推断。

【拆句】题干主干 What does the author think X constitutes Y，think 后为宾语从句，从句里 What 同时是 constitutes 的主语，constitutes = 构成；该结构需要把 What 还原到从句 主语位才能读顺，是四级长难句的小考点。

【定位】However, they fail to provide a genuine education with an emphasis on convenience rather than critical thinking. 然而，网课未能提供真正的教育，因为它强调便利而非批判性思维。 50. What does the author think constitutes a key part of genuine education? A) Acquisition of useful knowledge. B) Training of real-life skills on campus. C) Development of students' personalities. D) Cultivation of analytical thinking ability.

【选项】A) 以偏概全：用常识替代作者主张 Acquisition of useful knowledge. 把「真教育」化约为「获取有用知识」，但 P8 强调 的是思维而非知识，且原文也未把「有用知识」列为真教育的关键。 B) 无中生有：用文章主题的相邻概念造干扰 Training of real-life skills on campus. 强调「校园里」「真实生活技能」两个限定，但 P8 既未谈 real-life skills 也未谈 on campus，是利用「网课—线下」对立常识捏造的 对立项。 C) 无中生有：搬用流行教育口号 Development of students' personalities. 把真教育的关键说成「学生人格的发展」， 原文 P8 通篇未涉及 personalities/character 之类的人格概念。 D) ✓ 正确 critical thinking ↔analytical thinking ability 预判核心是 critical thinking，四个选项里只有 Cultivation of analytical thinking ability. 直接对应 critical thinking 的同义改写，故锁定。

items.title: 2022年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2022年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 In the age of the internet, there's no such thing as a private debate. But is that bad for science? Some scientists have had concerns. When debates in any sector move beyond the halls of universities and government agencies, there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion; yet, open debate can also promote communication between the scientific community and the public. Recent open debates on scientific research, health, and policy have aroused greater public attention and encouraged more diverse voices. If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems—and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly—then this is good for everyone, including scientists.

P2 A recent debate published in The New York Times discussed the question of how quickly medicine should be developed and produced. Issues such as safety of the product and perception of the public were examined and considered. But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine.

P3 The anxiety seems misplaced. Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices. These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place.

P4 For many scientists, public debate is a new frontier and it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules. But rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held. If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self- correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed. With the validity of science coming under attack, there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life. Let everyone see the noisy, messy deliberations that advance science and lead to decisions that benefit us all.

questions.q: What does the author think open debate can do?
options: Help the public to better understand science.
Clear up confusion in the scientific community.
Settle disputes between universities and government agencies.
Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think open debate can do是一个具体的做什么问题，不含infer、 imply、mainly about等推断或主旨信号词，属于围绕一个话题点的细节定位题

【拆句】主干是What does the author think open debate can do，think后省略that，引出宾语 从句open debate can do (what)。问句的What其实是宾语从句里do的宾语，被前置到句 首。结构简单、无陷阱。 51. What does the author think open debate can do? A) Help the public to better understand science. B) Clear up confusion in the scientific community. C) Settle disputes between universities and government agencies. D) Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public.

【定位】If this trend spurs scientists to agree more quickly about the best solutions to our problems— and at the same time helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly —then this is good for everyone, including scientists. 如果这一趋势能推动科学家更快地就我们面临问题的最佳解决方案达成一致，并同时帮助公 众更清楚地观察科学讨论的过程，那么对所有人，包括科学家在内，都是好事。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 helps the public observe the process of scientific discourse more clearly ↔ Help the public to better understand science 预判让公众更清楚地观察、理解科学讨论与Help the public to better understand science在语义上同构，仅是observe到understand、scientific discourse到science的 上下位替换 B) 偷换概念 Clear up confusion in the scientific community说的是消除科学界内部的困惑，但原 文potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion点 明confusion存在于公众一侧、而非科学界内部 C) 无中生有 Settle disputes between universities and government agencies声称开放辩论能解 决高校与政府机构之间的纠纷；原文虽提及halls of universities and government agencies，但只是说辩论的发生地，并未说要去settle什么disputes D) 与原文相反 Prevent information from being used incorrectly by the public把防止信息被误用说 成open debate的功能；但原文there's potential for information to be used incorrectly, leading to public confusion里，这一可能性是开放辩论的副作用而非它的 解决目标 为什么《纽约时报》上发表的一场近期辩论在专家中引起了担忧? A) 它可能会阻碍医学研究的进展。 B) 它可能会滋生公众对现代医学的不信任。 C) 它可能会增加获取研究资金的难度。 D) 它可能会妨碍医学科学家达成共识。

questions.q: Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts?
options: It might hinder the progress in medical research.
It might breed public distrust in modern medicine.
It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds.
It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts问的是某一具体事件下专家担心的具体原因，原因可在文中直接找到，不需要跨段 推断 52. Why did a recent debate published in The New York Times arouse concerns among experts? A) It might hinder the progress in medical research. B) It might breed public distrust in modern medicine. C) It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds. D) It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus.

【拆句】主干是Why加did加a recent debate加arouse加concerns。a recent debate后带过去分词 短语published in The New York Times作后置定语，限定是哪一场debate；among experts限定concerns的范围。理清后题干即那场登在某报上的辩论，为何让专家担心。

【定位】But some experts worried that such public speculation might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine. 但一些专家担心，这种公开揣测可能让人们相信：对细节的分歧意味着科学界对现代医药的 安全与效率缺乏足够的共识。

【选项】A) 无中生有 It might hinder the progress in medical research谈的是阻碍医学研究的进展，原文 只说公开辩论可能让公众产生误解，并未说会拖慢医学研究本身 B) ✓ 正确 might lead people to believe that disagreement about the details meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus over the safety and efficiency of modern-day medicine ↔It might breed public distrust in modern medicine 预判中的对现代医药产生不信任正好对应public distrust in modern medicine；原文的 多步表述被压缩成一个名词distrust，是典型的名词化同义替换 C) 无中生有 It might add to the difficulty of getting research funds说会增加获得研究经费的难 度；原文从未提及funds、funding、money相关概念 D) 偷换概念 It might prevent medical scientists reaching consensus说会阻止医学科学家达成共 识；原文是meant a lack of adequate scientific consensus——即让公众以为科学界 没共识，但事实是科学界已有共识，并不是公开辩论会真的让科学家无法达成共识 为什么作者说一些专家的焦虑似乎是错位的? A) 在会议上辩论科学问题现在已经过时了。 B) 科学家和公众都可以辩论各种话题。 C) 无论如何公众都能接触到关于科学的辩论。 D) 科学家可以用任何他们喜欢的方式表达自己的观点。

questions.q: Why does the author say some experts' anxiety seems misplaced?
options: Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned.
Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public.
Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway.
Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author say some experts' anxiety seems misplaced问的是作者下此判断 的依据，依据明示在原文紧随其后的句子中，属于因果细节 53. Why does the author say some experts' anxiety seems misplaced? A) Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned. B) Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public. C) Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway. D) Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like.

【拆句】Why does the author say后接一个宾语从句some experts' anxiety seems misplaced。 anxiety前是some experts'所有格作定语；seems是系动词、misplaced是表语形容词。理 解为为什么作者说某些专家的担心是放错地方的。

【定位】Gone are the days of going to a conference and debating scientific issues, and that's good because those gatherings were not diverse enough and excluded many important voices. These days, the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place. 去开会、在会上辩论科学问题的日子已经过去了，这是好事，因为那些聚会不够多元，把许 多重要的声音排除在外。如今，无论辩论在哪里举行，公众都能接触到。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Debating scientific issues at a conference is now old-fashioned只是原文Gone are the days of going to a conference的复述，确实存在于文中，但它只是支撑句之一， 不是作者用来回答为什么misplaced的核心理由；核心理由是公众如今随处可获取辩论 B) 偷换概念 Diverse topics can be debated by both scientists and the public说的是多元话题可 被科学家与公众共同辩论；原文diverse是修饰those gatherings本身（聚会不够多 元），并不是说话题多元，更没说公众能与科学家共同辩论 C) ✓ 正确 the public can access debates about science regardless of where they take place ↔ Debates about science are accessible to the public anyway 预判中的无论在哪都能接触到正是accessible to the public anyway的内涵；从access （动词）到accessible（形容词）的词性转换加主被动互换是四级最典型的同义替换手法 D) 张冠李戴 Scientists can voice their opinions whatever way they like说的是科学家可以以他们 喜欢的方式发声；原文谈论的是公众能接触到辩论，主语和动作都不是科学家 作者建议科学家如何对待公开辩论? A) 对此进行更多讨论。 B) 张开双臂拥抱它。 C) 为它制定新规则。 D) 将它限制在理性的程度。

questions.q: What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate?
options: Have more discussions about it.
Embrace it with open arms.
Formulate new rules for it.
Restrain it to a rational degree.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate问的是一个具体建 议，答案在原文祈使句中能直接找到，无需推断 54. What does the author suggest scientists do about public debate? A) Have more discussions about it. B) Embrace it with open arms. C) Formulate new rules for it. D) Restrain it to a rational degree.

【拆句】主干What does the author suggest scientists do。suggest后接的是宾语从句省略 that，scientists是从句主语、do是从句动词（虚拟语气省略should），about public debate是范围状语。句意：作者建议科学家们对于公共辩论应该怎么做。

【定位】But rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous, wherever they are held. 但与其回避这类对话，不如让辩论变得透明而有力，无论它们在哪里举行。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Have more discussions about it说对公共辩论本身展开更多讨论——它把公共辩论变 成被讨论的对象；原文是要科学家参与到公共辩论中，而不是开会讨论公共辩论应不应 该做 B) ✓ 正确 rather than avoiding such conversations, let the debates be transparent and vigorous ↔ Embrace it with open arms 预判拥抱并积极参与与Embrace it with open arms在意象与态度极性上完全一致； rather than avoiding的反面正是embrace C) 与原文相反 Formulate new rules for it说要为公共辩论制定新规则；原文it may feel like a place with few restraints or rules承认公共辩论缺规则，但下一句紧接着以But rather than avoiding such conversations转向拥抱而非立规则，作者并未建议立新规 D) 与原文相反 Restrain it to a rational degree说要把公共辩论约束到一个合理程度；原文却用let the debates be transparent and vigorous强调放开而非约束，方向相反 作者在最后一段关于科学说了什么? A) 它是通过教科书传播的。 B) 它是被证明有效且符合实际的东西。 C) 它是一个动态的自我完善过程。 D) 它是事实和既定规则的集合。

questions.q: What does the author say about science in the last paragraph?
options: It is transmitted through textbooks.
It is what proves valid and true to life.
It is a dynamic and self-improving process.
It is a collection of facts and established rules.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about science in the last paragraph问的是末段里关于 science的具体描述，不问全文主旨也不问态度极性，定位段已给出，属段内细节题

【拆句】主干What does the author say about science。in the last paragraph是地点状语限定回 答范围。say about science是动词搭配对…作出说明。理解为在末段里作者关于science说 了什么。 55. What does the author say about science in the last paragraph? A) It is transmitted through textbooks. B) It is what proves valid and true to life. C) It is a dynamic and self-improving process. D) It is a collection of facts and established rules.

【定位】If the public is to understand that science is an honorably self-correcting process, the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed. 如果想让公众明白科学是一个光荣的自我修正过程，那么科学就是教科书里一组固定事实这 一观念就必须被抛弃。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 It is transmitted through textbooks说科学通过教科书传播；原文the idea that science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook needs to be dismissed恰好是作者要否 定的观念 B) 张冠李戴 It is what proves valid and true to life说科学是被证明有效且符合现实的东西；原文 there's a need for scientific debates to be perceived as open and true to life里 true to life修饰的是scientific debates（辩论）如何被感知，而不是用来定义science 本身 C) ✓ 正确 science is an honorably self-correcting process ↔It is a dynamic and self-improving process 预判自我修正的动态过程与a dynamic and self-improving process逐字对应；self- correcting对应self-improving是同根同义的复合形容词替换 D) 与原文相反 It is a collection of facts and established rules说科学是事实与既定规则的集合—— 这与原文science is a fixed set of facts in a textbook想抛弃的旧观念完全对齐

items.title: 2022年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2022年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Social media can be a powerful communication tool for employees, helping them to collaborate, share ideas and solve problems. Research has shown that 82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes. These beliefs contribute to a majority of workers connecting with colleagues on social media, even during work hours.

P2 Employers typically worry that social media is a productivity killer; more than half of U.S. employers reportedly block access to social media at work. In my research with 277 employees of a healthcare organization I found these concerns to be misguided. Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention.

P3 In the first part of the study I surveyed the employees about why and how they used platforms like Facebook, Twitter, or LinkedIn. Respondents were then asked about their work behaviors, including whether they felt motivated in their jobs and showed initiative at work. I found employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers through social media blogs tend to be more motivated and come up with innovative ideas. But when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated and show less initiative.

P4 In the second part of the study I found 76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media. When I examined how respondents expressed openness to new careers and employers, I found that they engaged in some key activities including researching new organizations and making new work connections.

P5 These findings present a dilemma for managers: employees using social media at work are more engaged and more productive, but they are also more likely to leave your company. Managers should implement solutions that neutralize the retention risk caused by social media.

P6 They can create social media groups in which employees will be more likely to collaborate and less likely to share withdrawal intentions or discussions about external job opportunities. Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover( 跳槽) intentions, by recognizing employees' accomplishments and giving visibility to employees' success stories.

questions.q: What does previous research about social media reveal?
options: Most employees think positively of it.
It improves employees' work efficiency.
It enables employees to form connections.
Employees spend much of their work time on it.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does previous research about social media reveal? 用 what...reveal 直接问研究 揭示的事实，没有 infer/imply 等推断信号，是典型细节题。 46. What does previous research about social media reveal? A) Most employees think positively of it. B) It improves employees' work efficiency. C) It enables employees to form connections. D) Employees spend much of their work time on it.

【拆句】题干主干 What does previous research about social media reveal? 结构平铺：what 作 reveal 的宾语前置，about social media 是修饰 research 的介词短语。无陷阱。

【定位】Research has shown that 82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes. 已有研究表明：82% 的员工认为社交媒体能改善工作关系，60% 的员工相信它有助于决策 过程。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 82% of employees think social media can improve work relationships and 60% believe it can support decision-making processes ↔Most employees think positively of it 原文两条数据都是正面态度的多数比例，恰好对应预判中的"多数员工肯定它"，整段不 含工作效率提升或工作时间被占用的客观数据，故锁定选项首字母为 A。 B) 偷换概念 原文只说员工"认为"社交媒体能改善关系和决策，是主观看法；It improves employees' work efficiency 把这种看法说成了已被证明的客观事实，且把 work relationships 偷换成 efficiency。 C) 以偏概全 It enables employees to form connections 把原文 improve work relationships 改 成"建立联系"，并把"员工的看法"偷换成"它实际能够"，只触及关系一项却丢了决策，且 把主观信念伪装成已证事实。 D) 无中生有 原文只说员工 connecting with colleagues on social media, even during work hours，并没有给出"花费大量工作时间在上面"的程度判断；Employees spend much of their work time on it 凭空加上了"花费大量时间"的数量评估。 作者自己的研究发现社交媒体有什么影响? A) 它对员工的工作产生负面影响。 B) 它对员工忠诚度造成很大损害。 C) 它扼杀了员工的工作动力。 D) 它影响雇主的决策。

questions.q: What did the author's own research find about social media?
options: It influences employees' work negatively.
It does much harm to employee loyalty.
It kills employees' motivation for work
It affects employers' decision-making.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the author's own research find about social media? 用 what...find 问研究的 客观发现，是典型细节题。 47. What did the author's own research find about social media? A) It influences employees' work negatively. B) It does much harm to employee loyalty. C) It kills employees' motivation for work D) It affects employers' decision-making.

【拆句】题干 What did the author's own research find about social media? 主语 the author's own research，谓语 find，about social media 是 find 后的话题状语。结构清楚，无 陷阱。

【定位】Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention. 社交媒体降低生产力的程度，远远比不上它对员工留任的杀伤力。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 原文 Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention 已点明社交媒体并不显著降低生产力，所以"对工作产生负面影响"过于宽泛 ——它只在留任这一面有显著负面，工作本身（生产力、动力）并没有受到普遍负面 影响。 B) ✓ 正确 Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention ↔ It does much harm to employee loyalty not...as much as... 句式的语义重心在后半句"as much as"之后，定位句的论点核心 是"对员工留任的杀伤更大"，恰好对应预判与首字母 B 的选项。 C) 张冠李戴 原文第 2 段并未谈及对员工动力（motivation）的杀伤——动力一词出现在第 3 段，且 第 3 段中社交媒体反而是"使员工 more motivated"。本选项把作者研究的核心结论说 成"扼杀动力"，与原文位置和方向都不符。 D) 答非所问 原文第 1 段提及社交媒体被员工认为 can support decision-making processes，主语 是"员工的决策"，而非"雇主的决策"；本选项把"对雇主决策的影响"放进作者己研结论 里，既错位也答非所问。 作者在研究中发现在线社交互动有什么影响? A) 它因员工而异。 B) 它往往随使用的平台而变化。 C) 它与员工与谁互动有很大关系。 D) 当员工与外部人员互动时很难衡量。

questions.q: What did the author find in his study about the effect of online social interactions?
options: It differs from employee to employee.
It tends to vary with the platform used.
It has much to do with whom employees interact with.
It is hard to measure when employees interact with outsiders.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the author find in his study about the effect of online social interactions? 同样是 what...find 句式，问研究中的具体发现。 48. What did the author find in his study about the effect of online social interactions? A) It differs from employee to employee. B) It tends to vary with the platform used. C) It has much to do with whom employees interact with. D) It is hard to measure when employees interact with outsiders.

【拆句】题干主干是 What did the author find，in his study 是状语，about the effect of online social interactions 是 find 的宾语介词短语，进一步限定要找的发现内容。结构略长，但层 层并列，无陷阱。

【定位】I found employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers through social media blogs tend to be more motivated and come up with innovative ideas. But when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated and show less initiative. 我发现：通过社交媒体博客与同事进行在线社交互动的员工，往往更有动力、能想出更多新 点子；但当员工与组织外的人互动时，他们反而动力下降、缺少主动性。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文并未说"因人而异"或"每个员工不一样"，而是把员工按互动对象分成两类得出两种结 果；It differs from employee to employee 把分类标准偷换成"员工个体差异"。 B) 无中生有 原文 platforms like Facebook, Twitter, or LinkedIn 仅作为研究背景，没有把不同平台 作为造成结果差异的原因；It tends to vary with the platform used 把背景信息硬升级 成变量来源。 C) ✓ 正确 employees who engage in online social interactions with co-workers ... tend to be more motivated / when employees interact with individuals outside the organization, they are less motivated ↔It has much to do with whom employees interact with 原文两个分句除了对象不同（同事 vs. 外部人士）几乎所有别的条件都相同，结果却完 全相反——这正是"效果取决于互动对象"的最直接证据，故锁定首字母 C。 D) 与原文相反 原文恰恰已经测量出员工与外部人士互动会导致 less motivated and show less initiative，研究是给出了明确结果的，并不"难以衡量"。本选项与原文方向相反。 员工使用社交媒体工作发现了什么问题? A) 他们很少表达内心想法。 B) 他们中的大多数人探索新的工作机会。 C) 他们不愿意与他人合作。 D) 他们中的许多人最终生产力下降。

questions.q: What problem was found with employees using social media for work?
options: They seldom expressed their inner thoughts.
Most of them explored new job opportunities.
They were reluctant to collaborate with others.
Many of them ended with lower productivity.
questions.explain:
【判型】What problem was found with employees using social media for work? 用 what...found 问研究中发现的问题，仍是问客观事实。 49. What problem was found with employees using social media for work? A) They seldom expressed their inner thoughts. B) Most of them explored new job opportunities. C) They were reluctant to collaborate with others. D) Many of them ended with lower productivity.

【拆句】题干 What problem was found with employees using social media for work? 是 what 作主语的被动疑问句：problem 与 what 共同作主语，be found 是谓语，with employees using social media for work 是介词短语修饰 problem。读不顺时把它倒过来 想成 "researchers found what problem with these employees" 即可。

【定位】I found 76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media. When I examined how respondents expressed openness to new careers and employers, I found that they engaged in some key activities including researching new organizations and making new work connections. 我发现：76% 用社交媒体办公的员工会关注他们在社交媒体上看到的其他组织。当我考察 这些受访者如何表达对新职业、新雇主的开放态度时，我发现他们会从事几项关键活动，包 括研究新公司、建立新的工作联系。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文第 4 段没有提到员工"是否表达内心想法"——只说他们关注其他组织、研究新公 司、建立新人脉，这些都是外向行为；They seldom expressed their inner thoughts 把不存在的话题拉进来。 B) ✓ 正确 76% of employees using social media for work took an interest in other organizations they found on social media ↔Most of them explored new job opportunities openness to new careers and employers ↔explored new job opportunities 76% 的覆盖面+关注新公司、研究新公司、建立新人脉、对新职业开放等多项行为同向 叠加，正对应"多数人在物色新工作"，故锁定首字母 B。 C) 与原文相反 原文第 3 段已说与同事互动会让员工 more motivated and come up with innovative ideas，本身就是合作意愿强；They were reluctant to collaborate with others 与之 方向相反。 D) 与原文相反 原文第 2 段已经否定 Social media doesn't reduce productivity nearly as much as it kills employee retention，社交媒体并未明显降低生产力；本选项却说"很多人最终生 产力降低"，是把作者明确否定的结论又重新放回来。 作者建议管理者做什么来消除留任风险? A) 因员工的成就而给予晋升。 B) 为员工创造分享成功故事的机会。 50. What does the author suggest managers do to neutralize the retention risk? A) Give promotions to employees for their accomplishments. B) Create opportunities for employees to share success stories. C) Acknowledge employees' achievements through social media. D) Encourage employees to increase their visibility on social media. C) 通过社交媒体认可员工的成就。 D) 鼓励员工提高在社交媒体上的知名度。

questions.q: What does the author suggest managers do to neutralize the retention risk?
options: Give promotions to employees for their accomplishments.
Create opportunities for employees to share success stories.
Acknowledge employees' achievements through social media.
Encourage employees to increase their visibility on social media.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest managers do to neutralize the retention risk? 虽含 suggest，但问的是作者明文给出的建议方案，原文必有对应句，仍属细节题。

【拆句】题干主干 What does the author suggest managers do，managers do 是 suggest 后 省略 that 的虚拟语气从句（suggest sb. do），to neutralize the retention risk 是表目的 的不定式。难点在虚拟语气省略 that 的结构，主体考生易把 managers 看成全句主语。

【定位】Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover(跳槽) intentions, by recognizing employees' accomplishments and giving visibility to employees' success stories. 管理者还可以利用社交媒体直接降低跳槽意向：方法是表彰员工取得的成就、让员工的成功 故事更被看见。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文动作是 recognizing employees' accomplishments（公开承认成就），不是"提 拔"；Give promotions to employees for their accomplishments 把"承认"偷换成"提 拔"，并丢掉了"通过社交媒体"这一关键媒介。 B) 张冠李戴 原文是管理者借社交媒体 giving visibility to employees' success stories——动作发 起者是管理者；Create opportunities for employees to share success stories 把动作 主体换成员工自己分享，与原文恰好对调，且回避了"用社交媒体"这一关键媒介。 C) ✓ 正确 Managers can also use social media to directly reduce turnover(跳槽) intentions, by recognizing employees' accomplishments and giving visibility to employees' success stories ↔Acknowledge employees' achievements through social media 预判要求"用社交媒体表彰成就"中的动作与媒介两要素同时对齐，只有首字母 C 把"承认 成就"与"借助社交媒体"都准确保留，其余选项要么换错动作、要么丢掉媒介。 D) 偷换概念 原文是管理者 giving visibility to employees' success stories——是"让员工的事迹可 见"，主导者是管理者；Encourage employees to increase their visibility on social media 把"被表彰的事迹"偷换成"员工的曝光度"，且把管理者的动作变成鼓励员工自己 增加曝光，正好是文章想抑制的"个人外向行为"。

items.title: 2022年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2022年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 In the coming era of budget cuts to education, distance learning could become the norm.

P2 The temptation for those in charge of education budgets to trade teachers for technology could be so strong that they ignore the disadvantages of distance learning. School facilities are expensive to build and maintain, and teachers are expensive to employ. Online classes do not require buildings and each class can host hundreds of people simultaneously, resulting in greater savings, thus increasing the temptation of distance education for those concerned more about budgets than learning. But moving away from a traditional classroom in which a living, breathing human being teaches and interacts with students daily would be a disaster. Physically attending school has hidden benefits: getting up every morning, interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers are essential skills to cultivate in young people. Moreover, schools should be more than simple institutions of traditional learning. They are now places that provide meals. They are places where students receive counseling and other support.

P3 Those policy-makers are often fascinated by the latest technology in education and its potential to "transform" education overnight. But online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help. Educational videos may deliver academic content, but they are unable to make eye contact or assess a student's level of engagement. Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom. In their first 18 years of life, American children spend only 9% of their time in school. Yet teachers are expected to prepare them to be responsible citizens, cultivate their social skills, encourage successful time management, and enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market. Given these expectations, schools should not become permanently "remote".

P4 The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time. Personal teaching is about teachers showing students a higher path, and about young people going through the process together. Technology, no matter how advanced, should simply be a tool of a good teacher.

questions.q: What mainly accounts for the possibility that distance learning could become the norm?
options: Advances in education technology.
Shrinking financial resources.
Shortage of school facilities.
Lack of qualified teachers.
questions.explain:
【判型】What mainly accounts for the possibility that distance learning could become the norm?问「是什么导致」，是对文本中明确陈述事实的提取，不是态度也不是推断。

【拆句】题干主干是What mainly accounts for the possibility，that引导同位语从句解释 possibility的内容；that distance learning could become the norm整体作possibility的 同位语；副词mainly限定account for，提示要找「主要」原因而非次要原因。结构清晰、 无陷阱。

【定位】In the coming era of budget cuts to education, distance learning could become the norm. 在即将到来的教育预算削减时代，远程教育可能成为常态。 51. What mainly accounts for the possibility that distance learning could become the norm? A) Advances in education technology. B) Shrinking financial resources. C) Shortage of school facilities. D) Lack of qualified teachers.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文未提及教育技术本身的进步是导致远程教育常态化的原因；P1只字未提技术进步， 只谈预算。 B) ✓ 正确 budget cuts to education ↔Shrinking financial resources 预判「教育预算削减」与Shrinking financial resources「财政资源缩水」是同一概念的 不同表述，是细节题最典型的同义替换。 C) 偷换概念 Shortage of school facilities是「校舍短缺」，而原文School facilities are expensive to build and maintain说的是校舍「造价高、维护贵」，是「贵」不是「缺」；且这是 第二段提到的，并非第一段中远程教育常态化的原因。 D) 无中生有 原文从未提及「合格教师短缺」是远程教育常态化的原因；teachers are expensive to employ说的是教师「贵」，不是「缺」或「不合格」。 作者认为学生实地到校上学可能带来的一个好处是什么? A) 养成早起的习惯。 B) 吃营养均衡的饭菜。 C) 成长为有生命、会呼吸的人。 D) 培养与同龄人和教师的关系。

questions.q: What does the author say is one possible benefit of students attending school physically?
options: Developing the habit of getting up early.
Eating nutritionally well-balanced meals.
Growing into living and breathing human beings.
Cultivating relationships with peers and teachers.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say is one possible benefit问「作者说了什么好处」，是对作者 明示信息的提取。

【拆句】题干主干是What does the author say is one possible benefit，省略了关系代词的宾语 从句结构「the author say (that) [what] is one possible benefit」；介词of短语of students attending school physically作benefit的定语，其中students是动名词 attending的逻辑主语。结构无陷阱，注意one possible暗示文中可能列了多个好处，选项 里只要有一个对得上即可。

【定位】Physically attending school has hidden benefits: getting up every morning, interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers are essential skills to cultivate in young people. 实地上学有隐性的好处：每天早起、与同伴互动、与老师建立关系，这些都是年轻人需要培 养的关键能力。 52. What does the author say is one possible benefit of students attending school physically? A) Developing the habit of getting up early. B) Eating nutritionally well-balanced meals. C) Growing into living and breathing human beings. D) Cultivating relationships with peers and teachers.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Developing the habit of getting up early虽然对应原文getting up every morning， 但原文这只是三项并列好处之一，且作者强调的核心是skills to cultivate，而getting up属于日常生活动作；将「早起」提炼为「养成早起的习惯」是把动作误读成了一种习 惯养成训练，与原文核心语义有偏差。 B) 张冠李戴 原文末尾They are now places that provide meals提到学校提供餐食，但作者并未说 「营养均衡的餐食」是attending school physically的benefit；nutritionally well- balanced属于无中生有的修饰语，且provide meals被原文归入「学校的社会职能」而 非「实地上学的好处」——主体不同。 C) 偷换概念 原文a living, breathing human being teaches and interacts with students中living, breathing是修饰teacher的形容词，强调「活生生的」教师；选项Growing into living and breathing human beings把「形容老师的状态词」偷换成「学生成长的目标」， 且growing into是「成长为」的方向性动词，原文完全没有这层意思。 D) ✓ 正确 interacting with peers, and building relationships with teachers ↔ Cultivating relationships with peers and teachers 选项Cultivating relationships with peers and teachers精准合并了预判中的第二、三 项内容，且与原文cultivate呼应。 作者如何看待教育领域的最新技术? A) 它可能有潜在的弊端。 B) 它可能使许多教师失业。 C) 它可能增加学生的经济负担。 D) 它可能彻底改变课堂教学。

questions.q: What does the author think of the latest technology in education?
options: It may have potential disadvantages.
It may render many teachers jobless.
It may add to students' financial burden.
It may revolutionize classroom teaching
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think of直问作者对某事物的看法，是典型态度类信号。

【拆句】题干主干是What does the author think of the latest technology in education，think of是固定搭配「对……怎么看」；the latest是形容词最高级作定语。结构平铺直叙，无 陷阱。 53. What does the author think of the latest technology in education? A) It may have potential disadvantages. B) It may render many teachers jobless. C) It may add to students' financial burden. D) It may revolutionize classroom teaching

【定位】Those policy-makers are often fascinated by the latest technology in education and its potential to "transform" education overnight. But online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help. 那些政策制定者常常被教育领域最新技术及其「一夜变革」教育的潜力所迷住。但在线教育 不允许教师把学习吃力的学生留下来课后辅导。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help ↔It may have potential disadvantages Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom ↔ It may have potential disadvantages 预判得出作者对新技术持质疑或保留态度，It may have potential disadvantages恰好 用「可能有不足」概括了这种保留立场，与原文极性一致。 B) 无中生有 原文未提及新技术会「让教师失业」；作者讨论的是技术替代教师在功能上的局限，不 是技术造成教师失业的社会后果。 C) 张冠李戴 原文谈的是节约预算者的成本动机resulting in greater savings，从未提及学生的财务 负担会因此增加；把「学校省钱」误读为「学生多花钱」，方向完全相反。 D) 与原文相反 It may revolutionize classroom teaching即「可能彻底变革课堂教学」是政策制定者 的看法，不是作者的；原文用"transform"加引号、用But转折、用Distance education will never match the personal teaching in a traditional classroom反驳，明确否定 了这种乐观看法。考生若把fascinated误读成作者本人也「被迷住」，就会反选此项。 作者说教师被期望做什么? A) 增强学生的领导能力。 B) 提升学生到管理岗位。 C) 使学生能够适应生活中的变化。 D) 让学生为未来的竞争做好准备。

questions.q: What does the author say teachers are expected to do?
options: Enhance students' leadership capacity.
Elevate students to managerial positions.
Enable students to adapt to the changes in life.
Prepare students to be competitive in the future.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say teachers are expected to do?问「教师被期望做什么」，是 对原文明示信息的客观提取。 54. What does the author say teachers are expected to do? A) Enhance students' leadership capacity. B) Elevate students to managerial positions. C) Enable students to adapt to the changes in life. D) Prepare students to be competitive in the future.

【拆句】题干主干是What does the author say teachers are expected to do，author say后省略 了that引导的宾语从句；从句主干是「teachers are expected to do (what)」，be expected to do是固定结构「被期望做」。结构无陷阱。

【定位】Yet teachers are expected to prepare them to be responsible citizens, cultivate their social skills, encourage successful time management, and enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market. 然而，教师却被期望让他们成为有责任感的公民，培养他们的社交能力，鼓励他们成功管理 时间，并增强他们在日益严酷的劳动力市场上立足发展的能力。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文四项期望中没有提到培养「领导力」（leadership capacity）；社交能力不等于领 导力，二者不可等同。 B) 偷换概念 原文没有任何「把学生提升到管理岗位」的内容；该项利用原文management一词 （time management）做望文生义的偷换——time management是「时间管理」， managerial positions是「管理职位」，二者只是共享management词根，语义完全 不同。 C) 无中生有 原文四项期望中没有「让学生适应生活变化」（adapt to the changes in life）这一 项；adapt to changes是常见教育鸡汤，但原文未提及。 D) ✓ 正确 enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market ↔ Prepare students to be competitive in the future 预判得出最后一项enhance their capacity to flourish in an increasingly harsh labor market，选项Prepare students to be competitive in the future恰是此项的抽象 提炼。 为什么技术不能取代一位好教师? A) 它缺乏人性。 B) 它尚不成熟。 C) 它无法追踪学生的成长。 D) 它无法满足个人需求。

questions.q: Why couldn't technology replace a good teacher?
options: It lacks humanity.
It is still immature.
It cannot track students' growth.
It cannot cater to personal needs.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why couldn't technology replace a good teacher?问「为什么不能」，是对原文中给出 的明确原因的提取；末段P4给出了直接答案句，不需推断。 55. Why couldn't technology replace a good teacher? A) It lacks humanity. B) It is still immature. C) It cannot track students' growth. D) It cannot cater to personal needs.

【拆句】题干主干是Why couldn't technology replace a good teacher?，否定情态动词couldn't 与why连用，表达「为何不能」，注意这不是疑问句的常规反问，而是给定「不能取代」的 前提下追问原因。结构无陷阱，重点抓couldn't的否定意味。

【定位】The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time. 课堂的力量根植于聚集在同一地点、同一时间的人们身上的人性。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 The power of the classroom is rooted in the humanity of the people gathered in the same place, at the same time ↔It lacks humanity Technology, no matter how advanced, should simply be a tool of a good teacher ↔ It lacks humanity 预判得出原因为「技术缺乏人性」，选项It lacks humanity使用与原文同一个抽象名词 humanity，是同根词的正反极性替换，匹配度最高。 B) 与原文相反 原文未提及技术「尚不成熟」（still immature）；作者用no matter how advanced 反而承认了技术可以非常先进，否定的是技术的本质属性（非人性），不是技术的发展 阶段。 C) 无中生有 原文没有任何关于「技术无法追踪学生成长」的表述；track students' growth这一说法 是作者批评教育技术时未涉及的另一个方向。 D) 以偏概全 It cannot cater to personal needs即「不能满足个性化需求」听起来很对，且与第三 段online education does not allow a teacher to keep a struggling student after class and offer help有局部对应，但题目55题问的是技术为何不能取代好教师，根本原 因应回末段P4的humanity，而不是第三段的某个具体功能局限；选It cannot cater to personal needs是把局部理由当作根本理由，犯以偏概全的错误。这是本题最有迷惑性 的干扰项。

items.title: 2022年9月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2022年9月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Academic dishonesty is nothing new. As long as there have been homework assignments and tests, there have been cheaters. The way that cheating looks has changed over time, though, particularly now that technology has made it easier than ever. A study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics interviewed 23,000 high school students and asked them a variety of questions about academic ethics. Of the teens surveyed, 51 percent said that they had knowingly cheated at some point on an exam but that they did not feel uneasy about the behavior. A Common Sense Media survey found that 35 percent of students had cheated via smartphone, though the parents surveyed in that particular study did not believe their kids had ever cheated. In many cases, students did not realize that strategies like looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating at all.

P2 In today's classrooms, students who cheat are rarely caught. There are no formulas written on the insides of hands or students looking across the aisle, or whispering answers to their classmates. Today's students use smartphones, tablets or even in-class computers to aid their cheating attempts and leave no trace of their crimes. Since cheating through technology is not listed specifically as being against the rules in many school policies, students do not view the actions as unethical.

P3 The technology is being adopted so quickly that school districts cannot adequately keep up with cheating policies, or even awareness campaigns that alert students to the problem with using technology to find answers in a certain way. From a young age, students learn that answers exist conveniently at their fingertips through search engines and expert websites.

P4 Schools must develop anti-cheating policies that include technology and these policies must be updated consistently. Teachers must stay on guard when it comes to what their students are doing in classrooms and how technology could be playing a negative role in the learning process. Parents must also talk to their kids about the appropriate ways to find academic answers and alert them to unethical behaviours that may seem innocent in their own eyes.

questions.q: What do we learn from the study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics?
options: Over half of the students interviewed were unaware they were cheating.
Cheating was becoming a way of life for a majority of high school teens.
More than half of the interviewees felt no sense of guilt over cheating.
Cheating was getting more and more difficult for high school students.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the study 是对某项具体研究内容的客观转述提问,不涉及推断、主 旨、态度,属于针对单一信息源的细节题。

【拆句】结构是 What do we learn from the study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics?——主 干是 what do we learn from + 名词短语,介词短语 by the Josephson Institute of Ethics 修饰 the study,语序简单、无陷阱。 46. What do we learn from the study by the Josephson Institute of Ethics? A) Over half of the students interviewed were unaware they were cheating. B) Cheating was becoming a way of life for a majority of high school teens. C) More than half of the interviewees felt no sense of guilt over cheating. D) Cheating was getting more and more difficult for high school students.

【定位】Of the teens surveyed, 51 percent said that they had knowingly cheated at some point on an exam but that they did not feel uneasy about the behavior. 在受访的青少年中,51% 的人说他们曾在某次考试中明知故犯地作弊,但对这种行为并不感到 不安。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Over half of the students interviewed were unaware they were cheating. 说"过半 受访者不知道自己在作弊",但定位句明明用了 knowingly,与之相反;"不知情作弊"是后文 Common Sense Media 部分讨论的内容,被偷换到本题。 B) 过度推断 Cheating was becoming a way of life for a majority of high school teens. 把"曾在 某次考试作弊"升级为"成为生活方式",程度被无端拔高;定位句只说"曾经作弊过",并未 说"已成为日常"。 C) ✓ 正确 51 percent said that they had knowingly cheated ↔More than half of the interviewees did not feel uneasy about the behavior ↔felt no sense of guilt over cheating More than half of the interviewees felt no sense of guilt over cheating. 把"过 半"和"无负罪感"同时对上定位句,正是细节题最干净的同义替换。 D) 与原文相反 Cheating was getting more and more difficult for high school students. 说作弊 变得越来越难,但全文核心论点是 technology has made it easier than ever,方向完全 相反。 Common Sense Media 的调查揭示了什么? A) 大多数家长倾向于过度保护自己的孩子。 B) 许多学生在不知情的情况下作弊。 C) 学生迫切需要道德教育。 D) 家长和孩子对作弊的看法存在冲突。

questions.q: What did the Common Sense Media survey reveal?
options: Most parents tended to overprotect their children.
Many students committed cheating unknowingly.
Students were in urgent need of ethical education.
Parents and kids had conflicting ideas over cheating.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the Common Sense Media survey reveal? 同样指向某项具体调查的客观发现, 属于客观转述,不涉态度/推断。

【拆句】What did the Common Sense Media survey reveal?——主谓宾极简单,reveal 在此当及 物动词"揭示",一个主语一个宾语,无修饰、无从句。 47. What did the Common Sense Media survey reveal? A) Most parents tended to overprotect their children. B) Many students committed cheating unknowingly. C) Students were in urgent need of ethical education. D) Parents and kids had conflicting ideas over cheating.

【定位】A Common Sense Media survey found that 35 percent of students had cheated via smartphone, though the parents surveyed in that particular study did not believe their kids had ever cheated. In many cases, students did not realize that strategies like looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating at all. Common Sense Media 的一项调查发现 35% 的学生曾用智能手机作弊,尽管该项调查中受 访的家长并不相信自己的孩子曾经作弊。很多情况下,学生根本没意识到用手机查答案这种做 法其实就是作弊。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Most parents tended to overprotect their children. 中 overprotect(过度保护)是原 文里完全没出现的概念,文中只说家长 did not believe their kids had ever cheated(不 相信孩子作过弊),这是"不知情"而非"过度保护"。 B) ✓ 正确 students did not realize that strategies like looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating at all ↔Many students committed cheating unknowingly looking up answers on a smartphone were actually cheating ↔committed cheating Many students committed cheating unknowingly. 同时覆盖"作弊"和"不自知"两个要 点,正是定位句最干净的同义替换。 C) 答非所问 Students were in urgent need of ethical education. 是"应该"层面的建议(末段才有类 似主张),并非该调查所揭示的事实;47 题问的是 reveal,要求是事实,不是该做什么。 D) 偷换概念 Parents and kids had conflicting ideas over cheating. 把家长不知情与学生不自知放 在一起描述为"观念冲突",但原文里两方都不认为自己/孩子在作弊,实际上是"双方都没认 识到",不是冲突,而是同向盲区。 为什么现在学生很少因作弊被抓? A) 他们把公式抄在手掌上。 B) 他们互相帮助掩盖自己的行为。 C) 他们不断改变作弊方式。 D) 他们利用现代技术。

questions.q: Why do students rarely get caught cheating nowadays?
options: They copy formulas on their palms.
They help each other to cover up their acts.
They keep changing their ways of cheating.
They make use of modern technology.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why do students rarely get caught cheating nowadays? 用 Why 问原因,但原因往往在 原文同一句或紧邻句给出,不需多步推理,仍属细节定位。 48. Why do students rarely get caught cheating nowadays? A) They copy formulas on their palms. B) They help each other to cover up their acts. C) They keep changing their ways of cheating. D) They make use of modern technology.

【拆句】Why do students rarely get caught cheating nowadays?——副词 rarely 是隐性否 定"很少/几乎不",get caught doing 是"被抓到正在做某事"的固定结构,nowadays 限定时 间。基础薄弱考生注意:rarely 不是"罕见"的名词,而是"很少"的副词。

【定位】In today's classrooms, students who cheat are rarely caught. There are no formulas written on the insides of hands or students looking across the aisle, or whispering answers to their classmates. Today's students use smartphones, tablets or even in-class computers to aid their cheating attempts and leave no trace of their crimes. 在今天的教室里,作弊的学生很少被抓到。没人再在手心写公式、隔着过道偷看,或者向同学 小声报答案。今天的学生用智能手机、平板,甚至课堂电脑辅助作弊,不留任何痕迹。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 They copy formulas on their palms. 实际上正是原文用 no formulas written on the insides of hands 否定掉的旧做法,选项把这条已经被否定的现象当成"现在"还在做,方向 恰好反了。 B) 无中生有 They help each other to cover up their acts. 中 cover up(掩盖)的描述在原文里完全 没有;原文只说技术让作弊"不留痕迹",并未说学生互相帮忙打掩护。 C) 偷换概念 They keep changing their ways of cheating. 描述"学生不断改变作弊方式",但原文 是"作弊方式随时代而变"——主语是"作弊方式",不是"学生";而且 keep changing 强调 持续变化,原文只比较了"以前 vs 现在"两个时点。 D) ✓ 正确 use smartphones, tablets or even in-class computers ↔They make use of modern technology to aid their cheating attempts ↔make use of They make use of modern technology. 用 modern technology 一词覆盖原文三种设 备,且对应了 to aid their cheating attempts 的"借助"语义,是干净的概括化替换。 作者认为学校应该如何应对作弊? A) 更新反作弊政策使其跟上时代。 B) 不断改革考试方法。 C) 利用最新技术。 D) 提醒家长注意孩子的行为。

questions.q: What does the author think schools should do to tackle cheating?
options: Bring policies against cheating up to date.
Reform their exam methods constantly.
Take advantage of the latest technologies.
Alert parents to their children's behaviour.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think schools should do 问的是作者对学校的具体建议,原文末段 是直接的祈使/must 句,属客观陈述,不是推断。 49. What does the author think schools should do to tackle cheating? A) Bring policies against cheating up to date. B) Reform their exam methods constantly. C) Take advantage of the latest technologies. D) Alert parents to their children's behaviour.

【拆句】What does the author think schools should do to tackle cheating?——主句 What does the author think,后接宾语从句 schools should do,不定式 to tackle cheating 作目 的状语,逻辑就是"作者认为学校该做什么来解决作弊"。

【定位】Schools must develop anti-cheating policies that include technology and these policies must be updated consistently. 学校必须制定包含科技因素的反作弊政策,并且这些政策必须不断更新。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 these policies must be updated consistently ↔Bring policies against cheating up to date anti-cheating policies ↔policies against cheating Bring policies against cheating up to date. 把"持续更新政策"这一并列要点提炼 出来,正命中原文 must be updated consistently;且 against cheating 等值替换 anti-cheating。 B) 无中生有 Reform their exam methods constantly. 提到"改革考试方式",但原文末段对学校的建 议只涉及"制定/更新政策",未谈考试方式的改革。 C) 与原文相反 Take advantage of the latest technologies. 让学校利用最新技术(去解决作弊),但原文 里技术是问题源——students learn that answers exist conveniently at their fingertips through search engines——学校要做的是把技术纳入政策约束,而非利用技 术解决问题。 D) 张冠李戴 Alert parents to their children's behaviour. 让学校去提醒家长,但原文末段对学 校只字未提家长这件事;"alert"一词原文里出现在家长对孩子的位置 alert them to unethical behaviours。 作者建议教师在课堂上做什么? A) 防止学生过度使用电子设备。 B) 制定更有效的反作弊策略。 C) 寻找更多方法遏制学生的不道德行为。 D) 防范学生滥用技术。

questions.q: What does the author suggest teachers do in the classroom?
options: Prevent students from overusing electronic devices.
Develop more effective anti-cheating strategies.
Find more ways to curb students' unethical acts.
Guard against students' misuse of technology.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest teachers do in the classroom? 仍是对原文一句建议句的 转述,无推断需求,属细节题。 50. What does the author suggest teachers do in the classroom? A) Prevent students from overusing electronic devices. B) Develop more effective anti-cheating strategies. C) Find more ways to curb students' unethical acts. D) Guard against students' misuse of technology.

【拆句】What does the author suggest teachers do in the classroom?——suggest 后接省略 that 的宾语从句 teachers (should) do,基础薄弱考生注意:suggest 后从句的 should 常省 略,do 是动词原形而不是名词。

【定位】Teachers must stay on guard when it comes to what their students are doing in classrooms and how technology could be playing a negative role in the learning process. 老师必须时刻警惕——既要警惕学生在课堂里都在做什么,也要警惕科技可能在学习过程中 扮演的负面角色。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Prevent students from overusing electronic devices. 把"科技扮演负面角色"窄化为 单一的"过度使用电子设备";原文要警惕的核心不是"用得太多",而是"用得不当"(作弊)。 B) 张冠李戴 Develop more effective anti-cheating strategies. 让老师去"制定更有效的反作弊策 略",但末段把"develop policies"的任务给了 schools,老师只是"stay on guard"。 C) 过度推断 Find more ways to curb students' unethical acts. 让老师"找出更多办法去遏制不道德 行为",但原文里老师的动作只是"警惕",并未要求老师去找新办法或主动出击。 D) ✓ 正确 Teachers must stay on guard ↔Guard against how technology could be playing a negative role in the learning process ↔ students' misuse of technology Guard against students' misuse of technology. 把"警惕"与"科技的负面作用"两块拼 成一个干净的动宾结构,正命中原文要点。

items.title: 2022年9月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2022年9月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Remote work is about more than just working from home—it means working differently. Organizations should reconsider the appropriateness of their performance evaluation procedures in light of the shift to remote work. This requires a fundamental rethinking of what organizations expect from employees and what companies would look for in a model employee in a remote work context.

P2 It is likely that the "first to arrive and last to leave" mentality is no longer relevant, but should be replaced by a regard for the quality of an employee's contribution to the organization. This means that work should be measured in terms of the quality of the work, not just the quality of the process. As remote work is largely unobservable to supervisors, employers need to think about how they can objectively measure the quality of work in a way that is consistent for employees of similar rank.

P3 Focusing on output alone can have unintended consequences. Employers should think instead about the values and soft skills they want to emphasize in a remote work environment. Qualities like flexibility and the ability to work under minimal supervision might become critical.

P4 Much has been written about the importance of timely feedback. In the context of a global pandemic(大流行病), firms may want to provide additional support to employees by providing more frequent communication. This allows managers to both keep an eye on struggling employees and provide ongoing feedback on how employees are adapting to their new work environment.

P5 Compensation also needs to be revisited. The purpose of performance evaluation is ultimately to determine how to reward employees for their work. This means that pay structures need to adapt to the reality of working from home. However, organizations also need to be honest with employees about the financial impact of COVID-19.

P6 For organizations that have struggled to keep the lights on due to the pandemic, this might mean thinking of non-financial ways to reward employees, like unpaid time off or flexible work schedules. Employers can also consider how to bundle different types of compensation to help employees cope with their unique situations.

questions.q: What does the author say companies should do in the context of remote work?
options: Reform performance evaluation.
Rethink the organizational fundamentals.
Reexamine its effects on employees' behaviors.
Reflect on its differences from working in the office.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say companies should do 在问作者具体让公司做什么，落点是文 中明示的一条做法，没有 infer / imply / mainly about 之类的字眼，因此走常规定位路径 即可。

【拆句】题干主干是 What does the author say companies should do，what 既是 say 的宾语从 句中 do 的宾语，也是整句的疑问焦点；句尾 in the context of remote work 是介词短语 状语，限定背景。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What does the author say companies should do in the context of remote work? A) Reform performance evaluation. B) Rethink the organizational fundamentals. C) Reexamine its effects on employees' behaviors. D) Reflect on its differences from working in the office.

【定位】Organizations should reconsider the appropriateness of their performance evaluation procedures in light of the shift to remote work. 组织应当鉴于向远程办公的转变，重新审视其绩效评估程序是否仍然适当。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 reconsider the appropriateness of their performance evaluation procedures ↔ Reform performance evaluation Reform performance evaluation 既保留了 "重新审视"（reform）的动作，也保留了 "绩效评估"（performance evaluation）的对象，完全覆盖预判语义。 B) 偷换概念 Rethink the organizational fundamentals 把原文的 "绩效评估制度" 偷换成 "组织根 本"；原文虽提 a fundamental rethinking of what organizations expect from employees，但 fundamental 在原文是修饰 rethinking 的副词性形容词，并非要 "重 审组织根本" 这一对象。 C) 无中生有 Reexamine its effects on employees' behaviors 谈的是 "重新审视远程办公对员工行 为的影响"，原文从未谈论 "对员工行为的影响" 这一对象，只谈对评估制度的影响。 D) 答非所问 Reflect on its differences from working in the office 说的是 "反思远程办公与在办公 室办公的差异"，仅对应原文铺垫句 Remote work is about more than just working from home—it means working differently，没有触及作者真正提出的 "重审绩效评 估" 这一行动建议。 在评估员工远程工作时应优先考虑什么？ A) 他们的产出数量 B) 他们的工作时长 C) 他们的贡献质量 D) 他们工作时间表的灵活性

questions.q: What should be prioritized in assessing employees' remote work?
options: The quantity of their output.
The length of their work time.
The quality of their contribution.
The flexibility of their work schedules.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What should be prioritized 问 "什么应被优先考虑"，问的是一个具体的优先项；无 推断信号，原文必有明示。

【拆句】题干为 What should be prioritized in assessing employees' remote work：被动语态 should be prioritized，主语 what 是被优先项；in V-ing 短语作状语，标明范围。结构直 白，无陷阱。 52. What should be prioritized in assessing employees' remote work? A) The quantity of their output. B) The length of their work time. C) The quality of their contribution. D) The flexibility of their work schedules.

【定位】It is likely that the "first to arrive and last to leave" mentality is no longer relevant, but should be replaced by a regard for the quality of an employee's contribution to the organization. "早到晚走" 的心态很可能已不再适用，应该被对员工对组织所作贡献的质量的看重所取代。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 The quantity of their output 关心的是 "产出的数量"，与原文 the quality of an employee's contribution 中的 quality 形成数 vs 质的直接对立；第三段 Focusing on output alone can have unintended consequences 也明确反对单看产出。 B) 与原文相反 The length of their work time 即 "工作时长"，恰恰是原文 the "first to arrive and last to leave" mentality 所代表的旧心态，被作者明确判为 "no longer relevant"。 C) ✓ 正确 the quality of an employee's contribution to the organization ↔ The quality of their contribution The quality of their contribution 把 but 之后的新标准短语几乎原样搬过来，完全等于 预判结果。 D) 张冠李戴 The flexibility of their work schedules 谈 "工作时间安排的弹性"，对应的是第六段 flexible work schedules，那里讨论的是 "补偿" 而非 "评估优先项"，被嫁接到了第 52 题。 在远程工作背景下，员工的什么素质最为重要？ A) 产出高质量工作的能力 B) 最大化工作效率的能力 C) 及时完成任务的能力 D) 在最少监督下工作的能力

questions.q: What quality in the employees would be of great importance in a remote work context?
options: The ability to produce quality work.
The ability to maximize work efficiency.
The ability to finish tasks in a timely manner.
The ability to work with the least supervision.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What quality ... would be of great importance 问的是一项被作者点名为重要的素 质，原文必有明示项。

【拆句】题干主干 What quality in the employees would be of great importance in a remote work context：what 修饰 quality，构成疑问焦点；in the employees 与 in a remote work context 都是 in 短语作定语 / 状语；would be 是表 "一般陈述" 的虚拟语气。无 陷阱。 53. What quality in the employees would be of great importance in a remote work context? A) The ability to produce quality work. B) The ability to maximize work efficiency. C) The ability to finish tasks in a timely manner. D) The ability to work with the least supervision.

【定位】Qualities like flexibility and the ability to work under minimal supervision might become critical. 诸如灵活性以及在极少督导下工作的能力之类的素质可能会变得至关重要。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 The ability to produce quality work 谈 "产出高质量工作"，回到的是第二段 the quality of the work，与第 52 题答案重合；第三段开头 Focusing on output alone can have unintended consequences 已明确不再单看产出。 B) 无中生有 The ability to maximize work efficiency 提出 "工作效率最大化"，原文从未出现 efficiency 或与之对应的概念；远程办公段也未谈效率优化。 C) 张冠李戴 The ability to finish tasks in a timely manner 谈 "按时完成任务"，把第四段的 timely feedback 嫁接到第三段；原文谈的是反馈要及时，并非要求员工按时交付。 D) ✓ 正确 the ability to work under minimal supervision ↔ The ability to work with the least supervision The ability to work with the least supervision 与预判 "在极少督导下工作的能力" 在 动词、对象、形容词强度上一一对应。 为什么在疫情期间公司提供及时反馈很重要？ A) 以一致的方式评估级别相近的员工 B) 密切关注那些表现不佳的员工 C) 帮助有需要的员工适应新的工作环境 D) 与远离办公室的员工保持联系

questions.q: Why is it important for firms to provide timely feedback during the pandemic?
options: To evaluate their employees of similar rank in a consistent way.
To keep a watchful eye on those employees who perform poorly.
To help employees in need adapt to the new work environment.
To maintain connections with their employees away from office.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why is it important for firms to provide timely feedback 问 "为何及时反馈很重 要"，原文必然存在与之对应的 "to do / so that / in order to" 类目的句。

【拆句】题干 Why is it important for firms to provide timely feedback during the pandemic： 句型 "why is it important for sb to do sth"，it 是形式主语、to provide 是真正主语； during the pandemic 介词短语作状语限定时间。无陷阱。

【定位】This allows managers to both keep an eye on struggling employees and provide ongoing feedback on how employees are adapting to their new work environment. 这样做既能让管理者关注陷入困境的员工，又能持续就员工如何适应新的工作环境提供 反馈。 54. Why is it important for firms to provide timely feedback during the pandemic? A) To evaluate their employees of similar rank in a consistent way. B) To keep a watchful eye on those employees who perform poorly. C) To help employees in need adapt to the new work environment. D) To maintain connections with their employees away from office.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 To evaluate their employees of similar rank in a consistent way 谈 "以一致方式评 估同级员工"，对应的是第二段 in a way that is consistent for employees of similar rank，那里讲的是绩效度量、不是反馈目的。 B) 以偏概全 To keep a watchful eye on those employees who perform poorly 只对应原文 keep an eye on struggling employees 这一半目的，遗漏了 provide ongoing feedback on how employees are adapting；而且 perform poorly 把中性词 struggling 偷换成 了带负面评价的 "表现差劲"。 C) ✓ 正确 provide ongoing feedback on how employees are adapting to their new work environment ↔ To help employees in need adapt to the new work environment keep an eye on struggling employees ↔employees in need To help employees in need adapt to the new work environment 同时命中原文目的 中的两个核心元素——struggling employees（in need）与 adapting to their new work environment（adapt to the new work environment）。 D) 无中生有 To maintain connections with their employees away from office 谈 "维持与异地员 工的联系"，原文从未把 timely feedback 的目的描述为 "维持联系"，连 connection 一 词都没出现。 作者对经历疫情财务影响的雇主有什么建议？ A) 敦促员工适应新形势 B) 以非常规方式奖励员工 C) 识别贡献甚微的员工 D) 允许员工寻找兼职工作

questions.q: What is the author's suggestion to employers who experience the financial impact of the pandemic?
options: Urging their employees to adapt to the new situation.
Rewarding their employees in unconventional ways.
Identifying employees who make little contribution.
Allowing their employees to look for part-time jobs.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the author's suggestion 问一条明示的建议，落点具体，无推断信号词。

【拆句】题干 What is the author's suggestion to employers who experience the financial impact of the pandemic：主干 "What is the author's suggestion"，to employers 是 suggestion 的对象状语，who 引导定语从句修饰 employers。结构略长但逻辑清晰，无 陷阱。 55. What is the author's suggestion to employers who experience the financial impact of the pandemic? A) Urging their employees to adapt to the new situation. B) Rewarding their employees in unconventional ways. C) Identifying employees who make little contribution. D) Allowing their employees to look for part-time jobs.

【定位】For organizations that have struggled to keep the lights on due to the pandemic, this might mean thinking of non-financial ways to reward employees, like unpaid time off or flexible work schedules. 对于那些因疫情挣扎着维持运营的组织而言，这或许意味着要考虑用非财务的方式来奖励员 工，比如无薪假期或弹性工作安排。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Urging their employees to adapt to the new situation 把建议的发出对象与动作都改 了：原文要求雇主 "改用非金钱奖励"，而本项变成 "催促员工适应新形势"。adapt to the new situation 又把 adapting to their new work environment 拼贴过来。 B) ✓ 正确 non-financial ways to reward employees ↔ Rewarding their employees in unconventional ways Rewarding their employees in unconventional ways 既保留了原文的核心动作 reward，又把 non-financial 抽象到 unconventional，与预判 "用非金钱 / 非常规方式 奖励员工" 完全合拍。 C) 无中生有 Identifying employees who make little contribution 谈 "识别低贡献员工"，原文从 未提出在疫情下要 "挑出低贡献员工" 这种建议；contribution 一词只在第二段衡量标准 中出现，与第六段建议无关。 D) 过度推断 Allowing their employees to look for part-time jobs 谈 "允许员工找兼职"，原文虽 提到 unpaid time off or flexible work schedules，但没有任何 "找兼职" 的建议；二 者不可等同。

items.title: 2022年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2022年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 To write his 2010 book, The 5-Factor World Diet, nutritionist Harley Pasternak traveled to the healthiest countries around the world to learn more about what made their meals extra nourishing.

P2 He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. Pasternak also came away with some valuable observations about how different the North American way of life was, compared with many other countries.

P3 For starters, Americans eat much bigger portions than people in other countries. "We don't prioritize eating seasonally or locally, and we also add lots of salt, sugar and thickening agents to our foods," explained Pasternak. Contrast that to the healthy Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets listed in Pasternak's book. They all seem to stick to the ethos(特质) of regional, seasonal produce.

P4 For example, a traditional Mediterranean diet includes fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts and olive oil as the main components of nutritional intake. Fish, chicken and red wine make moderate appearances, while red meat, salt and sugar are used much less often. The benefits of a traditional Mediterranean diet have been studied since the 1970s, and researchers have found that living that olive oil life can help people lose weight, lower their heart disease risk and reverse diabetes.

P5 Most other healthy eating cultures also make meals an event—say, multiple courses around the family table, or a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch—as opposed to hastily wolfing down handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink and calling it dinner.

P6 Each of the healthy eating cultures has its own unique feature. But Pasternak did take note of one unifying factor in all of the healthy societies he observed. "The only overlapping feature in most of these healthy countries is that they all walk way more than the average American," said Pasternak, "So really, regardless of what you're eating, if someone's walking four miles more than you each day, they're going to be a lot thinner and live a lot longer than you."

questions.q: What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods?
options: Variety.
Flavor.
Color.
Naturalness.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods? 是 what 直接询问客观特征，没 有 infer/suggest/imply 之类的推断信号，要的就是原文写明的事实。

【拆句】题干 What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods? 是标准的 what 主语疑问句： what 作主语，characterizes 作谓语，Japanese and Chinese foods 是宾语，结构平铺直 叙，无陷阱。 46. What characterizes Japanese and Chinese foods? A) Variety. B) Flavor. C) Color. D) Naturalness.

【定位】He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. 他注意到日本人吃种类繁多的海藻，中国人则努力让每餐都包含至少五种不同的颜色。
