【选项】A) ✓ 正确 a wonderful variety of seaweeds ↔Variety at least five different colors in every meal ↔Variety 预判核心是"多样性"，Variety 既能覆盖 variety of seaweeds，也能覆盖 five different colors，是把两条并列事实的最大公约数提炼出来的上位词，与预判一致。 B) 无中生有 定位句 He noted that Japanese people ate a wonderful variety of seaweeds, and that Chinese people tried to include at least five different colors in every meal. 通 篇讲海藻种类和颜色，没有任何 flavor/taste 的描述；选项 Flavor 在原文里没有对应。 C) 以偏概全 选项 Color 只对应 at least five different colors in every meal 这一半，根本不能解释 a wonderful variety of seaweeds——日本人吃海藻种类多与颜色无关；以局部冒充 整体。 D) 无中生有 Naturalness 意为"天然性、未加工"，原文定位句没有 natural/unprocessed/raw 之类 的词；海藻和颜色多样不等于"自然"。 美国人在饮食方式上的典型特点是什么? A) 他们强调营养。 B) 他们往往吃得相当多。 C) 他们优先考虑便利性。 D) 他们在意味道。

questions.q: What is typical of Americans in the way of eating?
options: They emphasize nutrition.
They tend to eat quite a lot.
They prioritize convenience.
They care about flavors.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is typical of Americans in the way of eating? 用 typical 直接问"典型"，要求 原文里被作者明确点出的美国人吃饭特征。

【拆句】题干主干是 what is typical of Americans，in the way of eating 是修饰 typical 的范围介 词短语；结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】For starters, Americans eat much bigger portions than people in other countries. 首先，美国人吃的分量比其他国家的人要大得多。 47. What is typical of Americans in the way of eating? A) They emphasize nutrition. B) They tend to eat quite a lot. C) They prioritize convenience. D) They care about flavors.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文 We don't prioritize eating seasonally or locally, and we also add lots of salt, sugar and thickening agents to our foods 说的是美国人"不"重视当季当地、还要加 大量盐糖增稠剂——明显是不健康、不重营养的做法，emphasize nutrition 与原文方 向相反。 B) ✓ 正确 eat much bigger portions ↔tend to eat quite a lot than people in other countries ↔tend to 预判核心是"美国人吃得多"，They tend to eat quite a lot. 把定位句的数量比较结论直 接保留下来，没做引申，与预判完全一致。 C) 无中生有 原文讲的是分量大、不重视当季当地、爱加盐糖——没出现 convenience/quick/fast/easy 等"便利"语义的词；选项 prioritize convenience 在原 文中无依据。 D) 无中生有 原文谈份量、当季当地、盐糖增稠剂，未涉及 flavor/taste；care about flavors 在原文 中没有对应表述。 地中海、北欧和冲绳饮食的特征是什么? A) 水果和蔬菜。 B) 橄榄油和红酒。 C) 时令本地农产品。 D) 未加工的食材。

questions.q: What features are in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets?
options: Fruits and vegetables.
Olive oil and red wine.
Seasonal local produce.
Unprocessed ingredients.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What features are in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets? 直接询问几种 饮食"具备什么特征"，答案应是原文明写的共同特征。

【拆句】题干 What features are in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets?：what features 作主语、are 系动词、in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets 是表语介 词短语，把范围限定在这三种饮食里；结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】Contrast that to the healthy Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets listed in Pasternak's book. They all seem to stick to the ethos(特质) of regional, seasonal produce. 把这一点（指美国人的饮食习惯）与 Pasternak 书中列出的健康的地中海、北欧和冲绳饮食 对比一下。它们似乎都坚守着"当地、当季食材"这一特质。 48. What features are in Mediterranean, Nordic and Okinawan diets? A) Fruits and vegetables. B) Olive oil and red wine. C) Seasonal local produce. D) Unprocessed ingredients.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 fruits, vegetables 出现在 P4 段对地中海饮食的展开里；但题目问的是三种饮食的共有 特征，Fruits and vegetables 只是地中海饮食的成分，不能说北欧和冲绳饮食也以这两 样为主——选项错把局部例证当全局共性。 B) 以偏概全 olive oil 与 red wine 同样出现在 P4 段对地中海饮食的描写里，是地中海饮食的特色， 但不是北欧和冲绳饮食的特征；选项把地中海饮食的标志当成三地共同点。 C) ✓ 正确 regional, seasonal produce ↔Seasonal local produce 预判核心"当地、当季、食材"三层在 Seasonal local produce 中一一对应，无遗漏；这 是细节题正确项最干净的样子——预判几个要素，选项几乎逐词对接。 D) 无中生有 原文中谈到三地饮食的共同点只有 regional, seasonal produce（当地当季食材），并 未出现 unprocessed/raw/whole 之类强调"未加工"的语义；Unprocessed ingredients 是凭健康饮食的常识印象生造的特征。 大多数健康饮食文化中的人们有什么共同点? A) 他们让全家人在餐桌旁用餐。 B) 他们定时定点地进餐。 C) 他们早餐食用大量谷物。 D) 他们非常重视用餐。

questions.q: What do people in most healthy eating cultures have in common?
options: They get the whole family to eat at a table.
They eat their meals regularly and punctually.
They consume plenty of cereal for breakfast.
They attach great importance to their meals.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do people in most healthy eating cultures have in common? 直问"共同之 处"，不含推断信号词，只要找原文的归纳句即可。

【拆句】题干 What do people in most healthy eating cultures have in common?：what 作 have 的宾语前置，主语是 people in most healthy eating cultures；have…in common 是固定搭配"有共同点"，结构无陷阱。

【定位】Most other healthy eating cultures also make meals an event—say, multiple courses around the family table, or a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch—as opposed to hastily wolfing down handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink and calling it dinner. 大多数其他健康饮食文化都把吃饭当作一件"大事"——例如全家围桌吃几道菜，或者午餐时 悠悠喝上一两杯红酒——而不是匆匆抓把麦片站在水槽边解决一顿。 49. What do people in most healthy eating cultures have in common? A) They get the whole family to eat at a table. B) They eat their meals regularly and punctually. C) They consume plenty of cereal for breakfast. D) They attach great importance to their meals.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 get the whole family to eat at a table 只对应 multiple courses around the family table 这一个例子，没覆盖另一例 a glass or two of red wine at a long lunch，更没覆 盖"重视用餐"这个主旨；以一个例子冒充整段共性。 B) 无中生有 原文 P5 只说 long lunch（漫长的午餐），完全没有 regularly/punctually/on time 这类"规律/守时"的语义；选项 eat their meals regularly and punctually 在原文里无 对应。 C) 与原文相反 原文中 handfuls of cereal above the kitchen sink 是用来作"反例"的——讽刺美国人 草率吃法的——而选项 consume plenty of cereal for breakfast 反而把这条反例当成 健康文化的优点，方向南辕北辙。 D) ✓ 正确 make meals an event ↔attach great importance to their meals 预判核心"重视用餐"与 attach great importance to their meals 字字对应；同时这 一表达覆盖了原文后面三个例证（围桌、几道菜、长午餐），是所有例证背后的统一 主旨。 与普通美国人相比,健康社会中的人们___________。 A) 每天至少步行4英里 B) 步行明显更多 C) 更注重体型 D) 食用多得多的有机食品

questions.q: Compared with the average American, people in healthy societies ___________.
options: walk at least 4 miles a day
do considerably more walking
pay more attention to body shape
consume a lot more organic food
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Compared with the average American, people in healthy societies ___________. 是补全句、内容来自原文的事实性对比陈述，不要求做推断，按细节题走。

【拆句】题干 Compared with the average American, people in healthy societies ___________. 是不完整陈述句：Compared with the average American 是过去分词短语作状语，逻 辑主语是后面的 people in healthy societies；选项是句子谓语的延续，需保证主谓搭配 自然。

【定位】The only overlapping feature in most of these healthy countries is that they all walk way more than the average American. 这些健康国家唯一的共同特征是：他们走路都远远多于普通美国人。 50. Compared with the average American, people in healthy societies ___________. A) walk at least 4 miles a day B) do considerably more walking C) pay more attention to body shape D) consume a lot more organic food

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文 if someone's walking four miles more than you each day 中的 four miles 是 Pasternak 的进一步举例性数字，且是"多走 4 英里"（每天比对方多 4 英里），不是"至 少走 4 英里"；选项 walk at least 4 miles a day 把"多走的差值"偷换成"日行的总数"， 并加了原文没有的 at least。 B) ✓ 正确 walk way more than the average American ↔do considerably more walking 预判核心"走路远多于美国人"被 do considerably more walking 完整保留——比较级 more、程度副词 considerably（= 原文 way）、活动 walking，三层信息一一对应。 C) 偷换概念 原文 they're going to be a lot thinner 是"会瘦很多"——这是走路多带来的结果，不 是健康社会的人"在意身材"这一主观倾向；选项 pay more attention to body shape 是把客观结果错读成主观态度。 D) 无中生有 整篇文章谈份量、海藻、五色、当地当季食材、用餐重视度、走路——通篇没出现 organic（有机的）这个词；选项 consume a lot more organic food 在原文中完全无 对应。

items.title: 2022年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2022年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Recognizing when a friend or colleague feels sad, angry or surprised is key to getting along with others. But a new study suggests that being sensitive to people's feelings may sometimes come with an extra dose of stress. This and other research challenge the prevailing view that emotional intelligence is uniformly beneficial to its bearer.

P2 In a study, psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt of the Frankfurt School of Finance and Management in Germany asked 166 male university students a series of questions to measure their emotional intelligence. For example, they showed the students photographs of people's faces and asked them to what extent feelings such as happiness or disgust were being expressed. The students then had to give job talks in front of judges who displayed serious facial expressions. The scientists measured concentrations of stress hormones in the students' saliva(唾液) before and after the talk.

P3 In students who were rated more emotionally intelligent, the stress measures increased more during the experiment and took longer to go back to baseline. The findings suggest that some people may be too emotionally clever for their own good, says Bechtoldt. "Sometimes you can be so good at something that it causes trouble," she notes.

P4 Indeed, the study adds to previous research hinting at a dark side of emotional intelligence. A study published in 2002 in Personality and Individual Differences suggested that emotionally perceptive people might be particularly influenced by feelings of depression and hopelessness. Furthermore, several studies have implied that emotional intelligence can be used to manipulate others for personal gains.

P5 More research is needed to see how exactly the relation between emotional intelligence and stress would play out in women and in people of different ages and education levels. Nevertheless, emotional intelligence is a useful skill to have, as long as you learn to also properly cope with emotions —both others' and your own, says Bechtoldt. For example, some sensitive individuals may assume responsibility for other people's sadness or anger, which ultimately stresses them out. Remember, as Bechtoldt says, "you are not responsible for how other people feel."

questions.q: What is the finding of the new study?
options: Emotional intelligence helps people get along with others.
Emotional intelligence is generally beneficial to its bearer.
People who are aware of others' feelings may experience more stress.
People who are emotionally stressed may have trouble making friends.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the finding of the new study?直接问研究的发现，没有 infer/imply/suggest 等 推断信号词，答案应能在原文中找到客观对应。

【拆句】Q51是一个简单 What is + 主语 + of 短语的疑问句，主干是the finding of the new study，of 引导的介宾短语限定 finding 的归属，无从句、无否定，结构平铺直叙，无 陷阱。 51. What is the finding of the new study? A) Emotional intelligence helps people get along with others. B) Emotional intelligence is generally beneficial to its bearer. C) People who are aware of others' feelings may experience more stress. D) People who are emotionally stressed may have trouble making friends.

【定位】But a new study suggests that being sensitive to people's feelings may sometimes come with an extra dose of stress. 但一项新研究指出，对他人情绪敏感，有时会带来额外的压力。

【选项】A) 答非所问 Emotional intelligence helps people get along with others.说的是「情商有助于与 人相处」，这是Recognizing when a friend or colleague feels sad, angry or surprised is key to getting along with others.这句旧常识，而不是题干问的the new study的发现。 B) 与原文相反 Emotional intelligence is generally beneficial to its bearer.恰恰是新研究要 challenge的主流观点，原文用This and other research challenge the prevailing view that emotional intelligence is uniformly beneficial to its bearer.明确反对它， 把它当 finding 是把靶子当结论。 C) ✓ 正确 being sensitive to people's feelings ↔People who are aware of others' feelings come with an extra dose of stress ↔may experience more stress 预判的「敏锐感知他人情绪的人会承受更多压力」与People who are aware of others' feelings may experience more stress.从主语到谓语完全对应，且程度词 sometimes 与 may 等值，无超译。 D) 无中生有 People who are emotionally stressed may have trouble making friends.说的是 「情绪压力大→交不到朋友」——原文谈的方向恰好相反：「敏锐感知情绪→压力更 大」，且原文根本没提「交不到朋友」。 心理学家Myriam Bechtoldt实验的目的是什么? A) 定义不同类型的人类情感。 B) 评估情感敏锐的影响。 C) 演示如何区分不同的情感。 D) 识别情商方面的性别差异。

questions.q: What was the purpose of psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt's experiment?
options: To define different types of human feelings.
To assess the impacts of being emotionally clever.
To demonstrate how to distinguish different feelings.
To identify gender differences in emotional intelligence.
questions.explain:
【判型】What was the purpose of psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt's experiment?问的是实验目 的，是可在原文中找到客观依据的事实信息，不是推断或主旨。

【拆句】Q52主干是What was the purpose ... experiment?，of 后面跟一长串名词同位修饰 psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt's experiment，结构是简单的 What + be + 主语，没有 从句和否定，无陷阱。 52. What was the purpose of psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt's experiment? A) To define different types of human feelings. B) To assess the impacts of being emotionally clever. C) To demonstrate how to distinguish different feelings. D) To identify gender differences in emotional intelligence.

【定位】In a study, psychologist Myriam Bechtoldt of the Frankfurt School of Finance and Management in Germany asked 166 male university students a series of questions to measure their emotional intelligence. 在一项研究中，德国法兰克福金融与管理学院的心理学家 Myriam Bechtoldt 向 166 名男 大学生提了一系列问题，以测量他们的情商。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 To define different types of human feelings.意为「定义不同种类的人类情绪」，但 原文they showed the students photographs of people's faces and asked them to what extent feelings such as happiness or disgust were being expressed.中「看脸 辨情绪」是测量情商的手段细节，不是研究目的。 B) ✓ 正确 to measure their emotional intelligence ↔To assess the impacts of being emotionally clever The findings suggest that some people may be too emotionally clever for their own good ↔ the impacts of being emotionally clever 定位句给出的是研究手段（测量情商加测压力激素），而P1与P3共同指明，这一手段服 务于「评估情商高带来的影响」这一目的，与B完全对应。 C) 无中生有 To demonstrate how to distinguish different feelings.意为「演示如何区分不同情 绪」，但实验是测量学生情商，不是教学生区分情绪；原文没有 demonstrate / teach 类动词。 D) 无中生有 To identify gender differences in emotional intelligence.说研究目的是识别性别差 异，但实验对象是166 male university students——全是男生，根本没设性别对照； 末段还提到More research is needed to see how exactly the relation between emotional intelligence and stress would play out in women——女性差异是「待研 究」，不是本研究的目的。 Myriam Bechtoldt的研究发现表明了什么? A) 情感敏锐度越高意味着生活中的麻烦越少。 B) 情商帮助人们在求职面试中取得成功。 C) 人们的心理健康与多种因素有关。 D) 人们可能因拥有高情商而遭受痛苦。

questions.q: What does the finding of Myriam Bechtoldt's study indicate?
options: Greater emotional cleverness means less trouble in one's life.
Emotional intelligence helps people succeed in job interviews.
People's psychological wellbeing is related to various factors.
People may suffer from having a high emotional intelligence
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the finding of Myriam Bechtoldt's study indicate?问的是研究结果所「表 明」的内容，原文有研究者亲口下的结论句作为依据，仍属细节题，不需要超出原文做 推断。

【拆句】Q53结构是 What does + 主语 + indicate？主语the finding of Myriam Bechtoldt's study由 of 介宾限定，全句是简单宾语从句式提问，无否定无比较，无陷阱。

【定位】The findings suggest that some people may be too emotionally clever for their own good, says Bechtoldt. 研究者 Bechtoldt 说，研究结果表明，有些人的情商可能高过头反害了自己。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Greater emotional cleverness means less trouble in one's life.说情商越高麻烦越 少，与原文Sometimes you can be so good at something that it causes trouble完 全相反。 B) 无中生有 Emotional intelligence helps people succeed in job interviews.说情商帮人在求职面 试中成功——但原文里give job talks in front of judges只是实验任务场景（求职演 讲），原文从未说情商高能让人面试成功；恰恰相反，情商高的人压力更大。 C) 答非所问 People's psychological wellbeing is related to various factors.「心理健康与多种因 素有关」在常识上无可指摘，但原文研究只讲情商与压力的关系，没有讨论「多种因 素」，是模糊化的万能选项。 D) ✓ 正确 some people may be too emotionally clever for their own good ↔ People may suffer from having a high emotional intelligence Sometimes you can be so good at something that it causes trouble ↔ suffer from having a high emotional intelligence 预判「情商高反受其害」与People may suffer from having a high emotional intelligence在主语、谓语、宾语三层完全咬合，且都保留 may 的不确定语气，是定位 句的标准同义改写。 从许多研究中我们对情商了解到什么? A) 患有抑郁症的人在情感上不成熟。 B) 看待生活消极面的人往往感到抑郁。 C) 有些人可能利用它并使自己受益。 D) 有些人可能缺乏它并容易被他人操纵。 54. What do we learn about emotional intelligence from a number of studies? A) People suffering from depression are emotionally immature. B) People who look at the dark side of life often feel depressed. C) Some people may take advantage of it and benefit themselves. D) Some people may lack it and are easily manipulated by others.

questions.q: What do we learn about emotional intelligence from a number of studies?
options: People suffering from depression are emotionally immature.
People who look at the dark side of life often feel depressed.
Some people may take advantage of it and benefit themselves.
Some people may lack it and are easily manipulated by others.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about emotional intelligence from a number of studies?问的是 「从多项研究我们得知什么」，对应原文综述段的事实罗列，不是推断或主旨。

【拆句】Q54主干是 What do we learn? 后接 about + 话题 + from + 来源两个介宾短语限定 learn 的范围；about 限定话题、from 限定信息来源，两个限定都不能丢，结构清晰、无 陷阱。

【定位】Furthermore, several studies have implied that emotional intelligence can be used to manipulate others for personal gains. 此外，多项研究还暗示，情商可被用来操纵他人以谋取私利。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 People suffering from depression are emotionally immature.说抑郁者情绪不成熟 ——但原文emotionally perceptive people might be particularly influenced by feelings of depression and hopelessness说的是「情绪敏锐者更易受抑郁影响」，主 语和因果都被改了。 B) 偷换概念 People who look at the dark side of life often feel depressed.说「看人生消极面的 人常抑郁」——这是日常常识，但原文谈的是「情绪敏锐者易受抑郁情绪影响」，主语 错配、因果也错。 C) ✓ 正确 emotional intelligence can be used to manipulate others for personal gains ↔ Some people may take advantage of it and benefit themselves 预判的「情商可被用来操纵他人谋私」与Some people may take advantage of it and benefit themselves在主语、动词短语、目的三段完全对位，且 may 与 can 都是表 「可能性」的弱情态，无超译。 D) 与原文相反 Some people may lack it and are easily manipulated by others.说「有些人缺乏情 商，因此易被他人操纵」——但原文谈的是「情商高的人可以操纵别人」，而不是「缺 情商的人被人操纵」，施事与受事正好反过来。 作者建议敏感的人做什么? A) 避免让自己承担他人的感受。 B) 摆脱对世俗事务的担忧。 C) 学会应对人们的负面情绪。 D) 帮助人们处理生活中的烦恼。 55. What does the author suggest sensitive individuals do? A) Avoid burdening themselves with others' feelings. B) Rid themselves of worries over worldly affairs. C) Learn to cope with people's negative feelings. D) Help people to deal with their troubles in life.

questions.q: What does the author suggest sensitive individuals do?
options: Avoid burdening themselves with others' feelings.
Rid themselves of worries over worldly affairs.
Learn to cope with people's negative feelings.
Help people to deal with their troubles in life.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest sensitive individuals do?问作者给敏感者的具体建议， 原文应有明示的建议句作为依据。

【拆句】Q55是 What does + 主语 + suggest + 宾语从句的疑问句；宾语从句省略 that，形式为 sensitive individuals do——主语 sensitive individuals + 动词原形 do，是 suggest sb. (should) do 的虚拟语气省略式，do 表「做（什么）」，对应选项里的动词短语。

【定位】For example, some sensitive individuals may assume responsibility for other people's sadness or anger, which ultimately stresses them out. Remember, as Bechtoldt says, "you are not responsible for how other people feel." 举例来说，一些敏感的人可能会替别人的悲伤或愤怒揽责任，结果反而把自己压垮。记住 Bechtoldt 的话：你不必为别人的感受负责。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 you are not responsible for how other people feel ↔ Avoid burdening themselves with others' feelings some sensitive individuals may assume responsibility for other people's sadness or anger, which ultimately stresses them out ↔burdening themselves with others' feelings 预判的「别替别人的情绪扛锅」与Avoid burdening themselves with others' feelings 在动词、宾语、隐含主语三层完全对位，且都保留「避免、不要」的建议口吻。 B) 无中生有 Rid themselves of worries over worldly affairs.说「摆脱对世俗琐事的忧虑」—— 但原文谈的是「别人的情绪」，不是「世俗琐事」；worldly affairs 在原文完全没有 对应。 C) 偷换概念 Learn to cope with people's negative feelings.建议敏感者去「应对他人的负面情 绪」——但原文you are not responsible for how other people feel给的建议恰恰相 反：「不必为别人感受负责」，根本不主张主动去处理别人的情绪。要注意原文确实有 learn to also properly cope with emotions—both others' and your own，但那是 给所有人的总建议、且强调「包括自己的」；针对 sensitive individuals 的针对性建议 是 not responsible 这一句。 D) 与原文相反 Help people to deal with their troubles in life.建议敏感者去「帮别人解决生活中的麻 烦」——这与作者的建议方向完全相反，作者明示you are not responsible for how other people feel。

items.title: 2022年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2022年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 We're eating more fish than ever these days. At around 20 kilograms per person global fish consumption is now more than twice what it was in the 1960s. What's really remarkable, though, is where that fish comes from.

P2 For the first time in human history, most of our aquatic(水产的) food now comes from farming rather than fishing.

P3 People ate around 73 million tonnes of farmed fish—just more than half of the volume of fish that humans consumed—in 2014. That's out of a total fish supply of 167 million tonnes; the remaining 20 million or so tonnes go into things like animal feed and medical products.

P4 To keep eating fish at the current rate, we're definitely going to need to keep aquaculture(水产养殖) developing. That's because the volume of fish caught in the wild has leveled off since the 1990s.

P5 Back in 1974, only 10% of marine fish stocks had been overfished. Now, more than three-tenths are. Only a tenth of our oceans' fish stocks could sustain heavier fishing than current levels.

P6 But while catchings at sea have suffered, fish-farming has been growing at a fast rate. A lot of that is coming from China, which produces 60% of the world's farmed fish. In fact, some 35 countries, including China, now produce more farmed than wild-caught fish.

P7 This shift toward aquaculture isn't just good for ensuring salmon(三文鱼) on your plate; it's also crucial to ensuring food security and sustainability. By 2050, the world will need to feed an estimated 9.7 billion people. They'll have to get their protein somewhere. However, raising cattle, pigs, and other land-based animals requires vast sums of grain and water. For example, pound for pound, beef requires 15 times more feed to raise than carp, a freshwater fish farmed all over Asia. That grain—and the water needed to grow it—could be consumed by people instead.

P8 However, aquaculture is no silver bullet. In some southeast Asian countries, shrimp farming does disastrous damage to marine ecosystems. Despite these problems, however, shrimp continues to be among the most popular sea foods worldwide.

questions.q: What does the author say is remarkable about the fish we eat?
options: They reproduce quickly.
They are mostly farmed.
They have become as important as grain.
They have a longer history than humans.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say is remarkable about the fish we eat? 用 say 引出作者 明确表态的内容，不是让考生自行推断。 46. What does the author say is remarkable about the fish we eat? A) They reproduce quickly. B) They are mostly farmed. C) They have become as important as grain. D) They have a longer history than humans.

【拆句】题干 What does the author say is remarkable about the fish we eat? 主干是 What does the author say，宾语从句省略了 that，从句里 is remarkable about the fish we eat 又内嵌一个省略 that 的定语从句 we eat修饰 fish。结构属常规嵌套，无陷阱。

【定位】For the first time in human history, most of our aquatic(水产的) food now comes from farming rather than fishing. 人类历史上第一次，我们大多数的水产食物来自养殖而非捕捞。

【选项】A) 无中生有 They reproduce quickly 涉及鱼的繁殖能力，原文从第 1 段到第 3 段只谈消费量与来 源，未出现任何关于鱼繁殖速度的内容。 B) ✓ 正确 most of our aquatic(水产的) food now comes from farming rather than fishing ↔ They are mostly farmed 预判答案是「大多是养殖的」，They are mostly farmed 几乎一一对应——主语 They 回指题干 the fish we eat，谓语 are mostly farmed 等价于定位句的 most … comes from farming。 C) 偷换概念 They have become as important as grain 把鱼与谷物相提并论，原文 That grain— and the water needed to grow it—could be consumed by people instead 谈的是 「养鱼比养牛省粮」，并未把鱼的重要性提升到与谷物同等的高度。 D) 无中生有 They have a longer history than humans 称鱼的历史比人类长，文中 For the first time in human history 只是用「人类历史上第一次」这一时间状语，并未对比鱼与人 类哪个历史更悠久。 如果我们继续以目前的速度消费鱼类,我们需要做什么? A) 大幅增加捕捞量。 B) 开发更先进的捕捞技术。 C) 有效扩大海洋鱼类资源。 D) 持续扩大养鱼规模。

questions.q: What do we need to do if we keep consuming fish at the current rate?
options: Increase the fishing volume considerably.
Develop more advanced fishing technology.
Enlarge the marine fish stocks effectively.
Expand the scale of fish-farming continuously.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we need to do if we keep consuming fish at the current rate? 问的是文 中给出的具体应对动作，答案应在原文中直接呈现。 47. What do we need to do if we keep consuming fish at the current rate? A) Increase the fishing volume considerably. B) Develop more advanced fishing technology. C) Enlarge the marine fish stocks effectively. D) Expand the scale of fish-farming continuously.

【拆句】题干主句是 What do we need to do，后接 if 条件状语从句 if we keep consuming fish at the current rate；keep + 动名词 consuming 表示持续，at the current rate 修饰 consuming。结构清晰，对基础薄弱者唯一难点是把 if 从句视作整体条件而非干扰信息。

【定位】To keep eating fish at the current rate, we're definitely going to need to keep aquaculture(水 产养殖) developing. 要想保持目前的吃鱼速度，我们绝对需要让水产养殖持续发展下去。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Increase the fishing volume considerably 主张大幅增加捕捞量，而 the volume of fish caught in the wild has leveled off since the 1990s 与 more than three-tenths are 已经说明海洋鱼资源被过度捕捞，再增加捕捞与原文方向背离。 B) 无中生有 Develop more advanced fishing technology 谈的是发展更先进的捕鱼技术，原文从 P4 到 P6 完全没有出现 technology、advanced 等任何技术升级方面的表达。 C) 答非所问 Enlarge the marine fish stocks effectively 称要扩大海洋鱼类存量，Only a tenth of our oceans' fish stocks could sustain heavier fishing than current levels 说明现实 情况是大多数鱼类资源已被过度捕捞，扩大存量并非作者提出的对策——作者提的对策 是「转向养殖」。 D) ✓ 正确 keep aquaculture(水产养殖) developing ↔Expand the scale of fish-farming continuously 预判要点是「继续 / 发展 / 水产养殖」三个成分；Expand the scale of fish-farming continuously 用 continuously / expand the scale / fish-farming 三个对应件——同 义替换全部命中。 关于中国在水产食品方面,作者说了什么? A) 它现在越来越重视捕捞。 B) 它拥有世界上最大的渔业资源。 C) 它养殖的鱼比从野外捕获的更多。 D) 它供应全球60%的鱼类产品。

questions.q: What does the author say about China in terms of aquatic food?
options: It places increasing emphasis on fishing now.
It boasts of the world's largest fishing stocks.
It raises more fish than caught from the wild.
It supplies 60% of the world's fish products.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say about China in terms of aquatic food? 围绕中国这个具 体对象问事实陈述，作者在文中应有正面交代。

【拆句】题干 What does the author say about China in terms of aquatic food? 主干同 46 题， 介词短语 in terms of aquatic food 起范围限定，意为「就水产食物而言」。考生若不识 in terms of 容易整句失焦，需点明它的限定功能。 48. What does the author say about China in terms of aquatic food? A) It places increasing emphasis on fishing now. B) It boasts of the world's largest fishing stocks. C) It raises more fish than caught from the wild. D) It supplies 60% of the world's fish products.

【定位】A lot of that is coming from China, which produces 60% of the world's farmed fish. In fact, some 35 countries, including China, now produce more farmed than wild-caught fish. 其中很大一部分来自中国，中国生产了全球 60% 的养殖鱼。事实上，包括中国在内的约 35 个国家如今生产的养殖鱼已经超过野生捕捞的鱼。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 It places increasing emphasis on fishing now 称中国正在加大对捕捞的重视，但 fish-farming has been growing at a fast rate. A lot of that is coming from China 说明中国的重点恰恰是养殖而非捕捞。 B) 偷换概念 It boasts of the world's largest fishing stocks 声称中国拥有世界最大鱼资源量，而原 文 P6 只说中国生产了全球 60% 的养殖鱼，并没有把 fishing stocks（野生鱼资源储 量）与中国挂钩。 C) ✓ 正确 some 35 countries, including China, now produce more farmed than wild-caught fish ↔ It raises more fish than caught from the wild 预判指出关于中国的本质判断是「养殖量超过捕捞量」，It raises more fish than caught from the wild 正是这一结构对比；至于 60% 那条数据是关于「全球养殖鱼里 中国占比」，不是答案。 D) 偷换概念 It supplies 60% of the world's fish products 把原文限定语 farmed fish 改写成 fish products（鱼制品/水产品总和），范围被悄悄扩大。原文只说中国占全球养殖鱼的六 成，并未说占全部水产品的六成。 作者为什么说水产养殖在当今如此重要? A) 这是养活世界快速增长人口的必需。 B) 它证明是人类和动物可靠的蛋白质来源。 C) 它对维持身心健康至关重要。 D) 它确保世界各地的人们获得均衡健康的饮食。

questions.q: Why does the author say aquaculture is so important these days?
options: It is a must for feeding the world's fast-growing population.
It proves a reliable source of protein for humans and animals
It is essential to maintaining both mental and physical health.
It ensures a balanced healthy diet for people the world over.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why does the author say aquaculture is so important these days? 用 say 限定为 作者明说的原因，不需要考生自行推断。

【拆句】题干 Why does the author say aquaculture is so important these days? 主句 Why does the author say 后接宾语从句，从句主干 aquaculture is so important，时间状语 these days 表「如今」。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 49. Why does the author say aquaculture is so important these days? A) It is a must for feeding the world's fast-growing population. B) It proves a reliable source of protein for humans and animals C) It is essential to maintaining both mental and physical health. D) It ensures a balanced healthy diet for people the world over.

【定位】it's also crucial to ensuring food security and sustainability. By 2050, the world will need to feed an estimated 9.7 billion people. （这种向水产养殖的转变）对保障食品安全和可持续性也至关重要。到 2050 年，全世界将 不得不养活约 97 亿人。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the world will need to feed an estimated 9.7 billion people ↔ It is a must for feeding the world's fast-growing population crucial to ensuring food security and sustainability ↔a must 预判核心是「为养活快速增长的人口」，It is a must for feeding the world's fast- growing population 用 a must / feeding / fast-growing population 三处分别对位 原文的 crucial / feed / 9.7 billion people——逐一吻合。 B) 以偏概全 It proves a reliable source of protein for humans and animals 称水产养殖为人类与 动物都提供蛋白质，但 They'll have to get their protein somewhere 中的 They 是指 9.7 billion people，并没有把蛋白质来源扩大到 animals。 C) 无中生有 It is essential to maintaining both mental and physical health 谈维持身心健康，原 文 P7 谈的是粮食安全（food security）与可持续性（sustainability），从未涉及 mental health 这一维度。 D) 过度推断 It ensures a balanced healthy diet for people the world over 强调「全世界人民的 均衡健康饮食」，原文 P7 只说养殖能提供蛋白质来源，并未承诺它能保障均衡饮食。 作者说水产养殖不是灵丹妙药是在暗示什么? A) 对虾养殖是一项有风险的事业。 B) 鱼类养殖将不可持续。 C) 鱼类养殖也可能造成严重问题。 D) 对虾养殖可能变得相当昂贵。

questions.q: What does the author imply by saying aquaculture is no silver bullet?
options: Shrimp-farming is a risky business.
Fish-farming will not be sustainable.
Fish-farming may cause serious problems too.
Shrimp-farming can become quite expensive.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author imply by saying aquaculture is no silver bullet? 出现 imply，要求把习语的隐含意翻译成具体含义。

【拆句】题干 What does the author imply by saying aquaculture is no silver bullet? 主干 What does the author imply，介词短语 by saying aquaculture is no silver bullet 作方 式状语；by + 动名词短语 saying 后接宾语从句，从句是一句完整的判断句。结构看似复 杂，实则只需把方式状语整块理解为「通过说这句话」。 50. What does the author imply by saying aquaculture is no silver bullet? A) Shrimp-farming is a risky business. B) Fish-farming will not be sustainable. C) Fish-farming may cause serious problems too. D) Shrimp-farming can become quite expensive.

【定位】However, aquaculture is no silver bullet. In some southeast Asian countries, shrimp farming does disastrous damage to marine ecosystems. 然而，水产养殖也并非万灵药。在一些东南亚国家，对虾养殖给海洋生态系统造成了灾难性 的破坏。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Shrimp-farming is a risky business 只锁定对虾养殖一项，而题干问的是 aquaculture 整体；原文 shrimp farming 只是论据，结论是关于整个 aquaculture 的。 B) 过度推断 Fish-farming will not be sustainable 把原文「不是万灵药」推断为「将不可持续」， 跨度过大；Despite these problems, however, shrimp continues to be among the most popular sea foods worldwide 反而暗示养殖仍在继续，并未走向不可持续。 C) ✓ 正确 aquaculture is no silver bullet ↔Fish-farming may cause serious problems too shrimp farming does disastrous damage to marine ecosystems ↔serious problems 预判内容是「养殖也会带来严重问题」，Fish-farming may cause serious problems too 用 fish-farming 替代 aquaculture、用 may 表示推断的不确定性、用 serious problems 涵盖 disastrous damage——一一对位，且只推一步。 D) 偷换概念 Shrimp-farming can become quite expensive 把养殖的代价定为「变得昂贵」，原文 disastrous damage to marine ecosystems 谈的是对生态系统的破坏，是环境代价而 不是金钱代价。

items.title: 2022年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2022年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 In 2020, the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the World Food Programme (WFP).

P2 Why a Nobel Prize for the WFP, and why now? In 2019, the WFP assisted nearly 100 million people in 88 countries. It is the safety net for those who fall off the edge of existence. It is a response to solving the problem of food instability. Its Nobel Prize reminds us all of the moral hazard in imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else's problem.

P3 The WFP has been around since 1961 and has been the global coordinator of nationally based efforts to avoid disasters with food aid. Despite decades of effort to eliminate hunger, the latest estimate is that about 11% of people on the planet (about 820 million people) are suffering daily undernourishment. Progress at reducing undernourishment has stopped despite gains through the 1990s and 2000s.

P4 Developed countries sometimes offer food and aid to developing ones, but at a price. One American philosopher stated that addressing the needs of the poor and vulnerable is about more than money—it is mostly about creating conditions under which prosperity and opportunity can thrive. When aid is offered with heavy conditions attached, like loan repayment or food for resources, it often widens the gap between rich and poor and sustains the old world order. This is why the work of the WFP is so vital.

P5 The scientific community, however, can provide a helping hand to the WFP. By sharing knowledge of agriculture and climate with peers in countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger, scientists can help reduce these problems. By making its voice heard, science can lead by example. The ability to overcome food shortages that must be built into some of the poorest countries will not come from loans from wealthy countries, which may have food problems of their own, or world economic institutions. This ability will be built upon self-confident people using open and shared scientific knowledge to pull themselves out of their misery.

questions.q: What does the WFP's winning of the Nobel Peace Prize make us realize?
options: More and more people in the world are suffering from starvation.
All of us can be affected by food instability one way or another.
It is hazardous to leave millions of people poor and vulnerable.
It is morally wrong to think helping the poor is not our business.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the WFP's winning of the Nobel Peace Prize make us realize? 是用 What 提问的具体内容题，问的是文中明示的某句话，不涉及推断或主旨。

【拆句】主干是 What does ... make us realize，the WFP's winning of the Nobel Peace Prize 是 动名词短语作主语，winning 由所有格 the WFP's 修饰、of 短语补足对象；理解上等价 于"世界粮食计划署获诺贝尔和平奖这件事让我们认识到什么"。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What does the WFP's winning of the Nobel Peace Prize make us realize? A) More and more people in the world are suffering from starvation. B) All of us can be affected by food instability one way or another. C) It is hazardous to leave millions of people poor and vulnerable. D) It is morally wrong to think helping the poor is not our business.

【定位】Its Nobel Prize reminds us all of the moral hazard in imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else's problem. 它（世界粮食计划署）获诺贝尔和平奖一事提醒我们所有人：把贫困者与脆弱群体想成是别 人的问题，是一种道德上的危险。

【选项】A) 答非所问 More and more people in the world are suffering from starvation. 说的是饥饿人 数在增加，这只是 P3 中的一项数据陈述，并非诺贝尔奖让我们意识到的道德层面的 道理。 B) 无中生有 All of us can be affected by food instability one way or another. 称所有人都会以某 种方式受食物不稳定影响，原文从未做此论断；P2 强调的是不能把扶贫当别人的事，而 非"每个人都会饿肚子"。 C) 偷换概念 It is hazardous to leave millions of people poor and vulnerable. 说"让人陷入贫困 是危险的"，把"危险"指向贫困者的处境；而原文 the moral hazard in imagining that ... somebody else's problem 中危险指的是"把扶贫想成别人的事"这种道德态度，主语 错位。 D) ✓ 正确 the moral hazard in imagining that the poor and vulnerable are somebody else's problem ↔ morally wrong to think helping the poor is not our business 预判要求的两个关键义素"道德层面"与"不该认为帮穷人与己无关"都在 It is morally wrong to think helping the poor is not our business. 里齐备，匹配最严丝合缝。 关于世界粮食计划署消除饥饿的努力,我们了解到什么? A) 它已经确保了数百万人的充足粮食供应。 B) 尽管取得了进展,但距离目标仍然遥远。 C) 它在应对自然灾害方面做得很好。 D) 它正在防止全球范围内的饥饿发生。

questions.q: What do we learn about the WFP's effort to eliminate hunger?
options: It has ensured a sufficient food supply to millions.
It is still far from its goal despite the progress made.
It has done a good job in combating natural disasters.
It is preventing starvation occurring on a global scale.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about ... 问的是关于某一具体话题的明示信息，答案应是原文对该话题 的直接陈述。

【拆句】WFP's effort to eliminate hunger 是 about 的宾语；effort 后接动词不定式 to eliminate hunger 作后置定语，相当于"为消除饥饿所做的努力"。整句无陷阱。 52. What do we learn about the WFP's effort to eliminate hunger? A) It has ensured a sufficient food supply to millions. B) It is still far from its goal despite the progress made. C) It has done a good job in combating natural disasters. D) It is preventing starvation occurring on a global scale.

【定位】Despite decades of effort to eliminate hunger, the latest estimate is that about 11% of people on the planet (about 820 million people) are suffering daily undernourishment. Progress at reducing undernourishment has stopped despite gains through the 1990s and 2000s. 尽管已为消除饥饿付出了数十年的努力，最新估计仍有约 11%（约 8.2 亿人）正在遭受日 常营养不良。尽管 20 世纪 90 年代和 21 世纪头十年取得过进展，减少营养不良的进展已经 停止。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 It has ensured a sufficient food supply to millions. 称已确保数百万人的充足食物， 原文 11% of people ... are suffering daily undernourishment 恰恰相反——8.2 亿人 仍营养不良，谈不上已确保充足供给。 B) ✓ 正确 Progress at reducing undernourishment has stopped despite gains through the 1990s and 2000s ↔still far from its goal despite the progress made 预判要求的"取得过进展"与"目标未达"两要素，分别由 despite the progress made 与 still far from its goal 一一承接，且语气与原文同样冷静客观，匹配最优。 C) 答非所问 It has done a good job in combating natural disasters. 把话题偏移到自然灾害，P3 谈的是消除饥饿、营养不良，未对该机构在自然灾害方面的表现下结论。 D) 过度推断 It is preventing starvation occurring on a global scale. 称正在全球范围内阻止饥饿 发生，原文 Progress at reducing undernourishment has stopped 明确说进展已停 滞，更未给出该机构在阻止全球饥饿发生。 当粮食援助以有偿方式提供时会发生什么? A) 富人会变得更富,穷人会变得更穷。 B) 更多的人会愿意加入这项努力。 C) 更多的粮食将提供给有需要的人。 D) 救援努力的可持续性将降低。

questions.q: What will happen when food aid is offered at a price?
options: The rich will become richer and the poor poorer.
More people will be willing to join in the effort.
More food will be made available to the needy.
The relief effort will be rendered less sustainable.
questions.explain:
【判型】What will happen when food aid is offered at a price? 询问的是某条件下的具体后果， 文中应有明示的结果句。

【拆句】主干 What will happen，when 引导时间状语从句 when food aid is offered at a price， 从句采用被动语态 is offered；at a price 是固定搭配，意为"有代价地、附带条件地"，不 是字面"以一个价格"。基础薄弱考生若按字面理解 at a price 易跑偏，需把它当短语整体 记住。 53. What will happen when food aid is offered at a price? A) The rich will become richer and the poor poorer. B) More people will be willing to join in the effort. C) More food will be made available to the needy. D) The relief effort will be rendered less sustainable.

【定位】When aid is offered with heavy conditions attached, like loan repayment or food for resources, it often widens the gap between rich and poor and sustains the old world order. 当援助被附加沉重条件（例如要求偿还贷款或以资源换食物）时，它往往会拉大贫富差距并 维持旧有的世界秩序。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 widens the gap between rich and poor ↔The rich will become richer and the poor poorer 预判中"贫富差距更大"的核心义素，恰好被 richer ... poorer 比较级并列对偶句精确锁 定，且与定位句方向、程度完全一致。 B) 无中生有 More people will be willing to join in the effort. 称会有更多人愿意加入援助行动， 原文未做此推断，P4 的结果聚焦在贫富差距与旧秩序，与此选项无关。 C) 与原文相反 More food will be made available to the needy. 称会有更多食物送达需要的人，与 P4 强调附条件援助的负面后果（差距拉大、旧秩序延续）方向相反。 D) 偷换概念 The relief effort will be rendered less sustainable. 把后果转到"援助行动可持续性降 低"，原文未讨论可持续性，只说附条件援助维持旧秩序、扩大差距，未对援助本身能否 持续下结论。 科学家如何帮助应对贫困和饥饿? A) 通过与世界经济机构密切合作。 B) 通过与贫困国家的同行分享专业知识。 C) 通过在发展中国家建立更多的粮食研究项目。 D) 通过在遭受营养不良的人群中建立自尊。

questions.q: How can scientists help cope with poverty and hunger?
options: By collaborating closely with world economic institutions.
By sharing expertise with peers in poverty-stricken nations.
By setting up more food research programs in developing countries.
By building self-respect in people suffering from undernutrition.
questions.explain:
【判型】How can scientists help cope with poverty and hunger? 以 How 询问途径，文中通常 以 by 短语或具体动作句给出明示答案。

【拆句】How can scientists help cope with poverty and hunger? 中 help 后接动词原形 cope （省略 to 的动词不定式），相当于"帮助应对"；structure 平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】By sharing knowledge of agriculture and climate with peers in countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger, scientists can help reduce these problems. 通过与最易陷入贫困和饥饿的国家的同行分享农业和气候知识，科学家可以帮助减少这些 问题。 54. How can scientists help cope with poverty and hunger? A) By collaborating closely with world economic institutions. B) By sharing expertise with peers in poverty-stricken nations. C) By setting up more food research programs in developing countries. D) By building self-respect in people suffering from undernutrition.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 By collaborating closely with world economic institutions. 称与世界经济机构紧密合 作，P5 提到 world economic institutions 时是否定语气——说该能力不会来自这些机 构，并未让科学家与之合作。 B) ✓ 正确 sharing knowledge of agriculture and climate with peers in countries most vulnerable to poverty and hunger ↔sharing expertise with peers in poverty-stricken nations 预判中三个要素"分享""知识/专业""贫困国家同行"在 By sharing expertise with peers in poverty-stricken nations 中一一对应，结构与原文方式状语完全平行。 C) 无中生有 By setting up more food research programs in developing countries. 称在发展中 国家设立更多食品研究项目，原文 P5 仅讲分享知识，未提建立研究项目。 D) 偷换概念 By building self-respect in people suffering from undernutrition. 称在营养不良的 人身上建立自尊，原文 self-confident people using open and shared scientific knowledge 谈的是"自信的人借科学知识自救"——是结果导向的论断，并非给科学家的 方法；且 self-respect（自尊）与 self-confident（自信）也并不等同。 作者在文章结尾试图传达什么信息? A) 富裕国家应该首先解决自己的粮食问题。 B) 富裕国家在提供粮食援助方面应该更加慷慨。 C) 贫穷国家应该增强自身解决粮食短缺的能力。 D) 世界经济机构应该在抗击饥饿方面发挥更大作用。

items.title: 2022年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2022年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 Even though we are living in an age where growing old is thought of as an inevitable misery, this doctor has been changing the game for seniors over the last 25 years.

P2 It all started in 1991 when the Harvard-educated physician was transferred from working in a stressful emergency room to being the medical director of a nursing home in upstate New York. The depressing and regimented(严格管制的) environment got him thinking on what exactly could improve the residents' conditions.

P3 Even though animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time, Dr. Bill Thomas took a chance. Based on a hunch(直觉), he brought in two dogs, four cats, hens, rabbits, 100 birds, a multitude of plants, a flower garden, and a vegetable patch.

P4 The change was dramatic. There was a 50% drop in medical prescriptions along with a dramatic decrease in death rates—but most importantly, the residents were simply happier.

P5 Dr. Thomas's approach, named the Eden Alternative, has driven nursing homes to allow a more autonomous(自主的) and creative living space for their elderly. It erases the belief that growing old means growing useless. He encourages residents to think of their age as an enriching new phase of life rather than the end of it.

P6 Thomas, now a speaker and author of several books, also created small, independently-run residences with their own bedrooms and bathrooms, and he has been preaching a singular message that getting old is not a bad thing.

P7 "Within six weeks, they had to send a truck around to pick up all the wheelchairs," Thomas told the Washington Post. "You know why most people in nursing homes use wheelchairs? Because the buildings are so big."

P8 The 56-year-old doctor's methods have been adopted in Australia, Japan, Canada, and America with enormous success. Last year he published Second Wind: Navigating the Passage to a Slower, Deeper, and More Connected Life, a guide on how to shift our perspectives on aging and growth.

P9 He is currently traveling through North America performing with his guitar and his enthusiasm on his Age of Disruption Tour.

questions.q: What has Bill Thomas been doing for a quarter of a century?
options: Transforming people's lifestyle.
Honoring his Harvard education.
Changing people's philosophy of life.
Shifting people's perspective on aging.
questions.explain:
【判型】What has Bill Thomas been doing for a quarter of a century? 用 what 直接问做了什 么事，且锁定了二十五年的具体时间，没有 infer/suggest/imply 等推断信号，也不问全文 主旨。

【拆句】现在完成进行时 has been doing 强调「一直在做、且仍在继续」，for a quarter of a century 是时间段状语；对应原文要找「持续二十五年都在做的那件事」。

【定位】Even though we are living in an age where growing old is thought of as an inevitable misery, this doctor has been changing the game for seniors over the last 25 years. 尽管我们生活在一个把变老视为难免之苦的时代，这位医生在过去 25 年里一直在为老年人 改变这一局面。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Transforming people\'s lifestyle 偷换了 changing the game 的对象——原文改变的 是观念/局面，不是 lifestyle（衣食住行的生活方式）。 B) 无中生有 Honoring his Harvard education 原文虽提 the Harvard-educated physician，但只 是介绍背景，并未说他二十五年所做的事是「为哈佛教育争光」。 C) 以偏概全 Changing people\'s philosophy of life 把「对变老的看法」扩大为「整套人生哲 学」，范围被无限放大，且对象从 seniors 变成了 people 全体。 D) ✓ 正确 growing old is thought of as an inevitable misery ↔perspectives on aging changing the game for seniors ↔Shifting people\'s perspective 预判说他在改变「对变老的看法」，Shifting people\'s perspective on aging 在字面 与语义上同时复现这一判断，无须额外推断。 为什么 Bill Thomas 要在养老院尝试一些不同的做法? A) 他想让养老院对老年人来说更加愉快。 B) 他想将自己在哈佛所受的训练应用于实践。 C) 他认为彻底改革养老院的管理是自己的责任。 D) 他对在这种环境中工作感到失望。

questions.q: Why did Bill Thomas try something different in the nursing home?
options: He wanted to make it more pleasant for seniors.
He wanted to apply his Harvard training to practice.
He felt it his duty to revolutionize its management.
He felt disappointed working in the environment.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did Bill Thomas try something different in the nursing home? 用 why 直接问动 机，原文有明确的因果或心理描写句即可定位，不必跨段推断。 47. Why did Bill Thomas try something different in the nursing home? A) He wanted to make it more pleasant for seniors. B) He wanted to apply his Harvard training to practice. C) He felt it his duty to revolutionize its management. D) He felt disappointed working in the environment.

【拆句】一般过去时 did，问的是过去某次具体动机；try something different 是「尝试不一样的做 法」，对应原文「引入动植物」这一动作。

【定位】The depressing and regimented(严格管制的) environment got him thinking on what exactly could improve the residents' conditions. 那种压抑而管制严格的环境促使他思考究竟怎样才能改善住户的处境。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 improve the residents\' conditions ↔make it more pleasant for seniors 预判说「让老人住得更舒心」，make it more pleasant for seniors 在动宾结构与对象 层面同时复现，无需推断。 B) 无中生有 apply his Harvard training to practice 把 Harvard-educated physician 这一背景细 节拼到动机上——原文从未说他这么做是为了「把哈佛所学落地」。 C) 过度推断 felt it his duty to revolutionize its management 把「想改善老人处境」夸张成「觉得 自己有责任去革命化养老院管理」，原文既无「职责感」亦无「revolutionize management」的表述。 D) 张冠李戴 felt disappointed working in the environment 把 The depressing and regimented(严格管制的) environment 这一对环境的描写，错置成他个人情绪。原文 是环境压抑，而非他心情失望；且这是触发思考的背景，不等于动机本身。 关于 Bill Thomas 将动物和植物带入养老院,我们了解到什么? A) 他把养老院搞得一团糟。 B) 他做了所有专业人士都会做的事情。 C) 他赢得了州政府的即时支持。 D) 他的行为违反了州法律。

questions.q: What do we learn about Bill Thomas bringing animals and plants into the nursing home?
options: He made a mess of the nursing home.
He did something all professionals would do.
He won instant support from the state authorities.
He acted in violation of the state law.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about Bill Thomas bringing animals and plants into the nursing home? 锁定一个具体事件，问围绕它能从原文得到什么信息，无推断标记。

【拆句】动名词短语 bringing… into… 作介词 about 的宾语，整句问「关于他往养老院里搬动植物 这件事，我们能知道什么」。

【定位】Even though animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time, Dr. Bill Thomas took a chance. 尽管当时养老院里养动物是违法的，比尔·托马斯医生还是冒了险（这么做了）。 48. What do we learn about Bill Thomas bringing animals and plants into the nursing home? A) He made a mess of the nursing home. B) He did something all professionals would do. C) He won instant support from the state authorities. D) He acted in violation of the state law.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 made a mess of the nursing home 把引入动植物说成「把养老院弄得乱七八糟」，与 原文完全相反——原文紧接着是 dramatic decrease in death rates 和 the residents were simply happier，效果是正面的。 B) 与原文相反 did something all professionals would do 说这是「所有专业人士都会做的事」，但 原文 Dr. Bill Thomas took a chance 与 animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time 都指向「冒险特例」，并非行业常规。 C) 与原文相反 won instant support from the state authorities 把 took a chance（冒险）反向虚构 成「立即获得州政府支持」，与原文「违法」事实完全冲突。 D) ✓ 正确 animals in nursing homes were illegal at the time ↔acted in violation of the state law 预判抓住「违法」这一事实，acted in violation of the state law 用名词 violation＋介 宾 of the state law 复现了 illegal，语义重心一致。 Bill Thomas 一直坚持倡导什么? A) 健康并非只是年轻人的特权。 B) 养老院的规模应受到严格限制。 C) 变老绝不是什么悲惨的事情。 D) 老年人住所应该独立运营。

questions.q: What has Bill Thomas been persistently advocating?
options: Good health is not just a privilege of the young.
Nursing homes should be strictly limited in size.
Getting old is by no means something miserable.
Residences for seniors should be run independently.
questions.explain:
【判型】What has Bill Thomas been persistently advocating? 问的是他一贯主张的具体内容；原 文有「preaching a singular message」句可直接对接，仍属细节题。

【拆句】现在完成进行时 has been advocating＋副词 persistently 强调持续性；what 是 advocating 的宾语前置。

【定位】Thomas, now a speaker and author of several books, also created small, independently-run residences with their own bedrooms and bathrooms, and he has been preaching a singular message that getting old is not a bad thing. 如今他既是演讲者又是几本书的作者，他建立了独立运营、带独立卧室和卫生间的小型住 所，并一直在传播一个核心讯息：变老并不是一件坏事。 49. What has Bill Thomas been persistently advocating? A) Good health is not just a privilege of the young. B) Nursing homes should be strictly limited in size. C) Getting old is by no means something miserable. D) Residences for seniors should be run independently.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Good health is not just a privilege of the young 把话题从「对变老的看法」偷换成 「健康权」；原文虽提 50\% drop in medical prescriptions，但讨论的是养老院环境 改善的效果，并未上升为「健康是不是年轻人专属」的命题。 B) 以偏概全 Nursing homes should be strictly limited in size 借用 the buildings are so big 这 一例证，伪装成他的「长期主张」。原文只是用大养老院解释轮椅多，并未上升为「养 老院必须严格限制规模」的口号。 C) ✓ 正确 getting old is not a bad thing ↔Getting old is by no means something miserable think of their age as an enriching new phase of life rather than the end of it ↔ Getting old is by no means something miserable 预判核心是「变老不糟糕」，Getting old is by no means something miserable 在主 谓宾与否定逻辑上完全复现这一判断。 D) 以偏概全 Residences for seniors should be run independently 借用 created small, independently-run residences 这一具体做法，伪装成他的中心主张；但 preach a singular message 后的同位语清楚说明他反复在传的核心讯息是 getting old is not a bad thing，而非「独立运营」。 Bill Thomas 的新理念受到了怎样的反响? A) 它正在许多国家获得认同。 B) 它正在世界范围内引发热烈讨论。 C) 它在各地都被认为具有革命性。 D) 它正在赢得政府的认可。

questions.q: How is Bill Thomas's new concept received?
options: It is gaining ground in many countries.
It is being heatedly debated worldwide.
It is considered revolutionary everywhere.
It is winning approval from the government.
questions.explain:
【判型】How is Bill Thomas\'s new concept received? 问「被如何接受」，原文必有一句直陈反 响的句子，无须跨段推断。

【拆句】一般现在时被动语态 is received，主语是 new concept，问外界对其评价；how 在句首作 方式状语。

【定位】The 56-year-old doctor's methods have been adopted in Australia, Japan, Canada, and America with enormous success. 这位 56 岁的医生的方法已经在澳大利亚、日本、加拿大和美国得到采纳，并大获成功。 50. How is Bill Thomas's new concept received? A) It is gaining ground in many countries. B) It is being heatedly debated worldwide. C) It is considered revolutionary everywhere. D) It is winning approval from the government.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 have been adopted in Australia, Japan, Canada, and America ↔ gaining ground in many countries with enormous success ↔gaining ground 预判强调「被多国接受、正在扩展」，gaining ground in many countries 同时复现 「多国」与「势头良好」两个要点。 B) 与原文相反 being heatedly debated worldwide 把「被接受」反扭成「被激烈争论」，原文 enormous success 是正向评价，没有任何争议、反对的语义。 C) 以偏概全 considered revolutionary everywhere 既无原文支持的「革命性」评价，又把多国采 用扩大为「everywhere」——原文只列了四国，不能等同于「到处」。 D) 无中生有 winning approval from the government 凭空虚构「获得政府批准」，原文只说被采 用并成功，未指明任何一个政府机构层面的官方批准。

items.title: 2022年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2022年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 Research shows that in developed countries, more affluent and educated people tend to consume higher-quality diets—including more fruits and vegetables, fish and whole grains. On the contrary, economically disadvantaged people report diets that are nutrient-poor and energy-dense. They are less likely to have food-purchasing habits that conform to public health recommendations.

P2 These dietary differences are often accompanied by higher rates of obesity and diabetes among lower-income people. This relationship between social class and diet quality and health is extensively documented. However, the research does not explain why this is the case—a question that has significant implications for designing effective policies and initiatives to improve diets and prevent chronic diseases.

P3 Public-health initiatives to promote healthy diets often focus on providing nutrition education and recipes(食谱). These approaches, however, often presume less food literacy (i.e., food knowledge and skills) among low-income people. Are unhealthy diets really the result of poor choices, limited food skills and knowledge?

P4 Research suggests that adults in food-insecure households are just as likely as those in food- secure households to adjust recipes to make them more healthy. They are also just as proficient in food preparation and cooking skills. There is no indication that increasing food skills or budgeting skills will reduce food insecurity.

P5 Instead, disadvantaged groups are constrained by their economic, material and social circumstances. For example, low income is the strongest predictor of food insecurity in Canada, where one in eight households experiences insufficient access to nutritious foods.

P6 It's well-established that food prices are an important determinant of food choice. Low-income households report that they find it difficult to adopt dietary guidelines because food prices are a barrier to improving their diets.

P7 When researchers estimate the cost of diets people actually eat, higher-quality diets are typically more costly.

P8 While this may be so, it does not, in itself, prove that healthy diets are necessarily more expensive or cost-prohibitive. After all, not all socioeconomically disadvantaged people consume poor diets.

P9 We can easily think of a number of foods and recipes that are both inexpensive and nutritious. The internet is full of recipes for "eating well on a budget."

questions.q: What can we learn from research on diets in developed countries?
options: Dietary recommendations are not fit for underprivileged people.
People from different social groups vary in their dietary habits.
People's choice of food depends on their individual taste
There is no consensus on what high-quality diets are.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we learn from research on diets in developed countries 没有 infer/imply 等 推断信号，问的是研究的客观结论。

【拆句】题干 What can we learn from research on diets in developed countries 是 What 引导 的特殊疑问句，主干是 What can we learn，后接介词短语 from research on diets in developed countries 修饰 learn 的来源；无从句、无否定、无陷阱。

【定位】Research shows that in developed countries, more affluent and educated people tend to consume higher-quality diets—including more fruits and vegetables, fish and whole grains. On the contrary, economically disadvantaged people report diets that are nutrient-poor and energy-dense. 研究表明，在发达国家，更富裕且受过良好教育的人倾向于消费更高质量的饮食——包括 更多水果蔬菜、鱼类和全谷物；相反，经济弱势人群所报告的饮食则是营养贫乏而能量密 集的。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文只说弱势群体 less likely to have food-purchasing habits that conform to public health recommendations，是"他们不照做"，并非 Dietary recommendations are not fit for underprivileged people 这种"建议本身不适合"。 B) ✓ 正确 more affluent and educated people tend to consume higher-quality diets ... On the contrary, economically disadvantaged people report diets that are nutrient-poor and energy-dense ↔People from different social groups vary in their dietary habits 预判中的"不同社会群体在饮食上存在差异"恰好被 People from different social groups vary in their dietary habits 直接覆盖，匹配度最高。 C) 无中生有 全段讨论的是阶级、收入、教育对饮食的影响，没有任何关于 individual taste 的 论述。 D) 无中生有 原文以列举 fruits and vegetables, fish and whole grains 等方式默认了高质量饮食的 内涵，没有讨论是否存在 consensus。 51. What can we learn from research on diets in developed countries? A) Dietary recommendations are not fit for underprivileged people. B) People from different social groups vary in their dietary habits. C) People's choice of food depends on their individual taste D) There is no consensus on what high-quality diets are. 作者认为在制定改善饮食和健康的政策时什么是重要的? A) 更好地理解社会阶层与健康之间的关系。 B) 更加重视研究肥胖和慢性疾病的成因。 C) 优先为较低阶层提供更好的营养。 D) 设计关于公共健康的教育项目和举措。

questions.q: What does the author say is important in formulating policies to improve diets and health?
options: A better understanding of the relationship between social class and health.
A greater emphasis on studying the cause of obesity and chronic diseases.
Prioritizing the provision of better nutrition for lower classes.
Designing education programs and initiatives on public health.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say is important 直接索取作者的明示判断，不是要考生自己 推断。

【拆句】题干 What does the author say is important in formulating policies to improve diets and health 是嵌套疑问句，主语 the author，谓语 say，宾语为省略 that 的从句 What ... is important in formulating policies，to improve diets and health 是不定式作目的状 语，结构清楚不绕。

【定位】However, the research does not explain why this is the case—a question that has significant implications for designing effective policies and initiatives to improve diets and prevent chronic diseases. 然而，研究并未解释"为何如此"——而这恰是一个对设计有效政策、推动饮食改善与慢病预 防具有重大意义的问题。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the research does not explain why this is the case—a question that has significant implications for designing effective policies ↔A better understanding of the relationship between social class and health 预判的"弄清阶级与健康关系的成因"被 A better understanding of the relationship between social class and health 一句直接对应。 B) 以偏概全 原文谈的是 designing effective policies 的关键，是"理解关系成因"；选项却把焦点收 缩到 cause of obesity and chronic diseases，丢掉了"社会阶级"这一关键。 C) 偷换概念 原文强调政策制定需要先理解"为何如此"，并没有主张直接 Prioritizing the provision of better nutrition。 D) 张冠李戴 education programs and initiatives on public health 是第三段才出现的话题 nutrition education，且作者后文持质疑态度，并非他认定为政策制定的关键。 52. What does the author say is important in formulating policies to improve diets and health? A) A better understanding of the relationship between social class and health. B) A greater emphasis on studying the cause of obesity and chronic diseases. C) Prioritizing the provision of better nutrition for lower classes. D) Designing education programs and initiatives on public health. 研究揭示了食物不安全家庭中的成年人有什么特点? A) 他们的饮食习惯需要改变。 B) 他们的食物素养一直在提高。 C) 他们不太关注自己的食谱。 D) 他们并不缺乏食物知识或预算技能。

questions.q: What does research reveal about adults in food-insecure households?
options: Their eating habits need to be changed.
Their food literacy has been improving.
They do not pay much attention to their food recipes.
They do not lack food knowledge or budgeting skills.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does research reveal about adults in food-insecure households 问的是研究客观 结论，正确项是原文一句的同义改写。

【拆句】题干 What does research reveal about adults in food-insecure households 主干 research reveal，宾语为 What，about adults in food-insecure households 是宾语补足 的范围状语，限定研究对象，结构无陷阱。

【定位】Research suggests that adults in food-insecure households are just as likely as those in food- secure households to adjust recipes to make them more healthy. They are also just as proficient in food preparation and cooking skills. There is no indication that increasing food skills or budgeting skills will reduce food insecurity. 研究表明，食物不安全家庭的成年人，在调整食谱以使其更健康方面，与食物安全家庭的成 年人一样可能；他们在食物准备与烹饪技能上也同样熟练；没有迹象表明提升食物技能或预 算技能能减少食物不安全。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文整段都在论证"他们的饮食与烹饪并无问题"，Their eating habits need to be changed 反而把矛头指向他们的饮食习惯。 B) 无中生有 原文说他们"已经一样熟练"，并未谈到 has been improving 这种"正在提升"的进程。 C) 与原文相反 原文明确说他们 adjust recipes to make them more healthy，反而是在认真对待食 谱；do not pay much attention to their food recipes 与之相反。 D) ✓ 正确 just as proficient in food preparation and cooking skills ↔ They do not lack food knowledge or budgeting skills There is no indication that increasing food skills or budgeting skills will reduce food insecurity ↔They do not lack food knowledge or budgeting skills 预判中的"不缺食物知识与预算技能"与 They do not lack food knowledge or budgeting skills 是肯定—否定的等值改写。 53. What does research reveal about adults in food-insecure households? A) Their eating habits need to be changed. B) Their food literacy has been improving. C) They do not pay much attention to their food recipes. D) They do not lack food knowledge or budgeting skills. 什么有助于改善加拿大弱势群体的食物安全? A) 教他们预算技能。 B) 增加他们的食物选择。 C) 使他们能够更多地获得营养食品。 D) 采取更有效的措施来增加食物供应。

questions.q: What would help improve food security among the disadvantaged groups in Canada?
options: Teaching them budgeting skills.
Increasing their food choices.
Enabling them to have more access to nutritious foods.
Taking more effective measures to increase food supplies.
questions.explain:
【判型】What would help improve food security among the disadvantaged groups in Canada 问对应措施，原文应有明确陈述，不必推断。

【拆句】题干 What would help improve food security among the disadvantaged groups in Canada 主干 What would help improve food security，help 后省略 to，among the disadvantaged groups in Canada 是限定 food security 范围的介词短语，三层修饰但平 铺直叙。

【定位】For example, low income is the strongest predictor of food insecurity in Canada, where one in eight households experiences insufficient access to nutritious foods. 举例来说，在加拿大，低收入是食物不安全最强的预测因子，那里有八分之一的家庭无法充 分获取营养食物。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 第四段已明确 no indication that increasing food skills or budgeting skills will reduce food insecurity，作者直接驳斥 Teaching them budgeting skills 这种做法。 B) 偷换概念 原文谈的是 insufficient access to nutritious foods 即"获取渠道不足"，不是 Increasing their food choices 即"扩大可选范围"。 C) ✓ 正确 one in eight households experiences insufficient access to nutritious foods ↔ Enabling them to have more access to nutritious foods 预判中的"让他们更多获取营养食物"与 Enabling them to have more access to nutritious foods 一一对应。 D) 偷换概念 原文聚焦弱势人群的低收入与获取不足，并未主张 increase food supplies 这种宏观供 给端的对策。 54. What would help improve food security among the disadvantaged groups in Canada? A) Teaching them budgeting skills. B) Increasing their food choices. C) Enabling them to have more access to nutritious foods. D) Taking more effective measures to increase food supplies. 作者建议弱势群体做什么来改善健康? A) 对饮食指南采取积极态度。 B) 选择既健康又实惠的饮食。 C) 确保在互联网上购买健康食品。 D) 改变他们的饮食习惯和消费模式。

questions.q: What does the author suggest disadvantaged people do to improve their health?
options: Adopt a positive attitude towards dietary guidelines.
Choose diets that are both healthy and affordable.
Make sure to purchase healthy foods on the internet.
Change their eating habits and consumption patterns.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest disadvantaged people do to improve their health 问 作者明示的建议，不是要考生跨段推断。

【拆句】题干 What does the author suggest disadvantaged people do to improve their health 是含 suggest 的特殊疑问句，宾语从句省略了 that 与 should，故 do 以原形出 现；to improve their health 是不定式目的状语，整体结构清晰。

【定位】We can easily think of a number of foods and recipes that are both inexpensive and nutritious. The internet is full of recipes for "eating well on a budget." 我们可以轻易想到一些既便宜又有营养的食物与食谱；互联网上充满了"在预算内吃得好"的 食谱。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只提到弱势群体 find it difficult to adopt dietary guidelines，并未让他们 Adopt a positive attitude towards dietary guidelines。 B) ✓ 正确 foods and recipes that are both inexpensive and nutritious ↔ Choose diets that are both healthy and affordable eating well on a budget ↔Choose diets that are both healthy and affordable 预判的"选择既健康又负担得起的饮食"与 Choose diets that are both healthy and affordable 是 both…and… 结构的整体同义改写。 C) 过度推断 原文只是说 The internet is full of recipes for "eating well on a budget."，是举例说 明网上有这类食谱，并非建议人们"必须" Make sure to purchase healthy foods on the internet。 D) 与原文相反 作者反复说明弱势群体的饮食问题不出在饮食习惯本身，而在经济与获取层面，Change their eating habits and consumption patterns 把矛头重新指向习惯，与全文立场 相悖。

items.title: 2023年3月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2023年3月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 It's good to be smart. After all, intelligent people earn more money, accumulate more wealth, and even live longer. But there's another side to the story. The brightest people and strongest leaders sometimes make errors others don't, especially in situations that require common sense.

P2 Travis Bradberry, president at TalentSmart, explained in his post Why Smart People Act So Stupid that "Rational thinking and intelligence don't tend to go hand in hand. Intelligent people are more prone to silly mistakes because of blind spots in how they use logic. These blind spots exist because smart people tend to be overconfident in their reasoning abilities." They are so used to being right and having quick answers that they don't even realise when they're making a mess by answering without thinking things through.

P3 A lifetime of praise leads smart people to develop too much faith in their intelligence and abilities. They often fail to recognise when they need help, and when they do recognise it, they tend to believe that no one else is capable of providing it.

P4 "It's hard for anyone to graciously accept the fact that they're wrong. It's even harder for smart people because they grow so used to being right all the time that it becomes a part of their identity," Bradberry wrote. "For smart people, being wrong can feel like a personal attack, and being right, a necessity."

P5 Smart people also have a hard time accepting feedback. They tend to undervalue the opinions of others, which means they have trouble believing that anyone is qualified to give them useful feedback. Not only does this tendency hinder their growth and performance, it can lead to harmful relationships, both personally and professionally.

P6 Smart people develop overachieving personalities because things come so easily to them. They simply don't understand how hard some people have to work to accomplish the same things, and because of that, they push people too hard. They set the bar too high, and when people take too long or don't get things quite right, they assume it's due to a lack of effort. So they push even harder.

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about the brightest people?
options: They can make silly mistakes in straightforward situations.
They usually turn a blind eye to their own weaknesses.
They are admired by people around them.
They can differ in their personalities.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn from the passage about the brightest people? 是开放式问 "关 于聪明人我们知道了什么"，没有 infer/imply 之类的推断信号，也不问主旨或态度——属 于覆盖全篇的细节判断题。 46. What do we learn from the passage about the brightest people? A) They can make silly mistakes in straightforward situations. B) They usually turn a blind eye to their own weaknesses. C) They are admired by people around them. D) They can differ in their personalities.

【拆句】What do we learn from the passage about the brightest people? 主干是 what do we learn，about the brightest people 是后置介词短语修饰 learn 的内容范围；结构平铺直 叙，无陷阱。

【定位】The brightest people and strongest leaders sometimes make errors others don't, especially in situations that require common sense. 最聪明的人和最强的领导者有时会犯别人不会犯的错，尤其是在那些需要常识的场合。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 make errors others don't, especially in situations that require common sense ↔ make silly mistakes in straightforward situations They can make silly mistakes in straightforward situations. 把预判的 "在常识场景中 犯错" 完整复现，且与定位句逐成分对应，是定位句的同义替换。 B) 无中生有 文章只说聪明人有 blind spots in how they use logic，并没有说他们对 "自己的弱点 视而不见"——turn a blind eye to their own weaknesses 是凭文字面感受瞎想出来的 关联。 C) 无中生有 文章只提到 intelligent people earn more money, accumulate more wealth, and even live longer，没说他们被人 "敬仰"——admired by people around them 属原文 未提的事实陈述。 D) 答非所问 末段确实提到 Smart people develop overachieving personalities，但全文聚焦的是 聪明人的共性问题，并未论述他们 "个性各异"——differ in their personalities 与文章 问的 "我们了解到什么" 不在一个频道。 聪明人的逻辑盲点存在的原因是什么? A) 他们不理性的思维方式。 B) 对自己思考能力过度自信。 C) 他们对行为科学的无知。 D) 对工作过度关注。

questions.q: What accounts for the existence of intelligent people's logical blind spots?
options: Their irrational way of thinking.
Too much faith in their ability to think.
Their ignorance of behavioural science.
Too much concern about their work
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What accounts for the existence of intelligent people's logical blind spots? 指向 一个具体概念（逻辑盲点）的成因，是回到具体段落找因果句的细节题。 47. What accounts for the existence of intelligent people's logical blind spots? A) Their irrational way of thinking. B) Too much faith in their ability to think. C) Their ignorance of behavioural science. D) Too much concern about their work

【拆句】What accounts for the existence of intelligent people's logical blind spots? 主干 what accounts for X，X 是 the existence of intelligent people's logical blind spots （名词化结构，相当于问 "为什么聪明人会存在逻辑盲点"），把名词化拆回动词理解即可。

【定位】Intelligent people are more prone to silly mistakes because of blind spots in how they use logic. These blind spots exist because smart people tend to be overconfident in their reasoning abilities. 聪明人更容易犯傻错，是因为他们运用逻辑时存在盲点。这些盲点之所以存在，是因为聪明 人倾向于对自己的推理能力过度自信。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文说聪明人 Rational thinking and intelligence don't tend to go hand in hand ——意思是聪明人未必理性，但这并不等于他们 "思维不理性" 就是盲点的成因；真正的 成因是过度自信。irrational way of thinking 把伴生现象当成因，属于因果倒置。 B) ✓ 正确 overconfident in their reasoning abilities ↔Too much faith in their ability to think Too much faith in their ability to think. 把原文 "对推理能力过度自信" 的核心搬过 来，且 faith / ability to think 两个成分都能在定位句里逐一着落。 C) 无中生有 ignorance of behavioural science 把 "行为科学" 这种学科概念引进来——但文章自始 至终没有提行为科学，是凭空捏造的成因。 D) 无中生有 文章没有说聪明人 "过度关心工作"——Too much concern about their work 是凭日常 对 "聪明人=工作狂" 的刻板印象瞎编出来的。 聪明人在被发现错误时会如何反应? A) 他们把责任推给别人。 B) 他们大度地接受事实。 C) 他们可能会感到震惊。 D) 他们可能会感到被ଛ冒犯。

questions.q: How do smart people react when they are found to be wrong?
options: They shift the blame to others.
They graciously accept the facts.
They may feel shocked.
They may get offended.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 How do smart people react when they are found to be wrong? 限定了具体情境 "被发现错了"，问对应反应，是定位到具体段落求证的细节题。

【拆句】How do smart people react when they are found to be wrong? 主句 How do smart people react，when 引导时间状语从句限定情境；从句用被动语态 are found to be wrong（被发现错了），主体仍是 smart people。 48. How do smart people react when they are found to be wrong? A) They shift the blame to others. B) They graciously accept the facts. C) They may feel shocked. D) They may get offended.

【定位】For smart people, being wrong can feel like a personal attack, and being right, a necessity. 对聪明人来说，被认定为错可以感觉像一次人身攻击，而正确则是一种必需。

【选项】A) 过度推断 原文没有说聪明人会 "把责任推给别人"——shift the blame to others 是凭 "聪明人不 愿承认错" 这一印象想象出来的下游行为。 B) 与原文相反 原文恰恰说 It's hard for anyone to graciously accept the fact that they're wrong. It's even harder for smart people——聪明人尤其难以坦然接受。graciously accept the facts 直接照搬原文短语却把否定关系反过来，是典型反向陷阱。 C) 偷换概念 feel shocked 把 "被冒犯/受攻击感" 偷换成 "震惊"——shocked 强调对事实意外， offended 强调对自尊受损的反应，两种情绪不同。 D) ✓ 正确 being wrong can feel like a personal attack ↔They may get offended. They may get offended. 把比喻 a personal attack 翻译成 get offended，是情绪反 应的同义动词化，且 may 与原文 can 在语气上一致。 那些难以接受建议的聪明人可能会发生什么? A) 他们可能在职业和私人生活中遭受困扰。 B) 他们可能对自己的管理能力失去信心。 C) 他们可能比以往犯更多错误。 D) 他们可能经历大量情绪压力。

questions.q: What may happen to smart people who find it difficult to accept suggestions?
options: They may suffer in their professional and private life.
They may lose faith in their administrative abilities.
They may commit more errors than ever before.
They may experience a lot of emotional stress.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What may happen to smart people who find it difficult to accept suggestions? 问 "对接受不了建议的聪明人会发生什么"，是对特定情境后果的细节求证。

【拆句】What may happen to smart people who find it difficult to accept suggestions? 主干 是 what may happen to smart people；who find it difficult to accept suggestions 是 修饰 smart people 的定语从句，限定了 "哪一类聪明人"。

【定位】Not only does this tendency hinder their growth and performance, it can lead to harmful relationships, both personally and professionally. 这种倾向不仅会阻碍他们的成长与表现，还可能导致有害的人际关系——无论是私人层面还 是职业层面。 49. What may happen to smart people who find it difficult to accept suggestions? A) They may suffer in their professional and private life. B) They may lose faith in their administrative abilities. C) They may commit more errors than ever before. D) They may experience a lot of emotional stress.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 harmful relationships, both personally and professionally ↔ suffer in their professional and private life suffer in their professional and private life 既覆盖了原文 "professionally" 又覆盖了 "personally"——两个并列限定都能落地，是定位句的完整同义改写。 B) 偷换概念 原文说 hinder their growth and performance，是 "阻碍成长与表现"，并未说他们 "对自己的管理能力失去信心"——lose faith in their administrative abilities 把 "成长 与表现受阻" 偷换成 "对管理能力失去信心"。 C) 无中生有 原文没有把 "接受不了反馈" 与 "犯更多错" 直接挂钩——commit more errors than ever before 是把第一段的 errors 概念硬拉到第五段后果中。 D) 无中生有 experience a lot of emotional stress 把后果限定为 "情绪压力"——但原文说的是 "成 长与表现受阻 + 关系有害"，从未提及情绪压力。 关于那些与成就卓越的人共事或在其手下工作的人,文中说了什么? A) 他们在工作中投入大量精力。 B) 他们为自己设定更高的目标。 C) 他们承受着越来越大的压力。 D) 他们完成事情所需的时间更少。

questions.q: What is said about those working with or under overachieving people?
options: They put a lot of effort into their work.
They set higher goals for themselves.
They are under increasing pressure.
They take less time to get things done.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is said about those working with or under overachieving people? 问 "关于 和聪明人共事的人，文章说了什么"，是末段定位的细节题。

【拆句】What is said about those working with or under overachieving people? 主干 What is said about X；X 是 those working with or under overachieving people，其中 working with or under overachieving people 是分词短语后置修饰 those，表示 "那些与 过分追求成就的人共事或在其手下做事的人"。注意 with or under 是并列介词，对象都是 overachieving people。

【定位】They set the bar too high, and when people take too long or don't get things quite right, they assume it's due to a lack of effort. So they push even harder. 他们把标杆定得太高，当别人花的时间过长或事情做得不够准确时，他们就认定这是因为对 方努力不够，于是施压得更狠。 50. What is said about those working with or under overachieving people? A) They put a lot of effort into their work. B) They set higher goals for themselves. C) They are under increasing pressure. D) They take less time to get things done.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文说聪明人 assume it's due to a lack of effort——是聪明人 "以为" 别人不努力， 并不是别人真的努力。put a lot of effort into their work 把聪明人的 "以为" 当成事 实，恰好与原文意涵相反。 B) 张冠李戴 set higher goals for themselves 这一行为在原文里属于聪明人——They set the bar too high，主语是聪明人；选项却把它安在 "和聪明人共事的人" 头上，是把行为主体张 冠李戴。 C) ✓ 正确 they push people too hard ↔They are under increasing pressure. So they push even harder. ↔increasing pressure They are under increasing pressure. 既覆盖 push people 的施压主轴（变成 under pressure），又覆盖 push even harder 的加码动态（变成 increasing），两个成分都 能在原文找到落点。 D) 与原文相反 原文说聪明人 when people take too long——意思是这些人花的时间 "过长"，而 take less time to get things done 把 "过长" 反成 "更短"，方向相反。

items.title: 2023年3月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2023年3月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Of the endless troubles that come with being driven from one's home country, losing educational certificates may seem small. But it isn't. Refugees who settle in other countries often find themselves unable to continue on their previous career path due to a new set of employer standards or skills requirements. To solve this problem, the U.S. State Department is posing a solution: online learning.

P2 The State Department will announce a partnership with an online education platform called Coursera. The platform will allow refugees worldwide to take thousands of online courses for free. "Coursera for Refugees" will be available for any non-profit group that supports refugees in any country, as well as individual refugees. They can apply for fully funded access to Coursera's course catalog, which means they can take all of the platform's classes and obtain professional certificates for free. The platform currently offers professor-led lectures on a broad range of topics, from data science to fashion design.

P3 As the world migrant crisis intensifies, employment is becoming a global concern. The new program aims to aid refugees by offering "important skills that will help them in the global economy," Evan Ryan, U.S. assistant secretary of state for educational and cultural affairs, said on a press call last week. "What we don't want to do is not act," added Coursera chief operations officer Lila Ibrahim.

P4 The idea isn't without problems. For one, starting a new career path isn't as simple as watching a few videos and obtaining an online certificate; even those looking to continue previous careers can't simply rely on an online lecture to get them up-to-date on standards, policies, and practices. For another, most of the classes on Coursera are in English, and though there are plans to add translations, language barriers can be a big obstacle. Then there are the questions over the value of massive open online courses (MOOCs) themselves—both for refugees and for average learners.

P5 But it's still early days and there are signs of hope. In 2015, a joint study found 72% of people taking the MOOCs saw career benefits afterwards.

questions.q: Why is the U.S. State Department launching an online learning program for refugees?
options: To enable them to settle down in host countries.
To allow them to learn as many job skills as possible.
To offer them a platform to pursue advanced degrees.
To help them to meet new employment standards.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why is the U.S. State Department launching an online learning program for refugees?问的是一个具体的发起原因，答案应能在原文中明确找到对应句。

【拆句】Why is the U.S. State Department launching an online learning program for refugees?是一个 Why 引导的现在进行时疑问句，主语是机构名，介词短语for refugees点 明服务对象，结构平铺、无陷阱。 51. Why is the U.S. State Department launching an online learning program for refugees? A) To enable them to settle down in host countries. B) To allow them to learn as many job skills as possible. C) To offer them a platform to pursue advanced degrees. D) To help them to meet new employment standards.

【定位】Refugees who settle in other countries often find themselves unable to continue on their previous career path due to a new set of employer standards or skills requirements. To solve this problem, the U.S. State Department is posing a solution: online learning. 在他国安顿的难民常常发现，自己因雇主新一套的标准或技能要求而无法延续原来的职业路 径。为解决这个问题，美国国务院正在推出一个方案：在线学习。

【选项】A) 偷换概念：把前提说成目的 To enable them to settle down in host countries.把项目目的说成帮助难民「在东道 国安顿下来」，但原文中settle in other countries是难民已经发生的状态、是项目的前 提，不是项目的目的。 B) 过度推断：拔高程度词 To allow them to learn as many job skills as possible.把目的扩成「学尽可能多的工 作技能」，而原文目的是「应对一套新的雇主标准」，原文并没有用「尽可能多」这类 极端量词。 C) 偷换概念：证书↔学位 To offer them a platform to pursue advanced degrees.把目的说成「追求高等学 位」，但原文第二段说的是obtain professional certificates，是专业证书而非学位。 D) ✓ 正确 a new set of employer standards or skills requirements ↔new employment standards To solve this problem, the U.S. State Department is posing a solution ↔To help them to meet 预判答案是「帮助难民应对他国雇主的新标准」，与To help them to meet new employment standards.在主语、动作、对象、目的状语上四点全部对应，是唯一与定 位句构成同义替换的选项。 关于"Coursera for Refugees"我们了解到什么? A) 它免费为难民提供广泛的课程。 B) 它为全世界的难民提供免费的在线数据服务。 C) 它允许难民获得各个学术领域的学位。 D) 它为难民提供各种各样的就业机会。

questions.q: What do we know about "Coursera for Refugees"?
options: It provides refugees with a wide range of courses free of charge.
It offers free online data services for refugees around the world.
It allows refugees to obtain degrees in various academic fields.
It supplies refugees with a great variety of job opportunities.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we know about "Coursera for Refugees"?要求选出关于该项目可以确认的事 实，属于客观信息核对。

【拆句】What do we know about "Coursera for Refugees"?结构非常简单，主句是What do we know，介词宾语就是引号里的专名，无干扰修饰。 52. What do we know about "Coursera for Refugees"? A) It provides refugees with a wide range of courses free of charge. B) It offers free online data services for refugees around the world. C) It allows refugees to obtain degrees in various academic fields. D) It supplies refugees with a great variety of job opportunities.

【定位】They can apply for fully funded access to Coursera's course catalog, which means they can take all of the platform's classes and obtain professional certificates for free. The platform currently offers professor-led lectures on a broad range of topics, from data science to fashion design. 他们可以申请由项目全额资助的Coursera课程目录访问权限，这意味着他们可以免费修读该 平台的所有课程并获得专业证书。该平台目前提供由教授主讲的讲座，主题广泛，从数据科 学到时装设计。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 a broad range of topics ↔a wide range of courses for free ↔free of charge 预判要求「免费+各种各样的课」，It provides refugees with a wide range of courses free of charge.在主语、动作、对象、范围、付费方式上五点齐备，是定位句 最干净的同义复述。 B) 偷换概念：把举例项当成核心 It offers free online data services for refugees around the world.把项目说成「提供 免费在线数据服务」，但原文from data science to fashion design中的 data science 只是众多课程主题之一，不是项目所提供的服务内容。 C) 偷换概念：证书↔学位再现 It allows refugees to obtain degrees in various academic fields.说项目能让难民拿 到「各学术领域的学位」，但原文是professional certificates——专业证书而非学位， 也没有强调「学术领域」。 D) 无中生有：用近义类比制造跳跃 It supplies refugees with a great variety of job opportunities.把项目说成提供「多 种多样的工作机会」，但原文从头到尾说的是「课程」与「证书」，不是「工作」。 文章指出全球移民危机的一个后果是什么? A) 收容国的不稳定性增加。 B) 全球经济危机加剧。 C) 更多难民在迁移过程中死亡。 D) 难民发现找工作更加困难。

questions.q: What does the passage say is a consequence of the global migrant crisis?
options: Instability increases in host countries.
The global economic crisis intensifies.
A lot more refugees die during migration.
Refugees find it more difficult to get a job.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say is a consequence of the global migrant crisis?直接问「文 章说……的后果是什么」，答案应能在原文明确找到。 53. What does the passage say is a consequence of the global migrant crisis?
