A) Instability increases in host countries. B) The global economic crisis intensifies. C) A lot more refugees die during migration. D) Refugees find it more difficult to get a job.

【拆句】What does the passage say is a consequence of the global migrant crisis?是 「What+助动词+主语+谓语+从句宾语」的疑问句，从句is a consequence of...提示答案 的逻辑位置是后果一端，结构平铺。

【定位】As the world migrant crisis intensifies, employment is becoming a global concern. 随着全球移民危机加剧，就业正成为全球性的关切。

【选项】A) 过度推断：从一点滑向全局 Instability increases in host countries.说东道国整体不稳定上升，但原文只说就业一 项成为全球关切，并未提社会稳定层面。 B) 张冠李戴：动词从一个主语挪到另一个主语 The global economic crisis intensifies.说全球经济危机加剧，但原文只说就业问题， 不是「经济危机」；intensifies 在原文里是用来形容 migrant crisis 的，不是 economic crisis。 C) 无中生有：用常识联想替代文本 A lot more refugees die during migration.说更多难民死于迁徙途中，但原文从头到 尾没有涉及死亡话题，属典型无中生有。 D) ✓ 正确 employment is becoming a global concern ↔Refugees find it more difficult to get a job a global concern ↔more difficult 预判结论是「就业难度上升」，本篇主体始终是难民，Refugees find it more difficult to get a job.既保留了主体，又把抽象的「关切」落地到「找工作变难」，是唯一与定 位句因果直接对应的选项。 作者认为是什么导致难民难以参加在线课程? A) 文化环境。 B) 变化的学术要求。 C) 缺乏语言技能。 D) 教学平台的差异。

questions.q: What does the author say causes refugees' difficulty in taking online courses?
options: Cultural environment.
Changed academic requirements.
Lack of language skills.
Difference in teaching platforms.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say causes refugees' difficulty in taking online courses?问的是 「作者说」的具体原因，回原文找归因句即可。

【拆句】What does the author say causes refugees' difficulty in taking online courses?主干是 What causes ... difficulty，does the author say是插入语，in taking online courses做后 置定语限定 difficulty，结构稍绕但无陷阱。 54. What does the author say causes refugees' difficulty in taking online courses? A) Cultural environment. B) Changed academic requirements. C) Lack of language skills. D) Difference in teaching platforms.

【定位】For another, most of the classes on Coursera are in English, and though there are plans to add translations, language barriers can be a big obstacle. 另一方面，Coursera上的大多数课程都是英文授课，尽管有添加翻译的计划，语言障碍仍可 能是一个大问题。

【选项】A) 无中生有：用相关话题替换原文话题 Cultural environment.把困难归因到「文化环境」，但原文第四段从未涉及文化差异， 是无中生有。 B) 张冠李戴：把另一困难的原因装到本题 Changed academic requirements.想说的是「学术要求改变」，但原文can't simply rely on an online lecture to get them up-to-date on standards, policies, and practices说的是行业「标准、政策、做法」的更新，而非学术要求；且这是第一条困 难，不是题54问的「上网课的困难原因」，而是「换行业的困难」。 C) ✓ 正确 language barriers can be a big obstacle ↔Lack of language skills most of the classes on Coursera are in English ↔Lack of language skills 预判明确指向「语言」，四个选项中只有Lack of language skills.提及语言；与定位句 构成最干净的因果对应。 D) 偷换概念：把对一物的质疑换成多物之差异 Difference in teaching platforms.说困难是「教学平台之间的差异」，但原文there are the questions over the value of massive open online courses (MOOCs) themselves谈的是对MOOCs整体价值的质疑，不是不同平台之间的差异。 几年前的联合研究关于MOOCs发现了什么? A) 它们帮助解决了学习者的经济问题。 B) 它们使大多数学习者受益。 C) 它们改变了一些学习者的职业道路。 D) 它们提供了最需要的职业技能。

questions.q: What did the joint study find about the MOOCs several years ago?
options: They helped solve learners' financial problems.
They benefited most of the learners.
They changed some learners' career path.
They provided the most needed vocational skills.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the joint study find about the MOOCs several years ago?问一个具体研究的 具体发现，是直白的事实核对。

【拆句】What did the joint study find about the MOOCs several years ago?是过去时一般疑问 句，主语the joint study，宾语为 what，时间状语several years ago提示要找过去时句 子，结构平铺。 55. What did the joint study find about the MOOCs several years ago? A) They helped solve learners' financial problems. B) They benefited most of the learners. C) They changed some learners' career path. D) They provided the most needed vocational skills.

【定位】In 2015, a joint study found 72% of people taking the MOOCs saw career benefits afterwards. 2015年，一项联合研究发现，参加MOOCs课程的人中有72%在之后获得了职业上的益处。

【选项】A) 偷换概念：用常识把「职业」换成「财务」 They helped solve learners' financial problems.说MOOCs帮学习者解决「财务问 题」，但原文只说career benefits——职业益处，不是钱。 B) ✓ 正确 72% of people taking the MOOCs ↔most of the learners saw career benefits afterwards ↔benefited 预判结论是「大多数学习者获益」，They benefited most of the learners.在主语、动 词、对象上三点对应——只是用程度词代替数字、用动词代替名词短语，是最干净的同 义改写。 C) 过度推断：把益处程度拔高到根本改变 They changed some learners' career path.说MOOCs「改变了某些学习者的职业路 径」，但原文只说saw career benefits——获得职业益处，从「获益」到「改变路径」 是过度推断。 D) 过度推断+无中生有：加最高级、加具体内容 They provided the most needed vocational skills.说MOOCs提供「最需要的职业技 能」，但原文只笼统说「职业益处」，并未说提供了什么具体技能，更没有「最需要」 这种最高级。

items.title: 2023年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 The United States is facing a housing crisis: Affordable housing is inadequate, while luxury homes abound(充裕), and homelessness remains a persistent problem. Despite this, popular culture and the housing industry market happiness as living with both more space and more amenities(便利设施). Big houses are advertised as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury.

P2 This is reflected in our homes. The average single-family home built in the United States before 1970 was less than 1,500 square feet in size. By 2016, the average size of a new, single-family home was 2,422 square feet. What's more, homes built in the 2000s were more likely than earlier models to have more of all types of spaces: bedrooms, bathrooms, living rooms, dining rooms, recreation rooms and garages.

P3 There are consequences of living big. As middle-class houses have grown larger, two things have happened. First, large houses take time to maintain, so cleaners and other low-wage service workers are required to keep these houses in order. Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many. Take swimming pools. While in 1950, only 2,500 U.S. families owned pools, by 1999 this number was 4 million. At the same time, public municipal pools were often closed, leaving low-income people nowhere to swim.

P4 The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions. Should Americans accept a system in which the middle and upper classes enjoy a luxurious lifestyle, using the low-wage labor of others? Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor?

P5 I believe neither is acceptable. We must change the way we think: living well does not need to mean having more private spaces; instead, it could mean having more public spaces. A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all.

questions.q: What are big houses promoted to be in the United States?
options: A luxury for the homeless.
A reward for industriousness.
An abundant source of comforts.
An absolute necessity for happiness.
questions.explain:
【判型】Q46 问的是 What are big houses promoted to be，要的是文中明写的一个事实陈述，不 需推理。

【拆句】Q46 是一个被动语态疑问句，主干为"big houses are promoted to be 什么"，promoted to be 后面接的内容就是答案要补的成分，结构平铺，无陷阱。 46. What are big houses promoted to be in the United States? A) A luxury for the homeless. B) A reward for industriousness. C) An abundant source of comforts. D) An absolute necessity for happiness.

【定位】Big houses are advertised as a reward for hard work and diligence, turning housing from a basic necessity into a luxury. 大房子被宣传成对努力工作和勤勉的一种回报，把住房从基本必需品变成了奢侈品。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 原文宣传是面向勤奋者的回报，A luxury for the homeless 把奢侈品安到 homeless 头 上，而原文 homelessness 只是危机背景，并非大房子的宣传对象。 B) ✓ 正确 a reward for hard work and diligence ↔A reward for industriousness 预判的"对勤奋的回报"在 A reward for industriousness 中 reward 与 industriousness 双双对应，锁定该项。 C) 答非所问 An abundant source of comforts 取自第三段及背景里 amenities/abound 的语义， 但 Q46 问的是大房子被"宣传成什么"，定位句给的是 reward，不是"舒适之源"。 D) 与原文相反 原文恰恰说大房子使住房 from a basic necessity into a luxury（从必需变奢侈），An absolute necessity for happiness 反把它说成"幸福的绝对必需品"，与原文相反。 住大房子的后果之一是什么？ A) 许多美国人的生活质量变得更低了。 B) 来自不同背景的人们不再社交了。 C) 人们不再能使用公共游泳池了。 D) 许多美国人的私人生活受到了负面影响。

questions.q: What is one of the consequences of living big?
options: Many Americans' quality of life has become lower.
People from diverse backgrounds no longer socialize.
People no longer have access to public swimming pools.
Many Americans' private life has been negatively affected.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is one of the consequences 用 one of 限定，答案是原文列举的多项后果中的一 项，属可直接定位的细节。

【拆句】Q47 主干为"What is one of the consequences"，of living big 是后置定语修饰 consequences，one of 提示原文有多项后果，结构简单。

【定位】Second, once-public spaces, where people from diverse backgrounds used to come together, have increasingly become privatized, leading to a reduction in the number of public facilities available to all, and a reduced quality of life for many. 第二，曾经的公共空间——不同背景的人过去常在此相聚——日益被私有化，导致面向所有 人的公共设施数量减少，许多人的生活质量随之下降。 47. What is one of the consequences of living big? A) Many Americans' quality of life has become lower. B) People from diverse backgrounds no longer socialize. C) People no longer have access to public swimming pools. D) Many Americans' private life has been negatively affected.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 a reduced quality of life for many ↔Many Americans' quality of life has become lower 预判的"生活质量下降"与 quality of life has become lower 字面同义，直接锁定。 B) 过度推断 原文只说公共空间被私有化、不同背景的人"过去"常相聚（used to），并未说人们 no longer socialize（彻底不再社交），属过度引申。 C) 以偏概全 游泳池只是说明私有化的一个例子，原文说 public municipal pools were often closed（常被关闭），no longer have access to public swimming pools 把"常被 关"绝对成"再也用不上"，且以个例顶替本题要的总后果。 D) 偷换概念 原文受影响的是 quality of life（生活质量），private life has been negatively affected 偷换成 private life（私人生活），概念不同。 住大房子引发了什么问题？ A) 与道德原则相关的问题。 B) 与劳动力成本有关的问题。 C) 关于提倡什么样的生活方式的问题。 D) 关于住房发展的问题。

questions.q: What questions arise from living big?
options: Questions related to moral principles.
Questions having to do with labor cost.
Questions about what lifestyle to promote.
Questions concerning housing development.
questions.explain:
【判型】What questions arise from living big 问的是原文明确点出的问题性质，文中有直接对应 的形容词限定，属细节。

【拆句】Q48 主干"What questions arise"，from living big 为原因状语，整句问"住大房子引发哪 类问题"，无复杂从句。

【定位】The trend for bigger housing thus poses ethical questions. 因此，住房越来越大的趋势引出了伦理（道德）层面的问题。 48. What questions arise from living big? A) Questions related to moral principles. B) Questions having to do with labor cost. C) Questions about what lifestyle to promote. D) Questions concerning housing development.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 ethical questions ↔Questions related to moral principles 预判的"伦理/道德问题"与 moral principles 同义，直接锁定。 B) 答非所问 labor cost 取自第四段反问里 using the low-wage labor of others，但那只是伦理问 题的内容举例，问题的"性质"是伦理性，labor cost 答非所问。 C) 张冠李戴 lifestyle to promote 接近第五段"该提倡什么生活方式"的话题，但 Q48 问的是第四段 引发的问题性质，what lifestyle to promote 张冠李戴到了下一段内容。 D) 无中生有 housing development（住房开发/发展）在第四段问题里并无对应表述，原文谈的是 伦理而非开发问题，属凭空捏造。 作者认为什么样的社会制度是不可接受的？ A) 一个富人剥削建造他们房屋的低工资劳动者的制度。 B) 一个富人以越来越难以证明合理的价格购买便利设施的制度。 C) 一个上层阶级剥夺下层阶级负担得起的住房的制度。 D) 一个富人以穷人为代价享受更舒适生活的制度。

questions.q: What kind of social system does the author think is unacceptable?
options: One in which the wealthy exploit the low-wage laborers building their houses.
One in which the rich purchase amenities at an increasingly unjustifiable price.
One in which the upper classes deprive the lower classes of affordable housing.
One in which the affluent enjoy a more comfortable life at the expense of the poor.
questions.explain:
【判型】What kind of social system does the author think is unacceptable 答案在原文有 a system in which... 的直接描述，是可定位的细节，而非需推断的整体态度。

【拆句】Q49 主干"What kind of social system is unacceptable"，中间插入 does the author think 表明这是作者的判断，从句嵌套但语义清晰：找作者认为不可接受的那种制度。

【定位】Are we willing to accept a system in which an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor? 我们是否愿意接受这样一种制度：富人购买的便利设施增加，就意味着穷人可享的便利设施 减少？ 49. What kind of social system does the author think is unacceptable? A) One in which the wealthy exploit the low-wage laborers building their houses. B) One in which the rich purchase amenities at an increasingly unjustifiable price. C) One in which the upper classes deprive the lower classes of affordable housing. D) One in which the affluent enjoy a more comfortable life at the expense of the poor.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 原文第一个反问确提到 using the low-wage labor of others，但 the low-wage laborers building their houses 把"他人的低薪劳动"窄化为"盖房工人"，且第二个反问 （富人便利↔穷人便利）才是更完整的对应，A 项以偏概全。 B) 无中生有 原文说富人购买便利使穷人便利减少，从未谈 an increasingly unjustifiable price（越 来越不合理的价格），价格维度是捏造的。 C) 偷换概念 deprive the lower classes of affordable housing（剥夺下层的平价住房）取自首段背 景 Affordable housing is inadequate，但作者第四段否定的制度是"便利的增减对 立"，不是剥夺平价住房，概念被偷换。 D) ✓ 正确 an increase in amenities purchased by the affluent means a reduction in amenities for the poor ↔the affluent enjoy a more comfortable life at the expense of the poor 预判的"富人享乐、穷人受损"恰是 enjoy a more comfortable life at the expense of the poor 的含义，锁定该项。 作者提倡人们怎样才能生活得好？ A) 找到将私人空间转变为公共空间的方法。 B) 建造更多那些不太富裕的人负担得起的房屋。 C) 创造更多供每个人享受的公共空间。 D) 让所有便利设施对富人和穷人一样可及。

questions.q: What does the author advocate for people to live well?
options: Finding ways to turn private spaces into public ones.
Building more houses affordable to those less affluent.
More public spaces created for everyone to enjoy.
All amenities made accessible to the rich and the poor alike.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author advocate 答案是末段作者直接给出的建议，有明写对应句，属细 节定位题。

【拆句】Q50 主干"What does the author advocate"，for people to live well 是目的状语（为了 让人们住得好），整句问"作者为此提倡什么"，结构清楚。

【定位】A better goal than building bigger houses for some is to create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all. 比起为少数人盖更大的房子，更好的目标是为所有人创造更多可公共使用的空间与设施。 50. What does the author advocate for people to live well? A) Finding ways to turn private spaces into public ones. B) Building more houses affordable to those less affluent. C) More public spaces created for everyone to enjoy. D) All amenities made accessible to the rich and the poor alike.

【选项】A) 无中生有 作者主张是"创造更多公共空间"，并未说要把私人空间 turn private spaces into public ones（改造成公共空间），这一具体做法原文没有。 B) 与原文相反 Building more houses affordable 回到了"盖房子"，而作者主张的恰恰是别再盖大 房子、转向公共空间，且 affordable housing 是首段背景非作者的提倡，方向与主张 相悖。 C) ✓ 正确 create more publicly accessible spaces and amenities for all ↔ More public spaces created for everyone to enjoy 预判的"为人人创造公共空间"与 More public spaces created for everyone to enjoy 字面同义，锁定该项。 D) 偷换概念 原文是"为所有人创造公共空间与设施"，All amenities made accessible to the rich and the poor alike 用 All amenities 把范围绝对化为"所有便利设施都对贫富开放"，超 出作者所说的"公共空间"范围。

items.title: 2023年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Most of us in the entrepreneurial community are blessed—or cursed—with higher-than-average ambition. Ambitious people strongly desire accomplishments and are willing to take more risks and spend more effort to get them.

P2 Overall, this is a positive quality, especially for people trying to build their own businesses. Apparently, if you're more naturally driven to set goals, you are more likely to succeed.

P3 Actually, this isn't always the case. In fact, in some cases, extreme ambition may end up doing more harm than good.

P4 One major side effect of excessive ambition is the tendency to focus too determinedly on one particular vision or end goal. This is problematic because it hinders your ability to adapt to new circumstances, which is vital if you want to be a successful entrepreneur. If a new competitor emerges to threaten your business, you may need to change direction, even if that means straying from your original vision. If you have too much ambition, you'll find this hard, if not impossible.

P5 Few people are successful when they try to build their first brand. Unfortunately, for the most ambitious entrepreneurs, a failure is seen as disastrous, and impossible to recover from.

P6 It's a clear departure from the intended plan toward the intended goal. For people with limited ambition, however, failure is viewed as something closer to reality. Remember, failure is inevitable, and every failure you survive is a learning experience.

P7 Ambitious people tend to be more materialistically successful than their non-ambitious counterparts. However, they're only slightly happier than their less-ambitious counterparts, and tend to live significantly shorter lives. This implies that even though ambitious people are more likely to achieve conventional "success," such success means nothing for their health and happiness—and if you don't have health and happiness, what else could possibly matter?

P8 Clearly, some amount of ambition is good for your motivation. Without any ambition, you wouldn't start your own business, set or achieve goals and get far in life. But an excess of ambition can also be dangerous, putting you at risk of burnout, stubbornness and even a shorter life.

questions.q: What does the author think of most entrepreneurs?
options: They are more willing to risk their own lives.
They are more ambitious than ordinary people.
They achieve greater nonconventional success.
They have more positive qualities than most of us.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author think of most entrepreneurs? 直接问对一个明确对象的看 法，答案能在原文某句找到对应陈述，不需跨段综合，属细节题而非推断。

【拆句】题干 What does the author think of most entrepreneurs? 是 think of 引导的特殊疑问 句，think of sb 意为"对某人的看法"，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。

【定位】Most of us in the entrepreneurial community are blessed—or cursed—with higher-than- average ambition. 我们创业圈里的大多数人，都被赋予——或者说被困于——高于常人的野心。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文说野心者 willing to take more risks 指愿冒事业风险，选项却说 risk their own lives（拿命冒险），把"风险"偷换成"生命危险"。 B) ✓ 正确 higher-than-average ambition ↔more ambitious than ordinary people 选项 They are more ambitious than ordinary people 与预判"野心高于普通人"完全吻 合，是定位句的同义替换。 C) 无中生有 原文谈的是 conventional "success"（传统成功），选项却说 nonconventional success（非传统成功），文中从无此说法。 D) 以偏概全 原文只说野心 this is a positive quality 是"一种"积极特质，选项却说创业者 more positive qualities than most of us"比我们多"，既夸大数量又把比较对象搞错（原文 most of us 本就包含创业者）。 作者说"情况并非总是如此"(第3段第1行)意味着什么? A) 有雄心的人可能没有更大的成功机会。 B) 有雄心的人可能没有更多积极品质。 C) 企业家的雄心带来的好处和坏处一样多。 D) 企业家更天然地被驱使走向成功。

questions.q: What does the author imply by saying "this isn't always the case" (Line 1, Para. 3)?
options: Ambitious people may not have a greater chance of success.
Ambitious people may not have more positive qualities.
Entrepreneurs' ambition does as much good as harm.
Entrepreneurs are more naturally driven to success.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author imply by saying "this isn't always the case" 用 imply by saying 问一个具体句子的含义，要求理解 this 指代什么、否定的是什么，属词义句意题。

【拆句】题干主干 What does the author imply，by saying "..." 是方式状语；关键在引文里的 this 是指代词，须回原文找它替代的上文内容；isn't always 是部分否定，意为"并非总 是"，不是全盘否定。 52. What does the author imply by saying "this isn't always the case" (Line 1, Para. 3)? A) Ambitious people may not have a greater chance of success. B) Ambitious people may not have more positive qualities. C) Entrepreneurs' ambition does as much good as harm. D) Entrepreneurs are more naturally driven to success.

【定位】Actually, this isn't always the case. 实际上，情况并非总是如此。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 you are more likely to succeed ↔may not have a greater chance of success 选项 Ambitious people may not have a greater chance of success 正是"this（野心 者更易成功）＋部分否定"的还原，与预判一致。 B) 偷换概念 this 指代的是"更易成功"，并非"积极特质"；选项 may not have more positive qualities 把否定矛头指向上一段的 positive quality，找错了 this 的指代。 C) 与原文相反 原文只说极端野心 may end up doing more harm than good（弊"大于"利），选项 却说 does as much good as harm（利害"相当"），把"大于"篡改成"相等"。 D) 与原文相反 选项 more naturally driven to success 几乎照搬上文 more naturally driven to set goals，可这恰是本句要否定的观点，方向正好相反。 作者认为对于成为成功的企业家来说,什么是极其重要的? A) 坚持自己最初的愿景。 B) 能够适应新的情况。 C) 坚定地专注于某一特定目标。 D) 避免在职业方向上发生剧烈变化。

questions.q: What does the author say is of extreme importance for one to become a successful entrepreneur?
options: Holding on to one's original vision.
Being able to adapt to new situations.
Focusing determinedly on one particular goal.
Avoiding radical change in one's career direction.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author say is of extreme importance 用 say 直问作者明说的内容， 答案是原文一句强调重要性的话，属细节题。

【拆句】题干 What does the author say is of extreme importance for one to become a successful entrepreneur?，主干是 What...is of extreme importance；of+抽象名词等于 形容词，of extreme importance＝extremely important；for one to become... 是不定 式目的状语，指明"为了成为成功创业者"。

【定位】This is problematic because it hinders your ability to adapt to new circumstances, which is vital if you want to be a successful entrepreneur. 这是有问题的，因为它会损害你适应新环境的能力，而这种能力对于想成为成功创业者的人 至关重要。 53. What does the author say is of extreme importance for one to become a successful entrepreneur? A) Holding on to one's original vision. B) Being able to adapt to new situations. C) Focusing determinedly on one particular goal. D) Avoiding radical change in one's career direction.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文说过度野心导致 focus too determinedly on one particular vision 反而有害，需 straying from your original vision；选项 Holding on to one's original vision（死守 原愿景）正是文章要批评的做法。 B) ✓ 正确 adapt to new circumstances ↔adapt to new situations 选项 Being able to adapt to new situations 与预判"适应新环境的能力"几乎逐词对 应，确为答案。 C) 与原文相反 选项 Focusing determinedly on one particular goal 直接抄自 focus too determinedly on one particular vision，而原文说这是过度野心的"副作用"，绝非"极 其重要"之事。 D) 与原文相反 原文说有时须 change direction"改变方向"，选项却说 Avoiding radical change in one's career direction"避免大改方向"，与文意相左。 最有雄心的企业家如何看待他们事业中的失败? A) 失败会让他们认清现实。 B) 失败是他们必须学习的一课。 C) 失败意味着他们职业生涯的终结。 D) 失败会导致缓慢的恢复。

questions.q: How do the most ambitious entrepreneurs regard failure in their endeavor?
options: It will awaken them to reality.
It is a lesson they have to learn.
It means the end of their career.
It will result in a slow recovery.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 How do the most ambitious entrepreneurs regard failure 问一个明确群体对失败 的态度，原文有明文表述，属细节题。

【拆句】题干 How do the most ambitious entrepreneurs regard failure in their endeavor?， regard sth 意为"看待某事"，in their endeavor（在其奋斗中）是范围状语；结构清晰、无 陷阱。

【定位】Unfortunately, for the most ambitious entrepreneurs, a failure is seen as disastrous, and impossible to recover from. 不幸的是，对那些野心最大的创业者来说，一次失败被视为灾难性的、且无法翻身的。 54. How do the most ambitious entrepreneurs regard failure in their endeavor? A) It will awaken them to reality. B) It is a lesson they have to learn. C) It means the end of their career. D) It will result in a slow recovery.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 awaken them to reality 对应的是第六段 failure is viewed as something closer to reality，那讲的是"野心有限者"，而非题干问的"野心最大者"。 B) 张冠李戴 a lesson they have to learn 对应第六段 every failure you survive is a learning experience，同样是说"野心有限者"，张冠李戴。 C) ✓ 正确 disastrous, and impossible to recover from ↔means the end of their career 选项 It means the end of their career 把"灾难、无法恢复"提炼成"事业到头"，与预判 一致，确为答案。 D) 与原文相反 原文说 impossible to recover from"无法恢复"，选项却说 result in a slow recovery"导致缓慢恢复"，恢复从"不可能"被偷改成"慢"。 关于雄心,作者建议我们做什么? A) 区分传统成功与我们的人生目标。 B) 效仿最有雄心的企业家的榜样。 C) 创业时避免承担不必要的风险。 D) 将健康和幸福置于物质成功之上。

questions.q: What does the author advise us to do concerning ambition?
options: Distinguish between conventional success and our life goal.
Follow the example of the most ambitious entrepreneurs.
Avoid taking unnecessary risks when starting a business.
Prioritize health and happiness over material success.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author advise us to do concerning ambition? 问作者的建议，原文 未必有一句直说"我建议你……"，需综合全文对野心利弊的论述提炼，属推断题。

【拆句】题干 What does the author advise us to do concerning ambition?，advise sb to do 意为"建议某人做某事"，concerning ambition（关于野心）是话题状语；结构平铺直叙、 无陷阱。 55. What does the author advise us to do concerning ambition? A) Distinguish between conventional success and our life goal. B) Follow the example of the most ambitious entrepreneurs. C) Avoid taking unnecessary risks when starting a business. D) Prioritize health and happiness over material success.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文要区分的是 conventional "success" 与 health and happiness，选项 Distinguish between conventional success and our life goal 把后一项换成了文中没有的"人生目 标"，区分对象被改错。 B) 与原文相反 全文都在指出 the most ambitious entrepreneurs 看待失败的方式有害，选项 Follow the example of the most ambitious entrepreneurs 却劝人效仿他们，与作者立场正 相反。 C) 以偏概全 Avoid taking unnecessary risks 只关乎 take more risks 这一点，并非全文劝诫的落 脚；作者最终落点是健康幸福，而非"少冒险"，以偏概全且无中生有。 D) ✓ 正确 such success means nothing for their health and happiness—and if you don't have health and happiness, what else could possibly matter? ↔Prioritize health and happiness over material success 选项 Prioritize health and happiness over material success 与主线"健康幸福重于成 功"吻合，且统摄全文对过度野心的批评，是建议题应有的全局答案。

items.title: 2023年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit. For more than a decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans fat, and accused of contributing to climate change.

P2 Supermarkets can technically be defined as giants housing 15,000 to 60,000 different products. The revolutionary idea of a self-service grocery, where people could hunt and gather food from aisles rather than asking a clerk to fetch items from behind a counter, first came about in America. There is some debate about which was the very first, but over the years a consensus has built around King Kullen Supermarket, founded in New York in 1930.

P3 For some 300 years, Americans had fed themselves from small stores and public markets. Shopping for food involved mud, noisy chickens, clouds of flies, nasty smells, bargaining, and getting short-changed. The supermarket imitated the Fordist factory, with its emphasis on efficiency and standardization, and reimagined it as a place to buy food. Supermarkets may not feel cutting-edge now, but they were a revolution in distribution at the time. They were such strange marvels that, on her first official state visit to the United States in 1957, Queen Elizabeth II insisted on an impromptu(即兴的) tour of a suburban-Maryland Giant Food.

P4 The typical supermarket layout has barely changed over the past 90 years. Most stores open with flowers, fruit and vegetables at the front as a breath of freshness to arouse our appetite. Meanwhile, they keep the milk, eggs, and other daily basics all the way back so you'll travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way.

P5 In the early days, as the supermarket multiplied, so did our suspicion of it. We have long feared that this "revolution in distribution" uses corporate black magic on our appetite. The book The Hidden Persuaders, published in 1957, warned that supermarkets were putting women in a "hypnoidal trance(催眠恍惚状态)," causing them to wander aisles bumping into boxes and "picking things off shelves at random."

questions.q: What problem have supermarkets been facing?
options: They are actually on the way to bankruptcy.
They have been losing customers and profits.
They are forced to use e-commerce strategies.
They have difficulty adapting to climate change.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What problem have supermarkets been facing? 直接问一个具体事实——超市在面 临什么难处，答案应能在原文找到明确对应句。 46. What problem have supermarkets been facing? A) They are actually on the way to bankruptcy. B) They have been losing customers and profits. C) They are forced to use e-commerce strategies. D) They have difficulty adapting to climate change.

【拆句】What problem have supermarkets been facing? 是一个 what 引导的特殊疑问句，主干 是"超市一直在面对什么难处"，have been facing 是现在完成进行时，强调"长期、持续"在 面对，这个时态暗示原文会有 long/for more than a decade 一类的长期信号词，结构本 身无陷阱。

【定位】Supermarkets have long been suffering as one of the thinnest-margined businesses in existence and one of the least-looked-forward-to places to work or visit. For more than a decade, they have been under attack from e-commerce giants, blamed for making Americans fat, and accused of contributing to climate change. 长期以来，超市一直是利润最薄的行业之一，也是人们最不愿去工作或光顾的场所之一。十 多年来，它们一直受到电商巨头的攻击，被指责让美国人发胖，还被指控加剧气候变化。

【选项】A) 过度推断 原文只说超市利润薄、处境难，从未说它"正走向破产"；on the way to bankruptcy 把"利润薄"夸大成"濒临破产"，程度严重超出原文。 B) ✓ 正确 thinnest-margined businesses ↔losing customers and profits under attack from e-commerce giants ↔losing customers 预判落在"生意难做、客流利润受损"，四个选项里只有 They have been losing customers and profits. 同时覆盖了原文的"利润薄"和"受电商攻击"，与预判最契合。 C) 偷换概念 原文说超市"受电商攻击"，并没说它们"被迫去采用电商策略"；forced to use e- commerce strategies 把"被攻击"偷换成"被迫效仿"，是原文未提的内容。 D) 偷换概念 原文是超市"被指责加剧气候变化"（超市是被指责方），而 have difficulty adapting to climate change 说成"超市难以适应气候变化"，把"被指责制造问题"换成了"自己适应 不了"。 文章对自助式杂货店这一理念有何评价? A) 它是由King Kullen提出的。 B) 它起源于美国。 C) 它一直处于持续争论之中。 D) 它即使在今天也被证明是革命性的。

questions.q: What does the passage say about the idea of a self-service grocery?
options: It was put forward by King Kullen.
It originated in the United States.
It has been under constant debate.
It proves revolutionary even today.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the passage say about the idea of a self-service grocery? 问的是原文 就这个想法"说了什么"，是对原文具体陈述的核对，属细节题。 47. What does the passage say about the idea of a self-service grocery? A) It was put forward by King Kullen. B) It originated in the United States. C) It has been under constant debate. D) It proves revolutionary even today.

【拆句】What does the passage say about the idea of a self-service grocery? 主干是"原文关于 这个想法说了什么"，of the idea of a self-service grocery 是层层嵌套的 of 介词短语作后 置定语，只是在限定"哪个想法"，剥掉修饰后主干很清楚，无理解陷阱。

【定位】The revolutionary idea of a self-service grocery, where people could hunt and gather food from aisles rather than asking a clerk to fetch items from behind a counter, first came about in America. 让人们能在货架间自行寻找采集食物、而不必请店员从柜台后取货的自助式杂货这一革命性 想法，最早出现在美国。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 原文说金库伦是公认的"第一家超市"，并未说这个"想法"是金库伦"提出"的；put forward by King Kullen 把"第一家店"错安成"想法的提出者"。 B) ✓ 正确 first came about in America ↔It originated in the United States. 预判核心是"起源地是美国"，四项里只有 It originated in the United States. 准确对应 定位句的起源信息，故锁定。 C) 偷换概念 原文 some debate about which was the very first 争论的是"哪家是第一家店"，而 非"这个想法本身"；under constant debate 把争论对象由"谁是第一家"偷换成"这个 想法"。 D) 与原文相反 原文只说该想法当年是 revolutionary，并称超市 may not feel cutting-edge now （如今未必前沿），并无"至今仍具革命性"之说；proves revolutionary even today 是 原文没有的论断。 超市通过采用福特主义工厂方式做了什么? A) 它们在许多方面使传统杂货店现代化。 B) 它们引入了最前沿的店面布局。 C) 它们提高了所售食品的质量。 D) 它们彻底改变了商品分销方式。

questions.q: What did supermarkets do by adopting the Fordist factory approach?
options: They modernized traditional groceries in many ways.
They introduced cutting-edge layout of their stores.
They improved the quality of the food they sold.
They revolutionized the distribution of goods.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What did supermarkets do by adopting the Fordist factory approach? 问超市靠 这一做法"做成了什么"，是对原文一个具体结果的核对，属细节题。

【拆句】What did supermarkets do by adopting the Fordist factory approach? 主干是"超市做 了什么"，by adopting... 是 by + 动名词的方式状语，表示"通过采用福特式工厂做法这一 手段"，by 在此不是"被"而是"通过"，基础薄弱者易误读，点明即可。 48. What did supermarkets do by adopting the Fordist factory approach? A) They modernized traditional groceries in many ways. B) They introduced cutting-edge layout of their stores. C) They improved the quality of the food they sold. D) They revolutionized the distribution of goods.

【定位】The supermarket imitated the Fordist factory, with its emphasis on efficiency and standardization, and reimagined it as a place to buy food. Supermarkets may not feel cutting- edge now, but they were a revolution in distribution at the time. 超市模仿了讲求效率与标准化的福特式工厂，并把它重新设想成一个买食物的地方。超市如 今也许感觉不再前沿，但它们在当时是分销领域的一场革命。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只说超市模仿福特工厂、成为分销革命，没说它"在许多方面把传统杂货店现代 化"；modernized traditional groceries in many ways 是原文未提的笼统说法。 B) 与原文相反 原文紧接着说超市 may not feel cutting-edge now（如今未必前沿），且布局九十年 几乎没变，并非"引入了前沿布局"；cutting-edge layout 与原文意思相反。 C) 无中生有 原文谈的是分销方式的革命，全程未涉及"食品质量"的提升；improved the quality of the food 在原文找不到任何依据。 D) ✓ 正确 a revolution in distribution ↔They revolutionized the distribution of goods. 预判核心是"在分销上掀起革命"，四项里只有 They revolutionized the distribution of goods. 与定位句 a revolution in distribution 直接等值，故锁定。 典型的超市布局旨在做什么? A) 激发顾客购买鲜花、水果和蔬菜的欲望。 B) 为顾客提供便捷途径获取他们想购买的商品。 C) 诱导顾客进行更多计划外购买。 D) 使顾客获得更愉快的购物体验。

questions.q: What is the typical supermarket layout intended to do?
options: Arouse customers' appetite to buy flowers, fruit and vegetables.
Provide customers easy access to items they want to buy.
Induce customers to make more unplanned purchases.
Enable customers to have a more enjoyable shopping experience.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the typical supermarket layout intended to do? 问布局的具体意图，是对 原文一处目的陈述的核对，属细节题。

【拆句】What is the typical supermarket layout intended to do? 主干是"布局意在做什么"，be intended to do 是"被设计用来做……"的固定结构，是被动语态，主语 layout 是被设计的 对象，看懂这个被动是解题前提，结构上无其他陷阱。

【定位】Meanwhile, they keep the milk, eggs, and other daily basics all the way back so you'll travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way. 与此同时，超市把牛奶、鸡蛋等日用必需品全放在最里面，好让你穿过尽可能多的店面，一 路上被诱惑。 49. What is the typical supermarket layout intended to do? A) Arouse customers' appetite to buy flowers, fruit and vegetables. B) Provide customers easy access to items they want to buy. C) Induce customers to make more unplanned purchases. D) Enable customers to have a more enjoyable shopping experience.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 原文说前端摆鲜花果蔬只是 a breath of freshness to arouse our appetite（唤起食 欲）的一个手段，最终目的是让人走遍全店；appetite to buy flowers, fruit and vegetables 把局部手段当成了整体布局的意图。 B) 与原文相反 原文布局恰恰把必需品放到最里、逼顾客绕远，并非"方便顾客买想买的东西"；easy access to items they want to buy 与原文意图相反。 C) ✓ 正确 travel through as much of the store as possible, and be tempted along the way ↔ Induce customers to make more unplanned purchases. 预判核心是"让顾客多走多买计划外的东西"，四项里只有 Induce customers to make more unplanned purchases. 抓住了布局的真实意图，故锁定。 D) 无中生有 原文讲的是诱导顾客多买，从未说布局是为"让购物更愉快"；more enjoyable shopping experience 是原文没有的说法。 人们长期以来对超市有什么担忧? A) 它们使用狡猾的策略来促进业务。 B) 它们将完全取代当地杂货店。 C) 它们对陈列的商品施加企业黑魔法。 D) 它们利用女性购物者的弱点。

questions.q: What have people long feared about supermarkets?
options: They use tricky strategies to promote their business.
They are going to replace the local groceries entirely.
They apply corporate black magic to the goods on display.
They take advantage of the weaknesses of women shoppers.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What have people long feared about supermarkets? 问人们长期害怕的具体内 容，是对原文一处陈述的核对，属细节题。

【拆句】What have people long feared about supermarkets? 主干是"人们长期害怕超市什么"， have long feared 是现在完成时夹一个副词 long，强调"长久以来一直害怕"，about supermarkets 是 fear 的对象，结构清楚无陷阱。

【定位】We have long feared that this "revolution in distribution" uses corporate black magic on our appetite. 长期以来我们一直害怕，这场"分销革命"在用企业的黑魔法操纵我们的食欲。 50. What have people long feared about supermarkets? A) They use tricky strategies to promote their business. B) They are going to replace the local groceries entirely. C) They apply corporate black magic to the goods on display. D) They take advantage of the weaknesses of women shoppers.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 uses corporate black magic on our appetite ↔ They use tricky strategies to promote their business. 预判核心是"用隐秘手段操纵食欲"，四项里只有 They use tricky strategies to promote their business. 把"黑魔法"这一比喻还原为"狡猾手段"，与定位句契合，故 锁定。 B) 无中生有 原文讲的是人们怕超市操纵食欲，全程未提"取代本地杂货店"；replace the local groceries entirely 是原文没有的内容。 C) 偷换概念 原文是黑魔法用在 our appetite（我们的食欲）上，而 black magic to the goods on display 把作用对象偷换成"陈列的商品"，对象张冠李戴。 D) 以偏概全 关于女性的内容出自被引用的《隐形说客》一书、只是个例证，并非人们"长期"害怕的 核心；weaknesses of women shoppers 拿书中一个局部例子当成了普遍的担忧。

items.title: 2023年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 The traditional school year, with three months of vacation every summer, was first implemented when America was an agricultural society and the summer months were needed for farm work. Since then, we've completely changed as a nation. Students no longer spend summers farming, but they aren't in school, either. The average American student receives 13 weeks off from school each calendar year- with about 11 of those during the summer. Few other countries have more than seven weeks off in a school calendar.

P2 With the U.S. lagging behind other countries in academics, it's time to consider year-round schooling. One benefit of this change is that students will not fall victim to the "summer slide," or the well-documented phenomenon where students forget some of the knowledge they have acquired when too much time is taken off from school. Decades of research shows that it can take from 8 to 13 weeks at the beginning of every school year for students to get back to where they were before the summer holiday.

P3 But year-round schooling isn't just about academics. Teachers and students experience a closer relationship in year-round schools than they do in traditional schools and, in the absence of any long- term break, students do not feel detached from the school environment. These closer bonds and greater attachment pay off. Research shows that students in year-round schools are more self-confident and feel more positive about their schooling experience.

P4 But don't kids need time to relax? Some childhood development experts believe that time off from school is vital to healthy development as kids are not designed to spend so much of their time inside classrooms and the summer break provides a perfect opportunity to get outside. The problem with this argument is that most children aren't playing outside or even spending time with other kids. While some children visit summer camps, most stay at home, watching TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits them.

P5 The U.S. has changed from a farming economy to a knowledge- and innovation-based economy, so it makes sense for the school year to change as well.

questions.q: Why did America's traditional school year have a three-month summer vacation?
options: Students needed to help with farm work.
Students needed time to learn necessary farming skills.
The agricultural society then attached less importance to academics.
America lagged behind other countries in making a scientific school calendar.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did America's traditional school year have a three-month summer vacation? 问 一个写在文中的具体事实原因，答案应能在原文直接找到。

【拆句】Q51 是一个 Why 引导的特殊疑问句，主干就是 school year have a three-month summer vacation，没有从句也没有否定，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱。 51. Why did America's traditional school year have a three-month summer vacation? A) Students needed to help with farm work. B) Students needed time to learn necessary farming skills. C) The agricultural society then attached less importance to academics. D) America lagged behind other countries in making a scientific school calendar.

【定位】The traditional school year, with three months of vacation every summer, was first implemented when America was an agricultural society and the summer months were needed for farm work. 传统学年带有每年夏季三个月假期，它最初设立于美国还是农业社会、夏季几个月需要用于 农活的时候。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the summer months were needed for farm work ↔Students needed to help with farm work 预判的"夏天要干农活"与 Students needed to help with farm work 完全吻合，故锁定 此项。 B) 无中生有 原文只说夏季需要去做农活，从未提学生需要时间去"学习"农业技能，learn necessary farming skills 文中没有依据。 C) 无中生有 原文只说当时是农业社会、夏天要务农，并未说农业社会 attached less importance to academics，这是文中没有的因果。 D) 张冠李戴 America lagged behind other countries 出自第二段 With the U.S. lagging behind other countries in academics，那是"如今"现状，并非当初设三个月暑假的原因，张冠 李戴。 除了提高学习成绩之外,全年制教育还会给学生带来什么好处? A) 它将帮助他们回到课程开始的地方。 B) 它将使他们能够消化所学的知识。 C) 它将使他们熟悉学校环境。 D) 它将加强他们与教师的关系。

questions.q: What benefit will year-round schooling bring students in addition to improving their learning?
options: It will help them get back to where their lessons started.
It will enable them to absorb what they have learned.
It will familiarize them with the school environment.
It will strengthen their relationship with teachers.
questions.explain:
【判型】What benefit will year-round schooling bring students in addition to improving their learning? 问一项写在文中的具体好处，属可直接核对的事实。

【拆句】Q52 主干是 What benefit will year-round schooling bring students，后接介词短语 in addition to improving their learning 作限定，提醒答案要排除学业类好处，是理解 关键。 52. What benefit will year-round schooling bring students in addition to improving their learning? A) It will help them get back to where their lessons started. B) It will enable them to absorb what they have learned. C) It will familiarize them with the school environment. D) It will strengthen their relationship with teachers.

【定位】But year-round schooling isn't just about academics. Teachers and students experience a closer relationship in year-round schools than they do in traditional schools and, in the absence of any long-term break, students do not feel detached from the school environment. 但全年制不仅仅关乎学业。在全年制学校里，师生关系比在传统学校里更亲近，而且由于没 有任何长期假期，学生不会感到与校园环境疏离。

【选项】A) 答非所问 get back to where their lessons started 套用第二段 get back to where they were， 那讲的是暑期遗忘后补回进度，属学业范畴，被题干限定排除，且原文是消除这一损耗 而非"帮学生回到起点"。 B) 答非所问 absorb what they have learned 仍是讲学习吸收，属 improving their learning 范 畴，被题干"除学业外"排除。 C) 偷换概念 原文说的是学生 do not feel detached from the school environment（不疏离），并 非 familiarize them with the school environment（使其熟悉环境），把"不疏远"偷 换成"变熟悉"。 D) ✓ 正确 Teachers and students experience a closer relationship ↔ strengthen their relationship with teachers 预判的"师生关系更近"正对应 strengthen their relationship with teachers，且它落 在"学业之外"的范围内，故选此项。 一些儿童发展专家对漫长的暑假有什么看法? A) 它满足了学生自主学习的需求。 B) 它使学生能够了解外部世界。 C) 它满足了学生希望在家待更长时间的愿望。 D) 它有助于学生的健康成长。

questions.q: What do some childhood development experts believe about the long summer vacation?
options: It meets students' need to study on their own.
It enables students to learn about the outside world.
It satisfies students' desire to stay longer at home.
It contributes to students' healthy growth.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do some childhood development experts believe about the long summer vacation? 问的是专家在文中直接表述的观点，可逐字核对，不需要读者推断。

【拆句】Q53 主干 What do some childhood development experts believe，后接 about the long summer vacation 点明评论对象；注意主语是 experts 而非作者，是"这话谁说的"的 关键。 53. What do some childhood development experts believe about the long summer vacation? A) It meets students' need to study on their own. B) It enables students to learn about the outside world. C) It satisfies students' desire to stay longer at home. D) It contributes to students' healthy growth.

【定位】Some childhood development experts believe that time off from school is vital to healthy development as kids are not designed to spend so much of their time inside classrooms and the summer break provides a perfect opportunity to get outside. 一些儿童发展专家认为，离开学校的休息时间对健康成长至关重要，因为孩子天生不适合把 这么多时间花在教室里，而暑假正好提供了走到户外的绝佳机会。

【选项】A) 无中生有 专家强调的是休息和户外，从未说放假满足学生 study on their own（自学）的需要， 原文无此意。 B) 过度推断 原文只说暑假给孩子 a perfect opportunity to get outside（到户外的机会），并不 等于 learn about the outside world（了解外部世界），后者把"到户外"拔高成"认识 世界"。 C) 张冠李戴 专家观点里没有"满足学生 stay longer at home"的说法；待在家看电视是后文作者反驳 时提到的现实，并非专家所赞同的需求。 D) ✓ 正确 time off from school is vital to healthy development ↔ It contributes to students' healthy growth 预判的"放假利于健康成长"正对应 It contributes to students' healthy growth，故选 此项。 反对专家关于漫长暑假观点的论据是什么? A) 它对大多数学生没什么好处。 B) 它只让少数在户外玩耍的学生受益。 C) 它导致学生忽视学业。 D) 它使学生沉迷于电脑游戏。

questions.q: What is the argument against the experts' idea of a long summer vacation?
options: It does little good to most students.
It benefits few students playing outside.
It leads students to neglect their studies.
It makes students addicted to computer games.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the argument against the experts' idea of a long summer vacation? 问一个写 在文中的具体反驳理由，可直接核对。

【拆句】Q54 主干 What is the argument against the experts' idea，介词 against 决定方向 是"反对专家"；读懂 against 才不会把专家自己的话误当反驳，是理解关键。 54. What is the argument against the experts' idea of a long summer vacation? A) It does little good to most students. B) It benefits few students playing outside. C) It leads students to neglect their studies. D) It makes students addicted to computer games.

【定位】The problem with this argument is that most children aren't playing outside or even spending time with other kids. While some children visit summer camps, most stay at home, watching TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits them. 这个论点的问题在于，大多数孩子并没有在户外玩耍，甚至没有和别的孩子相处。虽然有些 孩子去参加夏令营，但多数人待在家里看电视或玩电子设备上的游戏，这对他们几乎没有 好处。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 most stay at home, watching TV or playing games on electronic devices, which hardly benefits them ↔It does little good to most students 预判的"对多数孩子没好处"正对应 It does little good to most students，故选此项。 B) 以偏概全 原文 hardly benefits them 说的是待在家的"多数"孩子没好处，benefits few students playing outside 却把对象缩成"在外面玩的少数"，偷改了范围。 C) 无中生有 作者反驳讲的是放假对孩子无益，并未说放假让学生 neglect their studies（荒废学 业），文中无此意。 D) 以偏概全 原文把看电视和玩电子设备游戏并列为现象之一，并未断言放假使学生 addicted to computer games（沉迷电脑游戏），把众多居家活动之一夸成"上瘾"。 作者如何看待当今美国的传统学年? A) 有充分根据的。 B) 受文化束缚的。 C) 过时的。 D) 受欢迎的。

questions.q: What does the author think of the traditional school year in the U.S. today?
options: Well-grounded.
Culture-bound.
Outdated.
Welcomed.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think of the traditional school year in the U.S. today? 问的是作 者对旧学制的整体评价，需通览全文立场而非某句。

【拆句】Q55 主干 What does the author think of the traditional school year，关键是 today ——问的是"在今天看来"旧学制如何，提示要结合文章"时代已变"的论调判断，是解题 关键。 55. What does the author think of the traditional school year in the U.S. today? A) Well-grounded. B) Culture-bound. C) Outdated. D) Welcomed.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Well-grounded（有充分根据的）是褒义，意味旧学制合理；而作者全篇主张它该改， 态度恰好相反。 B) 无中生有 文章把旧学制归因于"农业经济"这一时代背景，并未从"文化"角度评价，Culture- bound（受文化局限）在原文找不到落点。 C) ✓ 正确 The U.S. has changed from a farming economy to a knowledge- and innovation-based economy, so it makes sense for the school year to change as well ↔Outdated 预判的"旧学制已不合时宜、该改"与 Outdated 一词对应，故选此项。 D) 与原文相反 Welcomed（受欢迎的）是褒义，暗示作者赞许旧学制；而作者主张它该改、显然不持 欢迎态度，方向相反。

items.title: 2023年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 Team-building exercises have become popular for managers trying to increase organisational and team harmony and productivity. Unfortunately many employees resent compulsory bonding and often regard these exercises as a nuisance.

P2 A paper published this week by University of Sydney researchers in Social Networks has reported participants' feelings about team-building interventions(干预), revealing ethical implications in forcing employees to take part.

P3 "Many people see team-building activities as a waste of time, so we decided to look in more depth at what's behind this," said the paper's lead researcher, Dr. Peter Matous.

P4 "Teams are formed, combined and restructured. Staff are relocated and office spaces redesigned. All this is done with the aim of improving workplace efficiency, collaboration and cohesion. But does any of this work?" said Dr. Matous.

P5 The study found that team-building exercises which focused on the sharing of and intervening into personal attitudes and relationships between team members were considered too heavy-handed and intrusive, although the researchers say some degree of openness and vulnerability is often necessary to make deep, effective connections with colleagues.

P6 "Some participants were against team-building exercises because they were implicitly compulsory. They didn't welcome management's interest in their lives beyond their direct work performance," said Matous. "Many people don't want to be forced into having fun or making friends, especially not on top of their busy jobs. They feel management is being too nosy or trying to control their lives too much."

P7 In this study the researchers recommended a self-disclosure(表露) approach where participants were guided through a series of questions that allowed them to increasingly disclose personal information and values. The method is well-tested and has been shown to increase interpersonal closeness. However, to be successful it must be voluntary.

P8 The researchers said there are numerous schools of thought that propose differing psychological methods for strengthening relationships. "With caution, many relational methods to improve teams and organisations can be borrowed from other fields. The question is how to apply them effectively to strengthen an entire collective, which is more than just the sum of individual relationships," said Dr. Matous.

questions.q: Why are many employees opposed to team-building exercises?
options: They consider such exercises annoying.
They deem these exercises counter-productive.
They see such exercises as harmful to harmony.
They find these exercises too demanding.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why are many employees opposed to team-building exercises? 用 Why 提问，问的是 原文已写明的具体理由，不需要跨段推理。

【拆句】题干 Why are many employees opposed to team-building exercises? 是一般疑问句， 主干为员工反对团建练习，be opposed to 是固定搭配表示反对、抵触，结构平铺直叙，无 陷阱。

【定位】Unfortunately many employees resent compulsory bonding and often regard these exercises as a nuisance. 遗憾的是，许多员工反感被强制团建，并常把这些练习视为一种麻烦。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 regard these exercises as a nuisance ↔consider such exercises annoying resent ↔annoying 预判员工嫌团建烦人，They consider such exercises annoying 正是定位句 regard these exercises as a nuisance 的同义改写，故锁定该项。 B) 无中生有 counter-productive 指适得其反、降低生产力，原文只说员工嫌烦，从未说团建会起反 作用，属凭空添加。 C) 与原文相反 harmful to harmony 称团建有害于和谐，但原文 increase organisational and team harmony 说团建本意是增进和谐，选项把目的反说成危害。 D) 答非所问 too demanding 指要求过高、太费力，这是 on top of their busy jobs 一带而过的另 一层意思，并非第 46 题问的反对的主要原因。 46. Why are many employees opposed to team-building exercises? A) They consider such exercises annoying. B) They deem these exercises counter-productive. C) They see such exercises as harmful to harmony. D) They find these exercises too demanding. Matous博士和他的团队做了什么来查明团队建设活动是否能提高生产力? A) 他们重新安置了团队领导及其办公室。 B) 他们重新安排了员工和办公空间。 C) 他们重新设计了员工的工作时间表。 D) 他们重新引入了一些凝聚性活动。

questions.q: What did Dr. Matous and his team do to find out whether team-building activities would improve
options: They relocated team leaders and their offices.
They rearranged the staff and office spaces.
They redesigned the staff's work schedules.
They reintroduced some cohesive activities.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did Dr. Matous and his team do 问的是研究团队具体做了什么，答案是原文明写的 动作清单，属事实查找。

【拆句】题干主干是 What did Dr. Matous and his team do，后接不定式目的状语 to find out whether...，其中 whether 引导宾语从句表示是否提升效率；理清主干问做法、状语说目 的，即无障碍。

【定位】Teams are formed, combined and restructured. Staff are relocated and office spaces redesigned. All this is done with the aim of improving workplace efficiency, collaboration and cohesion. 团队被组建、合并、重组。员工被调岗，办公空间被重新设计。所有这些都是为了提升工作 效率、协作与凝聚力。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 relocated team leaders 只说调动了团队领导，而原文 Staff are relocated 指全体员 工，选项把范围悄悄缩小到领导一类人。 B) ✓ 正确 Staff are relocated ↔rearranged the staff office spaces redesigned ↔office spaces 预判为调动员工与办公空间，They rearranged the staff and office spaces 把两个动 作合并改写，与定位句一一对应，故锁定该项。 C) 偷换概念 redesigned the staff's work schedules 说重新设计的是工作日程，但原文 redesigned 的对象是 office spaces 办公空间，选项偷换了被改造的对象。 D) 无中生有 reintroduced some cohesive activities 说重新引入凝聚性活动，原文从未提及重新引 入活动这一动作，纯属添加。 47. What did Dr. Matous and his team do to find out whether team-building activities would improve productivity? A) They relocated team leaders and their offices. B) They rearranged the staff and office spaces. C) They redesigned the staff's work schedules. D) They reintroduced some cohesive activities. Matous团队的研究对一些团队建设活动有什么发现? A) 它们旨在分享个人态度和关系。 B) 它们隐含地增加了团队成员的脆弱性。 C) 它们总是加强了同事之间的联系。 D) 它们被视为对员工私人生活的侵扰。

questions.q: What did the study by Matous' team find about some team-building exercises?
options: They were intended to share personal attitudes and relationships.
They implicitly added to the vulnerability of team members.
They invariably strengthened connections among colleagues.
They were regarded as an intrusion into employees' private lives.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the study by Matous' team find about some team-building exercises? 问的 是研究已写明的发现，可直接定位明文结论，属细节查找。

【拆句】题干 What did the study by Matous' team find about some team-building exercises? 主干为研究发现了什么，about 引出对象范围；注意 some 限定的是部分团建练习而非全 部，是本题理解关键。

【定位】The study found that team-building exercises which focused on the sharing of and intervening into personal attitudes and relationships between team members were considered too heavy- handed and intrusive, although the researchers say some degree of openness and vulnerability is often necessary to make deep, effective connections with colleagues. 研究发现，那些聚焦于分享并干预团队成员个人态度与关系的团建练习，被认为过于强硬且 具有侵入性，尽管研究者表示，某种程度的开放与脆弱往往是与同事建立深层有效联系所必 需的。 48. What did the study by Matous' team find about some team-building exercises? A) They were intended to share personal attitudes and relationships. B) They implicitly added to the vulnerability of team members. C) They invariably strengthened connections among colleagues. D) They were regarded as an intrusion into employees' private lives.

【选项】A) 答非所问 intended to share personal attitudes and relationships 说团建意在分享个人态度关 系，但 focused on the sharing of... 是研究者对这类团建特征的客观描述，且本题问的 是研究的发现而非团建的意图。 B) 与原文相反 added to the vulnerability 称团建增加了成员的脆弱，但原文 some degree of...vulnerability is often necessary 说一定程度的脆弱是建立联系所必需的，并非团建 恶意制造脆弱。 C) 过度推断 invariably strengthened connections 说团建无一例外地增进了联系，但原文只说脆 弱开放是建立联系所必需的前提，且整段强调这类团建被嫌侵入，并未说它总能增进 联系。 D) ✓ 正确 intrusive ↔an intrusion into employees' private lives interest in their lives beyond their direct work performance ↔into employees' private lives 预判某团建被嫌强硬侵入，They were regarded as an intrusion into employees' private lives 把 intrusive 与 P6 对私生活的窥探合并改写，完全对应。 自我披露方法如何能够成功增进人际亲密度? A) 通过允许参与者自由表达自己。 B) 通过将其应用于自愿参与的员工。 C) 通过恰当安排参与者面对的问题顺序。 D) 通过引导员工完成团队建设中的一系列步骤。

questions.q: How can the self-disclosure approach succeed in increasing interpersonal closeness?
options: By allowing participants freedom to express themselves.
By applying it to employees who volunteer to participate.
By arranging in proper order the questions participants face.
By guiding employees through a series of steps in team building.
questions.explain:
【判型】How can the self-disclosure approach succeed in increasing interpersonal closeness? 问的是原文明写的成功前提，可直接定位，属细节题。

【拆句】题干 How can the self-disclosure approach succeed in increasing interpersonal closeness? 主干问该方法如何才能成功，succeed in doing 是固定搭配表示成功做到某 事；结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】The method is well-tested and has been shown to increase interpersonal closeness. However, to be successful it must be voluntary. 该方法经过充分检验，已被证明能增进人际亲密。然而，要想成功，它必须是自愿的。 49. How can the self-disclosure approach succeed in increasing interpersonal closeness? A) By allowing participants freedom to express themselves. B) By applying it to employees who volunteer to participate. C) By arranging in proper order the questions participants face. D) By guiding employees through a series of steps in team building.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 freedom to express themselves 说让参与者自由表达，但原文规定的成功条件是 voluntary 自愿参加，而非表达自由，选项偷换了条件的内容。 B) ✓ 正确 it must be voluntary ↔employees who volunteer to participate 预判成功须自愿，By applying it to employees who volunteer to participate 把 voluntary 落实为只对自愿参与者使用，与定位句完全对应。 C) 答非所问 arranging in proper order the questions 说按顺序排好问题，这是 guided through a series of questions 描述的方法本身，而非题干所问的成功前提。 D) 偷换概念 guiding employees through a series of steps in team building 把自我表露法说成团 建中的引导步骤，原文的 a series of questions 是问题不是团建步骤，且仍未触及自愿 这一成功条件。 Matous如何看待从其他领域借鉴的用于加强关系的各种心理学方法? A) 它们必须结合使用才能作用于整个集体。 B) 它们将某些心理方面置于其他方面之上。 C) 它们过于强调个体关系。 D) 它们必须谨慎应用才能有效。

questions.q: What does Matous think of the various psychological methods borrowed from other fields for
options: They must be used in combination for an entire collective.
They prioritise some psychological aspects over others.
They place too much stress on individual relationships.
They have to be applied cautiously to be effective.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Matous think of the various psychological methods... 虽问看法，但 Matous 的观点在原文引语中已明说，可直接定位，按细节题处理。

【拆句】题干 What does Matous think of the various psychological methods borrowed from other fields for strengthening relationships? 主干为 Matous 怎么看这些方法，think of 表示对某事的评价，borrowed... 是后置定语修饰 methods；抓住主干即可。

【定位】"With caution, many relational methods to improve teams and organisations can be borrowed from other fields. The question is how to apply them effectively to strengthen an entire collective, which is more than just the sum of individual relationships," said Dr. Matous. Matous 博士说："谨慎地说，许多用于改善团队与组织的关系方法可以从其他领域借鉴。问 题在于如何有效地运用它们来强化一个整体，而这个整体不只是个体关系的简单相加。" 50. What does Matous think of the various psychological methods borrowed from other fields for strengthening relationships? A) They must be used in combination for an entire collective. B) They prioritise some psychological aspects over others. C) They place too much stress on individual relationships. D) They have to be applied cautiously to be effective.

【选项】A) 过度推断 used in combination for an entire collective 说必须组合使用，但原文 how to apply them effectively to strengthen an entire collective 说的是如何有效运用以强化整 体，并未要求把方法组合起来。 B) 张冠李戴 prioritise some psychological aspects over others 说这些方法偏重某些心理层面， 这呼应的是 numerous schools of thought that propose differing psychological methods，是对各派别的描述，并非 Matous 对借用方法的看法。 C) 与原文相反 place too much stress on individual relationships 说过分强调个体关系，但原文 more than just the sum of individual relationships 恰恰说整体不只是个体关系之 和，提醒不要只看个体，选项把意思说反了。 D) ✓ 正确 With caution ↔applied cautiously how to apply them effectively ↔to be effective 预判须谨慎且讲求有效，They have to be applied cautiously to be effective 同时覆 盖 With caution 与 apply them effectively，故锁定该项。

items.title: 2023年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2023年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 There are close to 58,000 homeless people in Los Angeles county. That's a shocking and tragic number for a region that's home to some of the richest people in the world. At last, the problem became so acute—and so visible—that Los Angeles took extraordinary action. The citizens of this county voted in November 2016 and again in March 2017 to raise their own taxes. The purpose of such action is to fund an enormous multibillion-dollar, 10-year program of housing and social services for the homeless.

P2 As a result, Los Angeles now has its best chance in decades to combat homelessness. This is an opportunity that surely all can agree must not be wasted. It is neither desirable nor morally acceptable nor practical for this county to tolerate the signs of deprivation more commonly associated with the slums(贫民窟) of Rio de Janiero.

P3 How did we get here? For as long as there are homeless people, there is a tendency to blame the victims themselves for their condition—to see their failure to thrive as an issue of character, of moral weakness, of laziness. But contrary to popular belief, the homeless in Los Angeles are not mostly mentally ill or drug addicted or frightening, although a sizable minority meet some of those descriptions. Today, a greater and greater proportion of people living on the streets are there because of bad luck or a series of mistakes, or because the economy forgot them—they lost a job or were evicted(逐出) or fled an abusive marriage just as the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving.

P4 The challenges are enormous, even if everyone is pulling in the same direction. That reality was driven home this month by a new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report showing that the county's homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing.

P5 In the world's richest nation, homelessness on this scale should be shameful and shocking. But most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed. Increasingly, we are uncomfortable, annoyed, disgusted, scared or unaware. Compassion(同情心) is being replaced by resignation.

questions.q: Why did the citizens of Los Angeles vote to raise their own taxes?
options: To combat the county's homelessness.
To reform the county's service system.
To fund the development of local infrastructure.
To narrow the gap between the rich and the poor.
questions.explain:
【判型】Q51 针对"市民投票加税"这一文中明确发生的事件追问原因，答案是文中写死的事实，不需 要推理。

【拆句】Q51 是一个标准疑问句，主干为 Why did the citizens vote to raise their own taxes，其 中 to raise their own taxes 是不定式作 vote 的目的，整句结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】The purpose of such action is to fund an enormous multibillion-dollar, 10-year program of housing and social services for the homeless. 此举的目的是资助一项数十亿美元、为期十年、面向无家可归者的住房与社会服务计划。 51. Why did the citizens of Los Angeles vote to raise their own taxes? A) To combat the county's homelessness. B) To reform the county's service system. C) To fund the development of local infrastructure. D) To narrow the gap between the rich and the poor.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 housing and social services for the homeless ↔combat the county's homelessness The purpose of such action ↔To combat 预判"为无家可归者出钱解决问题"与 To combat the county's homelessness 完全吻 合，故锁定。 B) 无中生有 原文只说资助住房与社会服务，从未提"改革服务体系"，reform the county's service system 是凭 services 一词臆造出的动作。 C) 偷换概念 加税资助的是 housing and social services，the development of local infrastructure 把"住房与社会服务"偷换成"地方基础设施建设"，二者并非一回事。 D) 无中生有 原文 some of the richest people in the world 只是用富裕反衬问题之刺眼，从未说 加税是为"缩小贫富差距"，narrow the gap between the rich and the poor 属臆造 目的。 人们往往对无家可归者持什么看法? A) 他们很少符合无家可归的描述。 B) 他们是经济快速发展的受害者。 C) 他们应该为自己的处境负责。 D) 他们占吸毒成瘾者的大多数。

questions.q: What do people tend to believe about the homeless?
options: They seldom meet the descriptions of homelessness.
They are the victims of fast economic development.
They are responsible for their own condition.
They account for the majority of drug addicts.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do people tend to believe 问的是文中明确描述过的一种社会观念，原文有现成陈 述，属事实细节而非作者本人观点的推断。

【拆句】Q52 主干为 What do people tend to believe about the homeless，tend to believe 是"倾向于相信"的固定搭配，about the homeless 限定讨论对象，结构简单无陷阱。

【定位】For as long as there are homeless people, there is a tendency to blame the victims themselves for their condition—to see their failure to thrive as an issue of character, of moral weakness, of laziness. 只要有无家可归者存在，就有一种倾向，把他们的处境归咎于受害者自身——把他们的潦倒 看作品格、道德缺陷或懒惰的问题。 52. What do people tend to believe about the homeless? A) They seldom meet the descriptions of homelessness. B) They are the victims of fast economic development. C) They are responsible for their own condition. D) They account for the majority of drug addicts.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文说无家可归者"多数并非"精神病或瘾君子，是作者驳斥偏见，seldom meet the descriptions 把"少数符合"歪曲成"很少符合"，且这是作者观点而非"人们倾向相信"的 内容。 B) 答非所问 victims of fast economic development 把原文 the economy forgot them（被经济 遗忘）偷换成"快速经济发展的受害者"，且这是作者给出的真实成因，并非题干所问 的"人们倾向相信"的偏见。 C) ✓ 正确 blame the victims themselves for their condition ↔responsible for their own condition the victims themselves ↔their own 预判"责任在他们自己"与 They are responsible for their own condition 直接对应，故 锁定。 D) 以偏概全 原文只说"相当一部分人"符合吸毒等描述，account for the majority of drug addicts 反过来说无家可归者"占瘾君子的大多数"，既夸大又颠倒了主从关系。 洛杉矶越来越多的人无家可归的原因之一是什么? A) 他们发现越来越难以负担住处。 B) 该县的离婚率一直在稳步上升。 C) 他们被迫从事低薪工作。 D) 社会未能原谅他们的过错。

questions.q: What is one of the causes for more and more people in Los Angeles to become homeless?
options: They find it increasingly difficult to afford a place to live.
The divorce rate in the county has been on a steady rise.
They have been compelled to take low-paying jobs.
The society fails to forgive them for their mistakes.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is one of the causes 用 one of 限定，只需在原文列举的若干成因里找出与某个选项 对得上的那一个，是定位细节而非推断。

【拆句】Q53 主干为 What is one of the causes，for more and more people in Los Angeles to become homeless 是介词 for 引导的长定语，修饰 causes，说明"什么的成因"；拆开后 即"越来越多洛杉矶人沦为无家可归者"的成因，理清这层修饰即无障碍。

【定位】Today, a greater and greater proportion of people living on the streets are there because of bad luck or a series of mistakes, or because the economy forgot them—they lost a job or were evicted or fled an abusive marriage just as the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving. 如今，越来越多流落街头的人是因为坏运气、一连串失误，或因为被经济遗忘——他们失 业、被逐出住所或逃离虐待性婚姻，恰逢房市变得越来越无情。 53. What is one of the causes for more and more people in Los Angeles to become homeless? A) They find it increasingly difficult to afford a place to live. B) The divorce rate in the county has been on a steady rise. C) They have been compelled to take low-paying jobs. D) The society fails to forgive them for their mistakes.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the housing market was growing increasingly unforgiving ↔ increasingly difficult to afford a place to live 预判"房市苛刻让人难有住处"与 They find it increasingly difficult to afford a place to live 吻合，故锁定。 B) 无中生有 原文只提个别人 fled an abusive marriage（逃离虐待婚姻），是个体经历，从未说"全 郡离婚率持续上升"，divorce rate … on a steady rise 属臆造统计趋势。 C) 无中生有 原文说有人 lost a job（失业），并未说他们被迫去做低薪工作，compelled to take low-paying jobs 与文意不符且属臆造。 D) 偷换概念 原文 unforgiving 形容的是 housing market（房市无情），society fails to forgive them for their mistakes 把"房市"偷换成"社会"、把"无情"曲解为"不原谅错误"，张冠 李戴式偷换。 我们从洛杉矶无家可归者服务管理局的新报告中了解到什么? A) 为无家可归者提供足够的就业机会仍然是一个挑战。 B) 每个人都在朝着同一个方向努力解决无家可归问题。 C) 新增住房的增长远远满足不了不断增长的无家可归人口的需求。 D) 洛杉矶的无家可归状况恶化速度比许多人预测的要快。

questions.q: What do we learn from the new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report?
options: Supplying enough job opportunities for the homeless remains a challenge.
Everyone is pulling in the same direction to solve the homelessness problem.
The increase in new housing falls short of the demand of the growing homeless population.
Los Angeles' homeless condition is deteriorating faster than many people predict.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the new … report 问一份具名报告的内容，答案就是报告所陈述 的事实，回原文读该报告对应句即可。

【拆句】Q54 主干为 What do we learn from the report，new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority 是一长串前置定语修饰 report，看着唬人，实为"洛杉矶无家可归者服务局的新 报告"，拆掉定语主干极简，无陷阱。

【定位】That reality was driven home this month by a new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report showing that the county's homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing. 本月一份新的洛杉矶无家可归者服务局报告印证了这一现实：本郡无家可归人口的增长速度 快于新住房的供给速度。 54. What do we learn from the new Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority report? A) Supplying enough job opportunities for the homeless remains a challenge. B) Everyone is pulling in the same direction to solve the homelessness problem. C) The increase in new housing falls short of the demand of the growing homeless population. D) Los Angeles' homeless condition is deteriorating faster than many people predict.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 报告比较的是"人口"与"住房"，Supplying enough job opportunities 把"住房供给"偷 换成"就业机会供给"，报告未涉及就业。 B) 答非所问 Everyone is pulling in the same direction 取自报告前一句 even if everyone is pulling in the same direction，那是作者的假设语气，并非报告内容，题干问的是"报 告说了什么"。 C) ✓ 正确 the county's homeless population is growing faster than the supply of new housing ↔ The increase in new housing falls short of the demand of the growing homeless population the supply of new housing ↔The increase in new housing 预判"住房供给跟不上需求"与 The increase in new housing falls short of the demand 完全对应，故锁定。 D) 无中生有 报告只说人口增长快于住房供给，从未提"恶化速度快于许多人的预测"，faster than many people predict 凭空加入"预测"这一参照，属臆造。 大多数洛杉矶居民现在对无家可归问题有何感受? A) 他们对其规模感到越来越羞愧。 B) 他们发现它并不像看起来那么可怕。 C) 他们对此越来越不冷漠。 D) 他们不再觉得震惊。

questions.q: How do most Los Angeles residents now feel about homelessness?
options: They are increasingly ashamed about its scale.
They find it no more scaring than it appears.
They are less and less indifferent to it.
They no longer find it shocking.
questions.explain:
【判型】How do most Los Angeles residents now feel 看似问态度，但原文末段把居民的感受逐 词列了出来，答案能逐字对应，按细节题回原文核对即可，无需揣摩作者立场。

【拆句】Q55 主干为 How do residents feel about homelessness，now 是关键时间状语，强 调"如今"而非过去，提醒答案要选"当下"的感受；句子结构简单，唯一要抓的是这个时间 限定。

【定位】But most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed. Increasingly, we are uncomfortable, annoyed, disgusted, scared or unaware. 但多数洛杉矶居民已不再震惊，也不再羞愧。我们越来越多地感到不适、恼火、厌恶、害怕 或浑然不觉。 55. How do most Los Angeles residents now feel about homelessness? A) They are increasingly ashamed about its scale. B) They find it no more scaring than it appears. C) They are less and less indifferent to it. D) They no longer find it shocking.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文说居民 no longer … shamed（不再羞愧），increasingly ashamed 说"越来越羞 愧"，与原文正相反。 B) 与原文相反 原文把 scared（害怕）列为居民如今增多的情绪之一，no more scaring than it appears 却说"不比看上去更可怕"，与原文相反。 C) 与原文相反 原文说居民越来越 unaware（漠然），同情 being replaced by resignation（被无奈 取代），less and less indifferent 说"越来越不漠然"，与原文趋势相反。 D) ✓ 正确 most Los Angeles residents are no longer either shocked or shamed ↔ They no longer find it shocking 预判"不再震惊"与 They no longer find it shocking 逐词吻合，故锁定。

items.title: 2023年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2023年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 One of my bad habits is saying "busy" when people ask me how I'm doing. Sometimes it's because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that's what I think I'm supposed to say. That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say. But working long hours doesn't drive better results. Never taking a vacation won't lead to a promotion. So why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are all the time?

P2 In 2016, researchers from Columbia, Harvard, and Georgetown conducted a study to figure it out. They found busy people are perceived to be of high status, and interestingly, these status attributions are heavily influenced by our own beliefs about social mobility. In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing.

P3 That's why we feel like we have to appear busy, and there's a real perception that if someone is knee-deep in meetings, emails, and stress, then they're probably a big deal. This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout(精疲力竭).

P4 Personally, I'm going to stop saying "busy" when people ask me how I am. It sounds self- righteous(自以为是的) and sets the wrong tone. Phrases like "I have limited access to email" and "I'll respond as soon as I get back" sound like you're being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off.

P5 That's why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back. Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same.

questions.q: What is a reason for the author to be in the habit of saying "busy" when asked how he is doing?
options: He just follows successful people's example.
He is actually proud to be fully occupied.
He thinks everyone should be devoted to work.
He believes busyness ensures accomplishments.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is a reason for the author to be in the habit 问一个具体可在原文找到的原 因，答案直接落在某句话里。

【拆句】主干是 What is a reason，后接 for 引导的逻辑主语 for the author to be in the habit of saying "busy"，再用 when 状语 when asked how he is doing 限定情境。结构清晰，无 陷阱，只需读成“作者在被问近况时爱说忙，原因是什么”。 46. What is a reason for the author to be in the habit of saying "busy" when asked how he is doing? A) He just follows successful people's example. B) He is actually proud to be fully occupied. C) He thinks everyone should be devoted to work. D) He believes busyness ensures accomplishments.

【定位】Sometimes it's because I actually am busy, but other times it's because that's what I think I'm supposed to say. That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say. 有时是因为我确实忙，但另一些时候是因为那是我以为自己应该说的话。重要人物就这么 说，得到晋升的人就这么说。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 That's what important people say. That's what people who get promoted say ↔ follows successful people's example 预判“效仿成功者的做法”与 He just follows successful people's example 完全吻合， 故锁定此项。 B) 张冠李戴 原文末尾反问 why are we so proud to talk about how busy we are 是带反思的反 问，并非作者承认自己“为忙而自豪”，选项把反问当作者的真实态度，属张冠李戴。 C) 无中生有 原文从未说作者认为“人人都应投身工作”；相反作者反思忙碌文化，everyone should be devoted to work 在文中无任何依据，属无中生有。 D) 与原文相反 原文明说 working long hours doesn't drive better results，即忙碌并不保证成就； busyness ensures accomplishments 与原文意思正好相反。 我们为什么倾向于认为忙碌的人地位高? A) 我们的地位可归因于我们的社会流动性。 B) 我们坚信努力工作会带来成功。 C) 我们自己的成功机会从来都不容易获得。 D) 我们发现很少有地位高的人有时间休闲。

questions.q: Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status?
options: Our status can be attributed to our social mobility.
We hold the belief that hard work leads to success.
Our own opportunity for success never comes easily.
We find few people of high status have time for leisure.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status 问的是原文研究已 经给出的解释，属可定位的明确事实。

【拆句】Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status 中 think 后接 that 宾语 从句 busy people are of high status。tend to 是“倾向于”，不是绝对，读时不必纠结，整 句即“我们为什么倾向认为忙人地位高”。 47. Why do we tend to think that busy people are of high status? A) Our status can be attributed to our social mobility. B) We hold the belief that hard work leads to success. C) Our own opportunity for success never comes easily. D) We find few people of high status have time for leisure.

【定位】In other words, the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work, the more we tend to think that people who skip leisure and work all the time are of higher standing. 换句话说，我们越是相信一个人靠努力工作就有成功的机会，就越倾向于认为那些放弃休 闲、一直工作的人地位更高。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文说我们对社会流动的信念影响了地位判断，并非“地位可归因于社会流动”；status can be attributed to our social mobility 把“信念影响判断”偷换成“地位源于流动”，颠 倒了关系。 B) ✓ 正确 the more we believe that one has the opportunity for success based on hard work ↔ We hold the belief that hard work leads to success 预判的“努力工作通向成功的信念”与 hold the belief that hard work leads to success 逐字对应，故锁定此项。 C) 无中生有 原文谈的是“相信有机会成功”，从未说“我们自己的成功机会来之不易”；opportunity for success never comes easily 在文中无依据，属无中生有。 D) 答非所问 题问“为何觉得忙人地位高”，few people of high status have time for leisure 是描述 高地位者的现象，没回答原因，且原文也未这么说，属答非所问兼无中生有。 从最近的一项研究中,我们对忙碌文化了解到什么? A) 它使员工陷入无休止的会议、邮件和压力之中。 B) 它迫使约20%的员工表现得总是很忙。 C) 它扭曲了许多员工对什么是满意生活的信念。 D) 它对许多忙碌员工的幸福感造成很大伤害。

questions.q: What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study?
options: It places employees in endless meetings, emails and stress.
It compels some 20% of employees to appear always busy.
It distorts many employees' belief of what a satisfying life is.
It does much harm to many busy employees' well-being.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study 问一项研究 的具体结论，答案在原文摆着。

【拆句】What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study：主干 What do we learn，about 短语限定话题，from 短语点明信息来源。三段修饰平铺，无陷阱。 48. What do we learn about the culture of busyness from a recent study? A) It places employees in endless meetings, emails and stress. B) It compels some 20% of employees to appear always busy. C) It distorts many employees' belief of what a satisfying life is. D) It does much harm to many busy employees' well-being.

【定位】This culture of busyness is making it hard for employees to find work-life balance. According to a recent study, one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout(精疲力竭). 这种忙碌文化正使员工难以找到工作与生活的平衡。根据近期一项研究，每五名高投入员工 中就有一名面临精疲力竭的风险。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 meetings, emails and stress 出自上一段对“显得忙的人”的描写 knee-deep in meetings, emails, and stress，并非“近期研究”的结论；题问研究发现什么，此项把别 处内容搬来，属张冠李戴。 B) 偷换概念 原文 one in five（约20%）指的是“面临精疲力竭风险”的人，compels some 20% of employees to appear always busy 把这20%偷换成“被迫显得忙”，数据所指对象 被改。 C) 无中生有 原文未提忙碌文化“扭曲了员工对满意生活的认知”；distorts…belief of what a satisfying life is 在文中找不到对应句，属无中生有。 D) ✓ 正确 one in five highly engaged employees is at risk of burnout ↔ It does much harm to many busy employees' well-being 预判“危害员工身心”与 does much harm to many busy employees' well-being 吻 合，故锁定此项。 根据作者的说法,像"我查看邮件的机会有限"这样的话听起来像什么? A) 某人太忙而无法及时查看所有邮件。 B) 某人反对当前盛行的工作文化。 C) 某人被环境所迫而停止工作。 D) 某人只是在享受他们的休息时间。

questions.q: What do such utterances as "I have limited access to email" sound like according to the author?
options: One is too busy to check all emails in time.
One is opposed to the prevailing work culture.
One is forced by circumstances to stop working.
One is simply enjoying their time off work.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do such utterances as … sound like according to the author 问作者认为这 类话听起来像什么，答案是原文作者的明确评价。

【拆句】What do such utterances as "I have limited access to email" sound like according to the author：such…as 举例结构，sound like 是“听起来像”。注意 sound like 后省略了表 语，正是要补的答案；according to the author 提示以作者原话为准。 49. What do such utterances as "I have limited access to email" sound like according to the author? A) One is too busy to check all emails in time. B) One is opposed to the prevailing work culture. C) One is forced by circumstances to stop working. D) One is simply enjoying their time off work.

【定位】Phrases like "I have limited access to email" and "I'll respond as soon as I get back" sound like you're being held against your will from working as opposed to making the most of your time off. “我邮件查看受限”“我一回来就回复”这类话听起来像是你被违背意愿地拦着不让工作，而不 是在充分利用你的休假时光。

【选项】A) 答非所问 题问这类话“听起来像”什么（即给人的印象），too busy to check all emails in time 描述的是字面情境而非作者说的负面印象；作者的重点是“像被迫”，此项答非所问。 B) 过度推断 作者只说这类话“听起来像被迫”、设错了基调，并未说它表示“反对主流工作文化”； opposed to the prevailing work culture 是读者强行拔高，属过度推断。 C) ✓ 正确 you're being held against your will from working ↔ One is forced by circumstances to stop working 预判“被迫无法工作”与 forced by circumstances to stop working 吻合，故锁定此项。 D) 与原文相反 原文用 as opposed to 把“被迫不能工作”与“充分享受休假”对立，明说这类话听起来 “不是”在享受休假；simply enjoying their time off work 恰是被否定的那一面，正好 相反。 作者和他的同事为什么推出"不在办公室邮件生成器"? A) 使忙碌的员工能够花更少的时间查看邮件。 B) 确保员工和雇主都真正拥有休息时间。 C) 阻止管理者谈论他们的团队通常有多忙。 D) 鼓励雇主和员工都及时回复邮件。

questions.q: Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator?
options: To enable busy employees to spend less time checking emails.
To ensure employees as well as employers truly have time off.
To stop managers from talking about how busy their teams usually are.
To encourage both employers and employees to answer emails promptly.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator 问一个具体动作的目的，答案藏在原文相应段落。

【拆句】Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator：主 干 Why did the author and his colleagues launch，宾语是专有工具名。一般疑问语序无 陷阱，落脚在“为何推出这个工具”。 50. Why did the author and his colleagues launch the Out of Office Email Generator? A) To enable busy employees to spend less time checking emails. B) To ensure employees as well as employers truly have time off. C) To stop managers from talking about how busy their teams usually are. D) To encourage both employers and employees to answer emails promptly.

【定位】That's why we recently launched the Out of Office Email Generator, a free tool you can use before your next long weekend or trip. You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back. Managers need to think twice about emailing their teams on the weekend and talking about how busy they are. Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same. 这就是我们最近推出“Out of Office Email Generator”这款免费工具的原因，你可以在下个 长周末或出行前使用它。你可以大方而自豪地宣告，回来之前不会查邮件。管理者需要三 思，别在周末给团队发邮件、别炫耀自己多忙。领导者应自己带头休假，并鼓励员工同样 如此。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 “少花时间查邮件”只是手段、且只覆盖员工一方，原文目的是让双方“真正休假”；spend less time checking emails 把整体目的缩成局部手段，属以偏概全。 B) ✓ 正确 You can share loud and proud that you won't be checking email until you're back ↔ To ensure employees as well as employers truly have time off Leaders should take time off themselves and encourage employees to do the same ↔ employers as well as employees 预判“让员工和雇主都真正休假”与 employees as well as employers truly have time off 完整对应、双方都覆盖，故锁定此项。 C) 以偏概全 “别谈论团队多忙”只是原文对管理者诸多建议之一 talking about how busy they are， 不是推出工具的总目的；stop managers from talking about how busy… 拿一个分支 当全部，属以偏概全。 D) 与原文相反 原文呼吁休假时“不查/不发邮件”，answer emails promptly（及时回邮件）与原文意图 正好相反。

items.title: 2023年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2023年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Female employees consistently pay lower airfares than men do for the same flights because they tend to book earlier.

P2 We compared the airfare paid by employees in the same position within a company for the same class of travel and used a common statistical technique to account for other factors that might affect differences in airfares. We found that women paid on average $18 less per ticket than their male colleagues. Further investigation allowed us to conclude that this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men, 1.8 days on average.
