P3 We wanted to determine what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips so we tested a variety of possible explanations, such as women choosing to plan ahead or male frequent travelers being inclined to book late. None of these explained away the gender gap, so we applied data collected from surveys that express consumer preferences that play a central role in economic decisions, such as patience and risk avoidance.

P4 We found that only the concept of "negative reciprocity"—in which an employee who feels unfairly treated engages in negative behaviors, such as spending their company's money less carefully— explains these differences. The surveys showed men tend to exhibit more of these negative behaviors than women. This isn't to say that all men engage in these behaviors—or that booking relatively late is a sign of abnormal behavior. It only means that the gender gap disappears when we plug in the negative reciprocity variable.

P5 Prior research on negative reciprocity among workers found that it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale(士气) and culture.

P6 Our results show another way these negative behaviors can manifest themselves, like in airline bookings, and add to evidence that women are less likely to engage in them.

P7 Companies spend significant sums of money on business travel. While that $18 difference per ticket may seem small, it adds up. Our analysis suggests early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year for a large multinational company with 20,000 regular travelers.

questions.q: What did the author's team conclude about the gender difference in airfares from their further
options: It is largely attributed to women booking earlier than men.
It is largely explained by women's choosing cheaper flights.
It is mainly accounted for by male employees' readiness to pay more.
It is due to the fact that women care more about their company's money.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What did the author's team conclude 问作者团队得出了什么结论，是对文中已陈述 事实的提取，不需推断。

【拆句】主干是 What did the author's team conclude about the gender difference in airfares，特殊疑问句，conclude 后接 about 引出结论的对象；句末 from their further investigation 是状语，交代结论的来源，是关键定位信号，结构平铺、无陷阱。

【定位】Further investigation allowed us to conclude that this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men, 1.8 days on average. 进一步调查使我们得出结论：这一差距很大程度上可由女性比男性订得更早这一事实来解 释，平均早 1.8 天。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 this gap is largely explained by the fact that women tended to book earlier than men ↔ It is largely attributed to women booking earlier than men 选项 largely attributed to women booking earlier than men 与预判“价差主要因女性 订得更早”完全吻合，是定位句的同义替换。 B) 无中生有 原文将价差归因于订得早，从未说女性“选了更便宜的航班”；women's choosing cheaper flights 是文中没有的新说法。 C) 偷换概念 原文成因是订得早晚，并非男性“更愿意多付钱”；male employees' readiness to pay more 把订得晚导致票价高，曲解成男性主动愿意付高价。 D) 张冠李戴 “女性更在乎公司的钱”是第 4 段负向回报机制的延伸，不是本题进一步调查的结论； women care more about their company's money 张冠李戴到本题。 研究人员想通过测试各种可能的解释来确定什么? A) 是什么使得经常出差的男性晚预订机票。 B) 是什么导致女性在预订商务旅行时提前计划。 C) 是什么促使女性预订更便宜的航班。 D) 是什么造成了机票价格的性别差距。

questions.q: What did the researchers want to determine by testing a variety of possible explanations?
options: What made male frequent travelers book air tickets late.
What caused women to plan ahead in booking business trips.
What motivated women to book cheaper flights.
What accounted for the gender gap in airfares.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What did the researchers want to determine 问研究者想弄清什么，答案是文中明 写的目的，属事实提取。 52. What did the researchers want to determine by testing a variety of possible explanations? A) What made male frequent travelers book air tickets late. B) What caused women to plan ahead in booking business trips. C) What motivated women to book cheaper flights. D) What accounted for the gender gap in airfares.

【拆句】主干 What did the researchers want to determine，后接介词短语 by testing a variety of possible explanations 作方式状语，by 表手段；理清“通过检验多种解释”是手段、“想 弄清什么”才是问点，避免把手段当答案。

【定位】We wanted to determine what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips so we tested a variety of possible explanations, such as women choosing to plan ahead or male frequent travelers being inclined to book late. 我们想弄清是什么造成了订商务差旅中的这些性别差异，于是检验了多种可能的解释，比如 女性选择提前规划，或男性常旅客倾向于晚订。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 What made male frequent travelers book air tickets late 取自文中举例的待检解释 male frequent travelers being inclined to book late，是被检验的假设之一，不是研 究总目的。 B) 以偏概全 What caused women to plan ahead in booking business trips 同样取自待检举例 women choosing to plan ahead，是子假设而非研究要弄清的总问题。 C) 无中生有 What motivated women to book cheaper flights 中“女性订更便宜的航班”文中从未 出现，价差源于订得早而非选便宜航班。 D) ✓ 正确 what was causing these gender differences in booking business trips ↔ What accounted for the gender gap in airfares What accounted for the gender gap in airfares 正是预判“弄清性别价差成因”的同义 表达，锁定该项。 当消极互惠变量被考虑在内时发生了什么? A) 男性和女性都被发现有消极行为。 B) 男性和女性都不认为晚预订是一种不良行为。 C) 机票费用的性别差异不再存在。 D) 性别差距倾向于显著缩小。

questions.q: What happened when the negative reciprocity variable was taken into account?
options: Both men and women were found to engage in negative behaviors.
Neither men nor women viewed booking late as a bad behavior.
The gender difference in airfare expenses no longer existed.
The gender gap tended to narrow to a significant degree.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What happened when the negative reciprocity variable was taken into account 问“当变量被纳入后发生了什么”，结果文中明写，属细节。

【拆句】主干 What happened when ...，when 引导时间状语从句，从句用被动 was taken into account；读懂“当负向回报这一变量被引入分析时”这个条件，结果句即答案。 53. What happened when the negative reciprocity variable was taken into account? A) Both men and women were found to engage in negative behaviors. B) Neither men nor women viewed booking late as a bad behavior. C) The gender difference in airfare expenses no longer existed. D) The gender gap tended to narrow to a significant degree.

【定位】It only means that the gender gap disappears when we plug in the negative reciprocity variable. 它只是意味着，当我们把负向回报这一变量代入后，性别差距就消失了。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文称男性比女性更常有此类行为 men tend to exhibit more of these negative behaviors than women，并非“男女都有”；Both men and women were found to engage in negative behaviors 与原文相悖，且非“代入变量后”的结果。 B) 偷换概念 原文只说晚订不必然是异常行为 booking relatively late is a sign of abnormal behavior 的免责说明，并非“男女都不视晚订为坏行为”，更不是代入变量后的结果。 C) ✓ 正确 the gender gap disappears ↔The gender difference in airfare expenses no longer existed The gender difference in airfare expenses no longer existed 与预判“性别差距消失” 完全对应，锁定该项。 D) 偷换概念 原文是差距“消失” the gender gap disappears，The gender gap tended to narrow to a significant degree 说成“显著缩小”，程度被改弱，与原文不符。 先前关于员工消极互惠的研究发现了什么? A) 它对工作场所的危害可能比对员工的危害更大。 B) 它加剧了工作场所的男女分化。 C) 它在多个方面被证明是适得其反的。 D) 它可能导致劳资冲突的增加。

questions.q: What did prior research on negative reciprocity among workers find?
options: It can do more harm to the workplace than to employees.
It contributes to the male-female divide in the workplace.
It proves to be counterproductive in a number of ways.
It can result in increasing labor-management conflicts.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What did prior research ... find 问先前研究发现了什么，是文中已陈述的内容，属事 实提取。

【拆句】主干 What did prior research on negative reciprocity among workers find，find 是问 点动词；among workers 限定研究对象，prior 限定时间，定位时认准“先前的、关于工人 的”那项研究。

【定位】Prior research on negative reciprocity among workers found that it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale(士气) and culture. 先前关于工人负向回报的研究发现，它会导致员工积极性、业绩、职场士气与文化的下降。 54. What did prior research on negative reciprocity among workers find? A) It can do more harm to the workplace than to employees. B) It contributes to the male-female divide in the workplace. C) It proves to be counterproductive in a number of ways. D) It can result in increasing labor-management conflicts.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文未比较“对职场”与“对员工”谁伤害更大；do more harm to the workplace than to employees 凭空造出一个原文没有的比较。 B) 张冠李戴 “造成职场男女分化”是后文 P6 对本研究结果的引申，不是先前研究的发现； contributes to the male-female divide in the workplace 张冠李戴。 C) ✓ 正确 it can result in lower employee motivation, business performance and workplace morale(士气) and culture ↔It proves to be counterproductive in a number of ways counterproductive in a number of ways 正是预判“多方面负面下降”的抽象概括，锁 定该项。 D) 无中生有 原文后果是积极性、业绩、士气、文化下降，无“劳资冲突加剧”；increasing labor- management conflicts 是文中没有的新后果。 作者在最后一段强调了他们分析的什么内容? A) 它可以帮助公司显著增加节省。 B) 它可以适当地促进公司的业务绩效。 C) 它可以将女性的预订做法转化为男性的行为。 D) 它可以增强大型跨国公司的竞争力。

questions.q: What does the author emphasize about their analysis in the last paragraph?
options: It can help companies increase their savings significantly.
It can duly contribute to companies' business performance.
It can translate women's booking practice into men's behavior.
It can enhance large multinational companies' competitiveness.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author emphasize about their analysis in the last paragraph 锁定 最后一段、问其强调点，答案在段内明写，属细节。

【拆句】主干 What does the author emphasize about their analysis，emphasize 后 about 引出强调对象 their analysis；末尾 in the last paragraph 限定到最后一段，定位即在该 段内。

【定位】Our analysis suggests early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year for a large multinational company with 20,000 regular travelers. 我们的分析表明，女性的早订每年可为一家拥有两万名常旅客的大型跨国公司带来一百万美 元的节省。 55. What does the author emphasize about their analysis in the last paragraph? A) It can help companies increase their savings significantly. B) It can duly contribute to companies' business performance. C) It can translate women's booking practice into men's behavior. D) It can enhance large multinational companies' competitiveness.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 early booking by women can translate into savings of $1 million a year ↔ It can help companies increase their savings significantly help companies increase their savings significantly 正是预判“早订为公司省大钱”的 概括，锁定该项。 B) 张冠李戴 “提升业绩”是第 5 段先前研究提到的 business performance，不是末段分析所强调的内 容；contribute to companies' business performance 张冠李戴到本段。 C) 偷换概念 原文 translate into 的宾语是 savings（节省），不是“把女性的做法变成男性的行为”； translate women's booking practice into men's behavior 借同一动词曲解原意。 D) 过度推断 原文只谈为公司省钱，未涉及“提升竞争力”；enhance large multinational companies' competitiveness 是过度引申出的新结论。

items.title: 2023年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2023年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance. But before you go out and find an entrepreneur to outcompete, it's important to understand and avoid the traps that often come with rivalry. After all, competitive rivalry can also hinder effective decision-making and increase your willingness to take risks, behaviors that can ultimately hurt your venture's success.

P2 Finding someone you're committed to outcompeting can be a great way to stay focused on your goals and push your venture to the next level. But when you're intently focused on outperforming your rivals, you may begin to develop a "win-at-all-costs" mentality that causes you to ignore how you achieve success. One group of researchers, for example, examined the link between rivalry and unethical behavior. They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win. But such behavior may stain your reputation and strain relationships important to your success. One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important. While outperforming your rivals may provide short-term benefits, the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences.

P3 One reason having a rival can enhance your venture's performance is that it creates a level of excitement that drives you to work harder. But this eagerness to win may also hurt your venture's success, particularly when it causes you to make impulsive, insensible decisions. But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture.

P4 The sense of eagerness that comes with having a rival can not only cause you to make poorer decisions, but it can also lead you to take greater risks that put your venture in peril. One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision- making.

questions.q: How can competitive rivalry benefit entrepreneurs according to the passage?
options: By enabling them to outcompete other entrepreneurs.
By enabling them to make their venture a success.
By helping them to reach long-term goals.
By helping them to stay goal-oriented.
questions.explain:
【判型】How can competitive rivalry benefit entrepreneurs 问的是"靠什么具体方式带来好处"， 答案是文中某句客观陈述，属细节题。

【拆句】主干是 How can competitive rivalry benefit entrepreneurs，competitive rivalry（竞争 性的对手关系）作主语，benefit 在这里是动词"使……受益"，entrepreneurs（创业者）是 宾语。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 46. How can competitive rivalry benefit entrepreneurs according to the passage? A) By enabling them to outcompete other entrepreneurs. B) By enabling them to make their venture a success. C) By helping them to reach long-term goals. D) By helping them to stay goal-oriented.

【定位】Having a rival can keep you committed to achieving your goals and enhance your overall performance. 有一个竞争对手能让你持续专注于实现自己的目标，并提升你的整体表现。

【选项】A) 答非所问 By enabling them to outcompete other entrepreneurs"使其胜过其他创业者"是"拥 有对手"的前提情境，文章首段说的好处是专注目标、提升表现，不是"胜过别人"本身。 B) 过度推断 By enabling them to make their venture a success"使其事业成功"是夸大结果；原文 只说 enhance your overall performance"提升表现"，并未说能"让事业成功"。 C) 无中生有 By helping them to reach long-term goals 多出 long-term"长期"这一限定；原文 achieving your goals 只说"目标"，并未区分长期短期。 D) ✓ 正确 keep you committed to achieving your goals ↔helping them to stay goal-oriented 四项中只有 helping them to stay goal-oriented 准确对应定位句"保持专注目标"这一 好处，与预判一致。 创业者在与对手竞争时可能经常陷入的陷阱之一是什么? A) 他们可能会采用注定会毁掉自己事业的策略。 B) 他们可能会诉诸不道德的手段来超越对手。 C) 他们可能过于急切地想要成功而忽视了巨大的人力成本。 D) 他们可能过度专注于在当前市场层面上获胜。

questions.q: What is one of the traps entrepreneurs may often fall into when competing with rivals?
options: They may adopt strategies that are bound to ruin their venture.
They may resort to unethical means to outperform their rivals.
They may be too eager to succeed while ignoring the huge labor cost.
They may be intently focused on winning at the current market level.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is one of the traps 问的是文中列出的某一个具体陷阱，答案直接来自原文陈述，属 细节题。

【拆句】What is one of the traps entrepreneurs may often fall into when competing with rivals：主干问 What is one of the traps，后接 entrepreneurs…fall into 是省略了关系词 的定语从句修饰 traps，when competing 是时间状语。fall into a trap 是固定搭配"落入 陷阱"。

【定位】They found that when people compete against their rivals, they are more willing to behave unethically to win. 他们发现，当人们与对手竞争时，更愿意为了取胜而采取不道德的行为。 47. What is one of the traps entrepreneurs may often fall into when competing with rivals? A) They may adopt strategies that are bound to ruin their venture. B) They may resort to unethical means to outperform their rivals. C) They may be too eager to succeed while ignoring the huge labor cost. D) They may be intently focused on winning at the current market level.

【选项】A) 过度推断 strategies that are bound to ruin their venture 用 bound to"必定"把后果说死；原 文 may stain your reputation 只是"可能"损害声誉，并非必然毁掉事业。 B) ✓ 正确 behave unethically to win ↔resort to unethical means to outperform their rivals resort to unethical means to outperform their rivals 与定位句"为赢而行不道德之 事"完全对应，与预判一致。 C) 无中生有 ignoring the huge labor cost 里的 labor cost"劳动成本"文中从未提及；第2段讲的是 忽视"如何取胜"的方式，不是忽视成本。 D) 偷换概念 winning at the current market level 把第3段 next level 的"层级"挪来，原文从未说陷 阱是"只盯当前市场层级"，属拼接错位。 建议创业者做什么来避免常常伴随竞争而来的陷阱? A) 慎重考虑什么才是真正重要的。 B) 优先考虑获取即时利益。 C) 评估长期后果。 D) 思考哪些成功是可以实现的。

questions.q: What are entrepreneurs advised to do to avoid traps that often accompany rivalry?
options: Deliberate on what really matters.
Prioritize reaping immediate benefits.
Estimate the long-term consequences.
Reflect on what successes are achievable.
questions.explain:
【判型】What are entrepreneurs advised to do 问作者建议的具体做法，答案是原文对策句的转 述，属细节题。

【拆句】What are entrepreneurs advised to do to avoid traps that often accompany rivalry： 被动结构 are advised to do（被建议做某事），to avoid… 是目的状语，that often accompany rivalry 是定语从句修饰 traps，accompany 意为"伴随"。

【定位】One way to avoid this trap is to stop and reflect on what's important. 避免这个陷阱的一个办法是停下来，反思什么才是重要的。 48. What are entrepreneurs advised to do to avoid traps that often accompany rivalry? A) Deliberate on what really matters. B) Prioritize reaping immediate benefits. C) Estimate the long-term consequences. D) Reflect on what successes are achievable.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 reflect on what's important ↔Deliberate on what really matters Deliberate on what really matters 精确对应对策句，与预判一致。 B) 与原文相反 Prioritize reaping immediate benefits"优先攫取眼前利益"恰与原文相悖：原文 the loss of your integrity will have long-term consequences 是提醒别只图短期，B 却让 人优先短期。 C) 偷换概念 Estimate the long-term consequences"评估长期后果"取自原文 long-term consequences，但那是说明丧失诚信的代价，并非作者建议的做法（作者建议是"反思 什么重要"）。 D) 偷换概念 Reflect on what successes are achievable 借用了原文 reflect on，却把宾语改成"哪 些成功可实现"；原文反思的对象是 what's important"什么重要"，而非"成功是否 可达"。 创业者如何避免做出冲动和不明智的决策? A) 通过让自己参与批判性思考。 B) 通过养成保持正直的习惯。 C) 通过批评自己以前的糟糕表现。 D) 通过克制自己不要对成功过于兴奋。

questions.q: How can entrepreneurs avoid making impulsive and insensible decisions?
options: By engaging themselves in critical reasoning.
By developing a habit of keeping their integrity.
By criticizing themselves for previous poor performances.
By refraining from being too excited about their successes.
questions.explain:
【判型】How can entrepreneurs avoid making impulsive and insensible decisions 问避免冲动 决策的具体办法，答案直取原文方法句，属细节题。

【拆句】How can entrepreneurs avoid making impulsive and insensible decisions：avoid 后 接动名词 making（avoid doing 固定用法），impulsive"冲动的"、insensible"不明智 的"两个形容词并列修饰 decisions。结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】But it's possible to avoid such costly mistakes by making a habit of engaging in critical thinking, such as considering opposing viewpoints and conducting cost-benefit analyses, especially for those decisions that are complex and can determine the future of your venture. 但可以通过养成进行批判性思考的习惯来避免这类代价高昂的错误，比如考虑相反的观点、 做成本收益分析，尤其是对那些复杂且能决定事业未来的决策。 49. How can entrepreneurs avoid making impulsive and insensible decisions? A) By engaging themselves in critical reasoning. B) By developing a habit of keeping their integrity. C) By criticizing themselves for previous poor performances. D) By refraining from being too excited about their successes.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 engaging in critical thinking ↔engaging themselves in critical reasoning engaging themselves in critical reasoning 精确对应对策句的方法，与预判一致。 B) 张冠李戴 keeping their integrity"保持诚信"是第2段针对"不道德行为"的对策，与本段"冲动决 策"无关，属跨段错位。 C) 偷换概念 criticizing themselves for previous poor performances"为以往糟糕表现自责"文中没 有依据；原文说的是 critical thinking 批判性思考，不是"自我批评"。 D) 偷换概念 refraining from being too excited about their successes"别为成功太兴奋"对错了对 象；原文 eagerness to win 指"求胜的急切"导致冲动，办法是批判性思考，而非"压抑 对成功的兴奋"。 创业者如何克服竞争带来的风险诱发效应? A) 通过密切关注他们当前的表现。 B) 通过采取可能危及对手成功的措施。 C) 通过监控他们的决策如何影响他们的心态。 D) 通过控制自己的情绪以避免做出糟糕的决策。

questions.q: How can entrepreneurs overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry?
options: By paying close attention to their current performance.
By taking steps that stand to endanger their rivals' success.
By monitoring how their decision-making impacts their mentality.
By keeping their emotions in check to avoid making poor decisions.
questions.explain:
【判型】How can entrepreneurs overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry 问克服风险效应 的具体方法，答案直取原文，属细节题。

【拆句】How can entrepreneurs overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry：主干 How can entrepreneurs overcome the effects，risk-inducing（诱发风险的）作定语修饰 effects，of rivalry 是后置定语说明这种效应的来源。无陷阱。

【定位】One way you can overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry that stand to endanger your venture's success is to remain attentive to your emotional state and actively monitor how such feelings are affecting your decision-making. 你能克服这种危及事业成功的、由竞争诱发风险的效应的一个办法，是持续关注自己的情绪 状态，并主动监控这些情绪如何影响你的决策。 50. How can entrepreneurs overcome the risk-inducing effects of rivalry? A) By paying close attention to their current performance. B) By taking steps that stand to endanger their rivals' success. C) By monitoring how their decision-making impacts their mentality. D) By keeping their emotions in check to avoid making poor decisions.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 paying close attention to their current performance 把对象换成 current performance"当前表现"；原文要关注的是 emotional state"情绪状态"，对象被换。 B) 与原文相反 taking steps that stand to endanger their rivals' success"采取危及对手成功的举 措"与原文相悖：原文 endanger your venture's success 担心的是危及"自己"的事业， 办法是管情绪，不是去害对手。 C) 与原文相反 monitoring how their decision-making impacts their mentality 说"监控决策如何影 响心态"，方向反了；原文是 how such feelings are affecting your decision- making"情绪如何影响决策"，主语宾语对调。 D) ✓ 正确 remain attentive to your emotional state ↔keeping their emotions in check how such feelings are affecting your decision-making ↔to avoid making poor decisions keeping their emotions in check to avoid making poor decisions 整体对应对策句 的两层意思，与预判一致。

items.title: 2023年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2023年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 A multitasker is one who can perform two or more tasks effectively at the same time, which— apart from the obvious differences—is similar to what a computer does. The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time. However, the question is: can a person really be a multitasker?

P2 For most scientists, the answer is no. So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well. As soon as two tasks require our attention, productivity suffers. What we call multitasking, therefore, is in reality the ability to move more or less quickly from one task to another. This requires two essential conditions: that one of the tasks needs to be automatic, like walking or eating, and that they both need different mental processes. Answering the phone and writing at the same time, for example.

P3 However, on the other side of the coin there are people who maintain that it is possible to be, or at least seem to be, multitasking. A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance.

P4 The business perspective offers a different view: multitasking is understood as the ability to adapt to all types of environment within a company and effectively undertake different activities within a set time frame. Indeed, many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking to improve their productivity. From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices.

P5 The benefits of multitasking are clear. Being quicker and more efficient increases our performance and the number of tasks completed. But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes.

questions.q: What does a "multitasker" originally refer to?
options: An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once.
A skilled worker executing more than one task at the same time.
A sophisticated technology doing several tasks effectively at once.
An efficient person able to perform multiple tasks at the same time.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does a "multitasker" originally refer to 直接问一个词「原本指什么」，考的 是文中对该词来源含义的界定。

【拆句】句子主干是 What does a "multitasker" originally refer to，结构平铺，refer to 意为「指 代、指的是」，originally 作状语修饰 refer to，意为「最初指的是」。无陷阱。 51. What does a "multitasker" originally refer to? A) An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once. B) A skilled worker executing more than one task at the same time. C) A sophisticated technology doing several tasks effectively at once. D) An efficient person able to perform multiple tasks at the same time.

【定位】The concept does indeed come from the realms of technology, where it is used to refer to an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time. 这个概念确实来自科技领域，在那里它被用来指一种能够同时执行多项任务的操作系统。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 an operating system that can execute multiple tasks at the same time ↔ An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once 预判要的「能同时多任务的操作系统」与 An operating system capable of doing several tasks at once 完全吻合，主体、能力、同时性三点都对上。 B) 偷换概念 A skilled worker（熟练工人）把主体说成人，而原词最初指的是操作系统，主体张冠 李戴。 C) 偷换概念 A sophisticated technology（一种复杂技术）只取了原文「来自科技领域」的背景， 却没说成「操作系统」，主体被放大成笼统的「技术」，与原文具体所指不符。 D) 答非所问 An efficient person（高效的人）把主体说成人，对应的是首句对 multitasker 的「现 今」描述，而非题干要的「最初」所指，时间与主体都错。 根据神经科学家的观点,为什么人们实际上无法成为多任务处理者? A) 他们没有充分接触多任务处理的情境。 B) 他们无法与机械操作系统相比。 C) 他们的大脑不允许他们进行多任务处理。 D) 他们的注意力持续时间无法延长。

questions.q: Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists?
options: They are not sufficiently exposed to multitasking situations.
They are not comparable to mechanical operating systems.
Their brains do not allow them to multitask.
Their attention span cannot be expanded.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists 问的是某方 观点下的具体理由，答案能在原文直接找到对应句。

【拆句】Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists：主干是 why ... can't people be multitaskers（人为什么不能成为多任务者），really 加强语气， according to neuroscientists 是状语，限定「按神经科学家的看法」。really 易让人误读 为「真的能吗」，其实它服务于全句的否定，意为「人确实当不了」。

【定位】So much so that, according to experts in neuroscience(神经系统科学), our brains do not handle multitasking situations well. 以至于，按照神经科学专家的说法，我们的大脑并不能很好地处理多任务情境。 52. Why can't people really be multitaskers according to neuroscientists? A) They are not sufficiently exposed to multitasking situations. B) They are not comparable to mechanical operating systems. C) Their brains do not allow them to multitask. D) Their attention span cannot be expanded.

【选项】A) 无中生有 not sufficiently exposed to multitasking situations（接触多任务情境不够）文中从 未提及，原文讲的是大脑机能，不是接触多少。 B) 答非所问 not comparable to mechanical operating systems（无法与机械操作系统相比）只是 首段把人和电脑作类比的延伸，并非神经科学家给出的不能多任务的理由。 C) ✓ 正确 our brains do not handle multitasking situations well ↔ Their brains do not allow them to multitask 预判的「大脑处理不好」与 Their brains do not allow them to multitask 一致，把原 因归于大脑这一生理层面，正合定位句。 D) 无中生有 attention span cannot be expanded（注意力广度无法扩展）文中并无此说，原文只 说两项任务争夺注意力时效率下降，没谈注意力能否扩展。 从最近一项关于多任务处理的研究结论中我们了解到什么? A) 人们通过保持他们正在做的事情是多任务处理这一认知而取得更大成就。 B) 人们对他们正在做的事情作为多任务处理的感知使其表现受益。 C) 人们活跃的心理过程对他们的多任务处理产生积极影响。 D) 人们可以通过处理多任务处理情境来提高他们的能力。

questions.q: What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study on multitasking?
options: People make greater achievements by maintaining whatever they are doing is multitasking.
People's performance benefits from the perception of what they are doing as multitasking.
People's active mental processes exert a positive effect on their multitasking.
People can improve their capabilities by handling multitasking situations.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study 问一项具体研究的结论， 原文有对应明示句，属可直接定位的细节。

【拆句】What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study on multitasking：主干 what do we learn（我们了解到什么），from the conclusion of a recent study 是状语，on multitasking 修饰 study，指「一项关于多任务的近期研究的结论」。结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】A recent study concluded that regardless of whether people are actually handling several tasks or not, the mere fact that they perceive this activity as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance. 一项近期研究得出结论：无论人们是否真的在处理多项任务，仅仅是他们把这一活动感知为 多任务这个事实，就对他们的表现有正面影响。 53. What do we learn from the conclusion of a recent study on multitasking? A) People make greater achievements by maintaining whatever they are doing is multitasking. B) People's performance benefits from the perception of what they are doing as multitasking. C) People's active mental processes exert a positive effect on their multitasking. D) People can improve their capabilities by handling multitasking situations.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 maintaining whatever they are doing is multitasking 用 maintaining（坚持主张/坚 持做）替换原文的 perceive（感知），「坚称是多任务」不等于「感知为多任务」，把 主观认知偷换成口头主张。 B) ✓ 正确 they perceive this activity as multitasking ↔ the perception of what they are doing as multitasking has a positive effect on their performance ↔performance benefits from 预判的「感知为多任务即提升表现」与 People's performance benefits from the perception of what they are doing as multitasking 完全对应，落点都在「感知」这 一主观因素。 C) 张冠李戴 active mental processes（积极的心理过程）借的是第二段讲切换需要不同 mental processes 的内容，与本研究结论的「感知」无关。 D) 与原文相反 improve their capabilities by handling multitasking situations 说「靠处理多任务来 提升能力」，而原文强调的恰是「无论是否真在处理多任务」，重点在感知而非实际处 理，方向相反。 商业界如何看待多任务处理? A) 它是一种在灵活组织中常见的稀有技能。 B) 它是所有员工都需要具备的适应性能力。 C) 它是许多员工缺乏的一种基本素质。 D) 它是一种可以培养的理想能力。

questions.q: How does the business world view multitasking?
options: It is a rare skill often found in fluid organisations.
It is an adaptable capability required of all workers.
It is an essential quality many employees lack.
It is a desirable ability that can be developed.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 How does the business world view multitasking 问商业界如何看待多任务，原文有 专段陈述该立场，属可定位细节。

【拆句】How does the business world view multitasking：view 在此是动词「看待」，主干为 the business world view multitasking（商业界如何看待多任务）。需注意 view 此处不是 名词「景观」而是动词，属熟词的常见用法。

【定位】From this different perspective, you can not only be multitasking but this ability can also be taught: something that is easier in fluid organisations, which favour flexibility in their working practices. 从这一不同视角看，你不仅可以做到多任务，而且这种能力还可以被传授：这在灵活的组织 里更容易做到，这类组织在工作方式上崇尚灵活性。 54. How does the business world view multitasking? A) It is a rare skill often found in fluid organisations. B) It is an adaptable capability required of all workers. C) It is an essential quality many employees lack. D) It is a desirable ability that can be developed.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 a rare skill（罕见技能）与原文 many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking 矛盾——能被许多公司寻得且可传授，说明并不罕见。 B) 以偏概全 required of all workers（对所有员工的要求）把范围夸大成「全体员工」，原文只说 many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking，是企业青睐某些 人，而非要求所有人都具备。 C) 无中生有 many employees lack（许多员工缺乏）文中并无此说，原文谈的是公司想要、能力可 教，没有说员工普遍缺乏这种能力。 D) ✓ 正确 many companies look for people who are skilled in multitasking ↔a desirable ability this ability can also be taught ↔that can be developed 预判的「可培养的实用能力」与 a desirable ability that can be developed 两点全 中：desirable 对应被公司追求，can be developed 对应可教。 如果我们必须专注于某项任务并把它做好,作者暗示我们应该做什么? A) 以灵活的方式工作。 B) 从错误中学习。 C) 避免多任务处理。 D) 提高效率。

questions.q: What does the author imply we should do if we have to focus on some task and do it well?
options: Work in a flexible way.
Learn from mistakes.
Avoid multitasking.
Increase efficiency
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author imply we should do 用 imply 问作者「暗示」我们该怎么 做，答案需基于原文推理而非直接摘录。

【拆句】What does the author imply we should do if we have to focus on some task and do it well：主干 what does the author imply we should do（作者暗示我们该做什么），if 引导条件状语从句 if we have to focus on some task and do it well（如果我们必须专注 某项任务并把它做好）。从句是答案成立的前提，须连同主句一起理解。

【定位】But having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced and that can lead to more mistakes. 但不得不同时关注好几件事，意味着专注力会下降，而这会导致更多错误。 55. What does the author imply we should do if we have to focus on some task and do it well? A) Work in a flexible way. B) Learn from mistakes. C) Avoid multitasking. D) Increase efficiency

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Work in a flexible way（以灵活方式工作）取自第四段商业视角的 favour flexibility in their working practices，与末段「要专注做好该怎么办」无关。 B) 无中生有 Learn from mistakes（从错误中学习）只是借了末段 mistakes 一词，原文说的是多任 务会「导致」更多错误，从未建议「从错误中学习」。 C) ✓ 正确 having to pay attention to several things at once means that the powers of concentration are reduced ↔Avoid multitasking 预判的「别同时做多件事」与 Avoid multitasking 一致——既然多任务降低专注、引发 错误，那要做好就该避免它。 D) 答非所问 Increase efficiency（提高效率）对应原文 Being quicker and more efficient，但那是 多任务的「好处」一面，并非「要专注做好」的对策；况且追求效率与多任务相伴，恰 是降低专注的根源。

items.title: 2023年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2023年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 In the history of horse racing, few horses have captured the affection of the British public like Red Rum. Today, three decades after his retirement, he is still one of the best-known and most beloved racehorses of all time.

P2 Red Rum was passed around to several owners before being purchased for Noel Le Mar. The agent who made the purchase was the now-legendary horse trainer Donald "Ginger" McCain.

P3 It wasn't apparent at the time, but Red Rum had a serious bone disease in his foot. For many horses (and many trainers) this would mean the end of a racing career before it even began. For Ginger and Red Rum, though, it was just an obstacle to greatness that had to be overcome.

P4 Red Rum's true talent came out in steeplechases( 障碍赛马). His power, speed and jumping ability carried him to his first Grand National title in 1973. The very next year, Red Rum returned to take his second title. He was the first horse to take successive firsts since Reynoldstown in 1935-1936. Red Rum's spirit and grace had already begun to charm the leagues of Grand National fans.

P5 In the following two years, Red Rum lost out on the title, coming in second both times. When he returned in 1977 to try again, he was largely regarded as past his prime. He was 12 years old and not expected to place highly. He surprised sporting fans around the world when he came in a remarkable 25 lengths ahead of the nearest horse, taking his third Grand National win. To this day, Red Rum's third win is known as one of the greatest moments in horse racing history.

P6 Red Rum was headed for the Grand National once again in 1978 but suffered an injury in one of his heels shortly before the race. He was retired soon after, but his public life and fame by no means decreased with the end of his career. Red Rum traveled all over the country for various engagements. He often led pre-race parades at Aintree Racecourse and was a popular guest at charity benefits and public events.

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about Red Rum the racehorse?
options: He captured public affection long before he won national titles.
He won enormous fame and love from British people.
He became a myth three decades after his retirement.
He owed his great success to several well-known horse trainers.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about Red Rum the racehorse 问对赛马的整体了 解，落点仍是文中可直接找到的客观陈述，而非要求读者跨段推断或归纳全文主旨。

【拆句】What do we learn from the passage about Red Rum the racehorse 主干是 What do we learn，介词短语 from the passage 表来源，about Red Rum the racehorse 表对 象，其中 the racehorse 是 Red Rum 的同位语，仅起身份补充，无陷阱。 46. What do we learn from the passage about Red Rum the racehorse? A) He captured public affection long before he won national titles. B) He won enormous fame and love from British people. C) He became a myth three decades after his retirement. D) He owed his great success to several well-known horse trainers.

【定位】In the history of horse racing, few horses have captured the affection of the British public like Red Rum. Today, three decades after his retirement, he is still one of the best-known and most beloved racehorses of all time. 在赛马史上，很少有马像 Red Rum 那样赢得英国公众的喜爱。今天，距它退役已有三十 年，它仍是有史以来最知名、最受爱戴的赛马之一。

【选项】A) 无中生有 He captured public affection long before he won national titles 凭空添加“夺冠之前 就赢得公众喜爱”的时间先后关系，原文 P1 只说他广受喜爱，未提“夺冠之前”。 B) ✓ 正确 few horses have captured the affection of the British public like Red Rum ↔ He won enormous fame and love from British people the affection of the British public ↔love from British people 预判说“他从英国公众那里获得巨大名声与喜爱”，He won enormous fame and love from British people 是这句话的同义复述，无需推断即可锁定。 C) 偷换概念 原文 three decades after his retirement, he is still one of the best-known and most beloved racehorses of all time 只说退役三十年后他仍然知名；He became a myth three decades after his retirement 把 still well-known 偷换成 became a myth（成为一个神话/传说），属于程度与性质的偷换。 D) 以偏概全 He owed his great success to several well-known horse trainers 说“他把成功归因 于多位知名教练”；但原文 The agent who made the purchase was the now- legendary horse trainer Donald "Ginger" McCain 全文只突出一位教练 Ginger，没 有 several。 Red Rum蹄部的严重骨病对他自己和他的驯马师意味着什么? A) 这只是他们必须克服才能出类拔萃的一个障碍。 B) 这确实是一个劣势,尽管不被认为是致命的。 C) 这实际上是一个刚刚开始的赛马生涯的终结。 D) 这确实是一个他们自己难以克服的主要障碍。

questions.q: What did the serious bone disease in Red Rum's foot mean to himself and his trainer?
options: It was simply a hindrance they had to get over to excel.
It was surely a disadvantage though not considered fatal.
It was actually the end of a racing career that had just begun.
It was really a major obstacle hard to overcome on their own.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干问 the serious bone disease 对二者意味着什么，答案是一句可直接从原文复制的评 价，不需要推断。 47. What did the serious bone disease in Red Rum's foot mean to himself and his trainer? A) It was simply a hindrance they had to get over to excel. B) It was surely a disadvantage though not considered fatal. C) It was actually the end of a racing career that had just begun. D) It was really a major obstacle hard to overcome on their own.

【拆句】What did the serious bone disease in Red Rum's foot mean to himself and his trainer 主干是 the bone disease mean to whom，其中 in Red Rum's foot 是 the serious bone disease 的后置定语，to himself and his trainer 是 mean 的对象。需留意 himself 在英语里指代上文出现的男性化主语，这里回指 Red Rum。

【定位】For Ginger and Red Rum, though, it was just an obstacle to greatness that had to be overcome. 然而对 Ginger 与 Red Rum 来说，这（病情）不过是通往伟大路上一道必须跨越的障碍。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 it was just an obstacle to greatness that had to be overcome ↔ It was simply a hindrance they had to get over to excel had to be overcome ↔they had to get over It was simply a hindrance they had to get over to excel 几乎是 it was just an obstacle to greatness that had to be overcome 的逐词同义改写，预判与选项几乎 重合。 B) 无中生有 It was surely a disadvantage though not considered fatal 加了一个 not considered fatal 的让步，原文从未拿“致命/非致命”来评价此病；选项偷偷在原句外塞 入新评价。 C) 与原文相反 原文 For many horses (and many trainers) this would mean the end of a racing career before it even began 用虚拟 would mean 描述“对很多马而言”的假设结果；It was actually the end of a racing career that had just begun 把这种他人假设包装成 himself and his trainer 身上的事实，与原文相反。 D) 过度推断 It was really a major obstacle hard to overcome on their own 在 obstacle 之外加 了 hard to overcome on their own 这种“难以靠自己克服”的修饰，原文 had to be overcome 只说“必须翻越”，未评价难度，也未提是否需要外援。 作者说Red Rum用他的力量、速度和跳跃能力做了什么? A) 他在12岁时赢得了他的第一个Grand National冠军。 B) 他在1935-1936年连续两次获得冠军。 C) 他在1973年让全世界的体育迷感到惊讶。 D) 他在20世纪70年代三次赢得Grand National冠军。

questions.q: What does the author say Red Rum did with his power, speed and jumping ability?
options: He won his first Grand National title at 12.
He took two firsts successively in 1935-1936.
He surprised sporting fans worldwide in 1973.
He took three Grand National wins in the 1970s.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say Red Rum did with his power, speed and jumping ability 问 凭这三种能力做成了什么，原文里必有承接句直接给出结果。

【拆句】What does the author say Red Rum did with his power, speed and jumping ability 句 中 the author say 是插入性主语从句框架，真正的问题核心是 Red Rum did what with his power, speed and jumping ability，介词 with 引出工具。基础薄弱的考生容易被 does the author say 带偏去找作者观点，实质仍是问赛马本身的行为。

【定位】Red Rum's true talent came out in steeplechases. His power, speed and jumping ability carried him to his first Grand National title in 1973. The very next year, Red Rum returned to take his second title. He was the first horse to take successive firsts since Reynoldstown in 1935-1936. Red Rum 真正的才华在障碍赛中绽放。他的力量、速度与跳跃能力把他带向 1973 年第一 座全国大赛冠军。次年他再度归来，拿下第二冠，成为自 1935-1936 年 Reynoldstown 之 后第一匹蝉联的马。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 He won his first Grand National title at 12 把首冠年龄定为 12 岁；但 his first Grand National title in 1973 是首冠时间，而 He was 12 years old 是 1977 年第三冠 时的年龄，选项把第三冠的年龄安到首冠头上。 B) 张冠李戴 He took two firsts successively in 1935-1936 把 1935-1936 连冠归到 Red Rum 名 下，但原文 He was the first horse to take successive firsts since Reynoldstown in 1935-1936 明确 1935-1936 的连冠属于另一匹马 Reynoldstown。 C) 张冠李戴 He surprised sporting fans worldwide in 1973 把“worldwide 惊讶”与 1973 挂钩， 但原文 He surprised sporting fans around the world 明确发生在 1977 年第三冠那 次，与 in 1973 无关。 D) ✓ 正确 his first Grand National title in 1973 ↔three Grand National wins in the 1970s the first horse to take successive firsts ↔three Grand National wins in the 1970s taking his third Grand National win ↔three Grand National wins in the 1970s 把 1973、1974、1977 三场冠军合并，正好对应 three Grand National wins in the 1970s，全部时间都落在 1970 年代。 当Red Rum在1977年重返赛场时,人们普遍对他有什么看法? A) 他已经过了赛马生涯的巅峰期。 B) 他在Grand National障碍赛中将没有对手。 C) 他已经失去了对Grand National众多粉丝的吸引力。 D) 可以期待他在职业生涯的黄金时期重现辉煌。

questions.q: What did people generally think of Red Rum when he returned to the racecourse in 1977?
options: He had already passed the peak of his racing life.
He would have no rival in Grand National steeplechases.
He had lost his charm with the leagues of Grand National fans.
He could be expected to repeat his glory in the prime of his career.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did people generally think of Red Rum when he returned to the racecourse in 1977 问的是原文中直接表述过的公众看法，不需要跨段推断。

【拆句】What did people generally think of Red Rum when he returned to the racecourse in 1977 主干 What did people think of X，时间状语从句 when he returned to the racecourse in 1977 用一般过去时锁定 1977 那次复出。考生注意 think of 在此是“对…… 有何看法”，不是“想到”。

【定位】When he returned in 1977 to try again, he was largely regarded as past his prime. He was 12 years old and not expected to place highly. 1977 年他再度归来尝试时，普遍被认为已过巅峰；他已 12 岁，不被看好会拿到好名次。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 was largely regarded as past his prime ↔He had already passed the peak of his racing life 原文 past his prime 与选项 passed the peak of his racing life 是同义改写，且 was largely regarded as 完整对应题干 people generally think。 B) 与原文相反 He would have no rival in Grand National steeplechases 说他在大赛中无敌手；原 文 he was largely regarded as past his prime 表达的是相反的预期——大家觉得他过 气了。 C) 与原文相反 He had lost his charm with the leagues of Grand National fans 说他对大赛粉丝失 去了魅力；但原文 Red Rum's spirit and grace had already begun to charm the leagues of Grand National fans 与 P5 处都未出现魅力消失的描述，反而 his public life and fame by no means decreased 进一步否定这一说法。 D) 与原文相反 He could be expected to repeat his glory in the prime of his career 说“大家期待他 在巅峰期再现辉煌”；但原文 not expected to place highly 明说他不被看好，且 past his prime 已说明他不在巅峰。 49. What did people generally think of Red Rum when he returned to the racecourse in 1977? A) He had already passed the peak of his racing life. B) He would have no rival in Grand National steeplechases. C) He had lost his charm with the leagues of Grand National fans. D) He could be expected to repeat his glory in the prime of his career. Red Rum的职业生涯结束后情况如何? A) 他的脚后跟遭受剧烈疼痛。 B) 他几乎把所有时间都花在旅行上。 C) 他靠各种慈善救济生活。 D) 他依然著名和受欢迎。

questions.q: What became of Red Rum after his career ended?
options: He suffered from severe pain in a heel.
He spent almost all his time traveling.
He lived on various charity benefits.
He remained famous and popular.
questions.explain:
【判型】What became of Red Rum after his career ended 问退役后的整体情况，原文末段直接 给出概括语句，无需跨段归纳。

【拆句】What became of Red Rum after his career ended 主干 What became of Red Rum， become of 是固定搭配，意为“……后来怎样了”，时间状语从句 after his career ended 限 定时间范围。考生容易把 became 理解成“成为”而读不懂句子，记住 became of 是整体短 语，不可拆。

【定位】He was retired soon after, but his public life and fame by no means decreased with the end of his career. Red Rum traveled all over the country for various engagements. He often led pre-race parades at Aintree Racecourse and was a popular guest at charity benefits and public events. 他随即退役，但他的公众生活与名气并未随职业结束而减退。他全国奔波出席各种活动，常 在 Aintree 赛马场领跑赛前游行，也是慈善活动与公众活动上的常客。 50. What became of Red Rum after his career ended? A) He suffered from severe pain in a heel. B) He spent almost all his time traveling. C) He lived on various charity benefits. D) He remained famous and popular.

【选项】A) 答非所问 He suffered from severe pain in a heel 把蹄部受伤说成退役后的状态；原文 suffered an injury in one of his heels shortly before the race. He was retired soon after 明 示受伤在退役前，且未提持续“severe pain”。 B) 过度推断 He spent almost all his time traveling 把 traveled all over the country for various engagements 夸大为“几乎所有时间都在旅行”，原文只说他经常奔波出席活动，没说 “几乎所有时间”。 C) 偷换概念 He lived on various charity benefits 中 lived on 意为“靠……生活”，把 was a popular guest at charity benefits 这种“出席慈善活动”误读为“靠慈善活动养活”，性质 完全不同。 D) ✓ 正确 his public life and fame by no means decreased ↔He remained famous and popular Red Rum traveled all over the country for various engagements ↔ He remained famous and popular P6 既有总括 by no means decreased 又有具体 popular guest，二者共同指向 He remained famous and popular。

items.title: 2023年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2023年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts. It is quite horrifying to see people being guided by some unknown force. But how wise is it, really, to let your instincts drive your decisions?

P2 In the decision-making process, relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you. Simply "feeling" that something is right or should be done is highly subjective and can drown you.

P3 On the other hand, there is a more rational approach to making decisions. Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions. These reduce the likelihood of errors and increase the chances of success. Big, systematic data is mostly the foundation of most of our decisions, personal and business alike. But with its extreme usability comes a complication: what do you do if you strongly feel something should not be done, even if the data insists that it should?

P4 This seemingly easy question is what drives the need to understand the relationship between instincts and data in the decision-making process. Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions.

P5 Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences or information, which acknowledges that instinctive decisions have worked in the past. Decisions are not about making the choice and braving the consequences because you want to blindly trust your instincts. They are about combining your inner wisdom with the knowledge of systematic data to make the best decisions.

P6 Sometimes, rational analysis and data are impractical to be employed in certain situations. Absence of definitive criteria, and time and resource constraints, and novel situations are instances which limit the practicality of data. The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you. In these situations, instincts can help you make effective and quick decisions.

P7 Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions. It reduces the chances of making mistakes, and has increasingly become a favorite approach to decision-making among leaders of today.

questions.q: What does the author say businesspeople often do?
options: Strive to make sense of some unknown forces.
Avoid being driven by their own feeling.
Draw on a vast wealth of past experience.
Rely on instincts in decision-making.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say businesspeople often do? 问的是「商人通常做什么」这一可 在原文逐字核实的客观行为，不含 infer/imply。

【拆句】题干主干是 What does the author say businesspeople often do?，what 作宾语前置； the author say 是插入成分，可剥离；剥离后等价于「Businesspeople often do what?」 结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】People in business often make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts. 商界人士常常基于自己的个人感觉或直觉做决策。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文用 unknown force 比喻直觉的神秘性，并未让商人「弄清未知力量」；Strive to make sense of some unknown forces 凭空给出动作。 B) 与原文相反 原文说商人「常凭感觉决策」，Avoid being driven by their own feeling 却说「避免 被感觉驱动」，完全反向。 C) 张冠李戴 relying on instincts only makes sense when you have a vast experience to support you 是作者给「合理使用直觉」开的条件，并非商人「实际正在做的事」。 D) ✓ 正确 make decisions based on their own personal feelings or instincts ↔ Rely on instincts in decision-making 预判「依赖直觉作决策」与 Rely on instincts in decision-making 高度重合，正确项 锁定。 为了做出明智的决策,我们应该考虑什么? A) 出错的可能性。 B) 系统性的数据和分析。 C) 情况的复杂性。 D) 个人感受和商业策略。

questions.q: What should we take into account in order to make informed decisions?
options: The likelihood of errors.
Systematic data and analysis.
The complexity of circumstances.
Personal feelings and business strategies
questions.explain:
【判型】What should we take into account in order to make informed decisions? 问的是「为 了做出明智决策应当考虑什么」，答案是原文直接陈述的因素。

【拆句】题干主干 What should we take into account，what 作 take into account 的宾语前置； in order to make informed decisions 是表目的的不定式状语；句式简单。

【定位】Data and analysis have long been associated with informed decisions. 数据与分析长期以来一直与明智的决策紧密相关。 52. What should we take into account in order to make informed decisions? A) The likelihood of errors. B) Systematic data and analysis. C) The complexity of circumstances. D) Personal feelings and business strategies

【选项】A) 答非所问 原文 These reduce the likelihood of errors 说数据与分析「降低出错概率」，The likelihood of errors 只是数据带来的「结果」，不是「应当考虑的因素」。 B) ✓ 正确 Data and analysis ↔Systematic data and analysis 预判「依靠数据与分析」与 Systematic data and analysis 完全对应，且原文 Big, systematic data 进一步加固，正确项锁定。 C) 无中生有 原文从未出现 The complexity of circumstances（环境的复杂性）这一表述，与「明 智决策的依靠」无关。 D) 偷换概念 原文把 personal feelings or instincts 视作「常被依赖却需谨慎」的对象，并未把它与 business strategies 并列为「做明智决策的因素」。 在决策过程中,如果直觉与数据不一致,人们应该怎么做? A) 用以往的经验解决这个两难困境。 B) 弄清楚两者中哪一个更可靠。 C) 将两者结合起来。 D) 让直觉优先于数据。

questions.q: What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data?
options: Resolve the dilemma with previous experience.
Figure out which of the two is more reliable.
Combine the two together.
Prioritize instincts over data.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data? 问的是作者给出的具体做法，原文有 using data and instincts in conjunction 直陈方案。

【拆句】题干 What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data? 主句是 What should people do，in a decision-making process 介词短语作地点 状语；if instincts disagree with data 是 if 引导的条件状语从句；结构清楚。

【定位】Without making things complicated, the solution to this dilemma is using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions. 简单来说，这一难题的解决方案是把数据和直觉结合起来使用，以达成最佳的决策。 53. What should people do in a decision-making process if instincts disagree with data? A) Resolve the dilemma with previous experience. B) Figure out which of the two is more reliable. C) Combine the two together. D) Prioritize instincts over data.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences 是「直觉的支撑机 制」，不是题干问的「矛盾时的解决办法」。 B) 无中生有 原文从未让人「比较谁更可靠」，Figure out which of the two is more reliable 是凭 空增加的取舍动作。 C) ✓ 正确 using data and instincts in conjunction ↔Combine the two together 预判「把数据与直觉结合使用」与 Combine the two together 完全等价，正确项 锁定。 D) 与原文相反 原文明确反对盲目信任直觉（you want to blindly trust your instincts 被作者否定）， Prioritize instincts over data 却把直觉摆在数据之上，反向。 当面对限制数据实用性的各种因素时,我们应该怎么做? A) 进行理性和系统的分析。 B) 探索最可行的选择。 C) 求助于我们内在的智慧。 D) 应用明确的标准。

questions.q: What should we do when facing various factors that limit the practicality of data?
options: Make a rational and systematic analysis.
Explore the most feasible options.
Resort to our inner wisdom.
Apply definitive criteria.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should we do when facing various factors that limit the practicality of data? 问 的是特定情境下的做法，仍是定位＋复述。

【拆句】题干主句 What should we do，when facing various factors 是 when 引导的现在分词时 间状语，省略主语 we；that limit the practicality of data 是定语从句，修饰 factors。基 础薄弱的同学要看清「factors」才是从句修饰对象，而不是「we」。

【定位】The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you. 唯一可行的办法，是依靠你的直觉告诉你的东西。 54. What should we do when facing various factors that limit the practicality of data? A) Make a rational and systematic analysis. B) Explore the most feasible options. C) Resort to our inner wisdom. D) Apply definitive criteria.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文明说数据在此场合「不可行」，Make a rational and systematic analysis 反让你 做理性系统分析，正好走反方向。 B) 偷换概念 原文说 The only feasible option is to rely on what your instincts tell you，给出的 是「唯一可行的办法」；Explore the most feasible options 把「唯一选项」偷换成 「探索多个最可行选项」，且把动作偷换成「探索」。 C) ✓ 正确 rely on what your instincts tell you ↔Resort to our inner wisdom 预判「依靠直觉」与 Resort to our inner wisdom（求助内在智慧）通过 P5 给出的等 价关系完全对应，正确项锁定。 D) 与原文相反 原文 Absence of definitive criteria 指出此场合「没有明确标准」，Apply definitive criteria 反让你「应用明确标准」，与原文完全对立。 根据作者的观点,决策要成为最佳决策需要什么? A) 结合运用直觉和数据。 B) 在做出选择时评估所有因素。 C) 回忆过去实际奏效的做法。 D) 避免随意相信直觉。

questions.q: What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author?
options: Applying instincts and data in conjunction.
Assessing all factors when making a choice.
Recalling what has actually worked in the past.
Refraining from trusting instincts arbitrarily.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? 问的是 「让决策成为最佳」的所需条件，是原文有明确句子可对应的细节，并非要从全文归纳的 主旨。

【拆句】题干 What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? 句 型为「it takes sth for sb/sth to do sth」，what 替换 sth 提前；for decisions 是 take 的逻辑主语；to become the best 是真正的目的不定式。看懂这个句型是关键，否则容易 把题干误读成主旨题。

【定位】Combining instinctive and rational analysis produces well-rounded decisions. 把直觉与理性分析结合起来，能产出周全的决策。 55. What does it take for decisions to become the best according to the author? A) Applying instincts and data in conjunction. B) Assessing all factors when making a choice. C) Recalling what has actually worked in the past. D) Refraining from trusting instincts arbitrarily.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Combining instinctive and rational analysis ↔Applying instincts and data in conjunction using data and instincts in conjunction to arrive at the best possible decisions ↔ Applying instincts and data in conjunction 预判「直觉＋理性分析联用」与 Applying instincts and data in conjunction 完全对 应，且 P4 与 P7 双句佐证，正确项锁定。 B) 无中生有 原文从未要求「评估所有因素」，Assessing all factors when making a choice 是无 来源的扩张表述。 C) 以偏概全 Instinctive decisions are always backed by previous experiences 只是说直觉以经验 为后盾，并不等于「让决策变最佳」的充分条件，Recalling what has actually worked in the past 把直觉一侧的支撑当成全部条件。 D) 以偏概全 you want to blindly trust your instincts 提到「不要盲目相信直觉」，但这只是「最佳 决策」的一个否定性前提，不是充分条件，Refraining from trusting instincts arbitrarily 把单一前提当成全部条件。

items.title: 2024年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2024年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Lao Zi once said, "Care about what other people think and you will always be their prisoner."

P2 People-pleasing, or seeking self-worth through others' approval, is unproductive and an exhausting way to go through life. Why do we allow what others think of us to have so much power over how we feel about ourselves? If it's true that you can't please all people all of the time, wouldn't it make sense to stop trying?

P3 Unfortunately, sense often isn't driving our behavior. For social beings who desire love and belonging, wanting to be liked, and caring about the effect we have on others, is healthy and allows us to make connections. However, where we get into trouble is when our self-worth is dependent upon whether we win someone's approval or not.

P4 This need to be liked can be traced back to when we were children and were completely dependent on others to take care of us: Small children are not just learning how to walk and communicate, they are also trying to learn how the world works. We learn about who we are and what is expected of us based on interactions with others, so, to a four-year-old, if Mommy or Daddy doesn't like him or her, there is the danger that they will abandon them. We need to understand that when we desperately want someone to approve of us, it's being driven by that little kid part of us that is still terrified of abandonment.

P5 As you become more capable of providing yourself with the approval you seek, your need for external validation will start to vanish, leaving you stronger, more confident, and yes, happier in your life. Imagine how much time we lose each moment we restrain our authentic selves in an effort to be liked.

P6 If we base our worth on the opinions of others, we cheat ourselves of the power to shape our experiences and embrace life not only for others but also for ourselves, because ultimately, there is no difference. So embrace the cliché(老话) and love yourself as it's highly doubtful that you'll regret it.

questions.q: What can we conclude from Lao Zi's quotation?
options: We should see through other people's attempt to make a prisoner of us.
We can never really please other people even if we try as hard as we can.
We can never be truly free if taking to heart others' opinion of us.
We should care about other people's view as much as they care about our own.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What can we conclude from Lao Zi's quotation?含conclude，要求由引语推出结 论，而非复述字面。 46. What can we conclude from Lao Zi's quotation? A) We should see through other people's attempt to make a prisoner of us. B) We can never really please other people even if we try as hard as we can. C) We can never be truly free if taking to heart others' opinion of us. D) We should care about other people's view as much as they care about our own.

【拆句】题干What can we conclude from Lao Zi's quotation?是常规 wh- 疑问句，主干为 What can we conclude，from 介词短语修饰 conclude，结构平直，无陷阱。

【定位】Lao Zi once said, "Care about what other people think and you will always be their prisoner." 老子曾说：在意别人怎么想，你就会永远做他们的囚徒。

【选项】A) 把比喻当字面属偷换概念 see through other people's attempt to make a prisoner of us把 prisoner 当成真有 人想囚禁我们，原文是比喻、不是有人主动加害。 B) 张冠李戴 We can never really please other people even if we try as hard as we can.说的是 讨好不可能成功，这是If it's true that you can't please all people all of the time的内 容，不是P1老子那句引语的结论。 C) ✓ 正确 Care about what other people think ↔taking to heart others' opinion of us you will always be their prisoner ↔can never be truly free We can never be truly free if taking to heart others' opinion of us.同时覆盖了原文 if-then 链条的两端，是定位句的完整同义改写。 D) 无中生有 as much as they care about our own提出一种对等关心的主张，但P1引语只说在意他 人会失自由，根本未涉及对方是否在意我们。 如果我们将自我价值建立在他人的认可之上,会发生什么? A) 我们被爱的渴望将得到满足。 B) 我们的生活将变得毫无成果且令人疲惫。 C) 我们作为社会存在的身份将受到影响。 D) 我们的自我意识将被强化和增强。

questions.q: What will happen if we base our self-worth on other people's approval?
options: Our desire to be loved will be fulfilled.
Our life will be unfruitful and exhausting.
Our identity as social beings will be affected.
Our sense of self will be sharpened and enhanced.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What will happen if we base our self-worth on other people's approval?问的是一 种行为的直接后果，答案应来自原文对应描述句的客观转述。

【拆句】题干What will happen if we base our self-worth on other people's approval?是 if 引 导条件状语从句的疑问句，主干 What will happen，base A on B 是固定搭配，意为以B为 基础。

【定位】People-pleasing, or seeking self-worth through others' approval, is unproductive and an exhausting way to go through life. 讨好他人，或者说通过他人的认可来寻求自我价值，是一种无成效且令人疲惫的活法。 47. What will happen if we base our self-worth on other people's approval? A) Our desire to be loved will be fulfilled. B) Our life will be unfruitful and exhausting. C) Our identity as social beings will be affected. D) Our sense of self will be sharpened and enhanced.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文将该行为定性为 unproductive、exhausting，选项Our desire to be loved will be fulfilled.却说愿望被满足，与原文极性相反。 B) ✓ 正确 unproductive ↔unfruitful an exhausting way to go through life ↔exhausting Our life will be unfruitful and exhausting.同时覆盖了原文两个评价形容词 unproductive 与 exhausting，正合预判。 C) 无中生有 For social beings who desire love and belonging是描述人之常情，原文并未说 social beings 这一身份会因 people-pleasing 而被影响。 D) 与原文相反 where we get into trouble is when our self-worth is dependent upon whether we win someone's approval or not说明此举使自我陷入麻烦，Our sense of self will be sharpened and enhanced.却说自我被强化，正好相反。 什么可以解释我们需要被喜欢或认可? A) 我们对与他人互动的强烈渴望。 B) 我们对世界运作方式的理解。 C) 我们对被抛弃之痛的认知。 D) 我们早期童年时对被遗弃的恐惧。

questions.q: What may account for our need to be liked or approved of?
options: Our desperate longing for interactions with others.
Our understanding of the workings of the world.
Our knowledge about the pain of abandonment.
Our early childhood fear of being deserted.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What may account for our need to be liked or approved of?问一种心理需求的成 因，原文若给出明确解释句，答案即其同义改写。

【拆句】题干What may account for our need to be liked or approved of?主语是 What，谓语 may account for，宾语为 our need to be liked or approved of。be liked 与 be approved of 是两个并列被动不定式，approved of 中 of 不可省，因 approve of 是固定 及物动词短语。

【定位】This need to be liked can be traced back to when we were children and were completely dependent on others to take care of us… We need to understand that when we desperately want someone to approve of us, it's being driven by that little kid part of us that is still terrified of abandonment. 这种想被喜欢的需求可以追溯到我们还是孩子、完全依赖他人照料的时候……我们要明白， 当我们极度渴望得到他人认可时，背后真正驱动的，是那个仍然害怕被遗弃的小小孩子。 48. What may account for our need to be liked or approved of? A) Our desperate longing for interactions with others. B) Our understanding of the workings of the world. C) Our knowledge about the pain of abandonment. D) Our early childhood fear of being deserted.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 We learn about who we are and what is expected of us based on interactions with others里 interactions 是孩子学习自我的途径，不是渴望被喜欢的成因。 B) 偷换概念 they are also trying to learn how the world works说孩子在学习世界运转方式，这是 孩子在做的事，不是想被喜欢的成因。 C) 偷换概念 knowledge about the pain of abandonment说我们已经知道被遗弃的痛苦；原文实 际说的是儿童害怕被遗弃 still terrified of abandonment，是恐惧而非已掌握的知识。 D) ✓ 正确 when we were children ↔early childhood terrified of abandonment ↔fear of being deserted Our early childhood fear of being deserted.同时锁住了童年这个时间端与害怕被遗弃 这个情感端，与原文因果链根源端完全对应。 当我们更有能力为自己提供所渴望的认可时,我们能做什么? A) 享受更幸福的生活。 B) 实行自我克制。 C) 获得更多外部认可。 D) 增强我们的想象力。

questions.q: What can we do when we become better able to provide ourselves with the desired approval?
options: Enjoy a happier life.
Exercise self-restraint.
Receive more external validation.
Strengthen our power of imagination.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What can we do when we become better able to provide ourselves with the desired approval?问的是某条件下发生的事/可获得的结果，属直接的客观陈述。

【拆句】题干What can we do when we become better able to provide ourselves with the desired approval?主句是 What can we do，when 引导时间状语从句。从句主干 we become…able to…，better 修饰形容词 able。provide sb. with sth. 是固定搭配，意为 给…提供…。

【定位】As you become more capable of providing yourself with the approval you seek, your need for external validation will start to vanish, leaving you stronger, more confident, and yes, happier in your life. 当你越来越能给自己所寻求的认可时，你对外部认可的需要会开始消退，让你变得更强、更 自信、并且——是的——在生活中更幸福。 49. What can we do when we become better able to provide ourselves with the desired approval? A) Enjoy a happier life. B) Exercise self-restraint. C) Receive more external validation. D) Strengthen our power of imagination.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 happier in your life ↔happier life Enjoy a happier life.精准对应三个并列结果中的最后一项 happier in your life，且最直 白、无歧义。 B) 与原文相反 原文we restrain our authentic selves是把克制真实自我描述为浪费时间的行为，不是 该条件下我们应做的事；Exercise self-restraint.反而把原文要批判的行为当成了结果。 C) 与原文相反 your need for external validation will start to vanish明确说对外部认可的需求会消 退，Receive more external validation.却说获得更多，方向相反。 D) 偷换概念 Imagine how much time we lose…是作者修辞性祈使，引导读者去想象浪费的时间， 并不是说我们会去强化想象力。 作者在最后一段建议我们做什么? A) 为自己和他人拥抱生活。 B) 将我们的价值建立在他人的看法之上。 C) 将我们的经历视为财富。 D) 爱现在的自己。

questions.q: What does the author advise us to do in the last paragraph?
options: Embrace life for ourselves and for others.
Base our worth on others' opinions.
See our experiences as assets.
Love ourselves as we are.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What does the author advise us to do in the last paragraph?限定段落+问具体建 议，按位置直接精读末段祈使句即可。

【拆句】题干What does the author advise us to do in the last paragraph?是 wh- 疑问句，主干 What does the author advise us to do，advise sb. to do sth. 是固定搭配，in the last paragraph 是地点状语限定范围。

【定位】So embrace the cliché(老话) and love yourself as it's highly doubtful that you'll regret it. 所以拥抱这句老话——爱自己吧，你几乎不可能后悔。 50. What does the author advise us to do in the last paragraph? A) Embrace life for ourselves and for others. B) Base our worth on others' opinions. C) See our experiences as assets. D) Love ourselves as we are.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 embrace life not only for others but also for ourselves说不仅为他人也为自己拥抱生 活，是过渡论述，不是末段 So 之后给出的最终建议；选项Embrace life for ourselves and for others.把它包装成建议，越权代替了真正的祈使句。 B) 与原文相反 If we base our worth on the opinions of others, we cheat ourselves of the power to shape our experiences明确指出以他人评价为基础是自我欺骗，作者反对这一做 法，Base our worth on others' opinions.反而把它当建议。 C) 无中生有 原文the power to shape our experiences说的是塑造自身体验的力量，不是把体验视 为财富。See our experiences as assets.借 experiences 一词制造表层相似，实则原文 从未把它定义为 assets。 D) ✓ 正确 love yourself ↔Love ourselves as we are Love ourselves as we are.忠实保留了原文祈使动作 love+反身代词的结构，是末段建 议的直译版。

items.title: 2024年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2024年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Some people have said aging is more a slide into forgetfulness than a journey towards wisdom. However, a growing body of research suggests that late-in-life learning is possible. In reality, education does an aging brain good.

P2 Throughout life, people's brains constantly renovate themselves. In the late 1960s, British brain scientist Geoffrey Raisman spied growth in damaged brain regions of rats through an electron microscope; their brains were forging new connections. This meant brains may change every time a person learns something new.

P3 Of course, that doesn't mean the brain isn't affected by the effects of time. Just as height usually declines over the years, so does brain volume: Humans lose about 4 percent every decade starting in their 40s. But that reduction doesn't necessarily make people think slower; as long as we are alive and functioning, we can alter our brains with new information and experiences.

P4 In fact, scientists now suspect accumulating novel experiences, facts, and skills can keep people's minds more flexible. New pathways can strengthen our ever-changing mental structure, even as the brain shrinks.

P5 Conventional fixes like word puzzles and brain-training apps can contribute to mental durability. Even something as simple as taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation can keep the brain healthy.

P6 A desire for new life challenges can further boost brainpower. Research about aging adults who take on new enterprises shows improved function and memory as well as a reduced risk of mental disease. Openness—a characteristic defined by curiosity and a desire for knowledge—may also help folks pass brain tests. Some folks are born with this take-in-the-world attitude, but those who aren't as genetically gifted aren't necessarily out of luck. While genes can encourage an interest in doing new things, a 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging found completing reasoning tasks like puzzles and number games can enhance that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain. That's why brain scientist Richard Kennedy says "It's not that old dogs can't learn new tricks. It's that maybe old dogs don't realize why they should."

questions.q: What do some people think of aging adults?
options: Their wisdom grows as time goes by.
Their memory gradually deteriorates.
They can benefit from late-in-life learning.
They are likely to have mental health issues.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do some people think of aging adults? 用 what do ... think of 直接问看法，且明 确限定主语 some people，属于对原文具体观点的事实复述。

【拆句】Q51 主干为 What do some people think of aging adults，think of 表示「对……的看 法」，think 与 of 分立但语义绑定，基础薄弱考生易把 think of 拆开理解为「想到」，注 意它是「评价」之义。

【定位】Some people have said aging is more a slide into forgetfulness than a journey towards wisdom. 某些人说，衰老与其说是一段通向智慧的旅程，不如说是一步步滑向健忘。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 题干问 some people 的看法，原文 some people 恰恰用 more A than B 否定了「通 向智慧」这一端，Their wisdom grows as time goes by. 正好与之相反。 B) ✓ 正确 a slide into forgetfulness ↔memory gradually deteriorates 预判「记性变差」与 Their memory gradually deteriorates. 的语义完全一致，且整句 都被原文 slide into forgetfulness 覆盖，无添加成分。 C) 张冠李戴 They can benefit from late-in-life learning. 是作者及研究方的观点（a growing body of research suggests that late-in-life learning is possible），不属于题干所问 的 some people。 D) 无中生有 首段并未提及 some people 认为衰老会导致 mental health issues（精神健康问 题），原文只说「健忘」（forgetfulness），健忘不等于心理疾病。 我们能从Geoffrey Raisman的发现中得出什么结论? A) 大脑损伤严重阻碍人的学习。 B) 脑力衰退的速度比我们想象的要慢。 C) 大脑可以通过学习得到更新和改善。 D) 大脑在新条件下建立连接。

questions.q: What can we conclude from Geoffrey Raisman's finding?
options: Brain damage seriously hinders one's learning.
Brain power weakens slower than we imagine.
Brains can refresh and improve with learning.
Brains forge connections under new conditions.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we conclude from Geoffrey Raisman's finding? 出现 conclude，要求从已述 事实再推一步得出结论。 52. What can we conclude from Geoffrey Raisman's finding? A) Brain damage seriously hinders one's learning. B) Brain power weakens slower than we imagine. C) Brains can refresh and improve with learning. D) Brains forge connections under new conditions.

【拆句】Q52 句中 what 是 conclude 的宾语，from Geoffrey Raisman's finding 是状语，结构平 铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】In the late 1960s, British brain scientist Geoffrey Raisman spied growth in damaged brain regions of rats through an electron microscope; their brains were forging new connections. This meant brains may change every time a person learns something new. 上世纪 60 年代末，英国脑科学家 Geoffrey Raisman 用电子显微镜观察到老鼠受损脑区长 出新生组织；它们的大脑正在缔结新连接。这意味着，每当一个人学到新东西，大脑都可能 发生改变。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只说 Raisman 在「受损脑区」观察到新连接，并未谈论 brain damage 对 learning 的影响，更没有 hinders 这种负向判断。 B) 无中生有 原文未做「比想象慢/快」的速度比较，brain power weakens slower 这种比较关系在 Raisman 段并不存在。 C) ✓ 正确 brains may change every time a person learns something new ↔ Brains can refresh and improve with learning. 预判核心是「学习—大脑改变/更新」，Brains can refresh and improve with learning. 用 refresh、improve 概括 change + forging new connections 的双层含 义，且 with learning 直接对应「每当学新东西」，整句无溢出。 D) 答非所问 Brains forge connections under new conditions. 几乎照搬 their brains were forging new connections，但题干问的是 conclude（结论意义），而该选项只重复了 实验事实，没把意义说出来。 即使大脑萎缩,有什么能帮助维持大脑健康? A) 用传统方式进行日常事务。 B) 避免担心我们的心智持久性。 C) 模仿老狗学新把戏的方式。 D) 用新颖的方式处理日常任务。

questions.q: What is one thing that helps maintain the health of our brain even as it shrinks?
options: Doing daily routines by conventional means.
Avoiding worrying about our mental durability.
Imitating old dogs' way of learning new tricks.
Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is one thing that helps maintain the health of our brain 用 one thing that ... 直 接问一件具体做法，属事实复述。 53. What is one thing that helps maintain the health of our brain even as it shrinks? A) Doing daily routines by conventional means. B) Avoiding worrying about our mental durability. C) Imitating old dogs' way of learning new tricks. D) Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways.

【拆句】Q53 主干 What is one thing，其后 that ... 是定语从句修饰 thing；even as it shrinks 是让步状语，as 此处等于 although，it 指代 brain，须留意 it 的指代关系不要错认 成 health。

【定位】Even something as simple as taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation can keep the brain healthy. 哪怕是像换条路去超市、或换个地方度假这样简单的事，也能让大脑保持健康。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文强调要「换新方式」做日常事，而 Doing daily routines by conventional means. 强调用 conventional means（常规方式），方向完全相反。 B) 无中生有 Avoiding worrying about our mental durability. 提到「避免担忧脑力耐久度」，但原 文 P5 谈的是「具体做法」，从未谈论「担忧」或「避免担忧」这个心理层面。 C) 偷换概念 原文末段 It\'s not that old dogs can\'t learn new tricks. It\'s that maybe old dogs don\'t realize why they should. 中的 old dogs 是比喻人，不是真的「狗的学习方 式」；Imitating old dogs\' way of learning new tricks. 把比喻当字面，且并非 P5 的 护脑手段。 D) ✓ 正确 taking a different route to the grocery store or going somewhere new on vacation ↔ Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways. 预判的两个关键语义点「日常事」和「新方式」在 Approaching everyday tasks in novel ways. 中一一对应，没有任何额外成分。 作者认为什么有助于改善大脑功能? A) 保持好奇心和求知欲。 B) 渴望在年老时通过大脑测试。 C) 迎接生活挑战并避免风险。 D) 增强对严重精神疾病的免疫力。

questions.q: What does the author say can contribute to the improvement of brain function?
options: Being curious and desiring knowledge.
Being eager to pass brain tests at an old age.
Rising to life's challenges and avoiding risks.
Boosting immunity to serious mental diseases.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say can contribute to the improvement of brain function? 直 接问 author 提出的「促进项」，是对原文表述的事实复述。

【拆句】Q54 主干为 What does the author say can contribute to ...，what 既作 say 的宾语，又 作 can contribute to 的逻辑主语（省略关系代词的嵌套从句结构），基础薄弱考生易在两 个谓语间断错语义，建议拆为「作者说，[什么]能促进脑功能提升」。 54. What does the author say can contribute to the improvement of brain function? A) Being curious and desiring knowledge. B) Being eager to pass brain tests at an old age. C) Rising to life's challenges and avoiding risks. D) Boosting immunity to serious mental diseases.

【定位】Openness—a characteristic defined by curiosity and a desire for knowledge—may also help folks pass brain tests. 「开放性」——一种由好奇心和求知欲所定义的特质——也可以帮助人们顺利通过脑力 测试。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 curiosity and a desire for knowledge ↔Being curious and desiring knowledge. 预判的两个核心要素「好奇心」和「求知欲」在 Being curious and desiring knowledge. 中由同根词分别承接，且选项整体只表达这两点，无多余成分，无遗漏。 B) 偷换概念 原文说 openness 能帮助 pass brain tests，是「特质 → 通过测试」的因果；Being eager to pass brain tests at an old age. 把「通过测试」偷换成「渴望通过测试」， 把结果偷换成动机，方向不同。 C) 无中生有 原文 A desire for new life challenges can further boost brainpower. 只说「迎接新 挑战」能提升脑力，从未提到 avoiding risks（规避风险）；C 项硬加了「规避风险」 这一成分。 D) 偷换概念 原文 improved function and memory as well as a reduced risk of mental disease 中，reduced risk of mental disease 是 take on new enterprises 带来的「结果之 一」，而非「促进脑功能的手段」；Boosting immunity to serious mental diseases. 把这一结果倒置成促进手段。 2012年《心理学与衰老》期刊研究的发现是什么? A) 想要解决谜题能增强人的推理能力。 B) 玩数字游戏会意外刺激人的记忆力。 C) 渴望新体验有助于更新大脑。 D) 学习新把戏不应该只限于老狗。

questions.q: What is the finding of the 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging?
options: Wishing to solve puzzles enhances one's reasoning power.
Playing number games unexpectedly stimulates one's memory.
Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain.
Learning new tricks should not be confined to old dogs only.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the finding of the 2012 study 直接问研究发现内容，属定位+复述型问法。

【拆句】Q55 主干为 What is the finding，of the 2012 study 与 in the journal Psychology and Aging 都是修饰 finding 的介词短语，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 55. What is the finding of the 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging? A) Wishing to solve puzzles enhances one's reasoning power. B) Playing number games unexpectedly stimulates one's memory. C) Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain. D) Learning new tricks should not be confined to old dogs only.

【定位】While genes can encourage an interest in doing new things, a 2012 study in the journal Psychology and Aging found completing reasoning tasks like puzzles and number games can enhance that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain. 尽管基因能在一定程度上鼓励一个人对新事物的兴趣，但 2012 年发表在《Psychology and Aging》期刊上的一项研究发现，完成像谜题、数字游戏这样的推理任务能够强化「想 要新体验」的欲望，而这种欲望反过来又能刷新大脑。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文是「做推理任务（含 puzzles）→ 强化对新体验的欲望 → 刷新大脑」，Wishing to solve puzzles enhances one\'s reasoning power. 反过来变成「想做谜题 → 提升 推理力」，方向被颠倒，且原文从未谈 enhance reasoning power。 B) 无中生有 原文链条终点是 refresh the brain（刷新大脑），不是 stimulates one\'s memory （刺激记忆）；且 unexpectedly（出乎意料地）也不在原文里。 C) ✓ 正确 that desire for novel experiences, which can, in turn, refresh the brain ↔ Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain. 预判的落脚点「对新体验的欲望能刷新大脑」与 Desiring new experiences can help to renovate the brain. 在主语、动作、对象上一一对位，无添加成分。 D) 张冠李戴 Learning new tricks should not be confined to old dogs only. 改写自结尾的 Richard Kennedy 引语，是 brain scientist Kennedy 的比喻金句，而非 2012 年那项 研究的 finding。

items.title: 2024年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2024年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 People often wonder why some entrepreneurs have greater success than others. Is it habits, connections, luck, work ethic or any other behavior? I believe the key to success is willpower. Willpower is the ability to control yourself. It is a strong determination that allows you to do something difficult. It is a behavior we are born with more than one we learn; however, it is possible to not only learn it, but also strengthen it with constant exercise.

P2 Willpower is just like a muscle; to keep it strong you need to constantly exercise it. People with a great amount of willpower have the discipline to develop positive, successful habits. Even with an incredible amount of talent, without the discipline and motivation to create positive habits, it can be difficult to achieve success.

P3 Willpower and habits go hand in hand. It is critical to create good habits and take the actions necessary to stick to those habits day in and day out for greater success. Almost half of our daily actions are part of our habits and not decisions, so once the correct habits are in place, you will automatically perform those tasks on a day-to-day basis.

P4 The best way to create and stick to a habit is to have strong motivation. It's easier to change your habits to lose weight if you have a health issue and you want to be around longer for your kids, or if your business is something you're passionate about. Having a valuable outcome associated with a habit will help you stick to that habit permanently.

P5 The art of self-control is one that most successful individuals have mastered. Self-control enables you to avoid behaviors that don't contribute to your success and adopt those that do.

P6 Because there is a delayed satisfaction associated with self-control, it can be easy to get off track. However, if you work on sticking to those small positive habits one day at a time, it becomes easier to stay strong and achieve that delayed reward. Once a reward is achieved, it is much easier to continue sticking to your habits.

questions.q: What does the author say we need to do to strengthen our willpower?
options: Keep it under control.
Apply it continuously.
Learn from entrepreneurs.
Aim at success determinedly.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say we need to do to strengthen our willpower? 用 what...need to do 句式直接问具体做法，不含 infer/imply/mainly about，是标准的细节 题问法。 46. What does the author say we need to do to strengthen our willpower? A) Keep it under control. B) Apply it continuously. C) Learn from entrepreneurs. D) Aim at success determinedly.

【拆句】What does the author say we need to do to strengthen our willpower? 主干是 what does the author say (that) we need to do，后面的 to strengthen our willpower 是 目的状语；翻译时把目的状语提到前面："为了强化意志力，作者说我们需要做什么"。无 陷阱。

【定位】Willpower is just like a muscle; to keep it strong you need to constantly exercise it. 意志力就像一块肌肉；要让它保持强壮，你需要不断地锻炼它。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文说意志力本身就是 the ability to control yourself，是控制者，不是被控对象； Keep it under control. 把主客关系倒置。 B) ✓ 正确 constantly exercise it ↔Apply it continuously. 预判"持续锻炼"与 Apply it continuously. 字面同义，是 constantly exercise it 的标准 同义替换，无需推断。 C) 无中生有 why some entrepreneurs have greater success than others 只是引出话题的例子， 文中并未要求读者"向企业家学习"以强化意志力。 D) 张冠李戴 strong determination that allows you to do something difficult 说的是意志力"能让 人坚定追求成功"，是它的功能；选项把功能当成强化方法，张冠李戴。 根据文章,我们几乎一半的日常行为是如何进行的? A) 出于习惯。 B) 凭借决心。 C) 像锻炼肌肉一样。 D) 通过自律。

questions.q: How are almost half of our daily actions performed according to the passage?
options: Out of habit.
With determination.
Like muscle building.
By self-discipline.
questions.explain:
【判型】How are almost half of our daily actions performed according to the passage? 用 how 询问客观执行方式，并加 according to the passage 强调贴文回答，是细节题。

【拆句】How are almost half of our daily actions performed according to the passage? 这是 how 引导的被动语态疑问句，主语是 almost half of our daily actions，谓语 are performed；according to the passage 是状语。考生若不熟悉被动，需理解为"我们日常 行为中近一半是如何被完成的"。 47. How are almost half of our daily actions performed according to the passage? A) Out of habit. B) With determination. C) Like muscle building. D) By self-discipline.

【定位】Almost half of our daily actions are part of our habits and not decisions, so once the correct habits are in place, you will automatically perform those tasks on a day-to-day basis. 我们日常行为中近一半属于习惯而不是决定，因此一旦正确习惯到位，你就会每天自动去做 那些事。
