【选项】A) ✓ 正确 are part of our habits and not decisions ↔Out of habit. 预判"出于习惯"与 Out of habit. 字面一致，是 are part of our habits 的标准同义 替换。 B) 与原文相反 are part of our habits and not decisions 已明说"不是决定"；With determination. 与 decision 同属"有意识决断"的语义场，正好被否定。 C) 张冠李戴 muscle building 来自 Willpower is just like a muscle 的比喻，与 Q47 的执行方式无 关，被借来制造干扰。 D) 张冠李戴 self-discipline 与 Self-control 同义，但 P5 谈的是自控的功能，不是"日常行为如何被 执行"，被借来诱导。 什么会帮助人们自动坚持做有建设性的事情? A) 在日常生活中练习它。 B) 将它与改善健康联系起来。 C) 拥有合理的天赋。 D) 预见它将产生的预期结果。

questions.q: What will help people stick to doing something constructive automatically?
options: Practising it on a day-to-day basis.
Associating it with improving health.
Possessing a reasonable amount of talent.
Foreseeing the desired outcome it will yield.
questions.explain:
【判型】What will help people stick to doing something constructive automatically? 是 what + 具体行为，问"什么会帮助"，求客观条件，属细节题。

【拆句】What will help people stick to doing something constructive automatically? 主干 What will help people (to) stick to doing something；stick to 后接动名词 doing； constructive 与 automatically 分别修饰"事"和"做"。基础薄弱者要注意 stick to 不是"棍 子"，而是固定搭配"坚持"。

【定位】Having a valuable outcome associated with a habit will help you stick to that habit permanently. 把一个有价值的结果与某个习惯绑定，会帮助你长期坚持那个习惯。 48. What will help people stick to doing something constructive automatically? A) Practising it on a day-to-day basis. B) Associating it with improving health. C) Possessing a reasonable amount of talent. D) Foreseeing the desired outcome it will yield.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 you will automatically perform those tasks on a day-to-day basis 中 day-to-day 是养成习惯后"自动每日去做"的结果；选项把结果当方法，因果倒置。 B) 以偏概全 if you have a health issue 只是说明"有价值结果"的一个例子；选项把例子当成普适条 件，以偏概全。 C) 与原文相反 Even with an incredible amount of talent, without the discipline and motivation to create positive habits, it can be difficult to achieve success. 明确说光有天赋不 够；选项却把"有一定天赋"当成坚持习惯的条件，与原文相反。 D) ✓ 正确 Having a valuable outcome associated with a habit ↔ Foreseeing the desired outcome it will yield. 预判"预见到有价值回报"的语义被 Foreseeing the desired outcome it will yield. 精确 承担，是 P4 段尾结论句的同义替换。 自我控制的艺术如何帮助我们成功? A) 通过让我们永久保持头脑清醒。 B) 通过使我们能够不断改变行为。 C) 通过使我们能够采取积极行动。 D) 通过让我们避免冒险。

questions.q: How does the art of self-control help us succeed?
options: By allowing us to remain clear-headed permanently.
By enabling us to alter our behaviors constantly.
By enabling us to take positive actions
By allowing us to avoid taking risks.
questions.explain:
【判型】How does the art of self-control help us succeed? 用 how 询问机制，要求贴文给出 self-control 起作用的方式，属细节题。

【拆句】How does the art of self-control help us succeed? 主干 How does X help us (to) succeed；help 后省略 to，接动词原形 succeed。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Self-control enables you to avoid behaviors that don't contribute to your success and adopt those that do. 自控让你能够避开那些无助于成功的行为，并采纳那些有助于成功的行为。 49. How does the art of self-control help us succeed? A) By allowing us to remain clear-headed permanently. B) By enabling us to alter our behaviors constantly. C) By enabling us to take positive actions D) By allowing us to avoid taking risks.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文未提"保持头脑清醒"，更未说 permanently；选项凭空生造"永远清醒"。 B) 与原文相反 原文说自控让人"避开无益行为、采纳有益行为"，是有方向的取舍；alter our behaviors constantly 暗示"不断改来改去"，与作者"养成稳定好习惯"的立场相反。 C) ✓ 正确 adopt those that do ↔By enabling us to take positive actions Self-control enables you to ↔By enabling us to 预判同时含"避开"与"采纳"两面，选项 By enabling us to take positive actions 抓住其 中"采纳正向行为"的一面，是定位句的合法概括（避开 negative = 接近 positive，二者 同向）。 D) 偷换概念 原文是 avoid behaviors that don't contribute to your success，避的是"无益行为"， 不是 risks；"风险"是文中从未出现的概念。 为什么保持自我控制对我们来说可能很困难? A) 我们大多数人没有锻炼自我控制的习惯。 B) 我们可能无法从自我控制中获得即时回报。 C) 自我控制往往与痛苦相关联。 D) 自我控制只能带来微小的好处。

questions.q: Why can it be difficult for us to maintain self-control?
options: Most of us are not in the habit of exercising self-control.
We may not get immediate rewards from self-control.
Self-control tends to be associated with pains.
Self-control only brings about small benefits.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why can it be difficult for us to maintain self-control? 用 why 问"难以保持自控"的客观 原因，答案要能在文中找到，按细节题处理。

【拆句】Why can it be difficult for us to maintain self-control? 这是 why 引导的疑问句 + 形式 主语句型：it 形式主语，真主语是 to maintain self-control；can 表示"有可能、可能会"的 可能性，不要误译成"能够"。

【定位】Because there is a delayed satisfaction associated with self-control, it can be easy to get off track. 因为自控带来的是延迟的满足感，所以人很容易脱离正轨。 50. Why can it be difficult for us to maintain self-control? A) Most of us are not in the habit of exercising self-control. B) We may not get immediate rewards from self-control. C) Self-control tends to be associated with pains. D) Self-control only brings about small benefits.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文反复强调正确习惯一旦养成就会 automatically perform；选项却说"我们大多数人 没有自控的习惯"，与作者立场相反，且并非作者给出的难维持原因。 B) ✓ 正确 there is a delayed satisfaction associated with self-control ↔ We may not get immediate rewards from self-control. 预判"回报被推迟"被 We may not get immediate rewards from self-control. 精确承 担，是 because 句的正反同义改写。 C) 无中生有 原文谈的是 delayed satisfaction，是"满足感被推迟"，并非 pains"痛苦"；作者从未把 自控与痛苦绑定。 D) 偷换概念 原文说 if you work on sticking to those small positive habits...it becomes easier to...achieve that delayed reward，重点是"小习惯"带来"延迟的大回报"；small benefits 把延迟错读成"好处本身小"。

items.title: 2024年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2024年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Today, most scientific research is funded by government grants, companies doing research and development, and non-profit foundations. As a society, we reap the rewards from this science, but we also help pay for it. You indirectly support science through taxes you pay, products and services you purchase, and donations you make.

P2 Funding for science has changed with the times. Historically, science has been largely supported through private patronage(资助), church sponsorship, or simply paying for the research yourself. Today, researchers are likely to be funded by a mix of grants from various government agencies, institutions, and foundations. Other research is funded by private companies. Such corporate sponsorship is widespread in some fields. Almost 75% of U.S. clinical trials in medicine are paid for by private companies. And, of course, some researchers today still fund small-scale studies out of their own pockets. Most of us can't afford to do nuclear research as a private hobby, but birdwatchers, rock collectors, and others can do real research on a limited budget.

P3 In a perfect world, money wouldn't matter—all scientific studies would be completely objective. But in the real world, funding may introduce biases. Drug research sponsored by the pharmaceutical(制药的) industry is more likely to end up favoring the drug under consideration than studies sponsored by government grants or charitable organizations. Similarly, nutrition research sponsored by the food industry is more likely to end up favoring the food under consideration than independently funded research.

P4 So what should we make of all this? Should we ignore any research funded by companies or special interest groups? Certainly not. These groups provide invaluable funding for scientific research. Furthermore, science has many safeguards in place to catch instances of bias that affect research outcomes. Ultimately, misleading results will be corrected as science proceeds; however, this process takes time. Meanwhile, it pays to examine studies funded by industry or special interest groups with extra care. Are the results consistent with other independently funded studies? What do other scientists have to say about this research? A little examination can go a long way towards identifying bias associated with the funding source.

questions.q: What does the passage mainly discuss regarding scientific research?
options: Its foundation.
Its rewards.
Its prospect.
Its funding.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage mainly discuss regarding scientific research? 中的 mainly discuss 直接锁定主旨题。

【拆句】题干主句是 What does the passage mainly discuss，regarding scientific research 是介 词短语作状语，限定讨论的对象范围，句式平铺直叙、无陷阱。 51. What does the passage mainly discuss regarding scientific research? A) Its foundation. B) Its rewards. C) Its prospect. D) Its funding.

【选项】A) 无中生有：选项核心词在全文找不到主线对应 Its foundation 中的 foundation（基础／根基）在 P1~P4 中找不到对应；原文一次都 未把科研的‘基础’作为讨论对象。 B) 以偏概全：拿某段／某句的局部当全文主旨 we reap the rewards from this science 中确实出现 rewards，但只是一句话铺垫， P2~P4 都未围绕 ‘rewards’ 展开；Its rewards 把局部一句话上升为全文主旨。 C) 无中生有＋时态错位 Its prospect 中的 prospect（前景／未来展望）在 P1~P4 中无对应——作者讨论的是 ‘现状’与‘应对方式’，未对科研的未来作出预测。 D) ✓ 正确 most scientific research is funded by government grants, companies doing research and development, and non-profit foundations ↔Its funding Funding for science has changed with the times ↔Its funding Its funding 中的 Its 回指 scientific research，funding 则覆盖了 P1~P4 反复讨论的资 助来源、资助偏差、资助审慎度——是唯一覆盖四段共同主线的选项。 从文章中我们对像观鸟者和岩石收集者这样的研究人员了解到什么? A) 他们几乎无法获得政府资助。 B) 他们可以用有限的资源进行研究。 C) 他们可以在自己的领域从事业余工作。 D) 他们没有进行大规模研究的手段。

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about researchers like birdwatchers and rock collectors?
options: They have little access to government funding.
They can do research with limited resources.
They can do amateur work in their own fields.
They have no means for large-scale research.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about researchers like birdwatchers and rock collectors? 询问对某一特定群体的事实陈述，是典型细节题。

【拆句】主干是 What do we learn from the passage about researchers，like birdwatchers and rock collectors 是举例修饰 researchers，结构清晰、无陷阱。

【定位】Most of us can't afford to do nuclear research as a private hobby, but birdwatchers, rock collectors, and others can do real research on a limited budget. 我们大多数人无法把核研究当成私人爱好，但观鸟人、岩石收藏者等人可以用有限的预算做 真正的研究。 52. What do we learn from the passage about researchers like birdwatchers and rock collectors? A) They have little access to government funding. B) They can do research with limited resources. C) They can do amateur work in their own fields. D) They have no means for large-scale research.

【选项】A) 无中生有：原文未提即排除 They have little access to government funding 在 P2 中找不到对应陈述——原文只 说他们自掏腰包，并未对‘是否能拿到政府资助’作判断。 B) ✓ 正确 on a limited budget ↔with limited resources can do real research ↔can do research B 项 They can do research with limited resources 把定位句 can do real research on a limited budget 中的能力与资源条件一一对应替换，与预判完全吻合。 C) 偷换概念：把原文措辞替换为相近但意义偏移的表达 原文 can do real research 强调的是‘真正的研究’，而 amateur work in their own fields 把‘真正研究’偷换成‘业余工作’，且 in their own fields 也是原文未提的限定。 D) 张冠李戴＋绝对化 They have no means for large-scale research 把 Most of us can't afford to do nuclear research as a private hobby 中‘多数人’的处境强行套到 ‘birdwatchers, rock collectors’ 头上，并把陈述绝对化为 no means。 根据作者的观点,在一个完美的世界中科学研究会是什么样子? A) 它们将是完全无偏见的。 B) 它们将获得独立资助。 C) 它们将以负责任的方式进行。 D) 它们将受到严格监督。

questions.q: What would scientific studies look like in a perfect world according to the author?
options: They would be totally unbiased.
They would be independently funded.
They would be responsibly conducted.
They would be strictly supervised
questions.explain:
【判型】What would scientific studies look like in a perfect world according to the author? 用 would look like 询问作者对一个特定情境下的事实描述。

【拆句】主句是 What would scientific studies look like，in a perfect world 与 according to the author 都是状语修饰，按情境＋来源给约束，句式无陷阱。

【定位】In a perfect world, money wouldn't matter—all scientific studies would be completely objective. 在一个完美的世界里，钱不会成为问题——所有的科学研究都会是完全客观的。 53. What would scientific studies look like in a perfect world according to the author? A) They would be totally unbiased. B) They would be independently funded. C) They would be responsibly conducted. D) They would be strictly supervised

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 completely objective ↔totally unbiased A 项 They would be totally unbiased 用 unbiased 反向定义 objective，用 totally 替 换 completely，与预判 ‘完全客观’ 一一对应。 B) 偷换概念：把比较项当成主张 原文 Drug research sponsored by the pharmaceutical(制药的) industry is more likely to end up favoring the drug under consideration than studies sponsored by government grants or charitable organizations 仅把独立资助的研究当作偏差较 小的对照，并未说‘完美世界里所有研究都应独立资助’。 C) 无中生有：选项关键词在原文无对应 They would be responsibly conducted 中的 responsibly 在 P3 中没有对应词或近义 概念，属凭语感想当然。 D) 无中生有＋话题外推 They would be strictly supervised 引入‘严格监管’这一原文未涉及的维度。原文只谈 ‘客观’，未谈‘监管’。 作者对公司和特殊利益集团有何看法? A) 它们努力拆除研究的保障措施。 B) 它们为研究自己的产品付出额外努力。 C) 它们为科学研究提供宝贵的资源。 D) 它们从科学研究中获得最多利益。

questions.q: What does the author say about companies and special interest groups?
options: They try hard to pull down the safeguards for research.
They make extra efforts to research their own products.
They provide valuable resources for scientific research.
They reap the most benefits from scientific research.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about companies and special interest groups? 询问作者对 某一明确主体的具体陈述，是细节题。

【拆句】主句是 What does the author say about companies and special interest groups?， about 引导的介词短语锁定主体对象，句式简短无陷阱。

【定位】These groups provide invaluable funding for scientific research. 这些团体为科学研究提供了极其宝贵的资金。 54. What does the author say about companies and special interest groups? A) They try hard to pull down the safeguards for research. B) They make extra efforts to research their own products. C) They provide valuable resources for scientific research. D) They reap the most benefits from scientific research.

【选项】A) 与原文相反：把肯定语句逆转 原文 science has many safeguards in place to catch instances of bias that affect research outcomes 明确指出科学有 safeguards，作者也未指控这些团体‘试图打 掉’safeguards；A 项 They try hard to pull down the safeguards for research 直接 与原文事实对立。 B) 过度推断：把现象升级为意图 原文只说企业资助的研究‘更可能偏向其产品’（more likely to end up favoring the drug under consideration），并未说企业‘额外努力地’去研究自家产品；B 项 They make extra efforts to research their own products 是从结果反推动机，越界。 C) ✓ 正确 provide invaluable funding for scientific research ↔ provide valuable resources for scientific research C 项 They provide valuable resources for scientific research 与定位句结构、谓语、 宾语短语高度对齐，是定位句最纯粹的同义改写。 D) 无中生有＋绝对化 They reap the most benefits from scientific research 中‘获益最多’这一比较级在 P4 中找不到任何对应陈述——原文谈他们是‘出资方’，未谈‘获益方排序’。 作者对由产业界或特殊利益集团资助的研究有何看法? A) 应该检查其建议的可行性。 B) 应该及时纠正其误导性结果。 C) 应该格外谨慎地检查其有效性。 D) 应该独立识别其隐藏的偏见。

questions.q: What does the author think of research funded by industry or special interest groups?
options: Its recommendations should be examined for feasibility.
Its misleading results should be corrected in time.
Its validity should be checked with additional care.
Its hidden biases should be identified independently.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think of research funded by industry or special interest groups? 询问作者对特定 research 的明确看法，属于带观点色彩的细节题，仍可单点定位 作者评价句。

【拆句】主句是 What does the author think of research，funded by industry or special interest groups 是 research 的过去分词后置定语，相当于 the research that is funded by…，句式直白无陷阱。

【定位】Meanwhile, it pays to examine studies funded by industry or special interest groups with extra care. 同时，对工业界或特殊利益团体资助的研究多加小心地审视，是值得的。 55. What does the author think of research funded by industry or special interest groups? A) Its recommendations should be examined for feasibility. B) Its misleading results should be corrected in time. C) Its validity should be checked with additional care. D) Its hidden biases should be identified independently.

【选项】A) 无中生有＋话题偏移 原文谈的是‘核查这类研究的结论是否可靠’，并非‘检查其建议的可行性’；Its recommendations should be examined for feasibility 中 recommendations 与 feasibility 都是无中生有的概念。 B) 张冠李戴：把全局机制改成对单一对象的建议 原文 misleading results will be corrected as science proceeds 是说科学过程会自我 纠错，而 B 项 Its misleading results should be corrected in time 把这一过程改写为 作者对企业资助研究的具体建议，并加入 in time 这一原文未提的时限。 C) ✓ 正确 examine…with extra care ↔Its validity should be checked with additional care Are the results consistent with other independently funded studies? ↔Its validity C 项 Its validity should be checked with additional care 把作者 ‘要带着额外的小心 去审查这类研究’ 用被动语态、上位名词重写，与预判一一对应。 D) 偷换概念＋强加限定 原文 A little examination can go a long way towards identifying bias associated with the funding source 只说‘审视可帮助识别偏差’，并未要求‘独立地 （independently）识别 hidden biases’；D 项强加 hidden 与 independently 两层原 文没说的限制。

items.title: 2024年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2024年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 It may sound surprising, but you don't have to be interested in fashion, or even in history, to enjoy Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History. I happen to be interested in both, and ended up enjoying the book for completely different reasons.

P2 Richard Thompson Ford is a law professor, and you probably won't forget that for even one page. His carefully reasoned arguments, packed with examples, sound almost like reading a court opinion, only maybe wordier. You will probably never think of fashion as a trifle again.

P3 Ford's thesis is that the best way to understand what particular fashions meant in any given era is to look at the restrictions placed on them. Through this lens, he shows us that the first laws passed in the 1200s to ensure that only the nobility were allowed to wear certain fabrics, colors and ornaments reflected the rise of the middle class, who were now able to imitate some of these fashions. The status of the upper classes was threatened; fashion was a tool to preserve it.

P4 Ford takes the reader through the evolution of fashion while examining the underlying motivations of status, sex, power, and personality, which, he assumes, influenced all innovations in fashion in the past and which continue to influence us today. His writing is more than a little dense— dense with research, clauses, and precise adjectives and nouns. But there's also humor and enough interesting episodes to make the writing appealing. No one is spared his sharp analysis: not the easy targets of 19th century women's crippling(伤害身体的) fashions nor the modern uniforms of Silicon Valley T-shirts

P5 But the greatest strength of this book (on fashion!) is its intellectual profoundness. Ford asks us to question unconscious beliefs, to realize that we almost never do so, to understand that the simplest choices are charged with meaning, and yet that meaning can and does change all the time. Consider the fact that a 1918 catalog insisted that boys and girls be dressed in the appropriate color. We believe our thinking today is evolved; Ford shows us it's not.

questions.q: What does the author think of the book Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History?
options: It is read by people for entirely different reasons.
It is meant for those interested in fashion history.
It makes enjoyable as well as informative reading.
It converts fashion into something for deliberation.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think of the book 问的是作者对整本书的看法，不针对任何细节 段，属于全文评价层面的主旨态度问题。

【拆句】主干 What does the author think of the book：think of 在此是「认为……怎么样」的固 定搭配，of 后接评价对象；书名作 of 的宾语。无陷阱。 46. What does the author think of the book Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History? A) It is read by people for entirely different reasons. B) It is meant for those interested in fashion history. C) It makes enjoyable as well as informative reading. D) It converts fashion into something for deliberation.

【选项】A) 过度推断 It is read by people for entirely different reasons 把 I happen to be interested in both, and ended up enjoying the book for completely different reasons 中「我个 人因不同理由喜欢」错误推广到所有读者群体。 B) 与原文相反 It is meant for those interested in fashion history 与 you don't have to be interested in fashion, or even in history, to enjoy 直接矛盾——原文是「不必对这两 者感兴趣也能享受」，选项却限定「专为感兴趣者而写」。 C) ✓ 正确 enjoy Dress Codes: How the Laws of Fashion Made History ↔enjoyable intellectual profoundness ↔informative enough interesting episodes to make the writing appealing ↔enjoyable It makes enjoyable as well as informative reading 用 enjoyable as well as informative 两个形容词分别对应「P1/P4 阅读体验」和「P5 思想深度」两条主线，是 唯一同时覆盖两面的选项。 D) 过度推断 It converts fashion into something for deliberation 把 You will probably never think of fashion as a trifle again 过度解读为「把时尚转化为可供深思的事物」，把作 者对一句话的预测拔成全书定位。 根据Ford的观点,人们如何才能最好地理解某个时代的特定时尚? A) 通过审视施加在时尚上的限制。 B) 通过观察贵族的穿着。 C) 通过浏览时尚的面料、颜色和装饰。 D) 通过对上层阶级和中产阶级进行调查。

questions.q: How can people best understand a particular fashion in an era, according to Ford?
options: By examining the restraints imposed on it.
By looking at what the nobility were wearing.
By glancing at its fabrics, colors and ornaments.
By doing a survey of the upper and middle classes
questions.explain:
【判型】How can people best understand a particular fashion in an era, according to Ford? 用 how 问具体方法，且明确归属 according to Ford，是定位 Ford 观点句的细节题。

【拆句】主干 How can people understand…，best 修饰 understand 表程度；in an era 限定 fashion 所处时代；句末 according to Ford 标注观点归属。无陷阱。

【定位】Ford's thesis is that the best way to understand what particular fashions meant in any given era is to look at the restrictions placed on them. Ford 的核心论点是：要理解某一时代里特定时尚的含义，最好的方式就是看强加在这些时 尚之上的种种限制。 47. How can people best understand a particular fashion in an era, according to Ford? A) By examining the restraints imposed on it. B) By looking at what the nobility were wearing. C) By glancing at its fabrics, colors and ornaments. D) By doing a survey of the upper and middle classes

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 look at the restrictions placed on them ↔examining the restraints imposed on it 四个选项中只有 By examining the restraints imposed on it 完整还原「观察—限制」 这一对核心语义，与预判完全等值。 B) 拿例证替换方法 By looking at what the nobility were wearing 只截取 the nobility were allowed to wear certain fabrics, colors and ornaments 这处例证，没回到 Ford 真正提出的方法 ——「看限制」。 C) 偷换概念 By glancing at its fabrics, colors and ornaments 取自 certain fabrics, colors and ornaments，是 1200s 立法所限制的具体内容，被偷换成了「理解时尚的方法」。 D) 无中生有 By doing a survey of the upper and middle classes 中 doing a survey 文中并无任 何对应，Ford 谈的是「看限制」而非做问卷或调查。 13世纪通过的第一批有关时尚的法律的目的是什么? A) 促进中产阶级的崛起。 B) 放宽对着装规范的限制。 C) 帮助创立一些新颖的时尚。 D) 维护贵族的地位。

questions.q: What was the aim of the first laws passed regarding fashion in the 1200s?
options: To facilitate the rise of the middle class.
To loosen restrictions on dress codes.
To help initiate some novel fashions
To preserve the status of the nobles.
questions.explain:
【判型】What was the aim of the first laws 问的是某一具体历史事件的目的，需要回原文找对应 「目的/原因」表述。

【拆句】主干 What was the aim of the first laws…？aim of 后接修饰首批法律的两个定语 passed regarding fashion 和 in the 1200s。无陷阱。

【定位】the first laws passed in the 1200s to ensure that only the nobility were allowed to wear certain fabrics, colors and ornaments reflected the rise of the middle class, who were now able to imitate some of these fashions. The status of the upper classes was threatened; fashion was a tool to preserve it. 1200 年代通过的最早一批法律，规定只有贵族才能穿戴某些面料、颜色与饰品；这些法律 折射出中产阶级的崛起，因为他们已能模仿其中一些时尚。上层阶级的地位受到威胁，时尚 成为维持这一地位的工具。 48. What was the aim of the first laws passed regarding fashion in the 1200s? A) To facilitate the rise of the middle class. B) To loosen restrictions on dress codes. C) To help initiate some novel fashions D) To preserve the status of the nobles.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 To facilitate the rise of the middle class 把「中产阶级崛起」当成目的，但原文是中 产阶级崛起在前、立法在后，立法是为了反制这种崛起、保护贵族。 B) 与原文相反 To loosen restrictions on dress codes 与原文「立法是限制」的方向完全相反，原文 是 only the nobility were allowed to wear，明显是加紧而非放松。 C) 无中生有 To help initiate some novel fashions 称立法是为了开启新潮流，文中只字未提；原文 谈的是用法律压制模仿，而非鼓励创新。 D) ✓ 正确 The status of the upper classes was threatened; fashion was a tool to preserve it ↔ To preserve the status of the nobles only the nobility were allowed to wear certain fabrics, colors and ornaments ↔ To preserve the status of the nobles 预判「维护贵族地位」直接对应 To preserve the status of the nobles，preserve、 status、nobles 三个关键词全部命中，是直白的同义重述。 作者如何看待Ford的写作? A) 在描述不同时代的时尚时运用了比较和对照。 B) 阅读起来费力但不乏幽默感和吸引力。 C) 充满有趣的小插曲,使读者免于难以忍受的枯燥。 D) 在论证方面具有学术特征。

questions.q: What does the author think of Ford's writing?
options: It uses comparison and contrast in describing fashions of different eras.
It makes heavy reading but is not lacking in humor or appeal.
It is filled with interesting episodes to spare readers intolerable boredom.
It is characteristic of academics in presenting arguments.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think of Ford's writing? 评价对象是局部的 writing，不是全书， 属于一段内的评价细节题。

【拆句】主干 What does the author think of Ford's writing？think of 仍是固定搭配「对…怎么 看」。无陷阱。

【定位】His writing is more than a little dense—dense with research, clauses, and precise adjectives and nouns. But there's also humor and enough interesting episodes to make the writing appealing. 他的写作可以说相当密实——密集的研究、从句以及精准的形容词与名词。但其中也不乏幽 默与足够多的有趣片段，使得整本书读来仍具吸引力。 49. What does the author think of Ford's writing? A) It uses comparison and contrast in describing fashions of different eras. B) It makes heavy reading but is not lacking in humor or appeal. C) It is filled with interesting episodes to spare readers intolerable boredom. D) It is characteristic of academics in presenting arguments.

【选项】A) 无中生有 It uses comparison and contrast in describing fashions of different eras 谈 Ford 用了 comparison and contrast，P4 通篇没有这层评价。 B) ✓ 正确 His writing is more than a little dense ↔makes heavy reading there's also humor and enough interesting episodes to make the writing appealing ↔ not lacking in humor or appeal It makes heavy reading but is not lacking in humor or appeal 用 but 连接，分别 对接原文 dense 与 But there's also humor and …appealing 两个分句，与预判完全 一致。 C) 过度推断 It is filled with interesting episodes to spare readers intolerable boredom 把原文 「也有」夸成「充满」，把「使写作吸引人」放大为「拯救读者免于难以忍受的无 聊」，与 dense 评价并列存在的事实矛盾。 D) 以偏概全 It is characteristic of academics in presenting arguments 与 sound almost like reading a court opinion, only maybe wordier 有关，但题目问的是 P4 段的写作评 价；且选项遗漏了「幽默与吸引力」这一面。 作者认为Ford这本书的最大优势是什么? A) 丰富的信息。 B) 有意义的选择。 C) 深化的思考。 D) 思想深度。

questions.q: What does the author say is the greatest strength of Ford's book?
options: Plentiful information.
Meaningful choices.
Evolved thinking.
Intellectual depth
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say is the greatest strength of Ford's book? 问「最大优点是什 么」，文中必有显式表述，属细节定位题。

【拆句】主干 What does the author say is the greatest strength…？嵌套宾语从句 the author say + 主语 [the greatest strength of Ford's book] + 系动词 is，问的是表语的内容。无 陷阱。

【定位】But the greatest strength of this book (on fashion!) is its intellectual profoundness. 但这本（讲时尚的！）书最大的优点，是它在思想上的深刻。 50. What does the author say is the greatest strength of Ford's book? A) Plentiful information. B) Meaningful choices. C) Evolved thinking. D) Intellectual depth

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 Plentiful information 把 dense with research 误当作本段「最大优点」，跨段错位， 且 Ford 的写作密度在原文是写作风格而非最大优点。 B) 以偏概全 Meaningful choices 取自 the simplest choices are charged with meaning，那是支 撑思想深度的细节，不是最大优点本身。 C) 与原文相反 Evolved thinking 直接对应 We believe our thinking today is evolved; Ford shows us it's not，作者明确指出今天的思维其实并未进化——把它当作 Ford 书的最大优点， 与原文结论完全相反。 D) ✓ 正确 intellectual profoundness ↔Intellectual depth Intellectual depth 与预判「思想上的深刻」语义一一对应，无任何缩放或偷换。

items.title: 2024年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2024年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 The art of persuasion means convincing others to agree with your point of view or to follow your course of action. For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality and the power of influencing comes naturally. For the rest of us, persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time.

P2 Employers place a great value on employees with persuasion skills because they can impact several aspects of job performance. Besides, teamwork and leadership rely heavily on the power of persuasion to get things done. Without persuasion skills, employees may not be as committed to or convinced of the importance of an organization's vision and long-term mission. Effective use of persuasion skills will not only help get your coworkers excited about your ideas, it'll also help you motivate them to achieve a common goal.

P3 In order to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace, you need to understand how to handle conflicts and reach agreements. Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion, but logic and reasoning are just as important. Before you can get somebody on-board with your goal, you should help them understand why they should pursue it. Using visual aids to back up your ideas can help communicate your ideas better and make compelling arguments so your listeners will come to a logical choice and become fully committed to your ideas and plans.

P4 Successful persuasion skills are based on your ability to have positive interactions and maintain meaningful relationships with people. In order to sustain those relationships, you must be able to work in their best interests as well. Your coworkers are more likely to agree with you when they succeed alongside you. The more they achieve and the greater progress they make, the more they trust your judgement and strength.

P5 We persuade and get persuaded every day—we're either convincing or being convinced. A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational structures; no one likes to be told what to do or to be pushed around. Therefore, organizations and leaders should adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes.

questions.q: What does the author say about the ability to be persuasive in the first paragraph?
options: People may either be born with it or be able to cultivate it.
It proves crucial in making others follow one's course of action.
It refers to the natural and instinctive power of influencing one's coworkers.
People may view it as both a means to convince others and an art of communication.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about the ability to be persuasive in the first paragraph? 是典型的 What does the author say + 段落限定，问的是作者在指定段落对某事的具体说 法，无 infer/imply 字样。 51. What does the author say about the ability to be persuasive in the first paragraph? A) People may either be born with it or be able to cultivate it. B) It proves crucial in making others follow one's course of action. C) It refers to the natural and instinctive power of influencing one's coworkers. D) People may view it as both a means to convince others and an art of communication.

【拆句】题干 What does the author say about the ability to be persuasive in the first paragraph? 主干为 What does the author say about X，X 是 the ability to be persuasive；in the first paragraph 是地点状语修饰 say。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality and the power of influencing comes naturally. For the rest of us, persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time. 对我们中的一些人来说，说服是与生俱来的天赋，影响他人的能力是天生的；对我们其余的 人来说，说服技巧是可以随时间学习并培养的。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 For some of us, persuasion is an instinctive quality ↔born with it persuasion skills can be learned and developed over time ↔be able to cultivate it 预判要求“天生或后天习得”两端都覆盖，仅 People may either be born with it or be able to cultivate it 用 either...or 句式完整对应两端。 B) 答非所问 It proves crucial in making others follow one's course of action 把首段对“能力来 源”的说明换成了“能力的重要性”，回答的不是 What does the author say 这个角度的 问题。 C) 以偏概全 It refers to the natural and instinctive power of influencing one's coworkers 只截 取了“天生本能”那一半（some of us），漏掉了“后天习得”那一半（the rest of us）， 且把场景窄化到 coworkers。 D) 无中生有 People may view it as both a means to convince others and an art of communication 中的 art of communication 在首段并未提及，原文只说 the art of persuasion，把 persuasion 偷换成 communication。 为什么说服技巧在职场中备受重视? A) 它们使员工能够相信自己的长期收益。 B) 它们使员工能够无条件地信任他们的领导者。 C) 它们有助于激励同事为共同目标而奋斗。 D) 它们有助于组织有效地拓宽其愿景。

questions.q: Why are persuasion skills greatly valued in the workplace?
options: They enable employees to be convinced of their long-term gains.
They enable employees to trust their leaders unconditionally.
They help motivate coworkers to strive for a common goal.
They help an organization to broaden its vision effectively.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why are persuasion skills greatly valued in the workplace? 问的是被广泛重视的具体原 因，是文中可直接读出的事实，不要求跨段综合推断。 52. Why are persuasion skills greatly valued in the workplace? A) They enable employees to be convinced of their long-term gains. B) They enable employees to trust their leaders unconditionally. C) They help motivate coworkers to strive for a common goal. D) They help an organization to broaden its vision effectively.

【拆句】题干 Why are persuasion skills greatly valued in the workplace? 是 Why + be + 过去 分词 valued 构成的被动疑问句，主语是 persuasion skills；in the workplace 是地点状 语。被动语态把动作发出方（雇主）省略了，考生需要意识到“被谁所重视”的隐含主语在原 文是 employers。

【定位】Effective use of persuasion skills will not only help get your coworkers excited about your ideas, it'll also help you motivate them to achieve a common goal. 有效运用说服技巧不仅有助于让你的同事对你的想法感到兴奋，也有助于你激励他们为实现 共同目标而努力。

【选项】A) 无中生有 They enable employees to be convinced of their long-term gains 中的 long-term gains 在原文找不到对应，原文 long-term mission 谈的是组织的长期使命，并非员工 的长远收益。 B) 过度推断 They enable employees to trust their leaders unconditionally 中 unconditionally 是绝对化表述，原文只谈“激励”，从未要求“无条件信任”，属于过度推断。 C) ✓ 正确 help you motivate them to achieve a common goal ↔ help motivate coworkers to strive for a common goal 预判“激励同事为共同目标”两要素，They help motivate coworkers to strive for a common goal 在句法结构上几乎是原文的平移，是最贴近预判的选项。 D) 偷换概念 They help an organization to broaden its vision effectively 把原文的“让员工 committed to vision”（员工对愿景的认同）偷换成“拓展组织的愿景”（broaden its vision），动作和受体都被换掉。 人们应该做什么来学习职场中的说服艺术? A) 掌握有效的沟通技巧。 B) 避免卷入与他人的冲突。 C) 理解追求目标的原因。 D) 全身心地投入到自己的想法和计划中。

questions.q: What should people do to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace?
options: Acquire effective communication skills.
Avoid getting involved in conflicts with others.
Understand the reason for pursuing their goals.
Commit themselves fully to their ideas and plans.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should people do to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace? 提问“为达成 X 该做什么”，答案是原文中显性陈述的前置条件，无需推断。 53. What should people do to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace? A) Acquire effective communication skills. B) Avoid getting involved in conflicts with others. C) Understand the reason for pursuing their goals. D) Commit themselves fully to their ideas and plans.

【拆句】题干 What should people do to learn the art of persuasion at the workplace? 主干是 What should people do，to learn... at the workplace 是不定式做目的状语。考生易把 to learn 误读为定语修饰 do，正确理解应是“为了学会...，人们该做什么”。

【定位】Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion, but logic and reasoning are just as important. 良好的沟通是有效说服的第一步，但逻辑和推理同样重要。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Good communication is the first step in effective persuasion ↔ Acquire effective communication skills 预判要求“先做好沟通”，Acquire effective communication skills 用 acquire 动作动词 直译 first step 隐含的“获取动作”，匹配度最高。 B) 偷换概念 Avoid getting involved in conflicts with others 把原文 how to handle conflicts（处 理冲突）偷换成 avoid... conflicts（回避冲突），原文从未让人避开冲突。 C) 张冠李戴 Understand the reason for pursuing their goals 把原文中的“帮别人理解为什么要追 求该目标”张冠到“自己理解”，主语错位。 D) 答非所问 Commit themselves fully to their ideas and plans 描述的是听众被说服后的状态 （fully committed），是“说服成功”的结果，而题干问的是说服者该做的前置条件。 什么时候你更有可能成功说服你的同事? A) 当他们确信你在为他们的利益工作而牺牲自己的利益时。 B) 当他们意识到你所做判断的潜在力量时。 C) 当他们意识到你与他们保持的有意义的关系时。 D) 当他们确信自己将与你一起取得成就时。

questions.q: When are you more likely to succeed in persuading your coworkers?
options: When they are convinced you work in their interests while sacrificing your own
When they become aware of the potential strength of the judgements you make
When they become aware of the meaningful relationships you keep with them.
When they are convinced they will make achievements together with you.
questions.explain:
【判型】When are you more likely to succeed in persuading your coworkers? 问的是某客观条 件下的可能性，文中第四段直陈条件句，可直接定位。

【拆句】题干 When are you more likely to succeed in persuading your coworkers? 主干是 When are you more likely to succeed，to succeed in doing 是固定搭配。考生易把 more likely 误读作纯感情色彩词，应理解为“在何种条件下，更可能”，相当于在问触发 条件。 54. When are you more likely to succeed in persuading your coworkers? A) When they are convinced you work in their interests while sacrificing your own B) When they become aware of the potential strength of the judgements you make C) When they become aware of the meaningful relationships you keep with them. D) When they are convinced they will make achievements together with you.

【定位】Your coworkers are more likely to agree with you when they succeed alongside you. 当你的同事与你一起取得成功时，他们更可能同意你的看法。

【选项】A) 过度推断 while sacrificing your own 是原文从未提及的“牺牲自我利益”，原文只说“为对方利益 着想”，未要求牺牲自己。 B) 偷换概念 the potential strength of the judgements you make 把原文 they trust your judgement and strength 中的并列两件事偷换成“判断的潜在力量”，concept 被悄悄 合并改写。 C) 答非所问 meaningful relationships you keep with them 是说服力的前提条件（说服者需要做 的事），不是同事被说服的触发条件——题干问的是后者。 D) ✓ 正确 when they succeed alongside you ↔ When they are convinced they will make achievements together with you 预判“双方共同成功才更易被说服”，they will make achievements together with you 是定位句 they succeed alongside you 的同义改写，方向一致。 为什么建议组织和领导者采用强有力的说服技巧来带来必要的变革? A) 为了让员工相信协作的价值。 B) 为了照顾到当今大多数人的偏好。 C) 为了改进传统的组织结构。 D) 为了适应员工不断变化的工作方式。

questions.q: Why are organizations and leaders advised to adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about
options: To convince employees of the value of collaboration
To allow for the preferences of most people of today
To improve on traditional organizational structures
To adapt to employees' ever-changing working styles
questions.explain:
【判型】Why are organizations and leaders advised to adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes? 问的是该建议的事实依据，文中末段直陈，无须推断。

【拆句】题干 Why are organizations and leaders advised to adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes? 是 Why + 被动 are advised to do 的疑问句，to bring about... 是不定式做目的状语。该结构隐含的动作发出方是“作者”，被建议方是 organizations and leaders；考生需识别这是在问作者给出此建议的依据。 55. Why are organizations and leaders advised to adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes? A) To convince employees of the value of collaboration B) To allow for the preferences of most people of today C) To improve on traditional organizational structures D) To adapt to employees' ever-changing working styles

【定位】A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational structures; no one likes to be told what to do or to be pushed around. Therefore, organizations and leaders should adopt powerful persuasion skills to bring about necessary changes. 绝大多数人更喜欢协作与团队合作，而非传统组织结构；没人喜欢被指使或被任意摆布。因 此，组织和领导者应当采用有力的说服技巧来带来必要的变革。

【选项】A) 答非所问 To convince employees of the value of collaboration 把“顺应大多数人偏好”换成了 “说服员工相信协作的价值”——原文是员工自己已经偏好协作，无需再被说服其价值。 B) ✓ 正确 A vast majority of people prefer collaboration and teamwork over traditional organizational structures ↔To allow for the preferences of most people of today 题干问“为什么被建议这么做”，To allow for the preferences of most people of today 用 To do 不定式直接给出目的-原因，是最贴合预判的答案。 C) 无中生有 To improve on traditional organizational structures 把“改善传统组织结构”列为目 的，但原文 traditional organizational structures 出现的语境是“人们更偏好协作而非 传统组织结构”，并未把“改善”它作为说服技巧的目的。 D) 无中生有 To adapt to employees' ever-changing working styles 中的 ever-changing working styles（不断变化的工作方式）原文未提，原文谈的是“偏好”而非“工作方式的 变化”。

items.title: 2024年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people. A tipping point was reached in 2020 when human-made materials—such as steel, concrete and plastic—were found to weigh more than all life on Earth. Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted. Simply being in the nearest wood has such health benefits that the Woodland Trust successfully lobbied for it to be prescribed by doctors.

P2 Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world. For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later. It is not a moment too soon that teenagers will be able to take a natural history test, given that for decades children have been able to name more video game characters than wildlife species.

P3 Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil—while producing food sustainably.

P4 Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition. In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England. The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived(使复活) by green-thumbed(有园艺才能的) social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities.

P5 Apart from the urgent task of providing more healthy nutrients to those who increasingly can't afford them, publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens connect what we eat to where it comes from —the means of production, if you will. They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community. Plants are also, of course, our first defence against species loss and climate change. Such planting is a small step for humanity—in the right direction.

questions.q: What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph?
options: The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history.
Economic growth benefits people little in the long run.
It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature.
It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph? 问的是首段作者想强 调什么，是段落主旨而非局部细节。

【拆句】What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph? 是 What 引导的特殊 疑问句，want to emphasise 是一个简单的动词短语，无从句无否定，结构清爽，无陷阱。 46. What does the author want to emphasise in the first paragraph? A) The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history. B) Economic growth benefits people little in the long run. C) It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. D) It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 The year 2020 was a big turning point in human history. 把段落里一个支撑论据 （2020 年的 tipping point）当作主旨，且"in human history"是过度推断——原文只 说人造物质量超过生命这一比较点。 B) 偷换概念 Economic growth benefits people little in the long run. 把原文"对经济或许有利"扭 曲成"经济增长对人没好处"，攻击点从"与自然的连接"偷换到了"经济增长本身"，并把短 期权衡偷换为 in the long run。 C) ✓ 正确 The weakening of the human connection to nature might be good for economic growth but is bad for people. ↔It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. Continuing to grow concrete forests rather than real ones is shortsighted. ↔ It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. 预判要的是"削弱与自然的连接是不明智的"，It is unwise to weaken the human connection to nature. 正好是这一判断的同义表达，且覆盖整段而不偏向某个论据。 D) 过度推断 It is harmful to mankind to use human-made materials. 把"人造物总质量超过生 命"这一比较事实，推断成"使用人造物本身就有害"，原文从未否定使用人造物，只是反 对以此取代真实自然。 研究人员关于流行文化发现了什么? A) 它与自然界日益脱节。 B) 它充斥着各种电子游戏角色。 C) 它特别迎合青少年的口味。 D) 它仍然受到20世纪50年代热门歌曲的影响。

questions.q: What did researchers find about popular culture?
options: It is increasingly detached from the natural world.
It is filled with all kinds of video game characters.
It is especially appealing to the taste of teenagers.
It is still impacted by the hit songs of the 1950s.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did researchers find about popular culture? 直接问研究者发现了什么客观事实， 属于细节题。

【拆句】What did researchers find about popular culture? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，主谓 researchers find，about popular culture 限定 find 的对象，结构平铺，无陷阱。

【定位】For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later. 对于 1950 年代流行歌曲里每三个与自然相关的词，研究人员发现，50 年后只剩下略多于 一个。 47. What did researchers find about popular culture? A) It is increasingly detached from the natural world. B) It is filled with all kinds of video game characters. C) It is especially appealing to the taste of teenagers. D) It is still impacted by the hit songs of the 1950s.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 For every three nature-related words in hit songs of the 1950s, researchers found, there was only slightly more than one 50 years later. ↔It is increasingly detached from the natural world. Yet slipping from popular culture is the wonder and beauty of the natural world. ↔ It is increasingly detached from the natural world. 预判要的是"自然内容大量减少"，A 项用 increasingly detached 这一抽象升级精确对 应该数据，所以锁定 A。 B) 偷换概念 It is filled with all kinds of video game characters. 把原文"孩子认识的游戏角色比野 生动物多"偷换成"流行文化里充斥着游戏角色"——研究比较的是孩子的认知，不是流行 文化的内容构成。 C) 无中生有 It is especially appealing to the taste of teenagers. 全句"对青少年口味格外有吸引 力"在 P2 中没有任何对应；原文只是提到青少年将能参加自然史考试，并未谈流行文化 对青少年的吸引力。 D) 与原文相反 It is still impacted by the hit songs of the 1950s. 说流行文化仍受 50 年代流行歌曲 影响，但原文用 50 年代和 50 年后的数据对比，恰恰说明这种影响在减弱、自然主题在 流失，方向相反。 作者建议人们做什么? A) 采取措施确保可持续的食物发展。 B) 通过种植权利重新与自然建立联系。 C) 支持议会对抗社会疾病。 D) 用果树和蔬菜植物覆盖公共空间。

questions.q: What does the author propose people do?
options: Take measures to ensure sustainable food development.
Reconnect with nature through the right to grow.
Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases.
Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author propose people do? 问作者具体提议人们做什么，定位到对应主 张句即可作答，属于细节题。

【拆句】What does the author propose people do? 是 What 引导的特殊疑问句，propose 后 接"people do"是"propose sb do sth"句型省略了 that 与情态的简略问法，相当于问"作者 建议人们做什么"，无陷阱。 48. What does the author propose people do? A) Take measures to ensure sustainable food development. B) Reconnect with nature through the right to grow. C) Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases. D) Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants.

【定位】Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law, allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces into vegetable and fruit gardens. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil—while producing food sustainably. 矫正这一社会病的一部分举措，是让议会通过一项"种植权"法案，允许任何人把利用不足的 公共空间改造成菜园和果园。其理念在于让人们重新接触土壤——同时可持续地生产粮食。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Take measures to ensure sustainable food development. 把原文末尾"while producing food sustainably"这一附带的从属信息抬升成了核心主张，掩盖了"重新接 触土壤、与自然重连"这一真正的主诉。 B) ✓ 正确 Part of remedying this social disease would be for parliament to pass a "right to grow" law ↔ Reconnect with nature through the right to grow. The idea is for people to get back in touch with the soil ↔ Reconnect with nature through the right to grow. 预判要的两层信息——"通过种植权"和"重新接触自然"——B 项用 through 和 reconnect with nature 一并覆盖，所以是答案。 C) 偷换概念 Stand by the parliament in fighting social diseases. 把"议会通过法案"偷换成"人 们站在议会一边"，方向完全反过来——原文是作者建议议会行动，不是建议民众站队 议会。 D) 过度推断 Cover public spaces with fruit trees and vegetable plants. 把原文"allowing anyone to turn underused public spaces"的"利用不足的公共空间"扩展到"所有公共 空间"，并把"允许"扭曲为"全面覆盖"，方式与范围都被放大。 我们从文章中了解到关于蔬菜种植的什么信息? A) 这一切始于1649年的英格兰南部。 B) 它受到美国政府法规的保护。 C) 它长期以来一直被用于增加食物供应和改善城市景观。 D) 随着社交媒体影响力的增加,它已在全球范围内普及。

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting?
options: It all started in 1649 in Southern England.
It is protected by US government regulations.
It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape.
It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting? 问从文章中获取的事实 信息，属于细节题。 49. What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting? A) It all started in 1649 in Southern England. B) It is protected by US government regulations. C) It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. D) It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media.

【拆句】What do we learn from the passage about vegetable planting? 主干 What do we learn，from the passage 与 about vegetable planting 都是介词短语作状语，前者点出 来源、后者点出话题对象，结构清晰。

【定位】In April 1649, locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England. The practice of throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green took off in 1970s New York, and has been revived by green-thumbed social media influencers who defy local US regulations in a war on ugly spots in cities. 1649 年 4 月，英国南部居民为应对高物价与粮食短缺，在公共土地上种植蔬菜。把种子炸 弹扔到空地以使其变绿的做法在 1970 年代的纽约兴起，并被有园艺天分的社交媒体网红重 新带火，他们无视当地美国法规，向城市里的丑陋角落"开战"。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 It all started in 1649 in Southern England. 把段内一个时间点放大为"全部起源"，原 文只说 1649 年发生过一次，并未说蔬菜种植起源于此。 B) 与原文相反 It is protected by US government regulations. 与原文 defy local US regulations 直 接相反：原文说网红"无视"美国当地法规，选项说"受其保护"。 C) ✓ 正确 locals responded to high prices and food shortages by cultivating vegetables on common land in Southern England ↔It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. throwing seed bombs to turn vacant plots of land green ↔ It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. Vegetable planting has a respectable tradition. ↔ It has long been used to increase food supply and improve urban landscape. 预判要的"补食物 + 美化城市"两条线，C 项用 food supply 与 urban landscape 并 列，正好两条都覆盖，所以是答案。 D) 过度推断 It has been popularised worldwide with the increasing influence of social media. 把原文里"1970 年代纽约 + 美国网红重新带火"扩张为"全球普及"，并把"重振"延伸 为"日益增长的影响力"，超出原文范围。 除了实用功能外,可公开访问的果蔬园还能做什么? A) 提高人们的环保意识。 B) 增加植物物种的多样性。 C) 充当抵御自然灾害的第一道防线。 50. What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions? A) Raise people's environmental awareness. B) Add to the great variety of plant species. C) Act as the first defence against natural disasters. D) Enhance people's community spirit. D) 增强人们的社区精神。

questions.q: What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions?
options: Raise people's environmental awareness.
Add to the great variety of plant species.
Act as the first defence against natural disasters.
Enhance people's community spirit.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions? 问的是除实用功能之外这些菜园还能做什么，是对应原文并列项的细 节题。

【拆句】What can publicly accessible fruit and vegetable gardens do apart from their practical functions? 主干 What can ... gardens do，apart from their practical functions 作状语限定范围，相当于把"实用功能"这一已知项排除出去；其中 publicly accessible 是副词修饰形容词，整体修饰 gardens。

【定位】They can make unlovely spaces lovely, and marry use and beauty as well as help promote a sense of community. 它们能化丑为美，把实用与美感融合在一起，并有助于增强一种社区感。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 Raise people's environmental awareness. 把"连接食物与产地、对抗物种丧失"偷换 成"提升环保意识"，前者是行为层面的连接和效用，后者是心理认知层面的意识。 B) 无中生有 Add to the great variety of plant species. 说菜园会增加植物物种多样性，原文从未 谈"增加植物物种多样性"这一功能。 C) 偷换概念 Act as the first defence against natural disasters. 把 first defence against species loss and climate change 偷换成"对抗自然灾害"——物种丧失和气候变化不等于"自然 灾害"，并且选项主语 act as 暗示把整个菜园当成防线，与原文 Plants are 也对不上。 D) ✓ 正确 help promote a sense of community ↔Enhance people's community spirit. 预判要的"增强社区感"在原文里有直接对应的 "help promote a sense of community"，D 项把 promote 替换为 enhance、sense of community 替换为 community spirit，是高保真同义替换，可锁定。

items.title: 2024年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Engineering in the U.S. has long been a male-dominated profession. Fifty years ago, it looked like that might change.

P2 In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9%. Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate. But that's not what happened. Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000.

P3 I am a historian who, along with my colleagues, surveyed 251 women engineers who graduated from college in the 1970s. These pioneers reflected on the challenges they faced—and had advice for women entering the field today.

P4 One survey taker explained, "The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was."

P5 A chemical engineer who worked in manufacturing agreed, "You have to prove yourself just because you are female. And you have to work twice as hard!"

P6 A civil engineer said, "We are 'women engineers.' People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'—he's an engineer. We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong." Another civil engineer stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups."

P7 Women also talked about family caregiving responsibilities. A retired vice president from a major chemical company stated, "Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children, then they struggle to balance work and family—and compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities."

P8 But over the years things have changed a lot. Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them.

P9 Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career. A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree. A mechanical engineer said, "It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done."

questions.q: What does the passage say about the engineering profession in the United States?
options: It has seen a change in attitude towards women engineers since 1979.
It witnessed a significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s.
It has experienced the gradual weakening of male dominance.
It boasted the largest number of engineering majors in 2000.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about the engineering profession in the United States 没 有 infer/imply/mainly about 等推断或主旨标志，问 "the passage say"，是对原文已陈述 事实的核对，属四级最高频的细节题。

【拆句】题干主干是 What does the passage say about ...，是 say about 后接宾语的特殊疑问 句，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱，只要知道 say about="就……说了什么"即可。

【定位】In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9%. Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate. But that's not what happened. 1970 年，主修工程的女性占比不到 1%；1979 年这一数字升至 9%。许多人本希望女性能 以同样速度持续进入这一行业，但事实并非如此。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只给比例数据，没有提任何"对待女工程师态度的变化"，a change in attitude towards women engineers since 1979 属于凭空添加新概念。 B) ✓ 正确 In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9% ↔It witnessed a significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s In 1970 和 In 1979 ↔in the 1970s 预判要的是"70 年代女工程师比例大幅上升"，B 项 significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s 几乎逐词对应，无需犹豫即可锁定。 C) 与原文相反 Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000 明确说自 2000 年起男性主导未弱化，与 gradual weakening of male dominance 直接相反。 D) 偷换概念 原文 2000 年只是"21% 未变"的起算点，并未说 2000 年工程专业人数达到最大， boasted the largest number of engineering majors in 2000 属于把时间词原样搬， 结论却换了内容。 一位受访者表示她面临的最大挑战是什么? A) 不对资质较低的男性工程师产生优越感。 B) 不把她收到的所有信息都当真。 C) 在升职或加薪时不过高评价自己的资历。 D) 尽管不断受到打击或遭受不公平待遇,仍不失去自信。

questions.q: What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge?
options: Not to feel superior to less qualified male engineers.
Not to take seriously all the messages she was getting.
Not to think highly of her qualifications when promoted or given a pay raise.
Not to lose self-confidence though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge 是对原文一句引语的客观 还原，属细节题。

【拆句】What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge 是个嵌套问句，say 后面 接的是 "(that) her greatest challenge was ____"，疑问词 What 提到了句首，回原文找 "挑战是 ____" 这层语义即可。

【定位】The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was. 我最大的挑战是在收到"我永远不会像男性那样被认真对待、被晋升或被加薪——而那些男 性明显不如我合格、不如我聪明"这类信息时，仍然继续相信自己。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文受访者只是说"那些男性明显不如我合格"，是事实陈述；Not to feel superior to less qualified male engineers 把它扭曲成"不要觉得自己高人一等"，方向截然不同。 B) 答非所问 原文 all the messages I was getting 是"挑战的背景"，不是"挑战本身"；B 项却把"不 要把这些信息当真"说成挑战，错把背景当主体。 C) 与原文相反 原文说"她被晋升/加薪的待遇不如男性"，C 项却说"在被晋升/加薪时不要看高自己的资 历"，既颠倒了情境（她没有被同等晋升），也错读了态度。 D) ✓ 正确 continuing to believe in myself ↔Not to lose self-confidence all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men ↔though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated 预判要"在打压中坚持自信"，D 项 Not to lose self-confidence though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated 两个要素全有，是定位句的精准同义替换。 根据两位土木工程师的说法,女性工程师经常有何感受? A) 在许多层面上不具备资格。 B) 被排除在团体之外。 C) 被所在组织过度使用。 D) 被男性同事看不起。

questions.q: How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers?
options: Disqualified on many levels.
Excluded from the group.
Overworked by their organizations.
Looked down upon by male colleagues.
questions.explain:
【判型】How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers 问的 是"她们感觉如何"，依据 according to 直接锁定原文两位 civil engineer 的话，是细节归 纳题。

【拆句】How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers 主干 是 How do women engineers feel，frequently 是状语，according to ... 是介词短语作 状语，限定信息来源，没有从句也无否定，是直白的特殊疑问句。

【定位】A civil engineer said, "We are 'women engineers.' People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'—he's an engineer. We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong." Another civil engineer stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups." 一位土木工程师说："我们被叫作'女工程师'。人们不会把男人叫'男工程师'——他就是工程 师。我们时刻被提醒：我们并不真正属于这里。"另一位土木工程师说："在很多层面上，你 从来不算这个圈子的一员。"

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文 On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups 中的 on many levels 修 饰"在多个层面上"不属于群体，A 项 Disqualified on many levels 把它说成"在多个层 面上不合格"，是把"不属于群体"换成"不合格"。 B) ✓ 正确 We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong ↔Excluded from the group you're never quite one of the groups ↔Excluded from the group 预判要"不属于/被排除的情绪"，B 项 Excluded from the group 直接对应两位受访者的 核心情感，是最稳的同义替换。 C) 张冠李戴 P6 全段谈的是"不属于群体"的归属感问题，根本未涉及工作量；Overworked by their organizations 是从 work twice as hard 借来的概念，硬塞进了 53 题。 D) 过度推断 原文两位土木工程师讲的是"被整个圈子提醒不属于"，并未具体说"是男同事看低自己"； Looked down upon by male colleagues 把抽象的群体压缩成"男同事"这一具体施 动者。 什么可能使年轻女性工程师在当今更容易被接受? A) 她们在获得平等地位方面取得的成功。 B) 她们平衡工作与家庭的能力。 C) 她们职责的改变。 D) 她们数量的增加。

questions.q: What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays?
options: Their success in gaining an equal footing.
Their ability to balance work and family.
The change in their responsibilities.
The increase in their number.
questions.explain:
【判型】What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays 看似含 probably 像推断，实质问"原文里给出的原因是什么"，原文已经直说理由，仍是细节题。

【拆句】What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays 是 What makes sb. + 形容词 的使役结构，What 作主语，makes 是谓语，young women engineers 是宾语，more accepted nowadays 是宾语补足语，意为"是什么让年轻女工程 师如今更被接受"。

【定位】Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them. 年轻女工程师之所以如今更被接受，主要是因为她们的人数变多了。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 原文 Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children 只 说"育前与男性平起平坐"，是过去就存在的状态，不是"如今更被接受"的新原因；A 项 Their success in gaining an equal footing 把它包装成新成就，归错原因。 B) 与原文相反 原文 then they struggle to balance work and family 明明说"在生育后她们挣扎于平 衡工作与家庭"，B 项却说"她们有能力平衡工作与家庭"，方向完全相反。 C) 无中生有 原文 compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities 提 到"家庭责任不对等"，但从未说女工程师的责任发生了变化；C 项 The change in their responsibilities 是凭空增添一个变化。 D) ✓ 正确 there are just more of them ↔The increase in their number 预判要"人数变多"，D 项 The increase in their number 是这层意思的最贴近名词化表 达，无可争议。 从一位机械工程师的陈述中,我们可以对许多女性工程师得出什么结论? A) 她们对所选择的职业深感自豪。 B) 她们获得了灵活工作的好处。 C) 她们享受将工程工作做到最佳程度。 D) 她们已证明能够做几乎任何事情。

questions.q: What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer?
options: They take great pride in their chosen career.
They have reaped the benefits of being flexible.
They enjoy doing engineering to the best degree.
They have proved capable of doing almost anything.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer 中的 conclude+from 是典型推断题信号，需要从一位受访者的具体 话语得出"许多女工程师"层面的结论。 55. What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer? A) They take great pride in their chosen career. B) They have reaped the benefits of being flexible. C) They enjoy doing engineering to the best degree. D) They have proved capable of doing almost anything.

【拆句】What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer 主干为 What can we conclude，about many female engineers 是 conclude 的对象，from the statement of a mechanical engineer 是信息来源；问的 是"从这位机械工程师的话里能得出关于许多女工程师的什么结论"。

【定位】Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career. A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree. A mechanical engineer said, "It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done." 许多女工程师都盛赞自己所选职业的好处。一位制造业项目经理说工程是最好的学位。一 位机械工程师说："它会给你几乎可以做任何事的灵活度，看到自己所做工作的成果也令人 满足。"

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career ↔ They take great pride in their chosen career It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done ↔ take great pride in their chosen career 预判要"对职业感到自豪"，A 项 take great pride in their chosen career 在态度极性和 概括层级上都对得最准，是最贴预判的一项。 B) 偷换概念 原文 give you the flexibility to do almost anything 是说"这份职业能给你灵活度"， 强调的是职业本身的属性；B 项 reaped the benefits of being flexible 把它说成"她们 因"自己"灵活而获益"，把工具属性挪到了人本身。 C) 无中生有 原文 engineering is the best degree 是"工程是最好的学位"，整体作主系表；C 项 enjoy doing engineering to the best degree 把 the best degree 拆成 to the best degree（=最大程度地）作状语，意思变成"以最高程度享受做工程"，是字面拼凑出的 伪意思。 D) 过度推断 原文 give you the flexibility to do almost anything 是工程这个职业"能让你"做几乎 任何事，是潜在可能；D 项 proved capable of doing almost anything 说她们"已经 证明自己能做几乎任何事"，把可能性升级为既定事实。

items.title: 2024年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 As a university student, I've come to realise just how little I know about money. I've come to the brutal realisation that Australia's youth are being done a great disservice by not receiving any consistent financial education.

P2 Diving headfirst into the crash course of starting university, I've quickly tried to get myself up to speed with the financial terms of the modern era to help manage my personal finances.

P3 I've read some financial education books, done some online learning, and have spoken to my nearest and dearest for their pearls of financial wisdom.

P4 There are undoubtedly hundreds of great resources out there for those wishing to improve their financial literacy, but while I was researching, I still kept wishing that I didn't have to play catch-up with the money world. I felt that I was sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket!

P5 However, after talking to my friends who felt the same, I quickly realised that it wasn't my ignorance but the lack of financial education in our schooling system that is leaving high schoolers seriously behind in the modern world of money.

P6 Let's compare a theoretical financial education subject to the standard compulsory English class. On average, English may not be the most popular subject, but it's consistently on the schedule throughout high school, with all students graduating fluent in English.

P7 A financial education subject should do just the same. It shouldn't be just a one-day event but a course integrated throughout the whole of high school that would allow students to gradually expand their financial literacy, and would prevent the need for a 'catch up' phase once we're out on our own after graduation.

P8 In the same way that learning a language or new skills takes time, building financial skills requires practice and years to gradually accumulate bits and pieces of knowledge.

P9 Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money would provide them with a great advantage to enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money and look after themselves.

questions.q: What has the author come to realise since entering university?
options: He needs a crash course on financial terms.
He is very much lacking in financial literacy.
It requires consistent education to be financially independent.
It is unrealistic to give all Australian youth a financial education.
questions.explain:
【判型】What has the author come to realise直接问一个具体认知结果，不含infer/imply/mainly about等推断或主旨信号词。 46. What has the author come to realise since entering university? A) He needs a crash course on financial terms. B) He is very much lacking in financial literacy. C) It requires consistent education to be financially independent. D) It is unrealistic to give all Australian youth a financial education.

【拆句】What has the author come to realise since entering university?主干是What ... has come to realise，What作realise的宾语；since entering university是时间状语，结构平 铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】As a university student, I've come to realise just how little I know about money. 作为一名大学生，我已经意识到自己对金钱了解得有多么少。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 He needs a crash course on financial terms说作者需要一门速成课，而原文Diving headfirst into the crash course of starting university里的crash course指的是大学开 学这件事本身像速成课，不是金融术语速成课。 B) ✓ 正确 just how little I know about money ↔lacking in financial literacy 预判说我钱的知识少，He is very much lacking in financial literacy里的lacking in financial literacy正是这层意思的标准表达。 C) 答非所问 It requires consistent education to be financially independent谈的是要做到 financially independent的条件，而题干问的是作者意识到什么，P1里realise的宾语并 不是这个条件论。 D) 与原文相反 It is unrealistic to give all Australian youth a financial education说给澳洲青年金融 教育不现实，而原文Australia's youth are being done a great disservice by not receiving any consistent financial education恰恰是在痛心他们没有得到金融教育， 作者立场是该给而不是不现实。 作者在当今货币世界中感觉如何? A) 生存装备严重不足。 B) 对金融文献一无所知。 C) 几乎没有能力向前发展。 D) 被在线资源压得喘不过气来。

questions.q: How did the author feel in today's money world?
options: Badly equipped to survive.
Ignorant of financial literature.
Barely capable of moving ahead.
Overwhelmed by the resources online.
questions.explain:
【判型】How did the author feel直接问感受，是关于感受这个事实的细节题，不含推断信号词。

【拆句】How did the author feel in today's money world?主干How did the author feel，in today's money world是地点/情境状语；结构简单，无陷阱。

【定位】I felt that I was sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket! 我感觉自己正在金融的海洋上航行，却既没有技能也没有救生衣！ 47. How did the author feel in today's money world? A) Badly equipped to survive. B) Ignorant of financial literature. C) Barely capable of moving ahead. D) Overwhelmed by the resources online.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 sailing the financial seas with no skills and no life jacket ↔Badly equipped to survive 预判说作者缺装备处境危险，Badly equipped to survive里badly equipped to survive正是这层意思的标准等值表达。 B) 偷换概念 Ignorant of financial literature里financial literature是金融文献，而原文谈的是 financial literacy/skills，文献和素养是两回事，选项偷换了对象。 C) 程度副词偷换 Barely capable of moving ahead说勉强能前进，原文no skills and no life jacket描绘 的是完全无装备的处境，是不能前进而不是勉强能。 D) 答非所问 Overwhelmed by the resources online说被网络资源压垮，而原文hundreds of great resources out there并没有说作者被压垮，反而是肯定资源很多，作者的负面感受来自 缺装备不是资源多。 作者在与朋友交谈后意识到了什么? A) 他们和他一样热衷于金融事务。 B) 学校教育制度应该为他的困境负责。 C) 高中生对现代金融世界一无所知。 D) 金融课程和必修英语课一样不受欢迎。

questions.q: What did the author realise after talking to his friends?
options: They were as keen as he was on financial matters.
The schooling system was to blame for his trouble.
High schoolers knew nothing about the modern financial world.
Financial courses were as unpopular as compulsory English classes.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did the author realise after talking to his friends问的是一个具体认知结果，没有 infer/imply等信号词。

【拆句】What did the author realise after talking to his friends?主干What did the author realise，after talking to his friends是时间状语；结构平直，无陷阱。

【定位】However, after talking to my friends who felt the same, I quickly realised that it wasn't my ignorance but the lack of financial education in our schooling system that is leaving high schoolers seriously behind in the modern world of money. 然而，和有同感的朋友们聊过之后，我很快意识到，让高中生在现代金钱世界里严重落后 的，不是我的无知，而是我们学校系统里金融教育的缺失。 48. What did the author realise after talking to his friends? A) They were as keen as he was on financial matters. B) The schooling system was to blame for his trouble. C) High schoolers knew nothing about the modern financial world. D) Financial courses were as unpopular as compulsory English classes.

【选项】A) 过度推断 They were as keen as he was on financial matters说朋友们也对金融问题热心，而原 文my friends who felt the same只说朋友们有同感（同样觉得吃力），并没说他们热 心研究金融。 B) ✓ 正确 not...but the lack of financial education in our schooling system ↔ The schooling system was to blame for his trouble 预判说学校系统背锅，The schooling system was to blame for his trouble里was to blame正是这层归因意思。 C) 以偏概全 High schoolers knew nothing about the modern financial world说高中生对金融世 界一无所知，而原文leaving high schoolers seriously behind说的是严重落后不是一 无所知，knew nothing是把落后扩大成零知识。 D) 无中生有 Financial courses were as unpopular as compulsory English classes说金融课和必 修英语一样不受欢迎，原文English may not be the most popular subject只是承认英 语不算最受欢迎，从未说金融课不受欢迎或两者并列，且这点出现在48题区间之外，纯 属无中生有。 作者对金融教育课程的想法是什么? A) 它应该预见学生毕业后的需求。 B) 它应该为学生提供一些基础知识。 C) 它应该像英语教学那样授课。 D) 它应该融入高中教育。

questions.q: What is the author's idea of a financial education course?
options: It should foresee students' needs after graduation.
It should provide students with some basic knowledge.
It should be taught the same way as English is taught.
It should be integrated into high school education.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the author's idea of a financial education course?问的是作者明确提出的具体主 张，原文应有should句直接对应，不需推断。

【拆句】What is the author's idea of a financial education course?主干What is the author's idea，of短语限定idea的对象，结构平直无陷阱。

【定位】It shouldn't be just a one-day event but a course integrated throughout the whole of high school that would allow students to gradually expand their financial literacy, and would prevent the need for a 'catch up' phase once we're out on our own after graduation. 它不该只是一个一日活动，而该是一门贯穿整个高中阶段的课程，让学生逐步拓展自己的金 融素养，从而避免我们毕业独立生活后还得补课。 49. What is the author's idea of a financial education course? A) It should foresee students' needs after graduation. B) It should provide students with some basic knowledge. C) It should be taught the same way as English is taught. D) It should be integrated into high school education.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 It should foresee students' needs after graduation说该课该预见学生毕业后的需 求，而原文prevent the need for a 'catch up' phase once we're out on our own after graduation说的是避免毕业后补课，不是预见学生需求，foresee needs偷换了 prevent the need这层因果。 B) 以偏概全 It should provide students with some basic knowledge说该课只该提供基础知识， 而原文gradually expand their financial literacy说的是逐步拓展金融素养，且years to gradually accumulate bits and pieces of knowledge强调长期积累，some basic把整 个长期拓展过程缩成基础知识，是范围偷小。 C) 过度推断 It should be taught the same way as English is taught说该课该用和英语一样的教 法，而原文Let's compare a theoretical financial education subject to the standard compulsory English class只是拿英语做类比强调持续性，并没有说要在教法上完全一 样，taught the same way是把类比推过头。 D) ✓ 正确 a course integrated throughout the whole of high school ↔ It should be integrated into high school education 预判说该课应融入高中始终，It should be integrated into high school education里 integrated into high school education正是这层意思的同义表达。 金融素养会给年轻人带来什么? A) 让他们在经济有保障的情况下步入成年。 B) 使他们能够照顾自己而无需担心金钱问题。 C) 使他们在资金管理方面自信而有安全感。 D) 帮助他们熟悉货币世界。

questions.q: What would financial literacy do to young people?
options: Allow them to enter adulthood with financial security.
Enable them to look after themselves without worrying about money.
Render them confident and secure in terms of money management.
Help them become familiar with the world of money.
questions.explain:
【判型】What would financial literacy do to young people问的是金融素养对年轻人的具体作 用，原文应有直接对应句。

【拆句】What would financial literacy do to young people?主干What would financial literacy do，to young people是间接宾语；结构平直无陷阱。 50. What would financial literacy do to young people? A) Allow them to enter adulthood with financial security. B) Enable them to look after themselves without worrying about money. C) Render them confident and secure in terms of money management. D) Help them become familiar with the world of money.

【定位】Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money would provide them with a great advantage to enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money and look after themselves. 让年轻人有机会熟悉金钱世界，会让他们带着自信和安全感步入成年，并因此能够自己管理 钱财、照顾好自己。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Allow them to enter adulthood with financial security只保留了security丢掉了 confidence，且把confidence and security压缩为financial security一项，原文是双重 收益而不是只有金融安全。 B) 过度推断 Enable them to look after themselves without worrying about money里without worrying about money是说不必为钱发愁，而原文able to manage their own money只说能管理钱，不等于不必为钱发愁，without worrying是从能管理钱推过头。 C) ✓ 正确 enter adulthood with confidence and security so that they are able to manage their own money ↔Render them confident and secure in terms of money management 预判说在金钱管理上自信且有安全感，Render them confident and secure in terms of money management里confident and secure in terms of money management 正是这层意思最完整的同义替换。 D) 答非所问 Help them become familiar with the world of money说帮他们熟悉金钱世界，而原 文Giving young people the opportunity to become familiar with the world of money里熟悉金钱世界是金融素养这件事的前提条件而不是它带来的后果，题干问的是 financial literacy带来什么，不是它是什么。

items.title: 2024年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Chocolates save us from many things, especially emotional distress. They comfort us in times of trouble, calming down a racing heart by channelling happy calories inside us. We all have faith in chocolates to delight us in an instant!

P2 Recently, chocolate lovers were heartbroken as scientists claimed that they can become extinct by 2050! But hey, we have some happy news for you. Scientists can still help save chocolates from dying out! If you are not aware as to why scientists made the statement about the death of this wonderful thing, let us tell you the facts. Chocolate trees, whose seeds are used to make chocolate, grow in the tropical plant world and require very specific weather conditions to prosper.

P3 Now, fifty percent of the world's cocoa(可可) beans come from two countries in West Africa: Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana. Scientists believe that both of these countries will experience a 3.8°F temperature increase by 2050 due to global warming, endangering the cacao( 可可树) farms in the rainforests. These farms will then have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife. This will lead to some tough decisions: whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife.

P4 Unfortunately, the crisis of global warming has already had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields, leading to the prices of chocolates skyrocketing.

P5 Scientists, however, are trying to find a long-term and eco-friendly solution to this problem! They are trying to modify the species with a gene-editing technology, which will transform the seedlings into a species that survives even in a drier and warmer climate.

P6 According to a report by The Business Insider, in the University of California's new bio-sciences building, tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses for a new experiment by using a technology called CRISPR. By manipulating the DNA of plants, this technology is already being used across the world to make plants tougher and cheaper. Similarly, in this unconventional experiment, scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates.

questions.q: What do people believe chocolates can do?
options: Cheer them up instantly.
Create happy calories.
Conceal emotional distress.
Relieve them of heart trouble.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do people believe chocolates can do? 问的是巧克力能干什么这一具体功能，没有 infer/imply/mainly 等信号词。 51. What do people believe chocolates can do? A) Cheer them up instantly. B) Create happy calories. C) Conceal emotional distress. D) Relieve them of heart trouble.

【拆句】题干主干 What do people believe chocolates can do? 是一个嵌套宾语从句的特殊疑问 句：What 是 do 的宾语，people 是主语，believe 后跟省略 that 的宾语从句 chocolates can do (what)。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】We all have faith in chocolates to delight us in an instant! 我们都相信巧克力能在一瞬间让我们开心起来！

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 delight us in an instant ↔Cheer them up instantly 「瞬间让人开心」的预判与 Cheer them up instantly 在语义上完全重合，无差量，直 接锁定。 B) 偷换概念识别 Create happy calories 把原文 channelling happy calories inside us 中「输送/导入 愉快卡路里」当成「创造卡路里」，把比喻动作偷换成 create。 C) 与原文相反识别 原文是 They comfort us in times of trouble——「安抚」情绪，而 Conceal emotional distress 说「隐藏」情绪，安抚≠隐藏，意思相反。 D) 过度推断识别 原文 calming down a racing heart 是比喻「让狂跳的心平静下来」，而 Relieve them of heart trouble 把 racing heart 强行解为「心脏疾病」并把 calming down 换成 relieve…of，属于过度推断。 科学家最近关于巧克力的断言是什么? A) 在不久的将来它们可能会成为稀罕物。 B) 在危机时期它们可以让人们稍微平静下来。 C) 它们可以防止人们心碎。 D) 在不到30年的时间里它们可能会变得无法获得。

questions.q: What was scientists' recent assertion about chocolates?
options: They could become a rare treat in the near future.
They could calm people down a bit in times of crisis.
They could prevent people from getting heartbroken.
They could become unavailable in less than 30 years.
questions.explain:
【判型】What was scientists' recent assertion about chocolates? 问的是科学家断言的具体内 容，原文中可定位一句即可作答。

【拆句】题干 What was scientists' recent assertion about chocolates? 是 What…be 句型，主语 scientists' recent assertion 由所有格 + 形容词 + 名词构成，about chocolates 是后置介 词短语修饰 assertion。结构简单，无陷阱。

【定位】Recently, chocolate lovers were heartbroken as scientists claimed that they can become extinct by 2050! 最近，巧克力爱好者们伤心欲绝，因为科学家声称巧克力到 2050 年可能灭绝！ 52. What was scientists' recent assertion about chocolates? A) They could become a rare treat in the near future. B) They could calm people down a bit in times of crisis. C) They could prevent people from getting heartbroken. D) They could become unavailable in less than 30 years.

【选项】A) 过度推断识别 They could become a rare treat in the near future 说巧克力会变成「稀有美食」， 但原文是 extinct（灭绝/绝种），不是 rare（稀少），属于程度上的过度推断与偷换。 B) 答非所问识别 They could calm people down a bit in times of crisis 描述的是巧克力的安抚功能， 是首段的内容；题干问的是「科学家最近的断言」，不在第一段范围内。 C) 与原文相反识别 They could prevent people from getting heartbroken 利用 chocolate lovers were heartbroken 中的 heartbroken 反向拼凑，把「伤心」错改为「防止伤心」，与原文方 向完全相反。 D) ✓ 正确 they can become extinct by 2050 ↔They could become unavailable in less than 30 years 「2050 年前灭绝」的预判与 They could become unavailable in less than 30 years 完全重合，时间值与「灭绝/不可得」均对得上。 如果可可农场转移到更凉爽的山区会发生什么? A) 那里野生动物的自然栖息地将被破坏。 B) 可可农民适应起来会很艰难。 C) 热带雨林将急剧缩小。 D) 可可豆的质量将大受影响。

questions.q: What would happen if the cacao farms were shifted to cooler mountainous areas?
options: The natural habitat of wildlife there would be ruined.
The cacao farmers would have a tough time to adapt.
The rainforests would be shrinking dramatically.
The quality of cocoa beans would suffer greatly.
questions.explain:
【判型】What would happen if the cacao farms were shifted to cooler mountainous areas? 是 if 条件下的客观结果，可直接到原文条件句中找到表述。

【拆句】题干 What would happen if the cacao farms were shifted to cooler mountainous areas? 是 What + 虚拟条件句：主句 what would happen 用 would，从句 were shifted 是被动语态，整体表达「假设农场被迁走，会发生什么」。要注意 were shifted 是被动结 构，主体是农场而非农民。

【定位】These farms will then have to be shifted to cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife. 这些农场届时将不得不被迁到更凉爽的山区，而那里正是野生动物的自然栖息地。 53. What would happen if the cacao farms were shifted to cooler mountainous areas? A) The natural habitat of wildlife there would be ruined. B) The cacao farmers would have a tough time to adapt. C) The rainforests would be shrinking dramatically. D) The quality of cocoa beans would suffer greatly.
