【选项】A) ✓ 正确 cooler mountainous areas, which are the natural habitat of wildlife ↔ The natural habitat of wildlife there would be ruined whether to grow chocolate or save wildlife ↔would be ruined 「侵占并破坏野生动物栖息地」的预判与 The natural habitat of wildlife there would be ruined 完全重合。 B) 无中生有识别 The cacao farmers would have a tough time to adapt 谈的是「农民适应困难」，原 文从未提及农民的适应问题，纯属编造。 C) 答非所问识别 The rainforests would be shrinking dramatically 谈的是雨林萎缩，但题干问的是 「农场迁到凉爽山区之后」，迁出地（雨林）的变化并不是题干问的「会发生什么」的 核心后果，且原文未说雨林会因此显著萎缩。 D) 无中生有识别 The quality of cocoa beans would suffer greatly 说可可豆质量会大幅下降，原文从 未谈及「质量」问题，只提到产量（yields）下降；属于无中生有。 关于全球变暖危机中的可可农场我们了解到什么? A) 它们试图向基因编辑科学家寻求帮助。 B) 它们决定搬到更凉爽的山区。 C) 由于产量下降它们遭受了很大损失。 D) 它们通过提高可可豆价格而获益。

questions.q: What do we learn about the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming?
options: They try to seek help from gene-editing scientists.
They decide to move to cooler mountainous areas.
They have suffered a lot due to a decrease in produce.
They have benefited by raising prices of cocoa beans.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming? 问的是文中 告诉我们的客观事实，可在原文找一句直接陈述。

【拆句】题干 What do we learn about the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming? 主干为 What do we learn about Y，about 后接 the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming，in 引导的介词短语充当 farms 的处境状语。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Unfortunately, the crisis of global warming has already had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields, leading to the prices of chocolates skyrocketing. 不幸的是，全球变暖危机已经严重负面地影响了可可园的产量，导致巧克力价格飙升。 54. What do we learn about the cacao farms in the crisis of global warming? A) They try to seek help from gene-editing scientists. B) They decide to move to cooler mountainous areas. C) They have suffered a lot due to a decrease in produce. D) They have benefited by raising prices of cocoa beans.

【选项】A) 无中生有识别 They try to seek help from gene-editing scientists 说农场主动求助科学家，原文第 五、六段是科学家自己在研究、不是农场求助，属无中生有。 B) 时态偷换识别 They decide to move to cooler mountainous areas 把原文第三段 will then have to be shifted 这一未来「将不得不被迁」错读为已经「决定迁移」，时态与主动性都被 改了。 C) ✓ 正确 had a serious negative impact on cacao farms' yields ↔ They have suffered a lot due to a decrease in produce 「农场产量受严重负面影响」的预判与 They have suffered a lot due to a decrease in produce 在语义上一致；C 把「产量下滑」前移为原因，更贴合题干「What do we learn about the cacao farms」的视角。 D) 与原文相反识别 They have benefited by raising prices of cocoa beans 说农场因涨价获益，但原文是 「产量下降→巧克力价格飙升」，价格飙升是消极后果而非农场获益；属与原文相反。 科学家们正试图在加州大学的新生物科学大楼里做什么? A) 建造成排的冷藏温室用于可可幼苗研究。 B) 对可可幼苗进行基因编辑使其能够承受更干燥、更温暖的气候。 C) 用最新的基因编辑技术生产巧克力。 D) 将更强韧植物的基因移植到可可幼苗中。

questions.q: What are scientists trying to do in the University of California's new bio-sciences building?
options: Build rows of refrigerated greenhouses for research on cacao seedlings.
Gene-edit cacao seedlings for them to withstand a drier, warmer climate.
Produce chocolates with the latest gene-editing technology.
Transplant the genes of tougher plants to cacao seedlings.
questions.explain:
【判型】What are scientists trying to do in the University of California's new bio-sciences building? 问的是科学家在特定地点的具体行动，可在原文末段直接找到。

【拆句】题干 What are scientists trying to do in the University of California's new bio- sciences building? 是 What + 进行时疑问句：trying to do 表达科学家此刻正努力做某 事，in 引导的地点状语限定场景。结构清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】in this unconventional experiment, scientists will make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates. 在这个非常规实验中，科学家将对种苗的 DNA 做出细微而精确的改变，以使可可作物能在 更暖、更干的气候中存活。 55. What are scientists trying to do in the University of California's new bio-sciences building? A) Build rows of refrigerated greenhouses for research on cacao seedlings. B) Gene-edit cacao seedlings for them to withstand a drier, warmer climate. C) Produce chocolates with the latest gene-editing technology. D) Transplant the genes of tougher plants to cacao seedlings.

【选项】A) 答非所问识别 Build rows of refrigerated greenhouses for research on cacao seedlings 把原文 tiny green cacao seedlings are lined up in refrigerated greenhouses 中的「冷藏温 室」错读为科学家在「建造温室」，但温室只是已有的实验环境，不是科学家正在做的 目的。 B) ✓ 正确 make tiny, precise changes to the DNA of the seedlings ↔Gene-edit cacao seedlings to make the cocoa crops survive in warmer and drier climates ↔ for them to withstand a drier, warmer climate 「基因编辑可可种苗 + 让其耐暖耐旱」的预判与 Gene-edit cacao seedlings for them to withstand a drier, warmer climate 在两个语义成分上都重合。 C) 过度推断识别 Produce chocolates with the latest gene-editing technology 把目标直接定为「生 产巧克力」，但原文目的是先改造种苗使可可作物耐气候，距离「生产巧克力」还有多 步，属过度推断。 D) 无中生有识别 Transplant the genes of tougher plants to cacao seedlings 说把更耐性强植物的基 因移植到可可种苗，原文只说对种苗 DNA 做精细修改，未提「移植其他物种基因」， 属无中生有。

items.title: 2024年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof. Recent evidence points to drivers' limited understanding of what these systems can and cannot do as a contributing factor to system misuse. A recent study tackles the issue of over-trusting drivers and the resulting system misuse from a legal viewpoint. It looks at what the manufacturers of self-driving cars should legally do to ensure that drivers understand how to use the vehicles appropriately.

P2 One solution suggested in the study involves requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements (EULAs), similar to the terms and conditions that require agreement when using new software products. But this is far from ideal. The agreement may not provide enough information to the driver, leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications. Further, most end users don't read EULAs. A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading. Among young people, 97 percent agree without reviewing the terms.

P3 The issue is that, unlike using a smartphone app, operating a car has serious safety risks, whether the driver is human or software. And human drivers need to consent to take responsibility for the outcomes of the software and hardware.

P4 "Warning fatigue" and distracted driving are also causes for concern. For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message. Or, if the message is presented while the vehicle is in motion, it could represent a distraction. Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction(发生故障) or an accident occur.

P5 Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations. This needs to occur beyond the vehicle purchase. Recent evidence shows even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions. All of this considered, the road forward for self-driving cars is not going to be a smooth ride after all.

questions.q: What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction?
options: Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors.
Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people.
Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware of the legal matters involved.
There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction? 直接问研究告诉了我们 什么，答案必然是原文一句陈述的客观转述，不需要跨段推理。

【拆句】结构平铺直叙：主句是 What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction，from 引导的介宾短语限定信息来源，无从句、无否定、无陷阱。 46. What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction? A) Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors. B) Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people. C) Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware of the legal matters involved. D) There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles.

【定位】Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof. 人车交互领域的研究表明，即便是为自动驾驶而设计的系统，也远远谈不上无差错。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 systems designed to automate driving ↔Automatic driving systems far from being error-proof ↔by no means immune to errors 预判要的是系统并非无差错，A 项 Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors 是对 systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof 的逐部分同义替换，无添加无减少，锁定 A。 B) 偷换概念 Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people 谈的是车被滥用，而题 干问的是研究发现，定位句结论是系统易出错，两者不在同一语义层；滥用确实在 system misuse 中提到但只是后续展开，并非首句的研究结论。 C) 无中生有 Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware of the legal matters involved 称厂商 对法律毫无意识，而原文 A recent study tackles the issue…from a legal viewpoint 只是说有研究从法律角度切入，从未说厂商不知情。 D) 偷换概念 There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles 把 研究结论说成人车交互本身遥不可及，而原文人车交互只是研究领域名，研究真正的发 现是系统易错，与是否能交互无关。 要求购买者签署最终用户许可协议存在什么问题? A) 无论老少,最终用户都觉得条款难以理解。 B) 大多数最终用户签署时根本不会费心阅读条款。 C) 许多人经常对条款的措辞感到困惑。 D) 大多数最终用户即使通读后也不理解这些条款。

questions.q: What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements?
options: End users, young and old alike, find the terms complex to interpret.
Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms.
Many people are often confused by the wording of the terms.
Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 询 问一个具体做法的问题所在，属于对原文局部反面描述的提取。

【拆句】结构清晰：What is the problem with… 主句问的是 problem，with 后跟动名词短语 requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements 作 problem 的定语，整体无 难点。 47. What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements? A) End users, young and old alike, find the terms complex to interpret. B) Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms. C) Many people are often confused by the wording of the terms. D) Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through.

【定位】Further, most end users don't read EULAs. A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading. 更何况，大多数终端用户根本不读 EULA。2017 年的一项研究表明，91% 的人未读就同 意了。

【选项】A) 无中生有 End users, young and old alike, find the terms complex to interpret 说所有人都觉 得条款难以解读，但原文只说大家压根不读，从未说他们读了之后觉得难懂。 B) ✓ 正确 most end users don't read EULAs ↔ Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms 91 percent of people agree to them without reading ↔Most end users 预判要的是签前不读，B 项 Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms 正是这一行为的标准表述，与原文双句合并对应，锁定 B。 C) 偷换概念 Many people are often confused by the wording of the terms 说人们被措辞搞晕， 但原文 leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications 说的是对协议性质与含义的困惑，且这是协议信息不足的后果，不是 本题题干问的 EULA 整体的根本问题。 D) 与原文相反 Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through 隐含的 前提是用户把条款读完了，只是不懂；而原文 most end users don't read EULAs 的事 实是用户根本没读，两者前提相反。 当驾驶员遭受"警告疲劳"时会怎么做? A) 毫不拖延地保持汽车行驶。 B) 休息一会儿以避免疲劳驾驶。 C) 尽管反复警告也不采取行动。 D) 虽然疲劳但仍注意警告信息。

questions.q: What would drivers do when they suffer from "warning fatigue"?
options: Waste no time keeping the car moving.
Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving.
Take no action despite repeated warnings.
Take note of the message though fatigued.
questions.explain:
【判型】What would drivers do when they suffer from "warning fatigue"? 问的是在某情境下司 机会做出何种动作，属于对原文具体情境的事实提取。

【拆句】主句 What would drivers do 是常规疑问句，when 引导的时间状语从句 when they suffer from "warning fatigue" 限定情境，suffer from 意为遭受、深受其扰，无陷阱。 48. What would drivers do when they suffer from "warning fatigue"? A) Waste no time keeping the car moving. B) Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving. C) Take no action despite repeated warnings. D) Take note of the message though fatigued.

【定位】For example, a driver, annoyed after receiving continuous warnings, could decide to just ignore the message. 举例来说，一名司机在接到接连不断的警告后心生厌烦，可能干脆决定无视这条信息。

【选项】A) 无中生有 Waste no time keeping the car moving 是 抓紧时间让车继续走，与原文 ignore the message 描述的不作为完全不是一回事。 B) 偷换概念 Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving 在谈疲劳驾驶要休息，但原文 "Warning fatigue" 指对警告厌烦，并非生理疲劳。 C) ✓ 正确 could decide to just ignore the message ↔Take no action despite repeated warnings 预判要的是无视警告这一行为，C 项 Take no action despite repeated warnings 把无 视＝不作为、反复警告＝重复警告两端都精准对位，锁定 C。 D) 与原文相反 Take note of the message though fatigued 是 虽然疲惫但仍留意警告，与原文 just ignore the message 完全相反。 作者如何看待继续要求购买者签署最终用户许可协议? A) 这可能无法保证发生事故时驾驶员的安全。 B) 这可能无法确保自动驾驶系统正常运行。 C) 这可能无法充分保护汽车制造商免受蓄意欺诈的指控。 D) 这可能无法为制造商提供充分的法律责任保护。

questions.q: What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements?
options: It will probably not guarantee the safety of drivers in case of accidents.
It likely won't ensure that the automatic driving system functions properly.
It likely won't fully protect automakers against accusations of deliberate cheating.
It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 虽问作者看法，但锁定于 EULAs 这一局部做法，仍以一句明确表态句为答案 依据，属细节题。

【拆句】What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements? 中 think of 后接动名词 continuing，continuing 再接动词不定式 to ask buyers to sign…，是动名词+不定式连用的链式结构，意为对继续要求买家签 EULA 这件 事，作者怎么看。 49. What does the author think of continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements? A) It will probably not guarantee the safety of drivers in case of accidents. B) It likely won't ensure that the automatic driving system functions properly. C) It likely won't fully protect automakers against accusations of deliberate cheating. D) It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities.

【定位】Given these limitations and concerns, even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward, it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction(发生故障) or an accident occur. 鉴于这些局限与担忧，即使继续推行这种取得同意的方式，万一系统发生故障或事故发生， 它也很可能无法在法律责任上充分保护汽车制造商。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 It will probably not guarantee the safety of drivers in case of accidents 谈的是事 故中司机的安全保障，但原文 protect automakers from their legal liability 谈的是保 护厂商免于法律责任，对象与内容都错位。 B) 偷换概念 It likely won't ensure that the automatic driving system functions properly 谈的是 系统能否正常运行，但原文谈的是法律层面对厂商的保护，二者根本不是一回事。 C) 偷换概念 It likely won't fully protect automakers against accusations of deliberate cheating 谈的是免于被指故意欺诈，但原文 legal liability 仅指法律责任，未涉及 deliberate cheating 故意欺诈这一更窄、更带主观恶意的范畴。 D) ✓ 正确 it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability ↔ It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities automakers ↔manufacturers 预判要的是不能充分保护厂商的法律责任，D 项 It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities 与定位句逐字对 位，锁定 D。 应该做什么来帮助驾驶员充分了解系统的功能和局限性? A) 培训他们成为车辆自动化方面的专家。 B) 通过培训使他们熟悉这些系统。 C) 拓宽他们对事故预防机制的了解。 D) 便利他们获取销售方提供的信息。

questions.q: What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations?
options: Training them to be experts in vehicle automation.
Familiarizing them with the systems through training.
Broadening their knowledge of accident-prevention mechanisms.
Facilitating their access to the information provided by the seller.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations? 直接问该做什么以达成目的，属于对原文解决方案句的提取。

【拆句】主句 What should be done 是被动疑问句，to help 引导的不定式作目的状语，help drivers 后接动词原形 fully understand…，整句意思是：为帮司机充分理解系统能力与局 限，应该做什么。 50. What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations? A) Training them to be experts in vehicle automation. B) Familiarizing them with the systems through training. C) Broadening their knowledge of accident-prevention mechanisms. D) Facilitating their access to the information provided by the seller.

【定位】Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations. 针对自动驾驶汽车的司机培训，能够帮助确保司机充分了解系统的能力与局限。

【选项】A) 过度推断 Training them to be experts in vehicle automation 把目标拔到成为车辆自动化领域 专家的高度，而原文只要求 fully understand system capabilities and limitations，是 理解层级而非专家层级。 B) ✓ 正确 Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations ↔Familiarizing them with the systems through training fully understand system capabilities and limitations ↔Familiarizing them with the systems 预判要的是通过培训让司机熟悉系统，B 项 Familiarizing them with the systems through training 与定位句双层等值，锁定 B。 C) 无中生有 Broadening their knowledge of accident-prevention mechanisms 谈的是扩大防事 故机制的知识面，但原文谈的是理解系统的能力与局限，accident-prevention mechanisms 在文中并未出现。 D) 与原文相反 Facilitating their access to the information provided by the seller 主张方便司机获 取卖家信息，但原文 even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions 明确指出哪怕依赖卖家信息也无法解答许多问题， 二者方向相反。

items.title: 2024年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 Do you ever blend up a protein drink for breakfast, or grab a protein bar following an afternoon workout? If so, you are likely among the millions of people in search of more protein-rich diets.

P2 Protein-enriched products are found everywhere. But contrary to all the publicity that everyone needs more protein, most Americans get twice as much as they need.

P3 Many of us living in the most developed countries are buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts. Global retail sales of protein supplement products reached an astonishing US$18.9 billion in 2020.

P4 But are we really in need of more protein? Physicians in the U.S. have never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein.

P5 In fact, Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level.

P6 For example, if you're a dedicated athlete you might need to consume higher quantities of protein. Generally, though, a 140-pound person should not exceed 120 grams of protein per day, particularly because a high protein diet can strain kidney and liver function and increase risks of developing heart disease and cancer.

P7 While fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns since over a century ago, protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite.

P8 In the 1970s through the 1990s, protein products remained visible but moved back somewhat with the dietary spotlight firmly fixed on low-calorie, low-fat, sugar-free snack foods and beverages following the publication of studies linking sugar and saturated(饱和的) fat consumption to heart disease.

P9 Later research in 2003, however, suggested high-protein diets could aid in weight loss, and protein quickly regained its former nutrient-superstar status.

P10 Now most people living in high-income nations are consuming enough protein. When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on the rich sources of antioxidants(抗氧化剂), vitamins and many other benefits of real food.

questions.q: What do we learn about publicity over protein in America?
options: It has helped to create the myth of protein deficiency.
It has helped Americans in search of protein-rich diets.
It has raised a lot of health concerns among the public.
It has been funded by food companies and health experts.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about publicity over protein in America? 是一个 What…learn about 的事实型问句，直接问关于某对象（publicity）的某一事实，没有 infer/suggest/imply 等推断信号。

【拆句】句式平铺直叙：What do we learn about publicity over protein in America? 主干是 What do we learn about X，介词短语 over protein 是 publicity 的范围限定，in America 限定地域，无陷阱。

【定位】Many of us living in the most developed countries are buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts. 我们这些生活在大多数发达国家的人，正在接受一个由食品公司和自封的健康专家制造出来 的"蛋白质缺乏"神话。 51. What do we learn about publicity over protein in America? A) It has helped to create the myth of protein deficiency. B) It has helped Americans in search of protein-rich diets. C) It has raised a lot of health concerns among the public. D) It has been funded by food companies and health experts.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 buying into a myth of protein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts ↔It has helped to create the myth of protein deficiency. contrary to all the publicity that everyone needs more protein ↔ the myth of protein deficiency 预判说"宣传促成了蛋白缺乏的迷思"，helped to create the myth of protein deficiency 一字不差地落到这个语义上，是定位句的直接同义替换。 B) 与原文相反 原文用 buying into a myth 表明宣传是在"骗"美国人，并非"帮"他们；选项 helped Americans in search of protein-rich diets 把负面后果包装成正面服务，与原作者态度 相反。 C) 无中生有 原文从未说 publicity "raised health concerns"——P6 的健康风险讲的是高蛋白饮食 本身，而非舆论造成的恐慌；选项 raised a lot of health concerns among the public 在文中无落点。 D) 偷换概念 原文说迷思是 created by food companies and self-identified health experts，主语 是"食品公司和自封专家"在制造迷思；选项 funded by food companies and health experts 把 created 偷换成 funded（资助），且把 publicity 当受资助对象，主体与动 作都被改写。 为什么美国医生从未真正诊治过蛋白质缺乏症患者? A) 美国人可以在各处购买到多种富含蛋白质的食品。 B) 美国人能够摄入食品专家推荐的卡路里量。 C) 美国人只需每天摄入足够的食物就能获得充足的蛋白质。 D) 美国人可以依靠食品补充剂来预防蛋白质缺乏。

questions.q: Why have physicians in the U.S. never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency?
options: Americans can purchase many kinds of protein-rich foods everywhere.
Americans can absorb the number of calories recommended by food experts.
Americans can get sufficient protein just by eating adequate foods daily.
Americans can rely on food supplements to prevent protein deficiency.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why have physicians in the U.S. never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency? 用 Why 直问原因，要求按原文给出的解释作答，不需要自行推断。

【拆句】现在完成时 have…never actually examined，never 是关键否定词，actually 加强语气， 提示原文给出的解释是"压根没机会见到"层面的原因；理解时把 never examined 当作"从 未见过"即可。 52. Why have physicians in the U.S. never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency? A) Americans can purchase many kinds of protein-rich foods everywhere. B) Americans can absorb the number of calories recommended by food experts. C) Americans can get sufficient protein just by eating adequate foods daily. D) Americans can rely on food supplements to prevent protein deficiency.

【定位】Physicians in the U.S. have never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein. 美国医生从未真正诊治过蛋白缺乏的病人，因为只要每天摄入足够的卡路里，我们也就极可 能获得了足够的蛋白质。

【选项】A) 答非所问 原文给出的原因是"日常热量摄入足够蛋白也就够了"，与"能否买到"无关；选项 purchase many kinds of protein-rich foods everywhere 谈购买便利性，是另一 回事。 B) 偷换概念 原文说的是 an adequate number of daily calories"日常足量的卡路里"，选项 absorb the number of calories recommended by food experts 偷换为"食品专家推荐的卡路 里数"——多了"food experts recommended"这一未出现的限定，且 absorb 与 eating 含义偏移。 C) ✓ 正确 simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein ↔Americans can get sufficient protein just by eating adequate foods daily. 预判说"靠正常饮食的热量就够蛋白"，get sufficient protein just by eating adequate foods daily 几乎逐字对应，是 because 句的同义替换。 D) 与原文相反 原文的因果是"正常饮食就够蛋白，所以不必靠补剂"；选项 rely on food supplements to prevent protein deficiency 反过来说"靠补剂预防缺乏"，正是全文批判的对象。 人们在决定最理想的蛋白质摄入量时应考虑什么? A) 他们有多健康以及他们吃什么食物。 B) 他们的年龄以及他们从事什么活动。 C) 他们摄入多少蛋白质以及他们的体重是多少。 D) 他们的蛋白质缺乏有多严重以及他们使用什么补救措施。

questions.q: What should people take into consideration in deciding on the most preferable protein intake?
options: How healthy they are and what food they eat.
How old they are and what activities they do.
How much protein they consume and what their body weight is.
How serious their protein deficiency is and what remedies they use.
questions.explain:
【判型】What should people take into consideration in deciding on the most preferable protein intake? 在问决策依据，原文必会以并列形式给出依据项，照搬即可。

【拆句】in deciding on… 是 in doing 结构作状语，表"在做某事的时候"；主干是 What should people take into consideration，把状语剥掉，问句就回归"应考虑什么"，简单。 53. What should people take into consideration in deciding on the most preferable protein intake? A) How healthy they are and what food they eat. B) How old they are and what activities they do. C) How much protein they consume and what their body weight is. D) How serious their protein deficiency is and what remedies they use.

【定位】Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level. 尽管最理想的蛋白摄入量可能因年龄和活动量不同而有所差异，美国人现在的蛋白摄入仍接 近美国医学科学院推荐摄入量的两倍。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只列了 age and activity level，并未把"现在健康程度"或"吃什么食物"列入考虑因 素；选项 How healthy they are and what food they eat 是凭常识自造的因素。 B) ✓ 正确 depending on age and activity level ↔How old they are and what activities they do. 预判的"年龄+活动量"两项，与 How old they are and what activities they do 一一对 齐，是最直接的同义替换。 C) 偷换概念 原文要讨论的是"理想蛋白摄入量"本身，选项 How much protein they consume and what their body weight is 反过来把"已经摄入多少蛋白"和"体重"作为考量因素，循 环定义且无文本依据；P6 提到 140-pound 只是举例上限，并非"决定理想摄入量的 因素"。 D) 与原文相反 选项 How serious their protein deficiency is and what remedies they use 默认存 在"protein deficiency"，但原文 P4 明确说美国医生从未见过蛋白缺乏患者，根本不存 在这样的前提。 哪些食物在一个多世纪以来基本上不受欢迎? A) 无糖零食。 B) 富含蛋白质的食物。 C) 红肉和白肉。 D) 含糖和高脂肪食物。

questions.q: What foods have been largely out of favor for more than a century?
options: Sugar-free snacks.
Protein-rich foods.
Both red and white meats.
Sugary and fatty foods.
questions.explain:
【判型】What foods have been largely out of favor for more than a century? 是事实型问句， 答案就在原文某句的事实陈述里。

【拆句】现在完成时 have been largely out of favor 表过去到现在的持续状态；largely 是程度副 词，表"在很大程度上"，提醒不要选"完全/彻底"等绝对化误读。

【定位】While fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns since over a century ago, protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite. 一个多世纪以来，脂肪和糖轮流挨批，而蛋白质却始终是我们的红人。 54. What foods have been largely out of favor for more than a century? A) Sugar-free snacks. B) Protein-rich foods. C) Both red and white meats. D) Sugary and fatty foods.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文 dietary spotlight firmly fixed on low-calorie, low-fat, sugar-free snack foods 说"无糖零食"是 1970-90 年代受追捧的对象，不是被嫌弃的对象；选项 Sugar-free snacks 把追捧对象当成 out of favor，颠倒立场。 B) 与原文相反 原文 protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite 明说蛋白质始终是 favorite（红人），选项 Protein-rich foods 反过来说它失宠，180 度反向。 C) 无中生有 原文 P7-P9 整段都在讲脂肪、糖和蛋白质这几类宏量营养素，从未提到"红肉/白肉"被批 的话题；选项 Both red and white meats 是凭健康常识填空。 D) ✓ 正确 fats and sugar ↔Sugary and fatty foods. taken the beating in turns since over a century ago ↔ largely out of favor for more than a century 预判"脂肪和糖被批了一百多年"，Sugary and fatty foods 对齐对象，题干本身对齐时 间与态度，三要素全合。 作者暗示发达国家的人们应该做什么来保持健康? A) 享用天然食物。 B) 吃素食。 C) 每天摄入足够的蛋白质。 D) 用蛋白质棒代替正餐。

questions.q: What does the author imply people in developed countries should do to keep healthy?
options: Enjoy natural food.
Eat vegetarian diets.
Consume enough protein daily.
Replace meals with protein bars.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author imply people in developed countries should do to keep healthy? 题干直接用 imply，是推断题的标准句式。

【拆句】句式较长但分层清晰：主干 What does the author imply X should do，宾语从句的主语 是 people in developed countries，目的状语 to keep healthy；抓住"作者+暗示+发达 国家民众+保持健康"四要素即可。 55. What does the author imply people in developed countries should do to keep healthy? A) Enjoy natural food. B) Eat vegetarian diets. C) Consume enough protein daily. D) Replace meals with protein bars.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 rich sources of antioxidants(抗氧化剂), vitamins and many other benefits of real food ↔ Enjoy natural food. When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on… ↔ Enjoy natural food. 预判作者推荐"回到真实食物"，Enjoy natural food 正是这条推断的最贴文表达，且不 超过一步推。 B) 过度推断 原文只说不要靠补剂代餐、要享受真实食物的好处，从未要求 vegetarian diets（素 食）；从"少吃加工补剂"推不到"完全吃素"，跨度过大。 C) 与原文相反 全文一直在反驳"应该多吃蛋白"的舆论，Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy of Medicine's recommended daily intake of protein 明示已 经摄入过量；选项 Consume enough protein daily 仍劝读者每天摄入足够蛋白，与作 者立场相反。 D) 与原文相反 尾段明确告诫 When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink, we also risk missing out on…——"代餐"被定性为风险行为；选项 Replace meals with protein bars 反过来把它当成建议，立场颠倒。

items.title: 2025年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable. Experts say too much happiness can stop the bears from searching for new mates.

P2 Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival by "reducing or fragmenting their natural: habitats", The Times reported. But the new research suggests that a "modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation" may actually help preserve panda populations.

P3 The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity.

P4 For their study—outlined in a paper in the journal Conservation Biology—the team looked at genetic diversity and spread among a Chinese panda population. The ideal level of perfectly livable habitat was found to be only 80% of an area, with the remainder either too harsh or too affected by human activity.

P5 The experts concluded that pandas should ideally "be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates".

P6 Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something. The concept has been applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering.

P7 Claudio Sillero, a professor of conservation biology at Oxford University, told the newspaper that the new findings could have implications beyond panda conservation.

P8 "Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes," said Sillero, who was not involved in the research. "It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence."

P9 The most recent count of pandas found that there were more than 1,800 left in the wild, putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species.

questions.q: What do we learn from new research about pandas?
options: They are losing habitat due to the building of roads and houses.
They have stopped seeking new mates for reproduction.
They may not adapt to the fragmentation of their habitat.
They may cease to exist as a result of enjoying too good a life.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from new research about pandas? 问 "new research" 直接告诉了我 们什么，是对研究结论原文的客观转述题。

【拆句】题干 Q46 是一个标准 wh- 问句：What 作 learn 的宾语，from new research 是来源状 语，about pandas 修饰 research，限定研究对象。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】New research suggests that pandas may be at risk of dying out because they are too comfortable. 新的研究表明，熊猫可能因为生活得太舒适而面临灭绝的风险。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 losing habitat due to the building of roads and houses 是 P2 中 environmentalists "long believed" 的旧观点，并非新研究的结论。 B) 过度推断 原文是 pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable——条件状语限定，They have stopped seeking new mates for reproduction. 删掉条件、把可能性说成全体熊猫已经停止寻偶，与原文不符。 C) 与原文相反 新研究主张栖息地适度碎片化反而"helps preserve"熊猫，They may not adapt to the fragmentation of their habitat. 反过来说熊猫不能适应碎片化，与原文相反。 D) ✓ 正确 may be at risk of dying out ↔may cease to exist because they are too comfortable ↔as a result of enjoying too good a life D 选项把"太舒适 → 可能灭绝"两层语义都对位地复述了一遍，与预判完全等值，可直接 锁定。 46. What do we learn from new research about pandas? A) They are losing habitat due to the building of roads and houses. B) They have stopped seeking new mates for reproduction. C) They may not adapt to the fragmentation of their habitat. D) They may cease to exist as a result of enjoying too good a life. 从Michigan State University科学家的新研究中我们可以得出什么结论? A) 环保主义者关于熊猫保护的长期观点可能具有误导性。 B) 熊猫栖息地附近的住宅开发可能威胁到它们的生存。 C) 熊猫的自然栖息地正变得越来越不适合繁殖。 D) 熊猫数量的增加归因于它们栖息地的破碎化。

questions.q: What can we conclude from the new research by scientists at Michigan State University?
options: Environmentalists' long-time belief regarding panda conservation may be misleading.
Housing development near pandas' homes may threaten their survival.
Pandas' natural habitats are becoming less suitable for reproduction.
The increased panda population is attributed to the fragmentation of their habitat.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we conclude from the new research 中的 conclude 是推断/结论类信号词， 要求在原文事实之上做一步合理推导。

【拆句】What can we conclude from the new research by scientists at Michigan State University? 中 by scientists at Michigan State University 是介词短语后置修饰 research，限定研究来源；主干 What can we conclude 即 "我们可以得出什么结论"，结 构简单。

【定位】The research was conducted by scientists from Michigan State University. It concluded that pandas fail to wander off in search of new mates if they find their habitat too comfortable, resulting in a lack of vital genetic diversity. 这项研究由密歇根州立大学的科学家们开展。研究得出结论：如果熊猫觉得栖息地太舒服， 它们就不会外出寻找新的配偶，从而导致缺乏关键的遗传多样性。 47. What can we conclude from the new research by scientists at Michigan State University? A) Environmentalists' long-time belief regarding panda conservation may be misleading. B) Housing development near pandas' homes may threaten their survival. C) Pandas' natural habitats are becoming less suitable for reproduction. D) The increased panda population is attributed to the fragmentation of their habitat.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Environmentalists have long believed that building roads or homes near the bears may threaten their survival ↔Environmentalists' long-time belief regarding panda conservation But the new research suggests that a modest degree of discomfort and fragmentation may actually help preserve panda populations. ↔may be misleading A 项正是把 P2 的"旧信念"与 P3 新研究的反向结论合在一起得出的合理推断，与预判完 全一致。 B) 张冠李戴 Housing development near pandas' homes may threaten their survival. 几乎是 P2 旧观点的原文转述，不是新研究的结论。 C) 无中生有 原文只说舒适让熊猫不愿外出找新伴，未说栖息地"不适合繁衍"；Pandas' natural habitats are becoming less suitable for reproduction. 是无中生有。 D) 与原文相反 原文是"栖息地碎片化"对熊猫"种群延续"有帮助，而非"碎片化使熊猫数量增加"。The increased panda population is attributed to the fragmentation of their habitat. 把 帮助保存说成数量增加，且因果说法不准确，与原文相反。 专家们关于熊猫的结论是什么? A) 为它们提供理想的栖息地以便繁衍生息是紧迫的。 B) 保护它们的遗传多样性非常重要。 C) 它们找到新配偶的机会与它们的栖息地有很大关系。 D) 它们的生存环境一直在持续恶化。

questions.q: What is the experts' conclusion regarding pandas?
options: It is urgent to provide an ideal habitat for them to thrive.
It is very important to preserve their genetic diversity.
Their chances of finding new mates have a lot to do with their habitat.
Their environment for survival has been continuously worsening.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the experts' conclusion regarding pandas? 问专家给出的明确结论，是对一段 原文的客观复述。

【拆句】What is the experts' conclusion regarding pandas? 中 regarding pandas 是介词短 语作 conclusion 的修饰语，相当于 about pandas，限定结论的对象；句子是简单系表 结构。

【定位】The experts concluded that pandas should ideally "be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates". 专家们得出结论：熊猫理想的状态应当是"既能开心地繁衍生息，又不至于舒服到不愿四处 走动去寻找新的配偶"。 48. What is the experts' conclusion regarding pandas? A) It is urgent to provide an ideal habitat for them to thrive. B) It is very important to preserve their genetic diversity. C) Their chances of finding new mates have a lot to do with their habitat. D) Their environment for survival has been continuously worsening.

【选项】A) 无中生有 P5 强调的是"恰好的舒适度"，不是"提供一个理想的栖息地刻不容缓"。It is urgent to provide an ideal habitat for them to thrive. 中 urgent 是原文未提的紧迫态度，且 ideal habitat 把原文复杂的"sweet spot"过度简化。 B) 张冠李戴 遗传多样性出现在 P3 是机制说明，不是 P5 专家结论的内容。It is very important to preserve their genetic diversity. 直接把别处的细节当作"专家结论"。 C) ✓ 正确 be happy enough to thrive, but not so content that they don't want to move around and find new mates ↔Their chances of finding new mates have a lot to do with their habitat. their habitat（隐含于 happy/content 之中——"舒适"是栖息地状态）↔their habitat C 用"栖息地与找新伴几率有关"概括了预判中的两层逻辑，且未做超出原文的推论，是 最贴的概括项。 D) 无中生有 原文只在 P2 提到旧观点中道路住宅可能威胁栖息地，但新研究并未说生存环境"持续在 恶化"。Their environment for survival has been continuously worsening. 是无中 生有。 从文章中我们可以推断出关于Goldilocks原则的什么信息? A) 它需要通过更多关于熊猫的研究来证实。 B) 它也适用于熊猫的保护。 C) 它对未来的熊猫研究具有启示意义。 D) 它可以用来定位熊猫的合适地点。

questions.q: What can we infer from the passage about the Goldilocks principle?
options: It needs to be confirmed by more studies on pandas.
It applies to the preservation of pandas too.
It has implications for future panda research.
It can be used to locate the right spot for pandas.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we infer from the passage 中 infer 是推断题的标志词，要求基于原文做一步合 理推导。

【拆句】What can we infer from the passage about the Goldilocks principle?：about the Goldilocks principle 是介词短语，作 infer 的宾语补足说明，相当于 "关于 Goldilocks 原 则"。结构无陷阱。

【定位】Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle: that there can be just the right amount of something. 他们关于《卫报》所说的这个"甜点位"的结论，与所谓的 Goldilocks 原则一致：即任何事 物都可以有一个恰到好处的量。 49. What can we infer from the passage about the Goldilocks principle? A) It needs to be confirmed by more studies on pandas. B) It applies to the preservation of pandas too. C) It has implications for future panda research. D) It can be used to locate the right spot for pandas.

【选项】A) 无中生有 It needs to be confirmed by more studies on pandas. 原文未提及；Goldilocks 原 则是"被沿用"的概念，不存在"还需进一步研究确认"的语义。 B) ✓ 正确 Their conclusions about what The Guardian described as this "sweet spot" are in line with the so-called Goldilocks principle ↔It applies to the preservation of pandas too. applied to a wide range of disciplines, from developmental psychology to economics and engineering ↔applies to … too B 用 applies to … too 精确表达了"该原则同样适用于熊猫保护"，是 in line with 一步 推出的合理结论。 C) 与原文相反 原文是熊猫研究印证了原则，不是原则对熊猫研究有启示。It has implications for future panda research. 把作用方向反着写。 D) 偷换概念 It can be used to locate the right spot for pandas. 把 sweet spot 误当成熊猫的地理 sweet spot；原文的 sweet spot 是"恰好的舒适程度"的比喻，不是物理位置。 根据Sillero教授的说法,新发现能够做什么? A) 有助于发现保护熊猫的新方法。 B) 有助于将熊猫从濒危物种名单中移除。 C) 为大多数大型食肉动物的保护提供启示。 D) 展示人类与动物之间互动的复杂性。

questions.q: What can the new findings do according to Professor Sillero?
options: Help discover new ways for the conservation of pandas.
Help remove pandas from the list of endangered species.
Shed light on the conservation of most large meat-eating animals.
Show the complexity of interactions between humans and animals.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can the new findings do according to Professor Sillero? 直接问 Sillero 教授的原 话，是对引语原文的客观转述。

【拆句】What can the new findings do according to Professor Sillero? 主干是 What can the new findings do，according to Professor Sillero 是介词短语作来源状语；句中 do 是实 义动词，被 What 提前作宾语。

【定位】It may well be that the messy nature of their relationship with human efforts induces more animals to scatter or travel further, and might result in greater genetic connectivity and enhanced population persistence. 很可能正是它们与人类活动这种"乱糟糟"的关系，促使更多动物分散、走得更远，从而带来 更强的遗传连通性，以及种群存续能力的提升。 50. What can the new findings do according to Professor Sillero? A) Help discover new ways for the conservation of pandas. B) Help remove pandas from the list of endangered species. C) Shed light on the conservation of most large meat-eating animals. D) Show the complexity of interactions between humans and animals.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Sillero 的话恰恰是说"超出熊猫保护"，Help discover new ways for the conservation of pandas. 把启示范围又拉回熊猫，与原文方向相反。 B) 张冠李戴 putting them on the list of vulnerable, but not endangered, species 只是说现状已 不在 endangered 名单，并非新发现的功效。Help remove pandas from the list of endangered species. 把背景数据当作新发现的功效。 C) ✓ 正确 implications beyond panda conservation ↔ Shed light on the conservation of most large meat-eating animals. Most large animals that eat meat live in increasingly fragmented landscapes ↔ most large meat-eating animals C 用 Shed light on + most large meat-eating animals 直接对应原文 implications beyond panda conservation + Most large animals that eat meat，与预判完全 一致。 D) 偷换概念 Sillero 强调 induces more animals to scatter or travel further，给出的是积极效益， 不是 Show the complexity of interactions between humans and animals. 那种中 性"展示复杂性"。

items.title: 2025年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. But what about those of us who don't have a natural talent? We've been told all our lives that if you work hard, you too can succeed. But with the release of Angela Duckworth's Grit, we are given a new key to success.

P2 "As much as talent counts, effort counts twice," says Duckworth in Grit. She introduces a new concept that talent may be overrated, and if you want real success, what you need is grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence. Even if you have natural talent, it's nothing without grit.

P3 Duckworth says grit is the difference between success and failure. A person who has grit is more likely to succeed than a person who does not. When we think about attaining success—whether it's landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part—and you must be perfect at all of them. Grit is different because it tells us that perfection isn't the goal.

P4 Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. Grit allows us to redefine our goals. Think about it: what's something you've always wanted to do, but gave up because you "don't have the skills for it"? What's something you love but aren't good at?

P5 The real workings of grit are to have sustainable passion and continue to try. Effort means more than your natural ability. Even if you haven't mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed if you can transform your passion into action. In a way, Duckworth is giving new hope to people who have shut the doors on their dreams. She is saying it is possible that you can accomplish anything. If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit.

questions.q: What does the passage say about people born with natural talents?
options: They seem to outdo others without hard work.
They appear to know all the secrets to success.
They feel it only too logical to succeed.
They are bound to excel effortlessly.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about people born with natural talents 直接问文章对一个 具体对象的陈述，没有 infer/imply/mainly about 这类字眼，是典型细节复述题。

【拆句】主干是 What does the passage say about people，过去分词短语 born with natural talents 作后置定语修饰 people，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What does the passage say about people born with natural talents? A) They seem to outdo others without hard work. B) They appear to know all the secrets to success. C) They feel it only too logical to succeed. D) They are bound to excel effortlessly.

【定位】With those born with natural talents, it feels as if they excel without really trying. 对于那些天生有才的人，看上去就好像他们不太费力就能出类拔萃。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 it feels as if they excel without really trying ↔ They seem to outdo others without hard work 预判的「看似/不费力/胜过别人」三个语义点在 A 中一一落位，无增项无漏项，A 是定 位句的同义改写。 B) 无中生有 原文只说他们看似不费力就出色，没说他们 know all the secrets to success——「掌 握所有成功秘诀」是凭空添加的内容。 C) 偷换概念 原文是「看上去毫不费力就成功」，选项却说 They feel it only too logical to succeed ——「他们觉得自己成功理所当然」是从他们的主观视角描写，与原文「旁观者眼中显 得轻松」不一致。 D) 过度推断 原文只用 it feels as if（似乎）表达印象，选项却用 are bound to（必然、注定）把可 能性写成必然性，过度推断。 Duckworth 对才能有何看法? A) 这是一个被过分高估的新概念。 B) 它被证明对于重大成就是必要的。 C) 它在一个人的成功中起较小的作用。 D) 它是人生真正成功的保证。

questions.q: What does Duckworth say about talent?
options: It is a new concept much too overrated.
It proves necessary for big achievements.
It plays a lesser role in one's success.
It is a guarantee for real success in life.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Duckworth say about talent 问的是特定人物对特定对象的陈述，是细节题。

【拆句】结构与 51 题平行：What does Duckworth say about talent，主谓宾完整，无修饰 从句。

【定位】As much as talent counts, effort counts twice. 虽然才能很重要，但努力的重要性是它的两倍。 52. What does Duckworth say about talent? A) It is a new concept much too overrated. B) It proves necessary for big achievements. C) It plays a lesser role in one's success. D) It is a guarantee for real success in life.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 It is a new concept much too overrated 把 She introduces a new concept 中「新 概念」的所指对象——其实是 grit——硬安到 talent 头上；原文说的「新概念」指 grit，而非 talent。 B) 与原文相反 原文反复说 talent 不够、需 grit 加持（Even if you have natural talent, it's nothing without grit）；选项却说 talent proves necessary for big achievements，是反向 陈述。 C) ✓ 正确 As much as talent counts, effort counts twice ↔It plays a lesser role in one's success talent may be overrated ↔plays a lesser role 预判的「才能不如努力重要、被高估」与 C 的「作用较小」在比较义上完全等值，C 正确。 D) 与原文相反 原文称 grit 才是 real success 的关键（if you want real success, what you need is grit），选项却说 talent is a guarantee for real success，把被弱化的对象说成「保 证」，方向与程度同时反了。 文章对想要获得成功的人有何评价? A) 他们困惑于如何向雇主展示自己最好的一面。 B) 他们被自己对完美的期望所困扰。 C) 他们会努力找到最适合自己技能的工作。 D) 他们会发现自己缺乏所需的所有技能。

questions.q: What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success?
options: They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer.
They are burdened by their expectation of perfection.
They will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best.
They will find themselves lacking in all the skills they need.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success 仍是 say 句 型，针对一个具体场景，是细节题。

【拆句】主干仍是 What does the passage say about people，现在分词短语 thinking of attaining success 作后置定语修饰 people；其中 attaining 是动名词作 of 的宾语，整体 「想着去获得成功的人」。 53. What does the passage say about people thinking of attaining success? A) They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer. B) They are burdened by their expectation of perfection. C) They will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best. D) They will find themselves lacking in all the skills they need.

【定位】When we think about attaining success—whether it's landing that job or learning that new skill—our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn. If you want that new job, you have to learn the job skills, then the interview skills, then the dress part—and you must be perfect at all of them. 当我们考虑获得成功时——不管是拿下那份工作还是学会某项新技能——我们的思绪立刻被 「必须先学会的所有东西」压得沉甸甸的。如果你想要那份新工作，你得学工作技能，然后 学面试技巧，再学穿衣得体——而且你必须在每一项上都做到完美。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 They are puzzled how to present their best to the employer 把原文里「找工作」举 例中的「dress part/interview skills」放大成全部困扰，且把 burdened 改成 puzzled ——既缩小到一例又改写状态词。 B) ✓ 正确 our thoughts are immediately burdened by all the things we must first learn ↔ They are burdened by their expectation of perfection 预判要求「负担 + 完美」两点齐备，B 正好同时命中——burdened 锁住「负担」， expectation of perfection 锁住「完美主义」。 C) 与原文相反 原文是「想成功的人感到被各种要求压垮」，选项却说他们 will try hard to land a job that fits their skills best——把焦虑负担改写成积极行动，方向反了。 D) 过度推断 原文说他们意识到要学很多东西，选项却说他们 lacking in all the skills they need ——把「要学的东西多」推到「所有技能都欠缺」，all 是绝对化程度词，原文未明说 欠缺。 作者认为毅力如何对我们有帮助? A) 它让我们知道自己擅长什么。 B) 它为我们打开了新机会的眼界。 C) 它使我们的注意力集中在所做的事情上。 D) 它让我们重新考虑要实现的目标。

questions.q: How does the author think grit can be helpful to us?
options: It allows us to know what we are good at.
It opens our eyes to new opportunities.
It focuses our attention on what we do.
It lets us reconsider the goals to achieve.
questions.explain:
【判型】How does the author think grit can be helpful to us 问的是 grit 的具体作用，不是隐含 推断，是细节题。

【拆句】How does the author think grit can be helpful to us 是宾语从句嵌套结构：think 后接 省略 that 的从句 grit can be helpful to us，how 修饰整个 think 的方式逻辑——实际问 的是「作者认为 grit 以何种方式有帮助」。 54. How does the author think grit can be helpful to us? A) It allows us to know what we are good at. B) It opens our eyes to new opportunities. C) It focuses our attention on what we do. D) It lets us reconsider the goals to achieve.

【定位】Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders. Grit tells us that the door is open wider than we first thought possible. Grit allows us to redefine our goals. grit 把不合理的期待从我们肩上卸下来。grit 告诉我们这扇门比我们最初以为的开得更宽。 grit 允许我们重新定义自己的目标。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文从未说 grit 让我们 know what we are good at（知道自己擅长什么）；P4 反而提 到「你一直想做但因『没技能』就放弃的事」，强调 grit 让你即便不擅长也去做，与 「让你知道擅长什么」无关。 B) 过度推断 原文比喻 the door is open wider than we first thought possible，意思是给我们的 可能性变多；选项 opens our eyes to new opportunities 把「门开宽」改成「让我们 看见新机会」——「打开眼界」是额外添加的动作，原文只说门更宽、未说我们因此看 见了新机会。 C) 无中生有 原文 Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders 是卸下「必须样样 完美」的负担，而非聚焦注意力；选项 focuses our attention on what we do 与「卸 担」无关，反而像「让你更专注」。 D) ✓ 正确 Grit allows us to redefine our goals ↔It lets us reconsider the goals to achieve let / reconsider / goals to achieve 三处都能在原文第三句找到一一对应，D 是 Grit allows us to redefine our goals 的同义改写。 Duckworth 在她的《坚毅》一书中试图传达什么信息? A) 我们应该完善自己以确保成功。 B) 我们应该即使面对失败也要坚持不懈。 C) 没有持续练习,我们永远无法掌握一项技能。 D) 没有热情,我们永远无法期望达到目标。

questions.q: What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit?
options: We should perfect ourselves to ensure success.
We should stay persistent even in face of failures.
We can never master a skill without constant practice.
We can never expect to reach our goals without passion.
questions.explain:
【判型】What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit 问的是整本书的核心信 息，是典型主旨题。

【拆句】What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit：宾语前置 What message，主干 Duckworth try to convey，介词短语 in her book Grit 作地点状语，无 难点。 55. What message does Duckworth try to convey in her book Grit? A) We should perfect ourselves to ensure success. B) We should stay persistent even in face of failures. C) We can never master a skill without constant practice. D) We can never expect to reach our goals without passion.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文反复说 perfection isn't the goal、Grit lifts the unreasonable expectations off our shoulders，明确否定完美主义；选项却让我们 perfect ourselves to ensure success，方向反了。 B) ✓ 正确 If at first you fail, then try one more time with grit ↔ We should stay persistent even in face of failures grit, the perfect combination of passion and persistence ↔stay persistent continue to try ↔stay persistent B 同时命中预判的两大语义点——「失败」和「坚持」，是把全文主线压缩到一句话的 最佳改写。 C) 以偏概全 Even if you haven't mastered a skill, grit tells you that you can still succeed 恰恰 说「没掌握技能也能成」；选项却把全书主旨说成 never master a skill without constant practice——把「关于 grit 的人生观」缩成「学技能要练习」，既偏题又用了 never 这种绝对化词。 D) 以偏概全 原文虽说 grit = passion + persistence，但全书主旨是「坚持着再试一次」，而非「没 激情就达不到目标」；选项 can never expect to reach our goals without passion 用 never 把 passion 描述为达成目标的「唯一条件」，把成对要素中的一个单独绝对化。

items.title: 2025年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 We all take a little extra effort to look nice for special occasions. But most of us have conflicting feelings about dressing up and feel guilty about taking the time to focus on clothes. Science now suggests the right dress may give ourselves the extra edge in our professional and personal lives.

P2 We hear sayings like "dress for the job you want; not the job you have". Most people don't really believe in them, but research into the impact of clothes on behavior now suggests that there may actually be a grain of truth in these sayings. Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing.

P3 We consider some clothes to be powerful, some to be fun, and so on. We even evaluate people whom we have just met based on their clothes. We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way they make us feel. This means that the experience of wearing something affects our attitudes and our choice of behavior.

P4 There's a reason tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'. It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business. Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance. This in turn helps us become better negotiators and abstract thinkers.

P5 While a good suit works wonders for our performance in the boardroom, wearing formal wear isn't a great idea when we want to socialize. Studies have found that people tend to be less open and less able to relax when they wear formal clothes.

P6 On the other hand, a casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative. These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday; since colleagues are most likely to take out time to socialize on the last work day of the week. I mean, who wants to hang out with people in their suits?

questions.q: What does science suggest the right dress may do?
options: Add to our advantage in work and life.
Enable us to look a lot more attractive.
Help us to enjoy a fuller personal life.
Provide extra energy for what we do.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does science suggest the right dress may do? 直接问 science 提出 dress 会 做什么，属于针对原文某句客观事实的复述。 46. What does science suggest the right dress may do? A) Add to our advantage in work and life. B) Enable us to look a lot more attractive. C) Help us to enjoy a fuller personal life. D) Provide extra energy for what we do.

【拆句】主干 What does science suggest the right dress may do? 是宾语从句嵌套：science 后 跟省略 that 的宾语从句 the right dress may do What；理解上把 What 还原到从句末 尾，即可看清问的是 dress 的功能/作用。

【定位】Science now suggests the right dress may give ourselves the extra edge in our professional and personal lives. 科学现在表明，穿对衣服可以在我们的职业与生活中给予我们额外的优势。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the extra edge ↔Add to our advantage in our professional and personal lives ↔in work and life 选项 Add to our advantage in work and life. 恰好覆盖「在职业与生活中增加优 势」，与预判完全吻合。 B) 偷换概念 原文谈的是 the extra edge（优势），选项 Enable us to look a lot more attractive. 把它换成了外貌吸引力，方向不同。 C) 以偏概全 原文同时强调 professional and personal lives 两方面，选项 Help us to enjoy a fuller personal life. 只保留 personal life，丢掉了职业一面。 D) 偷换概念 原文是 the extra edge（优势），选项 Provide extra energy for what we do. 把 edge 换成 energy（精力），属于熟词僻义误读。 科学研究为何认为一个人所穿的衣服可能会影响他们与他人的互动? A) 衣服通常代表一个人的社会和经济地位。 B) 衣服在很大程度上决定一个人是否受到周围人的喜爱。 C) 不同类型的服装明显反映出不同的个性。 D) 不同类型的服装象征性地传达不同的信息。

questions.q: Why does science say the clothes one wears may affect their interaction with others?
options: Clothes usually represent one's social and economic status.
Clothes largely determine one's likability by people around.
Different types of clothing markedly reflect different personalities.
Different types of clothing convey different messages symbolically.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why does science say the clothes one wears may affect their interaction with others? 问的是原因，原文应有 because/due to 等显式因果标志。

【拆句】主干为 Why does science say … ；say 后是省略 that 的宾语从句 the clothes one wears may affect their interaction with others，其中 one wears 是修饰 clothes 的省略关系代 词的定语从句，理解为「人们穿的衣服」。 47. Why does science say the clothes one wears may affect their interaction with others? A) Clothes usually represent one's social and economic status. B) Clothes largely determine one's likability by people around. C) Different types of clothing markedly reflect different personalities. D) Different types of clothing convey different messages symbolically.

【定位】Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing. 科学表明，我们所穿的衣服会影响我们的行为、情绪甚至我们与他人互动的方式，这是因为 我们赋予不同类型衣物的象征意义。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文从未提及 social and economic status，Clothes usually represent one's social and economic status. 是凭印象添加。 B) 偷换概念 原文谈的是衣服带来的象征意义影响互动，选项 Clothes largely determine one's likability by people around. 把它替换为「决定一个人受不受人喜欢」，并加重为 largely determine。 C) 偷换概念 原文说衣服传递象征意义，选项 Different types of clothing markedly reflect different personalities. 把它换成「反映性格」，personalities 是原文没有的概念。 D) ✓ 正确 the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing ↔ Different types of clothing convey different messages symbolically. assign ↔convey 选项 Different types of clothing convey different messages symbolically. 把原文因 果端逐一对应，是同义复述。 我们所穿的衣服如何影响我们对自己的评价? A) 通过对我们的判断力产生影响。 B) 通过影响我们对自己的感受。 C) 通过影响我们作为评估依据的内容。 D) 通过影响我们对象征性信息的解读。

questions.q: How do the clothes we wear sway our evaluation of ourselves?
options: By exerting an effect on our power of judgment.
By impacting how we feel about ourselves.
By affecting what we take as the basis for assessment.
By influencing our interpretation of symbolic messages.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 How do the clothes we wear sway our evaluation of ourselves? 问的是「通过什 么方式」，答案对应原文一句解释机制的话。

【拆句】题干主干 the clothes … sway our evaluation of ourselves；the clothes 后省略了 that， 跟着定语从句 we wear，整体读作「我们所穿的衣服如何影响我们对自己的评价」。 48. How do the clothes we wear sway our evaluation of ourselves? A) By exerting an effect on our power of judgment. B) By impacting how we feel about ourselves. C) By affecting what we take as the basis for assessment. D) By influencing our interpretation of symbolic messages.

【定位】We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way they make us feel. 我们也会基于所穿衣服来评价自己，因为衣服会影响我们的感受。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文 the way they make us feel 谈的是 feel（感受），选项 By exerting an effect on our power of judgment. 换成了 power of judgment（判断力），概念发生偏移。 B) ✓ 正确 the way they make us feel ↔how we feel about ourselves because of ↔By impacting 选项 By impacting how we feel about ourselves. 把原文 the way they make us feel 用 how we feel about ourselves 改写，完全贴合预判。 C) 答非所问 选项 By affecting what we take as the basis for assessment. 描述的是「影响我们用 什么作为评判依据」，等于反过来在说「clothes 改变了我们的评判标准」，可原文只说 clothes 让我们对自己有感受，再据此评价自己，并未谈「评判标准本身」。 D) 张冠李戴 symbolic messages 是第 2 段谈衣服影响互动的原因，选项 By influencing our interpretation of symbolic messages. 把它挪到了第 3 段评价自我的机制上，张冠 李戴。 作者为何说合身的西装外套与"为成功而着装"相关联? A) 它们是正式商务往来所必需的。 B) 它们可能帮助人们专注于自己的业务。 C) 它们对于在商务交易中保持主导地位至关重要。 D) 它们可能使人们拥有正确的经商心态。

questions.q: Why does the author say tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'?
options: They are necessary for formal business dealings.
They may help people concentrate on their business.
They are vital to keeping a dominant position in business transactions.
They may enable people to have the right mentality for doing business.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author say tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'? 问作者为何这么说，正是细节原因题的典型表述。

【拆句】主干 Why does the author say + 宾语从句 tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'；be associated with 是固定搭配「与……相关」，being 引导的动 名词短语作介词宾语，整体读作「为什么作者说西装外套与『为成功而着装』相关」。

【定位】There's a reason tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'. It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business. 西装外套之所以被认为与「为成功而着装」相关，是有原因的。看起来，穿正式办公着装会 让我们进入做生意的正确心理状态。 49. Why does the author say tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'? A) They are necessary for formal business dealings. B) They may help people concentrate on their business. C) They are vital to keeping a dominant position in business transactions. D) They may enable people to have the right mentality for doing business.

【选项】A) 过度推断 原文只说西装让人进入做生意心态，并未声称它是 necessary（必要条件），They are necessary for formal business dealings. 把「有帮助」拔高为「必备」。 B) 偷换概念 原文是 the right frame of mind（正确的心理状态），选项 They may help people concentrate on their business. 把它换成 concentrate（集中注意力），属于偷换。 C) 过度推断 原文 Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance. 是讲附加效果，选项 They are vital to keeping a dominant position in business transactions. 把它拔高为「对保持优势地 位至关重要」，既偏离了 Q49 问的「为何被称为 dressed for success」，又把程度上 拉到 vital。 D) ✓ 正确 puts us in the right frame of mind ↔enable people to have the right mentality to conduct business ↔for doing business 选项 They may enable people to have the right mentality for doing business. 把原 文「让我们处于做生意的正确心态」逐一对应，是同义复述。 当人们想要进行社交时,建议他们做什么? A) 注重服装。 B) 穿一套好西装。 C) 穿着随意。 D) 看起来与众不同。

questions.q: What are people advised to do when they want to socialize?
options: Focus on clothing.
Wear a good suit.
Dress casually.
Look unusual.
questions.explain:
【判型】What are people advised to do when they want to socialize? 询问具体建议行为，是典 型的细节复述。

【拆句】主干 What are people advised to do；when 引导时间状语从句 they want to socialize，整体读作「当人们想社交时，建议穿什么」。被动语态 are advised 隐含「文章 作者建议」。

【定位】On the other hand, a casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative. These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday; since colleagues are most likely to take out time to socialize on the last work day of the week. 另一方面，休闲着装能让我们变得更友好、更有创造力。这些发现支持周五穿商务休闲装的 做法，因为同事们最有可能在一周的最后一个工作日抽时间社交。 50. What are people advised to do when they want to socialize? A) Focus on clothing. B) Wear a good suit. C) Dress casually. D) Look unusual.

【选项】A) 答非所问 原文从未建议把注意力集中在「衣服」本身，Focus on clothing. 与「社交场合该穿什 么」毫无对应。 B) 与原文相反 原文明说 wearing formal wear isn't a great idea when we want to socialize，选项 Wear a good suit. 恰好建议穿西装，与原文方向相反。 C) ✓ 正确 a casual dress ↔Dress casually wearing formal wear isn't a great idea when we want to socialize ↔Dress casually 选项 Dress casually. 把 a casual dress 的建议浓缩为祈使句，完整对应原文。 D) 无中生有 原文从未提到「穿得与众不同」，Look unusual. 是凭空生造的建议。

items.title: 2025年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. Granted, you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive.

P2 The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic(交响乐的) orchestras have had on society's taste in music.

P3 A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas.

P4 Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans.

P5 Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.

questions.q: What does the author think of classical music and opera in today's world?
options: They still make their presence felt.
They have given way to electronic music.
They will not fade away from the public eye.
They are no longer relevant to teenagers' lives.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the author think of classical music and opera in today's world? 用 think of 直接问作者看法，对象又是全文核心话题，是典型的整体态度题。

【拆句】题干主干是 What does the author think of …，think of sth = 对某事物的看法；in today's world 是时间地点状语，限定评价的时间范围。结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。 51. What does the author think of classical music and opera in today's world? A) They still make their presence felt. B) They have given way to electronic music. C) They will not fade away from the public eye. D) They are no longer relevant to teenagers' lives.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 both opera and classical music are now still quite alive ↔They still make their presence felt 四个选项里只有 They still make their presence felt 与预判「仍有存在感」的肯定立场 吻合，其余三项要么表否定立场、要么改换主语。 B) 与原文相反 P1 只列举 pop music, jazz, and electronic music 作为崛起的对手，没说古典乐和歌 剧已 give way to（让位给）电子乐。 C) 无中生有 原文 started to fade away from the public eye 是已发生的事实，选项 They will not fade away from the public eye 把它改成对将来的否定预言，是无中生有的预言。 D) 以偏概全 you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon 只是承认青少年不常听，但作者用 Granted（诚然）让步后立刻 but 反转，重点 不在青少年身上。 关于当前制作的大部分流行音乐,我们了解到什么? A) 许多古典音乐爱好者可能难以欣赏它。 B) 它可以被视为古典音乐精致化的一个标志。 C) 它比古典音乐更微妙地迎合社会的音乐品味。 D) 它包含与某些古典音乐杰作相似的元素。

questions.q: What do we learn about much of the popular music currently produced?
options: It can be difficult for many classical music fans to appreciate.
It can be seen as an indicator of refinement on classical music.
It caters to society's taste in music in a more subtle way than classical music.
It contains elements similar to those in some masterpieces of classical music.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about much of the popular music currently produced? 是对某具体 对象的客观信息提问，不带 infer/imply，按细节题处理。

【拆句】much of the popular music currently produced 是名词短语：much of 限定范围（大部 分），currently produced 是过去分词短语作后置定语修饰 popular music = 当下被制作 出来的流行音乐。后置分词定语是四级长难句高频结构，识别它能避免把 produced 误读成 谓语。

【定位】The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. 古典乐在当今社会重要性的最显著标志是：当下被制作出来的大部分流行乐使用了与古典乐 一些最佳作品相似的节拍、和声与旋律。 52. What do we learn about much of the popular music currently produced? A) It can be difficult for many classical music fans to appreciate. B) It can be seen as an indicator of refinement on classical music. C) It caters to society's taste in music in a more subtle way than classical music. D) It contains elements similar to those in some masterpieces of classical music.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文说的是「不学乐理的人难以察觉这一现象」，没说流行乐让古典乐迷难以欣赏。 B) 过度推断 原文只说流行乐「使用相似要素」，并未称其是古典乐的 refinement（精炼/提升）。 C) 张冠李戴 原文是「交响乐对社会音乐品味的影响是 subtle 的」，主语是交响乐的影响、不是流 行乐。 D) ✓ 正确 uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works ↔It contains elements similar to those in some masterpieces of classical music 选项 D 把 similar 与 some of classical music's best works 都原样保留，仅把并列名 词上位为 elements，是定位句的标准同义替换。 作者为什么提到摇滚歌剧的发明? A) 为了说明如何用音乐讲述故事。 B) 为了给出歌剧最简单的定义。 C) 为了展示歌剧和古典音乐的相关性。 D) 为了证明在歌剧中使用管弦乐队的必要性。

questions.q: Why does the author mention the invention of the rock opera?
options: To illustrate how to tell a story using music.
To present the simplest definition of opera.
To show the relevance of opera and classical music.
To justify the necessity of using orchestras in opera.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why does the author mention the invention of the rock opera? 直接问举例的目 的，是例证目的题的最典型句式。

【拆句】题干主干 Why does the author mention X？X = the invention of the rock opera，of 短语作 the invention 的后置定语。结构简单，无陷阱。

【定位】A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. 歌剧与古典乐仍具相关性的一个更佳例证，可以从摇滚歌剧的发明中看出。 53. Why does the author mention the invention of the rock opera? A) To illustrate how to tell a story using music. B) To present the simplest definition of opera. C) To show the relevance of opera and classical music. D) To justify the necessity of using orchestras in opera.

【选项】A) 答非所问 Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form 只是为了 说明摇滚歌剧的合理性而插入的歌剧定义，不是举摇滚歌剧的目的。 B) 以偏概全 段中确实给了歌剧的最简定义，但那是为论证服务的工具，不是举摇滚歌剧的目的。 C) ✓ 正确 A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera ↔To show the relevance of opera and classical music 原文已把例子的服务对象 the relevance of opera and classical music 写在前置位置， 选项 C 用不定式 to show 把这个目的复述出来，是逐字命中。 D) 过度推断 原文只说 sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself ——是 sometimes（有时），不是 necessity（必要性）。 为什么古典音乐作品仍被用作现代电影的背景音乐? A) 电影制作人可选择的音乐类型很少。 B) 它们被认为是最具表现力的音乐类型。 C) 它们受到世界各地电影爱好者的好评。 D) 它们对于电影成为世界最受欢迎作品至关重要。

questions.q: Why are classical music pieces still used as background music in modern movies?
options: There are few types of music for movie producers to choose from.
They are considered to be the most expressive type of music.
They are well received by movie fans from all over the world.
They are essential for movies to become the world's greatest hits.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 Why are classical music pieces still used as background music in modern movies? 是对一个具体事实问原因，答案在原文有直接对应，按细节题处理。

【拆句】题干主干 Why are classical music pieces still used as background music ...？被动语态 are used，still 表「仍然」，in modern movies 是地点状语。识别 are used 是被动而非 主动是关键，能避免把题理解成「古典乐使用了什么」。

【定位】Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. 古典乐迷也会告诉你，没有多少类型的音乐比它更具表现力。所以，古典乐至今仍被用作现 代电影的背景音乐就一点也不意外了。 54. Why are classical music pieces still used as background music in modern movies? A) There are few types of music for movie producers to choose from. B) They are considered to be the most expressive type of music. C) They are well received by movie fans from all over the world. D) They are essential for movies to become the world's greatest hits.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文从未说「电影制作方可选的音乐类型很少」，only 谈古典乐自身的表现力强。 B) ✓ 正确 there are few types of music that are more expressive ↔ They are considered to be the most expressive type of music 题干问 why，定位句的 So 前那句被替换为最高级表达，正好回答原因；这是唯一与原 因句对应的选项。 C) 因果颠倒 原文 These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans 是讲电影 配乐的结果——观众接受——并未说这是它被选作配乐的原因。 D) 张冠李戴 Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas 谈的是摇滚歌剧 的成就，与电影配乐被使用的原因无关。 关于我们的现代音乐,我们了解到什么? A) 如果没有古典音乐和歌剧作为基础,它不可能产生。 B) 它在对当今社会的影响方面无法超越古典音乐和歌剧。 C) 它在音乐爱好者中不会像古典音乐和歌剧那样受欢迎。 D) 在未来几个世纪里,它在重要性上可能无法与古典音乐和歌剧匹敌。

questions.q: What do we learn about our modern music?
options: It could not have come into being without classical music and opera as its foundation.
It cannot outcompete classical music and opera in its impact on our current society.
It will not enjoy as much popularity as classical music and opera among music fans.
It might not be able to rival classical music and opera in importance for centuries to come.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about our modern music? 是对 modern music 的客观信息提问，按 细节题处理；但因对象是全文性概念，定位句多落在尾段总结。

【拆句】题干主干 What do we learn about our modern music？our modern music 是介词宾 语，about 引出谈论对象。结构简单，无陷阱。

【定位】Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. 古典乐与歌剧正是我们现代音乐所赖以建立的根基。 55. What do we learn about our modern music? A) It could not have come into being without classical music and opera as its foundation. B) It cannot outcompete classical music and opera in its impact on our current society. C) It will not enjoy as much popularity as classical music and opera among music fans. D) It might not be able to rival classical music and opera in importance for centuries to come.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon ↔ It could not have come into being without classical music and opera as its foundation 选项 A 用「否定 + without」的常见同义改写技法，把肯定陈述变成必要条件，逻辑完 全等价，是定位句标准的同义替换。 B) 无中生有 原文从未拿现代音乐和古典乐/歌剧比对社会影响力的高下，仅强调古典乐和歌剧仍 重要。 C) 偷换概念 原文谈的是「根基」与「重要性」，不是受欢迎程度（popularity）的比较。 D) 过度推断 原文 we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come 只是肯定古典乐和歌剧的持久重要，没有否定现代音乐重要性。

items.title: 2025年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 Our society places a high value on physical beauty. Americans spend an average of over $722 each year on their appearance. One in ten Americans has tried to look like a star.

P2 There's nothing wrong with trying to look our best, but excessive focus on physical appearance misses the soulful aspects of what it means to be beautiful. Trying to look like the magazine pictures can take us on a long ride away from what beauty is really about.

P3 Many of us spend far too much time, energy, and money trying to polish an image of what we think will bring attention, love, and connection. In the process, we may fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning.

P4 It may sound trite(老生常谈的), but beauty is only skin deep; it's not what brings love toward us. Just read about the latest Hollywood starlets whose seeming love turns into resentment and bitter court battles.

P5 Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing. We may develop a habit of being so focused on maintaining a perfect appearance that we never cultivate the inner qualities necessary to sustain and deepen intimacy and connection. As I describe in my book, The Authentic Heart, it is the courage to be authentic that connects us in a deeper way.

P6 While our initial attraction may be based, in part, on physical chemistry, it is the meeting of our inner worlds that creates the lasting intimacy and spiritual connection for which we long. If we redirect our attention toward cultivating inner qualities, we might find a magnetic attraction that moves us from something superficial to something that connects us to our depths.

P7 The path toward cultivating inner beauty is really simple. But what is simple is not always easy. Not everyone will see us and appreciate us as we take the courageous risk to allow ourselves to be seen as we really are. But if they don't, it is their loss, not ours. Eventually we'll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are.

questions.q: What do we learn about American society from the first paragraph?
options: It sees lots of personal income wasted on beauty products.
It considers one's physical appearance very important.
It places a high value on the physical fitness of stars.
It expects every individual to look their very best.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about American society from the first paragraph? 是 what...learn 型客观信息问答，且范围锁定首段，属于典型细节题。 46. What do we learn about American society from the first paragraph? A) It sees lots of personal income wasted on beauty products. B) It considers one's physical appearance very important. C) It places a high value on the physical fitness of stars. D) It expects every individual to look their very best.

【拆句】Q46 主干是 What do we learn about American society，from the first paragraph 是 状语限定信息来源；句子平铺直叙、无陷阱。

【定位】Our society places a high value on physical beauty. 我们的社会高度看重外貌。

【选项】A) 无中生有 It sees lots of personal income wasted on beauty products. 把 over $722 each year on their appearance 的客观花费篡改为 "被浪费"，原文从未做此评价。 B) ✓ 正确 places a high value on physical beauty ↔ considers one's physical appearance very important 预判 "美国社会把外貌看得很重要" 与 considers one's physical appearance very important 字面贴合，无需推断。 C) 偷换概念 places a high value on the physical fitness of stars 把 "看重外貌" 的主体悄悄换成 "明星的 physical fitness"；原文 One in ten Americans has tried to look like a star 只说有人想模仿明星，未谈明星本身的体魄。 D) 过度推断 It expects every individual to look their very best. 把 Our society places a high value on physical beauty 升级为 "要求每一个人都做到最好"，强度与范围都被拔高。 当人们努力让自己看起来更好时会发生什么? A) 他们必须为怨恨和激烈的法庭斗争做好准备。 B) 他们能够更好地获得关注、爱和人际联系。 C) 他们可能会忽视培养更重要的内在品质。 D) 他们觉得自己大量宝贵的时间、精力和资源被浪费了。

questions.q: What happens when people strive to look better?
options: They have to get prepared for resentment and bitter court battles.
They are better able to gain attention, love, and personal connection.
They may neglect to cultivate the inner qualities that matter more.
They feel much of their precious time, energy and resources is wasted.
questions.explain:
【判型】What happens when people strive to look better? 询问某动作引发的客观后果，是典型 的因果型细节题。

【拆句】Q47 主干 What happens 后接 when 引导的时间状语从句，提示发生条件；结构简单无 陷阱。 47. What happens when people strive to look better? A) They have to get prepared for resentment and bitter court battles. B) They are better able to gain attention, love, and personal connection. C) They may neglect to cultivate the inner qualities that matter more. D) They feel much of their precious time, energy and resources is wasted.

【定位】Many of us spend far too much time, energy, and money trying to polish an image of what we think will bring attention, love, and connection. In the process, we may fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning. 我们当中许多人花了过多的时间、精力和金钱去打磨一个我们以为会带来关注、爱与连结的 形象。在这个过程中，我们可能会忽略对自己的关照，错过本可带来更深亲密、满足与意义 的方式。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 They have to get prepared for resentment and bitter court battles. 把第 4 段说明 影星案例的 resentment and bitter court battles 强行移植到 Q47 的情境中，但原文 从未把这描述为追求外表的 "必然准备"。 B) 与原文相反 They are better able to gain attention, love, and personal connection. 把原文 what we think will bring attention, love, and connection 中 "我们以为会带来" 的主 观期待包装成客观事实，方向恰好与作者批评意图相反。 C) ✓ 正确 fail to attend to ourselves in a way that would move us toward deeper intimacy, fulfillment, and meaning ↔neglect to cultivate the inner qualities that matter more 预判 "疏于关照内在更要紧的部分" 几乎逐字对应 neglect to cultivate the inner qualities that matter more。 D) 偷换概念 They feel much of their precious time, energy and resources is wasted. 把作者对 time, energy, and money 的客观描述换成 "他们自己觉得被浪费"，主体变成 they feel；原文未提及当事人有此自觉。 作者对外在美有何看法? A) 它可能是遗传的或培养的。 B) 它可能导致坏习惯也可能导致好习惯。 C) 它可能创造联系也可能造成孤立。 D) 它可能带来的伤害和好处一样多。

questions.q: What does the author say about outer beauty?
options: It may be inherited or cultivated.
It may lead to bad as well as good habits.
It may create connection or isolation.
It may do as much harm as good.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about outer beauty? 询问作者就某概念的明确陈述，归入细 节题。

【拆句】Q48 主干 What does the author say，about outer beauty 是介词短语状语；无难句 结构。 48. What does the author say about outer beauty? A) It may be inherited or cultivated. B) It may lead to bad as well as good habits. C) It may create connection or isolation. D) It may do as much harm as good.

【定位】Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing. 外在美既可能是祝福，也同样可能是诅咒。

【选项】A) 无中生有 It may be inherited or cultivated. 谈外貌的来源（遗传/后天培养），原文从未讨论外 貌的获得方式。 B) 偷换概念 It may lead to bad as well as good habits. 把 Outer beauty can be as much of a curse as a blessing. 改成 "导致好坏习惯"，对象层面从 "对人生整体的祸福" 缩到 "习 惯"。原文确实提到 develop a habit，但说的是 "只关注外表的习惯"，并非 "好习惯/坏 习惯" 的对照。 C) 与原文相反 It may create connection or isolation. 称外貌可能创造 connection；但 P5 P6 都 说 connection 来自 inner qualities / meeting of inner worlds，外貌不直接创 造 connection。 D) ✓ 正确 as much of a curse as a blessing ↔do as much harm as good 预判 "坏处与好处一样多" 直接命中 do as much harm as good，无需推断。 是什么带来精神上的联系? A) 思想的交汇。 B) 一见钟情的吸引。 C) 身体上的化学反应。 D) 频繁的互动。

questions.q: What brings about spiritual connection?
options: Meeting of minds.
Attraction at first sight.
Physical chemistry.
Frequent interaction.
questions.explain:
【判型】What brings about spiritual connection? 询问导致某结果的原因，对应原文中一处明确 的因→果叙述。

【拆句】Q49 主干 What brings about spiritual connection，brings about=cause/lead to，是 一个三个单词的简单疑问句。

【定位】While our initial attraction may be based, in part, on physical chemistry, it is the meeting of our inner worlds that creates the lasting intimacy and spiritual connection for which we long. 虽然最初的吸引可能在一定程度上源于身体的化学反应，但真正创造我们所渴求的长久亲密 与精神连结的，是内在世界的相遇。 49. What brings about spiritual connection? A) Meeting of minds. B) Attraction at first sight. C) Physical chemistry. D) Frequent interaction.
