【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the meeting of our inner worlds ↔Meeting of minds. 预判 "内在世界相遇" 几乎逐字对应 Meeting of minds.。 B) 与原文相反 Attraction at first sight. 对应 our initial attraction，但原文明确说这只是 "in part" 的 初始吸引，并非 spiritual connection 的来源。 C) 与原文相反 Physical chemistry. 直接抓取 physical chemistry 这一原词，但原文用 While 让步结 构说明它只贡献 initial attraction，不是 spiritual connection 的来源。 D) 无中生有 Frequent interaction. 谈交往频率，原文从未提及 spiritual connection 来自频繁 互动。 当我们走上培养内在美的道路时会发生什么? A) 我们可能会找到通往他人灵魂的路径。 B) 我们可能会更被周围的人欣赏。 C) 我们会遇到那些因我们本来的样子而珍视我们的人。 D) 我们会被劝阻不要展现真实的自己。

questions.q: What happens when we take the path toward cultivating inner beauty?
options: We may find a route toward other people's souls.
We may be appreciated more by people around us.
We will meet people who value us for who we are.
We will be discouraged from revealing our true selves.
questions.explain:
【判型】What happens when we take the path toward cultivating inner beauty? 仍是 what happens when 的因果型问法，问的是文章对此动作所述的结果。

【拆句】Q50 主干 What happens，when 从句中 take the path toward cultivating inner beauty 用了介词短语作 path 的修饰，toward 后接动名词 cultivating，提示这是个比喻：把培养 内在美比作走一条路。

【定位】Eventually we'll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are. 最终我们会遇到那些欣赏真实的我们的契合灵魂。 50. What happens when we take the path toward cultivating inner beauty? A) We may find a route toward other people's souls. B) We may be appreciated more by people around us. C) We will meet people who value us for who we are. D) We will be discouraged from revealing our true selves.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 We may find a route toward other people's souls. 让 "我们走向别人的灵魂"；原文 P7 描述的是别人走向真实的我们，方向与重点都不一致。 B) 以偏概全 We may be appreciated more by people around us. 把 "被那些契合的人欣赏" 扩大 为 "被周围所有人更多地欣赏"；原文紧前一句明说 Not everyone will see us and appreciate us，恰好否定 "被周围人普遍更欣赏"。 C) ✓ 正确 Eventually we'll find those compatible souls who appreciate us as we are. ↔ We will meet people who value us for who we are. 预判 "最终遇到欣赏真实自我的人" 与 We will meet people who value us for who we are. 几乎逐字对应。 D) 与原文相反 We will be discouraged from revealing our true selves. 称我们会被打消展露真我的 念头；但原文 if they don't, it is their loss, not ours 是鼓励继续展露自我，与选项方向 相反。

items.title: 2025年6月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2025年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 Plant-based meats are coming soon to a dinner table near you, but do they deserve a spot on your plate? If you tried a vegetable burger years ago and dismissed it as rubbery and flavorless, it's a good time to give meatless meat another chance. Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat. Analysts don't expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge.

P2 Plant-based meats are no longer just for vegetarians. Companies such as Impossible Foods and Beyond Meat—the current superstars of the alternative protein sector—are pursuing consumers who enjoy meat but want to reduce their meat consumption for animal rights, health, or environmental reasons. So far, it's a winning strategy: More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat.

P3 Many vegetarians don't actually care for food that resembles meat. When reporter Joan Solsman, a longtime vegetarian, tried a dish from Impossible Foods, she felt so sick that she couldn't finish it. "Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn't stand to take another bite," she wrote.

P4 Meatless meats are generally a healthier choice than beef because they are cholesterol-free, plus they're a good source of vitamins, minerals, protein, and fiber.

P5 If meatless meat can help you stick to a plant-based diet, that in itself can lead to better health. Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels.

P6 However, just because it's plant-based doesn't mean it's health food. Most imitation meats are highly processed and contain high amounts of sodium(钠) compared to traditional beef.

P7 These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don't forget about whole grains and vegetables. Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute. They're nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today.

questions.q: What can we expect of plant-based meats?
options: An increasing interest in their analyses.
An enormous effort in their promotion.
A huge boost in their consumption.
A noticeable surge in their varieties.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we expect of plant-based meats? 没有出现 infer/imply/suggest，问的是一 个文中已表述的预期结果，属于事实细节题。 51. What can we expect of plant-based meats? A) An increasing interest in their analyses. B) An enormous effort in their promotion. C) A huge boost in their consumption. D) A noticeable surge in their varieties.

【拆句】What can we expect of plant-based meats? 结构是 expect sth of sb/sth（对……抱有什 么期待/预期），of 后接被期待的对象。考生熟悉的 expect sth from sb 在此处换成 of， 含义相近，不必紧张。

【定位】Analysts don't expect the meat-free movement to slow anytime soon; a 2021 report predicts the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge. 分析师们不预期植物肉浪潮短期内会放缓；一份 2021 年的报告预测，到 2030 年该市场将 猛增至 740 亿美元——增幅高达 957%。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 An increasing interest in their analyses 把原文里「分析师们的预期」偷换成「对它们 分析的兴趣增长」，文章并未说人们对植物肉的分析研究兴趣上升。 B) 无中生有 An enormous effort in their promotion 谈的是「推广上的巨大努力」，原文只说市 场规模会增长，没提企业或政府投入推广，属无中生有。 C) ✓ 正确 the market will skyrocket to $74 billion by 2030—a 957 percent surge ↔ A huge boost in their consumption 预判要的是「消费规模大增」，A huge boost in their consumption 正是这个语义， 锁定 C。 D) 偷换概念 A noticeable surge in their varieties 把 surge 的对象从原文的「市场规模」换成「种 类」，原文仅提到 Newer varieties imitate the look, flavor, and texture of meat，说 新品种已出现，但没说种类会激增。 关于购买Beyond Burger和Impossible Foods产品的消费者,我们了解到什么? A) 他们大多不是素食者。 B) 他们大多是动物权利倡导者。 C) 他们中的大多数出于健康原因不吃肉。 D) 他们中的大多数吃无肉肉类是为了保护环境。

questions.q: What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products?
options: They are mostly non-vegetarians.
They are mostly animal-rights advocates.
Most of them refrain from eating meat for health reasons.
Most of them eat meatless meat to protect the environment.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products? 是 learn about + 名词结构，问关于该人群在原文中已写明的属性。

【拆句】What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products? 主干 What do we learn about consumers，buying ... 是后置的现在分词短语 作 consumers 的定语，相当于 who buy ...，结构无陷阱。 52. What do we learn about consumers buying Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products? A) They are mostly non-vegetarians. B) They are mostly animal-rights advocates. C) Most of them refrain from eating meat for health reasons. D) Most of them eat meatless meat to protect the environment.

【定位】More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat. 在购买 Beyond Burger 和 Impossible Foods 产品的消费者中，有超过十分之九的人同时 也吃肉。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 More than nine out of ten consumers who buy Beyond Burger and Impossible Foods products also eat meat ↔They are mostly non-vegetarians 预判说的「多数也吃肉」正对应「多数非素食者」，A 命中。 B) 以偏概全 They are mostly animal-rights advocates 把动物权利说成消费者的主要身份，但原文 animal rights, health, or environmental reasons 是并列的三类动机之一，没有说大多 数是动物权利倡导者。 C) 以偏概全 Most of them refrain from eating meat for health reasons 同样把并列三动机里的 「健康」拎出来说大多数，且 refrain from eating meat（克制吃肉）与原文 reduce their meat consumption 程度被夸大。 D) 以偏概全 Most of them eat meatless meat to protect the environment 同样犯「三选一拎为 主因」的错误，无原文比例支撑。 从Joan Solsman的评论中,我们可以对Impossible Foods的产品得出什么结论? A) 它们更常吸引肉食者。 B) 它们非常像动物肉。 C) 有些已成为其招牌菜。 D) 它们大多作为真正的假肉出售。

questions.q: What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's remark?
options: They more often appeal to meat-eaters.
They very much resemble animal meat.
Some have become its signature dishes.
Most of them are sold as true fake meat.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's remark? 中 conclude from ... remark 表示要从她的话里推出关于产品的判断。

【拆句】What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's remark? 主干 What can we conclude about X from Y，about 引出推断对象（产品）， from 引出推断依据（她的话）；这是固定结构。 53. What can we conclude about Impossible Foods' products from Joan Solsman's remark? A) They more often appeal to meat-eaters. B) They very much resemble animal meat. C) Some have become its signature dishes. D) Most of them are sold as true fake meat.

【定位】Maybe the best sign that Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat is that I couldn't stand to take another bite. 或许 Impossible Foods 成功破解「逼真假肉」密码的最有力信号，就是连我（这个素食 者）都没法再吃一口。

【选项】A) 答非所问 题目要求从她的话推断 Impossible Foods 的「产品本身」特性，They more often appeal to meat-eaters 说的是「产品更受肉食者欢迎」，那是 Q52 答案，不是 Q53 的推断方向。 B) ✓ 正确 Impossible Foods has cracked the code to realistic fake meat ↔ They very much resemble animal meat 预判要的是「产品逼真像真肉」，They very much resemble animal meat 直接对应， 锁 B。 C) 无中生有 Some have become its signature dishes 说这些菜成了「招牌菜」，原文只说她试吃 了 a dish from Impossible Foods，并未说哪些是招牌。 D) 偷换概念 Most of them are sold as true fake meat 把 realistic fake meat（逼真的假肉）改成 sold as true fake meat（作为「真假肉」出售），不仅商业化（销售行为）是原文没有 的，true 修饰 fake meat 的逻辑也与「产品像真肉」相违。 为什么植物基饮食习惯能带来更好的健康? A) 它使人们摆脱任何已知的癌症关联。 B) 它提供保持健康所需的全部营养。 C) 它有助于维持正常的血压和血糖。 D) 它降低肉类消费带来的各种健康风险。

questions.q: Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health?
options: It frees people from any known link to cancer.
It provides all the nutrients for staying healthy.
It helps maintain normal blood pressure and blood sugar.
It reduces various health risks posed by meat consumption.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health? 用 Why 提问， 原文有明确因果链时仍属细节题。

【拆句】Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health? 中主语是 the habit of doing sth（做某事的习惯）这个抽象名词短语，谓语 lead to 表示导致，结构平 铺直叙，无陷阱。 54. Why can the habit of eating a plant-based diet lead to better health? A) It frees people from any known link to cancer. B) It provides all the nutrients for staying healthy. C) It helps maintain normal blood pressure and blood sugar. D) It reduces various health risks posed by meat consumption.

【定位】Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels. 不仅红肉被发现与癌症相关，研究还显示放弃吃肉的人血压更低、平均血糖更低、胆固醇水 平也更低。

【选项】A) 过度推断 It frees people from any known link to cancer 中 frees ... from any known link 表 示「完全免除任何已知关联」，但原文只说红肉与癌症「被发现相关」（red meat been linked to cancer），并未说弃肉就能彻底斩断所有癌症关联。 B) 过度推断 It provides all the nutrients for staying healthy 说植物饮食提供「所有保持健康所需 的营养」，P4 只列了维生素、矿物质、蛋白质、纤维四项，没说「全部」。 C) 以偏概全 It helps maintain normal blood pressure and blood sugar 只提血压和血糖，漏了胆 固醇和癌症，且 maintain normal 意为「维持正常」，比 lower 表达的「降低」程度 还弱。 D) ✓ 正确 Not only has red meat been linked to cancer, but studies show that people who ditch meat have lower blood pressure, lower average blood sugar, and lower cholesterol levels. ↔It reduces various health risks posed by meat consumption 预判要「综合性下降」，D 的 various health risks 正好覆盖了四种风险，是唯一概 括项。 作者在文章结尾建议我们吃什么? A) 天然生产的食物。 B) 加工蛋白质替代品。 C) 传统牛肉之类的红肉。 D) 新一代替代肉类。

questions.q: What does the author recommend we eat at the end of the passage?
options: Naturally produced foods.
Processed protein substitutes.
Red meats like traditional beef.
New generations of alternate meat.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author recommend we eat at the end of the passage? 位置写死、动作 写死，只问被推荐的事物，不涉及推断。

【拆句】What does the author recommend we eat at the end of the passage? 中 recommend (that) we eat 省略 that，we eat 是宾语从句；at the end of the passage 是位置状语， 结构无陷阱。 55. What does the author recommend we eat at the end of the passage? A) Naturally produced foods. B) Processed protein substitutes. C) Red meats like traditional beef. D) New generations of alternate meat.

【定位】These new generations of alternate meat get all the attention, but don't forget about whole grains and vegetables. Beans are an especially excellent protein substitute. They're nutritious, inexpensive, and far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes on the market today. 这些新一代的肉类替代品备受关注，但不要忘了全谷物和蔬菜。豆类是格外出色的蛋白替代 品。它们营养丰富、价格便宜，可持续性远胜于今天市面上任何加工过的植物肉替代品。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 whole grains and vegetables ↔Naturally produced foods far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes ↔ Naturally produced foods 预判要「天然食物」，Naturally produced foods 同时覆盖三类推荐对象的共同属性， 是唯一合适项。 B) 与原文相反 Processed protein substitutes 说的正是作者要反对的加工蛋白替代品，far more sustainable than any of the processed meatless substitutes 明确把这类产品当对 照面。 C) 与原文相反 Red meats like traditional beef 是全文反复劝退的对象（red meat been linked to cancer），作者绝不会在结尾推荐它。 D) 与原文相反 New generations of alternate meat 与 These new generations of alternate meat 原词复现，但原文用 but 转折表示「它们抢了风头但作者另有所荐」，并非推荐对象。

items.title: 2025年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 All living organisms on Earth are exposed to a 24-hour day-night cycle. This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day. Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health. For example, eating at night can lead to weight gain over time because food intake at night leads to increased fat storage.

P2 Many drug targets in the body follow a 24-hour cycle, too. This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period. Because how the body responds to a drug can differ depending on the time it is taken, it logically follows that taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects.

P3 When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it. There are two main reasons for that oversight. First, many physicians are not aware that some drugs work better during a specific time of the day. And second, most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle. Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance.

P4 Over 50 years ago, researchers found that the cholesterol drug simvastatin is more effective at lowering cholesterol levels when taken at night rather than during the day. This is because the liver enzyme(酶) these drugs target is more active at night.

P5 Taking medicine at the wrong time can even cause harm. My colleagues and I wondered whether midazolam, the most common sedative(镇静剂) used in surgical procedures worldwide, might interfere with the internal clock that protects the heart at night. Currently, there are no guidelines regarding when midazolam should be administered.

P6 More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases. I believe taking drug timing into account could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide.

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about the timing of our behaviors?
options: It has a considerable impact on our health.
It confines us to a 24-hour day-night cycle.
It requires us to follow a particular rhythm.
It holds the key to all human body functions.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about ... 问的是文章就「行为时机」明说了什么， 答案应能在原文直接找到对应句，不需推断。 46. What do we learn from the passage about the timing of our behaviors? A) It has a considerable impact on our health. B) It confines us to a 24-hour day-night cycle. C) It requires us to follow a particular rhythm. D) It holds the key to all human body functions.

【拆句】题干 What do we learn from the passage about the timing of our behaviors? 是一个 what 引导的特殊疑问句，主干是「我们从文中得知什么」，about 短语把范围锁定在「我 们行为的时机」上。结构平铺直叙，无从句、无否定，唯一要抓的是 about 后面的话题 词，它指明这道题只问「行为时机」相关的内容。

【定位】Consequently, all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm, and the timing of behaviors like exercise or food intake can significantly influence your health. 因此，人体的所有功能也都遵循这一日常节律，而锻炼、进食等行为的时机会显著影响你的 健康。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 can significantly influence your health ↔It has a considerable impact on our health 预判「行为时机大大影响健康」与 It has a considerable impact on our health 完全吻 合，故锁定该项。 B) 偷换概念 原文是「昼夜周期导致行为有节律」，It confines us to a 24-hour day-night cycle 却 说「行为时机把我们限制在 24 小时周期里」，把因当成了果，与原文 This cycle is the reason why people rest at night and are active during the day 相悖。 C) 张冠李戴 It requires us to follow a particular rhythm 说「行为时机要求我们遵循某节律」，但 原文里「遵循节律」的主体是人体功能（all human body functions also follow this daily rhythm），并非由「行为时机」提出要求。 D) 过度推断 It holds the key to all human body functions 称行为时机「掌握着人体所有功能的关 键」，原文只说人体功能遵循节律、行为时机影响健康，从未说时机决定一切功能，all 与 holds the key 属夸大。 作者关于我们体内的蛋白质说了什么? A) 它们能以不同方式改变药物的效果。 B) 它们能减少某些药物不想要的副作用。 C) 它们对药物的反应在昼夜周期中会发生变化。 D) 它们的设计决定了它们对药物反应的不同方式。

questions.q: What does the author say about the proteins in our body?
options: They can modify the effects of medicines in different ways.
They can reduce unwanted side effects of certain medicines.
Their reaction to medicines changes during the day-night cycle.
Their design determines how differently they react to medicines.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author say about the proteins 问作者对蛋白质的明确陈述，答案落在讲 蛋白质的那句话里，属客观查找而非推断。 47. What does the author say about the proteins in our body? A) They can modify the effects of medicines in different ways. B) They can reduce unwanted side effects of certain medicines. C) Their reaction to medicines changes during the day-night cycle. D) Their design determines how differently they react to medicines.

【拆句】题干 What does the author say about the proteins in our body? 主干是「作者关于我 们体内的蛋白质说了什么」，say about 后面的 the proteins in our body 是话题。注意四 个选项都是完整句子，需要逐个判断哪句和原文一致，题干本身无陷阱。

【定位】This means that the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period. 这意味着，药物所要作用的那些特定蛋白质，在 24 小时的进程中对药物的反应可能各不 相同。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 They can modify the effects of medicines in different ways 说「蛋白质改变药物的 效果」，但原文是药物去作用（modify）蛋白质（the specific proteins a drug is designed to modify），施受关系正好相反。 B) 张冠李戴 They can reduce unwanted side effects of certain medicines 把「减少副作用」说 成蛋白质的能力，可原文里减副作用的是「按特定时间服药」这一做法（taking medicines at specific times could help increase their effectiveness and reduce unwanted side effects），与蛋白质无关。 C) ✓ 正确 can react differently to the medicine over the course of a 24-hour time period ↔ Their reaction to medicines changes during the day-night cycle 预判「蛋白质对药反应随时段变化」正是 Their reaction to medicines changes during the day-night cycle 所述，锁定该项。 D) 无中生有 Their design determines how differently they react to medicines 称「蛋白质的 设计决定其反应差异」，原文从未谈蛋白质有何 design，更没说设计决定反应，纯属 臆造。 医生在为人们开药时会做什么? A) 他们很少考虑服药时间以达到最大效果。 B) 他们很少考虑哪种药物对哪个患者更有效。 C) 他们告诉患者药物在24小时内可能产生的副作用。 D) 他们告诉患者遵守药品生产商的说明。

questions.q: What do doctors do when prescribing medicine for people?
options: They give little thought to the time of taking it for maximum effect.
They rarely consider which medicine works better for which patient.
They tell patients its possible side effects during a period of 24 hours.
They tell patients to comply with the directions of drug manufacturers.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do doctors do when prescribing medicine 问医生实际做了什么，是可在原文直接 核对的事实。 48. What do doctors do when prescribing medicine for people? A) They give little thought to the time of taking it for maximum effect. B) They rarely consider which medicine works better for which patient. C) They tell patients its possible side effects during a period of 24 hours. D) They tell patients to comply with the directions of drug manufacturers.

【拆句】题干 What do doctors do when prescribing medicine for people? 主干「医生开药时做 什么」，when prescribing 是时间状语（现在分词作状语，相当于 when they prescribe）。结构清晰，关键是抓 doctors 与 prescribing 这一动作场景。

【定位】When doctors prescribe medicine for people, they rarely consider the best time to take it. 医生给人们开药时，很少考虑服药的最佳时间。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 they rarely consider the best time to take it ↔ They give little thought to the time of taking it for maximum effect 预判「医生很少考虑最佳服药时间」与 They give little thought to the time of taking it for maximum effect 一致，锁定该项。 B) 偷换概念 They rarely consider which medicine works better for which patient 把疏忽的对象 换成「哪种药对哪个病人更好」，而原文疏忽的是服药「时间」，话题被悄悄换掉。 C) 偷换概念 They tell patients its possible side effects during a period of 24 hours 说医生告知 24 小时内的副作用，原文讲的是药物未被研究其昼夜差异（most drugs have not been studied for possible different effects during a 24-hour cycle），并非医生告 知副作用。 D) 偷换概念 They tell patients to comply with the directions of drug manufacturers 说让病人遵 从药厂说明，但原文 compliance 指病人遵从医嘱按时服药（patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance），并未提 drug manufacturers。 为什么医生建议患者在早上或晚上服用大多数药物? A) 为了阻止他们提出投诉。 B) 为了确保他们按照指示服药。 C) 为了严格遵守新的研究发现。 D) 为了保证药物的最大效果。

questions.q: Why do doctors advise patients to take most drugs in the morning or in the evening?
options: To discourage them from making complaints.
To ensure they take the drugs as instructed.
To comply with new research findings strictly.
To guarantee the maximum effect of the drugs.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why do doctors advise ... 问的是原文已经给出的理由，定位到目的状语即可作答，不需自 己推因果。 49. Why do doctors advise patients to take most drugs in the morning or in the evening? A) To discourage them from making complaints. B) To ensure they take the drugs as instructed. C) To comply with new research findings strictly. D) To guarantee the maximum effect of the drugs.

【拆句】题干 Why do doctors advise patients to take most drugs in the morning or in the evening? 是 why 引导的因果问句，主干「医生为何建议病人在早上或晚上服大多数药」。 advise sb. to do 是「建议某人做某事」结构。问 why 意味着答案是原文里这一建议背后的 目的或原因。

【定位】Therefore, patients are directed to take most drugs during the morning or evening primarily to ensure compliance. 因此，病人被指示在早上或晚上服用大多数药物，主要是为了确保遵医服药。

【选项】A) 无中生有 To discourage them from making complaints 说目的是「阻止病人投诉」，原文目的 只有 ensure compliance，从未提 complaints，凭空捏造。 B) ✓ 正确 to ensure compliance ↔To ensure they take the drugs as instructed 预判「为确保病人按医嘱服药」与 To ensure they take the drugs as instructed 同 义，锁定该项。 C) 与原文相反 To comply with new research findings strictly 说目的是严格遵循新研究成果，但原文 恰恰指出多数药未做昼夜研究（most drugs have not been studied），医生让早晚服 药并非依据研究，方向相反。 D) 与原文相反 To guarantee the maximum effect of the drugs 说目的是保证药效最大，但全文论点 正是医生没考虑增效时机（they rarely consider the best time to take it），早晚服药 并非为了药效最大化，正好相反。 作者在文章结尾处建议了什么? A) 在为患者开药时考虑服药时机。 B) 通过将服药时机纳入考虑使治疗变得不那么复杂。 C) 开展更多研究以找出治疗不同疾病的最佳时机。 D) 通过进一步研究找出治疗疾病最有效的药物。

questions.q: What does the author suggest near the end of the passage?
options: Considering drug-taking timing when prescribing drugs for patients.
Making treatments less complex by taking drug timing into account.
Conducting more studies to find out the best timing for treating different diseases.
Finding out the most effective drugs for treating diseases through further research.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the author suggest near the end 问作者在收尾处的整体主张，需要把末段的 呼吁概括出来，而非抓某个孤立细节。

【拆句】题干 What does the author suggest near the end of the passage? 主干「作者在文章接 近结尾处建议了什么」，suggest 在此是「建议、主张」，near the end of the passage 是地点状语，明确把答案锁在文章末段。这是一道带位置提示的建议题。 50. What does the author suggest near the end of the passage? A) Considering drug-taking timing when prescribing drugs for patients. B) Making treatments less complex by taking drug timing into account. C) Conducting more studies to find out the best timing for treating different diseases. D) Finding out the most effective drugs for treating diseases through further research.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 Considering drug-taking timing when prescribing drugs for patients 是第三段对 医生开药的观点延伸，而题干问的是 near the end 的建议；末段真正的呼吁是「做更多 研究」，而非这条局部主张。 B) 无中生有 Making treatments less complex by taking drug timing into account 称考虑服 药时机可让治疗「不那么复杂」，原文末段只说能让治疗更有效、惠及更多人（could help make treatments more effective and help more people worldwide），从未提 less complex。 C) ✓ 正确 More research is needed to determine the best times to administer treatments for different diseases ↔Conducting more studies to find out the best timing for treating different diseases 预判「需更多研究找最佳给药时机」与 Conducting more studies to find out the best timing for treating different diseases 完全对应，锁定该项。 D) 偷换概念 Finding out the most effective drugs for treating diseases through further research 说要研究「最有效的药物」，可末段研究的目标是「最佳给药时间」（the best times to administer treatments），全文谈的是时机而非药物本身，对象被 偷换。

items.title: 2025年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Katharine Abraham, an economics professor, was chatting with her hairdresser(理发师) about retirement plans. The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money.

P2 Both scenarios(情况) are contributing to a big increase in the number of people in the U.S. working into their 70s. Over the past 20 years, the share of Americans working in their 70s has risen from less than 10% to nearly 15%.

P3 In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement. The decline of manufacturing and the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations also has contributed to the trend, says Abraham, who researches work and retirement decisions of older Americans.

P4 "Which matters more depends on what your history up until that point has been in the type of work you're doing," Abraham says.

P5 The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%.

P6 Martin Neil Baily, an economist who is leading a research project on retirement security, notes that quitting a career can lead to feelings of isolation and loneliness, particularly for men. He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons. They're also more likely to be in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more.

P7 Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons.

questions.q: What do we learn from the passage about the economics professor and her hairdresser?
options: They differ in their reasons for continuing to work.
They are both committed to working into their 70s.
They are happy about their current financial situation.
They hold different views about postponing retirement.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What do we learn from the passage about the economics professor and her hairdresser 锁定两位具体人物，要在原文里抓他们各自的具体说法，属于事实型细节题。 51. What do we learn from the passage about the economics professor and her hairdresser? A) They differ in their reasons for continuing to work. B) They are both committed to working into their 70s. C) They are happy about their current financial situation. D) They hold different views about postponing retirement.

【拆句】句子主干是 What do we learn from the passage about ...，about 引出涉及的对象；并 列结构 the economics professor and her hairdresser 由 and 连接两个名词短语，无从 句、无否定，结构平直无陷阱。

【定位】The economist said she plans to continue working because she wants to. The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason: She needs the money. 经济学家说她打算继续工作，因为她想这样做。理发师也同意继续工作，但理由不同：她需 要钱。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 The hairdresser agreed but for a different reason ↔ They differ in their reasons for continuing to work 预判强调 "两人继续工作的理由不同"，A 项 They differ in their reasons for continuing to work 恰好对此点 100% 命中，无引申无超纲，可直接锁定。 B) 答非所问 B 项 They are both committed to working into their 70s 把题目焦点偏到 "是否都坚 持工作到 70 多岁"，但题目问的是 "对照两人有何不同"，不是问共同点。 C) 无中生有 C 项 They are happy about their current financial situation 说两人都对当前财务状 况满意，但理发师明确说 She needs the money，怎么也谈不上 happy。 D) 偷换概念 D 项 They hold different views about postponing retirement 似乎与 A 相近，但 different views about postponing retirement 意为 "在是否推迟退休这件事上观点不 同"，而原文里两人都决定继续工作，差异在理由而不在观点。 人们推迟退休的原因之一是什么? A) 越来越多的人转向了智力挑战性较低的工作。 B) 私营部门适合老年人的工作岗位数量增加了。 C) 多年来,按购买力计算的工资增长率有所放缓。 D) 职场中越来越多的人发现难以依靠传统养老金。

questions.q: What is one of the reasons for people to delay retirement?
options: More and more people have switched to less intellectually challenging jobs.
The number of jobs suitable for older people has increased in the private sector.
The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years.
More and more people in the workplace find it hard to rely on traditional pensions.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is one of the reasons for people to delay retirement 询问具体原因，要在原 文清单里点对清单项，属典型细节题。

【拆句】主干 What is one of the reasons，后接介词短语 for people to delay retirement 作后置 定语；for 引导原因方向，不定式 to delay 表逻辑动作，结构清晰，无难点。 52. What is one of the reasons for people to delay retirement? A) More and more people have switched to less intellectually challenging jobs. B) The number of jobs suitable for older people has increased in the private sector. C) The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years. D) More and more people in the workplace find it hard to rely on traditional pensions.

【定位】In addition to people being healthier and living much longer, economists say that a combination of financial considerations such as years of slow rise in real wages and a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector are some of the reasons people delay retirement. 除了人们更健康、寿命更长之外，经济学家说，多重经济因素的叠加——例如实际工资多年 增长缓慢，以及私人部门远离传统养老金——是人们延迟退休的部分原因。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文说 the increase in the number of people working in less labor-intensive occupations——是 "从事劳动强度小的职业的人变多"，A 项 less intellectually challenging jobs 偷换为 "智力上挑战较小的工作"，labor-intensive（体力密集）与 intellectually challenging（智力挑战）不是一回事。 B) 无中生有 B 项 The number of jobs suitable for older people has increased in the private sector 说私人部门里适合老年人的岗位增多，但原文 a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector 谈的是养老金机制远离传统模式，并未谈岗位数量的 变化。 C) ✓ 正确 years of slow rise in real wages ↔ The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years 预判锁定 "实际工资多年涨得慢"，C 项 The rate of wage increase in terms of purchasing power has slowed down for years 把同一信息用购买力的角度表达，是 教科书式同义替换。 D) 偷换概念 原文 a shift away from traditional pensions in the private sector 是 "私人部门正在 远离传统养老金"——指制度变化；D 项 find it hard to rely on traditional pensions 偷换成 "人们觉得难以依赖传统养老金"——指主观感受。两者方向虽近，但原文从未谈 及人们的主观难度感。 人们推迟退休的总体趋势是什么? A) 收入越高,他们越有可能倾向于推迟退休。 B) 工作满意度更高的人往往比满意度较低的人退休得更晚。 C) 留在劳动力市场直到70多岁的男性可能多于女性。 D) 教育水平越高,他们越有可能推迟退休。

questions.q: What is the general trend in people delaying retirement?
options: The higher their earnings, the more likely they are tempted to delay retirement.
Those who have more job satisfaction tend to retire later than those who have less.
More men than women are likely to stay in the labor force until their late seventies.
The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the general trend in people delaying retirement 询问的是原文里已经写明 的整体规律，去找总括句即可，不需越级推断。

【拆句】主干 What is the general trend，介词短语 in people delaying retirement 中 people delaying retirement 是 in 的复合宾语（动名词短语带逻辑主语），结构平直、无从句。

【定位】The overall trend is hitting Americans of all different levels of educational attainment, although the percentages vary by category. The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% in 2018. For those with a high school degree or less, the proportion of those working in their 70s had risen to around 10%, while those with some college education were in the middle at around 15%. 这一整体趋势影响着所有学历层次的美国人，尽管各类别的比例有所不同。拥有本科学历、 且仍在 70 多岁工作的美国人比例在 2018 年达到近 20%；高中及以下学历者比例约 10%；有部分大学经历者居中，约 15%。

【选项】A) 无中生有 A 项 The higher their earnings, the more likely they are tempted to delay retirement 把维度换成 earnings（收入），原文 all different levels of educational attainment 谈的是学历，没有任何收入分层数据。 B) 张冠李戴 B 项 Those who have more job satisfaction tend to retire later than those who have less 谈职业满意度的影响，但本段只有学历分层数据，没有关于 job satisfaction 的对比；此话题虽在第 6 段简短出现，与 "general trend" 不是同一议题。 C) 张冠李戴 C 项 More men than women are likely to stay in the labor force until their late seventies 涉及性别差异，原文虽然第 6 段提到 particularly for men，但那是讲孤独 感、不是 general trend 数据；本段从未做性别对比。 D) ✓ 正确 The share of Americans with bachelor's degrees who were working into their 70s reached nearly 20% ↔The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement 预判出 "学历越高，延迟退休比例越高"，D 项 The higher their educational level, the more likely they are to delay retirement 正是这一规律的语句化，无遗漏无超纲。 根据一位经济学家的说法,受过大学教育的工人推迟退休的主要原因是什么? A) 享有财务保障。 B) 保持社交联系。 C) 在专业方面做出更多贡献。 D) 增加社会保障金支付。 54. What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement according to an economist? A) Enjoying financial security. B) Staying connected socially. C) Contributing more professionally. D) Increasing social security payments.

questions.q: What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement according to an economist?
options: Enjoying financial security.
Staying connected socially.
Contributing more professionally.
Increasing social security payments.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What is the chief reason for college-educated workers delaying retirement 询问 原文中经济学家明确给出的主因，按细节题处理即可。

【拆句】主干 What is the chief reason，介词短语 for college-educated workers delaying retirement 作后置定语，分词 delaying 修饰 workers 表正在延迟；末尾 according to an economist 是插入限定信息源，结构清晰。

【定位】He suggests that many college-educated workers are choosing to stay in the labor force more for social benefits than for financial reasons. 他指出，许多受过大学教育的劳动者选择继续留在劳动力市场，更多是出于社交方面的好 处，而不是经济原因。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 A 项 Enjoying financial security 把主因说成 "享受经济保障"，但原文明确 more for social benefits than for financial reasons —— financial 恰恰是被否定的次要原因， A 项正好反向。 B) ✓ 正确 more for social benefits than for financial reasons ↔Staying connected socially 预判抓 social benefits，B 项 Staying connected socially 正面命中；其余选项均与 social 无直接对应，可一眼锁定。 C) 过度推断 C 项 Contributing more professionally 说 "在专业上贡献更多"，原文 in professional occupations where they tend to enjoy their work more 只说他们多从事专业职业、 并享受工作，并未提 "为了贡献更多" 才不退休。 D) 无中生有 D 项 Increasing social security payments 把 social 与 financial 拼成 "提高社会保障 金"，是基于熟词 social 的乱凑，原文从未提及社会保障金（social security 是美国福利 专名）。 文章关于从事体力劳动的人说了什么? A) 他们渴望退休后享受生活。 B) 他们可能会遇到财务困难。 C) 他们通常不喜欢做这种工作。 D) 他们倾向于期待退休。

questions.q: What does the passage say about people doing manual work?
options: They are eager to enjoy life after retiring.
They are likely to have financial troubles.
They generally don't enjoy doing it.
They tend to anticipate retirement.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干 What does the passage say about people doing manual work 直接问原文对该群 体的具体说法，按细节题处理。

【拆句】主干 What does the passage say about ...，about 引出对象；现在分词短语 doing manual work 后置修饰 people，相当于 who do manual work，无从句无难点。

【定位】Workers in more physical jobs, meanwhile, may be more likely to look forward to retiring, Baily says, suggesting those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons. 另一方面，从事体力劳动较多的工人则可能更期待退休；Baily 说，那些继续留下来的多半 是出于经济原因。

【选项】A) 过度推断 A 项 They are eager to enjoy life after retiring 把原文 "期待退休" 引申到 "渴望享受 退休后的生活"，原文只说期待退休、未提退休后做什么，引申了一步。 B) 过度推断 B 项 They are likely to have financial troubles 把原文 those who stay on are more likely doing so for financial reasons 推到 "会陷入经济困境"，但 for financial reasons 只说 "出于经济原因"，不等同于 financial troubles。 C) 无中生有 C 项 They generally don't enjoy doing it 说 "他们通常不喜欢做这工作"，但原文只 说他们更期待退休、并未直接评价是否喜欢工作；不能由 "期待退休" 直接等同 "不喜欢 工作"。 D) ✓ 正确 may be more likely to look forward to retiring ↔They tend to anticipate retirement 预判抓 "期待退休"，D 项 They tend to anticipate retirement 是 look forward to retiring 的标准英英同义替换，选定无误。

items.title: 2025年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Junk food is now a staple of many Americans' diets. Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. But recent studies show a lack of exercise is not to blame for rising obesity rates. Bad diets are.

P2 Interventions(干预) to help reduce junk food consumption are especially important for children and teenagers. Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat. Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach.

P3 Now a large-scale study has tried an innovative approach to change teenagers' attitudes towards healthy eating, and the results are promising. The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice.

P4 To do this, researchers had students read an article on the food industry. It revealed a secret about the manipulative and deceptive strategies used to make junk food more addictive and characterize the products as healthy. The article also explained how advertising campaigns specifically target very young and poor people, causing harm for these vulnerable groups. Afterwards, the participants read a fictional survey of teens who wanted to "fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food"

P5 After the intervention, participants associated healthy eating with autonomy and social justice. The teenagers also rated healthy eating as being more appealing. Importantly, there were also some promising effects of the new intervention on actual behavior. A day later the students were offered a choice of snacks and drinks in a seemingly unrelated context. The teens chose healthy snacks and drinks (such as fruit or water) more often over unhealthy options (like biscuits and soda). Apparently associating a healthy diet with teenagers' own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity.

questions.q: What do we learn about advertising campaigns from the snack food companies?
options: They convey the idea that their products are ok if consumers exercise more.
They send the message that bad diets are responsible for Americans' obesity.
They usually feature sports stars to emphasize the benefits of their snack foods.
They claim that lack of exercise is to blame for the increasing obesity rates.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about advertising campaigns from the snack food companies? 是 What do we learn about X 句式，问的是关于 X 的已知事实，不 含 infer/suggest/imply。

【拆句】What do we learn about advertising campaigns from the snack food companies? 主 干 What do we learn about X，X = advertising campaigns，后面 from the snack food companies 是介词短语修饰 campaigns，结构平铺无陷阱。

【定位】Advertising campaigns from the snack food companies, often featuring sports stars, send the message that we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise. 零食公司的广告活动经常以体育明星为主角，传递的信息是：只要多做体育锻炼，就能抵消 食用其产品带来的任何负面影响。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 we can neutralize any negative effects of consuming their products simply by getting more physical exercise ↔their products are ok if consumers exercise more 预判"广告称多运动就能抵消坏处"和 A 的 their products are ok if consumers exercise more 完全对得上。 B) 张冠李戴 They send the message that bad diets are responsible for Americans' obesity. 说 的是广告传达"坏饮食才是肥胖元凶"——但这其实是 Bad diets are 这句作者引述研究 的结论，与广告立场恰恰相反。 C) 偷换概念 They usually feature sports stars to emphasize the benefits of their snack foods. 说请明星是为了"强调零食本身的好处"——但原文 often featuring sports stars 后接的 逻辑是"运动能抵消坏处"，明星是"运动"的化身，不是为吹嘘零食优点。 D) 与原文相反 They claim that lack of exercise is to blame for the increasing obesity rates. 说广 告主张"缺乏锻炼导致肥胖"——这是后文研究的反方观点 a lack of exercise is not to blame 的镜像，而且原文是 not to blame，D 偷偷把 not 去掉。 文章关于健康教育说了什么？ A) 它阐明了青少年叛逆和自主的本能。 B) 它更加强调治疗而非预防。 C) 它对反肥胖运动几乎没有贡献。 D) 它在使青少年远离垃圾食品方面基本上失败了。 47. What does the passage say about health education? A) It has shed light on teens' instinct for rebellion and autonomy. B) It has placed much more emphasis on cure than on prevention. C) It has contributed little to the campaigns against obesity. D) It has largely failed to turn teens away from junk food.

questions.q: What does the passage say about health education?
options: It has shed light on teens' instinct for rebellion and autonomy.
It has placed much more emphasis on cure than on prevention.
It has contributed little to the campaigns against obesity.
It has largely failed to turn teens away from junk food.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about health education? 直接问"文章关于 X 怎么说"，要 求复述事实。

【拆句】What does the passage say about health education? 主干 What does the passage say about X，X = health education，结构无陷阱。

【定位】Unfortunately, while health education has shown some success among young children, teens have been harder to reach. 遗憾的是，虽然健康教育在低龄儿童中取得了一定成效，但对青少年的影响一直很难触达。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 It has shed light on teens' instinct for rebellion and autonomy. 说健康教育"揭示了 青少年的叛逆本性"——但 instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy 是第三段的 new intervention 才用到的概念，与第二段 health education 无关。 B) 偷换概念 It has placed much more emphasis on cure than on prevention. 说健康教育"更重 治疗轻预防"——但原文 Prevention is better than cure because obesity is so difficult to treat. 是作者对干预总体的观点，并未说健康教育"更重治疗"。 C) 以偏概全 It has contributed little to the campaigns against obesity. 全盘否定健康教育，但原 文 health education has shown some success among young children 明确承认对 儿童有成效，并非"几乎无贡献"。 D) ✓ 正确 teens have been harder to reach ↔largely failed to turn teens away from junk food Unfortunately ↔largely failed 预判"对青少年没奏效"与 D 的 largely failed to turn teens away from junk food 完全 契合。 先前帮助减少垃圾食品消费的干预措施有什么重大缺陷？ A) 它们只是暂时激励青少年远离垃圾食品。 B) 它们关注年轻人未来将获得的益处。 C) 它们基于这样的假设：动机是唯一的关键。 D) 它们无法诉诸青少年的叛逆本能。

questions.q: What is a major flaw in previous interventions to help reduce junk food consumption?
options: They motivated teens to stay away from junk food only temporarily.
They focused on the benefits young people would reap in the future.
They were based on the assumption that motivation was the only key.
They were incapable of appealing to teens' instinct for rebelliousness.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is a major flaw in previous interventions to help reduce junk food consumption? 直问 What is，要的是文中明确写出的具体缺陷。 48. What is a major flaw in previous interventions to help reduce junk food consumption? A) They motivated teens to stay away from junk food only temporarily. B) They focused on the benefits young people would reap in the future. C) They were based on the assumption that motivation was the only key. D) They were incapable of appealing to teens' instinct for rebelliousness.

【拆句】What is a major flaw in previous interventions to help reduce junk food consumption? 主干 What is a major flaw，后跟两层修饰：in previous interventions 限 定缺陷的归属，to help reduce junk food consumption 是不定式修饰 interventions 的 功能。要看清 flaw 修饰的是 previous interventions，不是别的。

【定位】The researchers argued that previous interventions have probably been unsuccessful because of a major flaw: they focused on a future, healthier you and assumed that this would be enough motivation for teenagers. 研究者认为，以往的干预之所以可能失败，是因为一个重大缺陷：它们把重心放在"未来更 健康的你"，并假设这就足以激励青少年。

【选项】A) 无中生有 They motivated teens to stay away from junk food only temporarily. 说"只在短 期有效"——但原文从未提及干预的"短期/长期"时效问题，only temporarily 属凭空 捏造。 B) ✓ 正确 focused on a future, healthier you ↔ focused on the benefits young people would reap in the future 预判"押注未来好处"和 B 的 focused on the benefits young people would reap in the future 完全契合。 C) 过度推断 They were based on the assumption that motivation was the only key. 把原文 assumed that this would be enough motivation 扭成"动机是唯一关键"——原文只 说"这一点已经足够"，未说"动机是唯一"。 D) 张冠李戴 They were incapable of appealing to teens' instinct for rebelliousness. 说"以前的 干预无法触动叛逆本能"——叛逆本性是 new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness 的卖点，反推回去"以前没用"是考生自己脑补 的，原文并未把"未利用叛逆本能"列为 flaw。 新的干预措施在哪些方面具有创新性？ A) 它强调人们的社会责任感。 B) 它巧妙地利用了青少年的个人弱点。 C) 它利用了青少年的天然倾向。 D) 它承诺即时而非未来的益处。

questions.q: In what way is the new intervention innovative?
options: It emphasizes people's sense of social responsibility.
It cleverly exploits teenagers' personal weaknesses.
It takes advantage of teenagers' natural inclination.
It promises immediate rather than future benefits.
questions.explain:
【判型】In what way is the new intervention innovative? 问的是"以何种方式"，答案在原文有具 体描述。

【拆句】In what way is the new intervention innovative? 主干 the new intervention is innovative，前置 In what way 提问。innovative 是表语形容词，整句结构简单。

【定位】In contrast, the new intervention cleverly exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy, and the value they place on social justice. 与之相对，新干预巧妙地利用了青少年对叛逆和自主的本能，以及他们对社会公正的重视。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 It emphasizes people's sense of social responsibility. 只抓住 the value they place on social justice 这一点，且把 teenagers 扩大成 people、把 social justice 偷换成 social responsibility。 B) 偷换概念 It cleverly exploits teenagers' personal weaknesses. 把 instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy 这一中性偏正面的"本能"扭曲成 personal weaknesses（个人弱点）； 原文并未把叛逆视为"弱点"。 C) ✓ 正确 exploits teenagers' instinct for rebelliousness and autonomy ↔ takes advantage of teenagers' natural inclination 预判"顺势利用青少年天性"和 C 的 takes advantage of teenagers' natural inclination 一一对应。 D) 过度推断 It promises immediate rather than future benefits. 说新干预"承诺即时好处"——但 原文从未提"即时好处"，且作者把"许诺未来好处"作为 previous interventions 的缺 陷，并不意味着新干预走"即时好处"的反向路线。 从新研究中可以得出什么结论？ A) 可以采用完全不同的方法来对抗零食广告宣传活动。 B) 必须找到有效的干预措施来说服青少年转向更健康的生活方式。 C) 通过在青少年的价值观与健康饮食之间建立联系，有望预防肥胖。 D) 战胜肥胖的创新方法是揭露食品公司的操纵性和欺骗性做法。

questions.q: What conclusion can be drawn from the new research?
options: A totally different approach could be adopted to combat advertising campaigns for snack food.
An effective intervention has to be found to persuade teenagers to switch to a healthier lifestyle.
Obesity can be hopefully prevented by building links between teenagers' values and healthy eating.
An innovative way to beat obesity is to expose food companies' manipulative and deceptive
questions.explain:
【判型】What conclusion can be drawn from the new research? 让你为整篇研究下结论，覆盖 全文而非某一段。

【拆句】What conclusion can be drawn from the new research? 被动结构 conclusion can be drawn from X，相当于 What conclusion does the new research lead to。注意 drawn from 是"从…得出"，不要看反。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 A totally different approach could be adopted to combat advertising campaigns for snack food. 把"反击广告"当作研究结论——但 fight back against the companies by buying and eating less processed food 只是干预里使用的"虚构问卷"内容，是实 验素材，不是研究结论。 B) 与原文相反 An effective intervention has to be found to persuade teenagers to switch to a healthier lifestyle. 把"得找到有效干预"作为结论——但本研究本身已经提出并验证了一 种有效干预，结论是"这条路有希望"而不是"还得继续找"。 C) ✓ 正确 associating a healthy diet with teenagers' own values seems to be a promising avenue to prevent obesity ↔ Obesity can be hopefully prevented by building links between teenagers' values and healthy eating. teenagers' own values ↔teenagers' values C 既包含"青少年价值观"又包含"健康饮食"和"防肥胖"三个要素，正好对应主线串出的 结论。 D) 以偏概全 An innovative way to beat obesity is to expose food companies' manipulative and deceptive practices. 把"揭露食品公司套路"当结论——但 the manipulative and deceptive strategies 只是新干预里给学生看的材料之一，并非研究结论本身。研究结 论是"把饮食与青少年价值观挂钩"，揭露公司只是其中的具体手段。

items.title: 2025年12月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Adults dream during REM (rapid eye movement) sleep and infants have loads of REM. So, it might be fair to assume that babies have tons of dreams.

P2 But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. When babies are in REM, it allows their brain to develop pathways, connections, and eventually, learn languages.

P3 Since your baby doesn't dream at this stage of brain development, it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either. Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma(创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life.

P4 Are you wondering, what do babies dream about? Good question, but the answer is nothing! So, when do babies start dreaming? The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. In his lab, he lets kids fall asleep and then wakes them 3 times a night and asks them to describe what they recall.

P5 Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too.

P6 Dreams of very small kids are usually just snapshots(快照), looking much more like a slideshow than a movie, when compared to the dreams of adults. They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights, like images of people eating. According to Foulkes, "Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration." Kids ages 5 – 9 begin seeing moving images and characters in action. Dreams now include multiple events strung together, one after the other. They also start developing greater ability to remember dreams. Still, that's not always the case: When roused during REM sleep, 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming, a trend that continues through age 9.

P7 So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play.

questions.q: What do scientists think of REM?
options: It is a sign of dreaming in adults and infants alike.
It is essential to human beings' language learning.
It determines the formation of connections in the brain.
It performs a different function in babies than in adults.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do scientists think of REM? 直接问科学家对 REM 的看法，是对原文具体观点的客 观转述。 51. What do scientists think of REM? A) It is a sign of dreaming in adults and infants alike. B) It is essential to human beings' language learning. C) It determines the formation of connections in the brain. D) It performs a different function in babies than in adults.

【拆句】Q51 结构是 "What do scientists think of REM?"，主谓宾极简，think of 在此意为 "对……的看法"，无陷阱。

【定位】But scientists believe REM serves a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming. 但科学家认为，对新生儿和婴儿而言，REM 所起的作用与做梦完全不同。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 原文明说婴儿在 REM 期"不做梦"，It is a sign of dreaming in adults and infants alike 反而说成人婴儿都做梦，与文意相反。 B) 以偏概全 原文 eventually, learn languages 只把语言学习列为大脑发育的一个结果，It is essential to human beings' language learning 把它拔高为 REM 的本质功能，范围 被放大。 C) 偷换概念 原文是 REM "allows" 婴儿大脑发育连接（提供条件），It determines the formation of connections in the brain 把 "提供条件" 偷换为 "决定"，强度被改。 D) ✓ 正确 a completely different purpose for newborns and infants than dreaming ↔ a different function in babies than in adults 预判 "REM 在婴儿与成人身上作用不同" 对应 It performs a different function in babies than in adults.，两端同义替换链完整。 从文章中我们可以推断出关于噩梦的什么信息? A) 它们常常发生在想象力活跃的人身上。 B) 它们发生在遭受情绪压力的人身上。 C) 它们在大脑发育的不同阶段各不相同。 D) 它们出现在成人和婴儿的睡眠中。

questions.q: What can we infer about nightmares from the passage?
options: They occur often in people with an active imagination.
They occur in people suffering from emotional stress.
They vary in different stages of brain development.
They appear in the sleep of both adults and infants.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we infer about nightmares from the passage? 含 infer，属推断而非细节。

【拆句】Q52 主干 "What can we infer about nightmares"，about 引出推断对象，from the passage 是状语，结构简单。

【定位】Nightmares stem from exposure to trauma(创伤), an overactive imagination, and the normal stresses of everyday life. 噩梦源于创伤经历、过度活跃的想象，以及日常生活中的正常压力。 52. What can we infer about nightmares from the passage? A) They occur often in people with an active imagination. B) They occur in people suffering from emotional stress. C) They vary in different stages of brain development. D) They appear in the sleep of both adults and infants.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 P3 只把 an overactive imagination 列为三因之一，They occur often in people with an active imagination 把它单独抽出且加 often 强化，把一项当作主因。 B) ✓ 正确 the normal stresses of everyday life ↔emotional stress 预判 "承受情绪压力的人易做噩梦" 与 They occur in people suffering from emotional stress. 同义。 C) 无中生有 原文 P3 谈噩梦的成因，从未把噩梦与 "大脑发育阶段" 的关系作为话题；They vary in different stages of brain development 把别处的 brain development 概念硬套到 nightmares 上。 D) 与原文相反 原文 it's safe to assume babies do not have nightmares, either 明确婴儿不做噩 梦，They appear in the sleep of both adults and infants 反着说 "成人婴儿睡眠中都 出现"。 心理学家David Foulkes的研究目的是什么? A) 揭示儿童梦境的秘密。 B) 看儿童是否在两岁开始做梦。 C) 解决做梦与大脑发育之谜。 D) 证实关于儿童何时做梦的普遍共识。

questions.q: What is the aim of psychologist David Foulkes' study?
options: To reveal the secrets of children's dreams.
To see if children start dreaming at age two.
To solve the mystery of dreaming and brain growth.
To confirm the general consensus on when kids dream.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the aim of psychologist David Foulkes' study? 直接问研究目的，是对原文目的 句的客观转述。

【拆句】Q53 结构是 "What is the aim of psychologist David Foulkes' study?"，of 短语限定 aim，psychologist 是 David Foulkes 的同位身份说明，无陷阱。

【定位】Psychologist David Foulkes studies children (from very small kids to teens) to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day. 心理学家 David Foulkes 研究儿童（从年幼孩童到青少年），目的是把他们梦境的秘密揭示 于人前。 53. What is the aim of psychologist David Foulkes' study? A) To reveal the secrets of children's dreams. B) To see if children start dreaming at age two. C) To solve the mystery of dreaming and brain growth. D) To confirm the general consensus on when kids dream.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 to bring the secrets of their dreams to the light of day ↔ To reveal the secrets of children's dreams. 预判 "揭示儿童梦境秘密" 与 To reveal the secrets of children's dreams. 一一对应， 选 A。 B) 偷换概念 原文 they start dreaming around the age of two 是研究背景里的 "普遍共识"，并非 Foulkes 研究的目的；To see if children start dreaming at age two 把背景信息当成 研究目的。 C) 无中生有 原文未把 Foulkes 的目标说成 "解开做梦与大脑发育之谜"；To solve the mystery of dreaming and brain growth 引入了 P2 的 brain 概念硬接到 Foulkes 研究目的上。 D) 偷换概念 原文 The general consensus is that they start dreaming around the age of two. 表 示这是研究界已有共识，Foulkes 并非为证实它而研究；To confirm the general consensus on when kids dream 把 "已存在的共识" 当成 Foulkes 要证实的对象。 Foulkes关于儿童梦境的发现是什么? A) 它们以奇怪的动物为特征。 B) 它们对成人来说并不令人惊讶。 C) 它们随着年龄增长和演变。 D) 它们反映儿童的清醒生活。

questions.q: What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams?
options: They feature strange animals.
They are unsurprising to adults.
They grow and evolve with age.
They reflect kids' waking life.
questions.explain:
【判型】What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams? 直接问研究结论是什么，是细节题。

【拆句】Q54 结构是 "What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams?"，about kids' dreams 限定 findings 的范围，没有从句也没有否定，无陷阱。

【定位】Foulkes' findings are unsurprising. Basically, little kids have little dreams. But exactly what kids see while dreaming depends on their age. As children develop and grow, their dreams do too. Foulkes 的发现并不令人意外。本质上，小孩做的也是小梦。但孩子在梦中究竟看到什么， 取决于他们的年龄。随着孩子的发育成长，他们的梦也在发育成长。 54. What are Foulkes' findings about kids' dreams? A) They feature strange animals. B) They are unsurprising to adults. C) They grow and evolve with age. D) They reflect kids' waking life.

【选项】A) 以偏概全 They heavily feature animals and other familiar sights 只说幼儿梦多含动物等"熟悉 景象"，They feature strange animals 把动物拔成 "strange animals" 且当成所有孩子 梦的特征。 B) 答非所问 题问 findings 的内容；They are unsurprising to adults. 拿原文 "unsurprising" 的评 价词当做内容，Foulkes' findings are unsurprising 的 unsurprising 是对 "findings 本 身" 的评价，而非 findings 的实质内容。 C) ✓ 正确 As children develop and grow, their dreams do too ↔They grow and evolve with age. 预判 "梦随孩子发育而发育" 与 They grow and evolve with age. 完全对应，选 C。 D) 偷换概念 原文 Children's dream life…seems to be similar to their waking imagination and narration 的相似对象是 "清醒时的想象与叙事"，They reflect kids' waking life. 把 "想 象/叙事" 偷换成 "waking life"（清醒生活本身）。 关于醒来时看起来心烦意乱的婴儿,我们可以假设什么? A) 他们违背自己的意愿被唤醒了。 B) 他们被噩梦打扰了。 C) 他们难以回忆梦境的画面。 D) 他们受到了做梦以外的其他事物的影响。

questions.q: What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking?
options: They have been roused against their will.
They have been disturbed by a nightmare.
They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams.
They have been affected by something other than dreaming.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking? 含 assume，按 推断题处理。

【拆句】Q55 结构是 "What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking?"， who 引导定语从句修饰 babies，upon waking 是时间状语 "一醒来时"，整句无否定无比 较，理解关键是把 who 从句翻成 "那些一醒来就显得不安的婴儿"。

【定位】So, if your baby seems to be in a stressful state while sleeping or is upset upon waking, there may be other factors at play. 因此，如果你的婴儿睡觉时显得紧张、或一醒来就不安，那很可能是别的因素在起作用。 55. What can we assume about babies who appear upset upon waking? A) They have been roused against their will. B) They have been disturbed by a nightmare. C) They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams. D) They have been affected by something other than dreaming.

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文 P7 没有说婴儿被人弄醒；They have been roused against their will. 凭空添加 "被弄醒" + "违背意愿" 两个文本无据的语义。 B) 与原文相反 原文 babies do not have nightmares 明确说婴儿不做噩梦；They have been disturbed by a nightmare. 反着说婴儿被噩梦惊扰。 C) 答非所问 题问 "哭醒原因"，They have trouble recollecting the images of their dreams. 把焦 点换成 "回忆梦境困难"，且 25% of the kids in Foulkes' studies had no recollection of dreaming 说的是 5-9 岁孩子，而非 "babies"。 D) ✓ 正确 there may be other factors at play ↔ They have been affected by something other than dreaming. 预判 "原因不是做梦" 与 They have been affected by something other than dreaming. 完全对应，选 D。

items.title: 2025年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 New York's Eleven Madison Park has become the first vegan( 素食主义的) restaurant to be awarded three Michelin stars.

P2 The fine dining establishment received its first three-star Michelin rating in 2011 when the menu was famed for its fancy animal-based dishes.

P3 However, last year, the restaurant's co-owner and famous chef, Daniel Humm, made the bold decision to remove meat from the menu, citing our unsustainable food system. While cow milk is still served for tea and coffee, the menu is almost 100 percent vegan.

P4 At the time, Humm acknowledged the move was risky, admitting that "it wasn't clear if guests would come", but called the gamble "a risk worth taking."

P5 "In view of the climate crisis, I didn't want to open the same restaurant," Humm told the Financial Times in an interview. "If we can show the possibilities of eating plant-based food in this setting, it can open a lot of doors" for others to follow.

P6 Now, this impressive new accomplishment validates Eleven Madison Park's decision to take meat off the menu and embrace plant-based foods, with Michelin's 2022 New York guide branding it 'a bold vision of luxury dining'.

P7 "We took the jump to transform Eleven Madison Park into a plant-based fine dining restaurant knowing in our hearts this is what we believed in," stated Humm on Instagram. "Last night, we were honored to be awarded three Michelin stars for the 11th year in a row. I am so grateful to the team members who contributed through its nearly 25-year history. We are also grateful to our guests and partners who believed in our vision and encouraged us to push harder."

P8 Three Michelin stars is the highest award, given to chefs who are at the peak of their profession. "Their cooking is elevated to an art form and some of their dishes are destined to become classics," reads Michelin's website, in a clear nod to plant-based foods' growing significance in the culinary(烹饪的) world.

P9 "I think luxury companies have a real role to play and a responsibility," says Humm. "The more creative we are, the more beautiful and delicious our future will be."

questions.q: What do we learn about New York's Eleven Madison Park?
options: It is the first vegan restaurant to receive the highest Michelin rating.
It is the first restaurant in the city to remove meat from its menu.
It was famed throughout the U.S. for its fancy regional dishes.
It was established as a three-star Michelin restaurant in 2011.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about New York's Eleven Madison Park? 问的是关于某对象的客观信 息，没有 infer/imply 等推断信号，属典型细节题。

【拆句】What do we learn about New York's Eleven Madison Park? 是一句结构平铺直叙的特殊 疑问句，learn about 后跟宾语，无陷阱。

【定位】New York's Eleven Madison Park has become the first vegan(素食主义的) restaurant to be awarded three Michelin stars. 纽约的 Eleven Madison Park 成为首家获颁米其林三星的素食餐厅。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 the first vegan(素食主义的) restaurant to be awarded three Michelin stars ↔ the first vegan restaurant to receive the highest Michelin rating It is the first vegan restaurant to receive the highest Michelin rating. 完整覆盖了预 判的三要素，首家、素食、最高评级，且无任何额外信息，与定位句一一对应。 B) 偷换概念 原文说的是首家获三星的素食餐厅，the first restaurant in the city to remove meat from its menu 把首家偷换到了全市首家撤肉上，原文并无此说。 C) 无中生有 原文 famed for its fancy animal-based dishes 说的是过去以荤菜闻名，famed throughout the U.S. for its fancy regional dishes 一改 animal-based 为 regional （地方菜），二加范围 throughout the U.S.（全美），都无原文支持。 D) 偷换概念 原文 received its first three-star Michelin rating in 2011 说的是 2011 年首次获三 星，established as a three-star Michelin restaurant in 2011 把获评偷换成建立，与 原文 its nearly 25-year history 也矛盾。 Daniel Humm为什么决定从他的餐厅菜单中去除肉类？ A) 为了鼓励更多顾客选择纯素饮食。 B) 为了促进可持续食品系统的发展。 C) 为了展示植物性菜单的吸引力。 D) 为了争取米其林三星评级。

questions.q: Why did Daniel Humm decide to remove meat from the menu of his restaurant?
options: To encourage more customers to be vegan.
To contribute to a sustainable food system.
To show the appeal of a plant-based menu.
To strive for the three-star Michelin rating.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why did Daniel Humm decide to remove meat from the menu of his restaurant? 用 Why 直接问原因，对应原文必有显性的原因表述。

【拆句】Why did Daniel Humm decide to remove meat from the menu of his restaurant? 主 干为 Why did X decide to do Y，decide to 后接动作，无修饰陷阱。 47. Why did Daniel Humm decide to remove meat from the menu of his restaurant? A) To encourage more customers to be vegan. B) To contribute to a sustainable food system. C) To show the appeal of a plant-based menu. D) To strive for the three-star Michelin rating.

【定位】However, last year, the restaurant's co-owner and famous chef, Daniel Humm, made the bold decision to remove meat from the menu, citing our unsustainable food system. 然而，去年餐厅的联合所有者兼名厨 Daniel Humm 做出了大胆决定，将肉从菜单中撤下， 理由是我们的食物体系不可持续。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 To encourage more customers to be vegan. 把动机应对不可持续体系偷换成鼓励顾 客吃素，原文 Humm 的关注点是体系层面而非顾客饮食选择。 B) ✓ 正确 citing our unsustainable food system ↔To contribute to a sustainable food system. 四个选项中只有 To contribute to a sustainable food system. 含 sustainable 这个原 文核心词根，且其表达的目的与 citing 的事实方向自洽。 C) 答非所问 If we can show the possibilities of eating plant-based food in this setting, it can open a lot of doors 是 Humm 对该决定后续效果的展望，而非他做决定的原因，时间 和因果关系都被改写。 D) 与原文相反 三星米其林是撤肉之后才获得的结果，To strive for the three-star Michelin rating. 把 它说成做决定的目的，因果关系与原文相反。 Daniel Humm如何看待他转向无肉菜单的举措？ A) 这是一次值得的尝试，尽管他对其成功与否并无把握。 B) 这将为更多餐厅树立榜样。 C) 这是一次疯狂的冒险，很少有高级餐饮界的厨师敢于尝试。 D) 这将被证明是当今餐饮业正确的一步。

questions.q: What did Daniel Humm think of his move to a meat-free menu?
options: It was a worthwhile effort even though he was unsure of its success.
It would set a model for many more restaurants to follow.
It was a mad gamble few chefs in the fine dining world would risk taking.
It would prove a right step to take in today's catering business.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did Daniel Humm think of his move to a meat-free menu? 问的是 Humm 自己 怎么看，原文必有他直接表态的引语。

【拆句】What did Daniel Humm think of his move to a meat-free menu? think of 是固定搭 配，意为对...的看法，主干清晰，无陷阱。

【定位】At the time, Humm acknowledged the move was risky, admitting that "it wasn't clear if guests would come", but called the gamble "a risk worth taking." 当时 Humm 承认此举有风险，承认不清楚客人是否还会来，但他把这场赌博称作一次值得 冒的险。 48. What did Daniel Humm think of his move to a meat-free menu? A) It was a worthwhile effort even though he was unsure of its success. B) It would set a model for many more restaurants to follow. C) It was a mad gamble few chefs in the fine dining world would risk taking. D) It would prove a right step to take in today's catering business.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 it wasn't clear if guests would come ↔he was unsure of its success a risk worth taking ↔a worthwhile effort It was a worthwhile effort even though he was unsure of its success. 用 even though 把值得与不确定连起来，恰好对应原文 but 引出的双面态度。 B) 答非所问 It would set a model for many more restaurants to follow. 是 Humm 在 it can open a lot of doors 中说的对外效用，而非他对自己这一举动的内心评价。 C) 过度推断 a mad gamble few chefs in the fine dining world would risk taking 用 mad、few chefs would risk 把原文的 risky 与 a risk worth taking 夸大成几乎没人敢冒的疯狂赌 博，原文 Humm 并未做此横向比较。 D) 偷换概念 It would prove a right step to take in today's catering business. 把 Humm 对自己 这一步的个人评价换成对整个餐饮业的判断，且 a right step 也比 a risk worth taking 多了行业普遍正确的隐含。 米其林2022年纽约指南对Eleven Madison Park餐厅的决定有何评价？ A) 它将该餐厅的烹饪提升到了艺术形式的高度。 B) 它证明了米其林所授予评级的有效性。 C) 它展现了对未来高级餐饮的大胆远见。 D) 这是将该餐厅转变为奢华餐厅的努力。

questions.q: What does Michelin's 2022 New York guide say about Eleven Madison Park's decision?
options: It elevates the restaurant's cooking to an art form.
It proves the validity of ratings awarded by Michelin.
It shows a daring foresight regarding future fine dining.
It is an effort to transform the restaurant into a luxury one.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Michelin's 2022 New York guide say about Eleven Madison Park's decision? 问指南说了什么，对应原文必有指南的引语或转述。

【拆句】What does Michelin's 2022 New York guide say about Eleven Madison Park's decision? say about 后接讨论对象，结构线性、无陷阱。

【定位】Now, this impressive new accomplishment validates Eleven Madison Park's decision to take meat off the menu and embrace plant-based foods, with Michelin's 2022 New York guide branding it 'a bold vision of luxury dining'. 如今，这一令人瞩目的新成就印证了 Eleven Madison Park 撤肉、拥抱植物饮食的决定； 米其林 2022 纽约指南将其誉为奢华餐饮的大胆愿景。 49. What does Michelin's 2022 New York guide say about Eleven Madison Park's decision? A) It elevates the restaurant's cooking to an art form. B) It proves the validity of ratings awarded by Michelin. C) It shows a daring foresight regarding future fine dining. D) It is an effort to transform the restaurant into a luxury one.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 It elevates the restaurant's cooking to an art form. 取自 Their cooking is elevated to an art form，而那是米其林对三星厨师的总体描述，不是 2022 纽约指南对 Eleven Madison Park 这个决定的表态。 B) 与原文相反 It proves the validity of ratings awarded by Michelin. 把指南怎么说决定颠倒为决定 证明了米其林评级的有效性，原文 validates 的对象是 decision，而不是评级。 C) ✓ 正确 a bold vision of luxury dining ↔a daring foresight regarding future fine dining It shows a daring foresight regarding future fine dining. 同时给出大胆远见与高 端、未来餐饮两个要素，且整体语气与原文引号短语一致。 D) 无中生有 It is an effort to transform the restaurant into a luxury one. 把指南的评价改成餐厅 的主观努力（an effort to），且新增把餐厅变成奢华餐厅这一目的，原文从未提及。 米其林授予Eleven Madison Park餐厅三星表明了什么？ A) 对纯素食品成为主流的乐观愿景。 B) 烹饪界要承担的更大责任。 C) 对更多餐厅向顾客提供更健康食品的强烈激励。 D) 对提供纯素食品的餐厅日益增长的重要性的明确认可。

questions.q: What does the awarding of three Michelin stars to Eleven Madison Park indicate?
options: An optimistic vision of vegan foods becoming mainstream.
A greater responsibility for the culinary world to undertake.
A strong incentive for more restaurants to offer healthier foods to their customers.
An explicit recognition of the rising importance of restaurants serving vegan foods.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the awarding of three Michelin stars to Eleven Madison Park indicate? 中 的 indicate 是推断题专属信号词。

【拆句】What does the awarding of three Michelin stars to Eleven Madison Park indicate? 主 干为 What does X indicate，X 是动名词短语 the awarding of...，结构清晰、无陷阱。

【定位】"Their cooking is elevated to an art form and some of their dishes are destined to become classics," reads Michelin's website, in a clear nod to plant-based foods' growing significance in the culinary(烹饪的) world. 米其林官网写道：他们的烹饪被提升为一种艺术形式，他们的部分菜肴注定将成为经典；这 是对植物饮食在烹饪界日益增长的重要性的明确认可。 50. What does the awarding of three Michelin stars to Eleven Madison Park indicate? A) An optimistic vision of vegan foods becoming mainstream. B) A greater responsibility for the culinary world to undertake. C) A strong incentive for more restaurants to offer healthier foods to their customers. D) An explicit recognition of the rising importance of restaurants serving vegan foods.

【选项】A) 过度推断 An optimistic vision of vegan foods becoming mainstream. 把地位上升（rising importance）推到成为主流（becoming mainstream），且加上乐观愿景，跨度超过 原文一步可达的范围。 B) 答非所问 A greater responsibility for the culinary world to undertake. 取自 luxury companies have a real role to play and a responsibility 这种 Humm 的呼吁，而非 授星事件本身所表明的含义。 C) 偷换概念 A strong incentive for more restaurants to offer healthier foods to their customers. 一把素食或植物偷换成更健康的食物（healthier foods），二把地位上升变 成激励更多餐厅，原文从未谈健康层面，也未谈对其他餐厅的激励效应。 D) ✓ 正确 in a clear nod to plant-based foods' growing significance in the culinary(烹饪的) world ↔ An explicit recognition of the rising importance of restaurants serving vegan foods. An explicit recognition of the rising importance of restaurants serving vegan foods. 仅把植物饮食地位上升在表达载体上落到提供素食的餐厅，恰是从授星事件能合 理外推的一步，无超过原文的判断。

items.title: 2025年12月四级真题 第3套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2025年12月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
items.passage:
P1 With genetic testing becoming increasingly popular, many people are left wondering exactly how accurate it is. Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want precise information on inborn( 先天的) health conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon.

P2 How accurate DNA tests are relies greatly upon the kind of test being taken, on the specific question you ask, and on how complex the genetics behind a trait(特征) is. For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease- causing trait is present.

P3 Ancestry tests claim to reveal our genetic identities. But saying you are 30 percent East Asian or American hardly reflects your real ancestry.

P4 What about using DNA tests to discover distant family members? There are tools to compare one's DNA with others' to find distant relatives based on their genetic identification. These kinds of applications are generally accurate. It's relatively easy to tell whether two DNA samples belong to close relatives. With distant relatives, results become hazier.

P5 Genetic health tests claim to be able to detect certain hereditary( 遗传的) diseases, or other health conditions. While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone. The large majority of our traits and diseases also depend upon non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others.

P6 Genetic tests for multi-factorial traits are often very tricky to interpret. Height, for example, depends on hundreds of genes, each contributing a little to the outcome, together with a bunch of environmental factors. A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together. Then you should also account for non-genetic factors that are not written in the DNA.

P7 Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense. At the moment, the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak.

questions.q: What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests?
options: Knowing their accuracy.
Evaluating their applicability.
Utilizing the information they provide.
Weighing the consequences they have.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests 直接问文章"说了 什么"，没有 infer/imply 这种推断信号词，是查找型细节题。 51. What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests? A) Knowing their accuracy. B) Evaluating their applicability. C) Utilizing the information they provide. D) Weighing the consequences they have.

【拆句】What does the passage say is of importance regarding genetic tests 主干是 "What does the passage say"，宾语从句省略了 that，完整化即 "the passage say (that) ... is of importance"，regarding genetic tests 是介词短语作话题限定，相当于 about。无陷阱。

【定位】Whether you are taking a DNA test to build your extended DNA family tree, or want precise information on inborn health conditions, it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are, and what information we can rely upon. 无论你是为了构建延伸的 DNA 家谱树而做基因测试，还是想获得关于先天健康状况的精确 信息，搞清楚基因检测到底有多准、我们可以依赖哪些信息，都是很重要的。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 it is important to understand how accurate genetic tests are ↔Knowing their accuracy 预判说"知道它准不准"，Knowing their accuracy 一字不差地说"知道它的准确度"，直 接锁定 A。 B) 无中生有 Evaluating their applicability 中的 applicability（适用性/可用性）在 P1 里完全没 提，作者只强调准确度。 C) 偷换概念 what information we can rely upon 说的是"哪些信息可以依赖"——是判断可不可 信，而不是 Utilizing the information they provide 说的"利用它给出的信息"。 D) 无中生有 Weighing the consequences they have 里的 consequences（后果）在原文里没有任 何对应——作者通篇只在谈准确度，没谈"后果"。 什么样的基因检测往往相对可靠？ A) 那些足够复杂以揭示某一特征背后遗传机制的检测。 B) 那些寻找导致某些疾病的特征的检测。 C) 那些专注于所提出的特定问题的检测。 D) 那些寻找由单一基因决定的特征的检测。

questions.q: What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable?
options: Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait.
Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases.
Those focusing on the specific questions being asked.
Those looking for traits determined by a single gene.
questions.explain:
【判型】What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable 是查询事实性比较，找到 原文那句 "X 更可靠" 即可对答案。

【拆句】What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable 中 "tend to be" 是"倾向 于、往往是"的弱化系动词结构，相当于 are usually；comparatively 修饰 reliable，是"相 对来说"，并非"绝对可靠"。 52. What kind of genetic tests tend to be comparatively reliable? A) Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait. B) Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases. C) Those focusing on the specific questions being asked. D) Those looking for traits determined by a single gene.

【定位】For example, tests for traits that depend on a single gene provide much more reliable results, because you can see whether a disease-causing trait is present. 举个例子，对于那些只依赖单个基因的性状，相关检测能给出准确得多的结果，因为你可以 直接看到致病性状到底存不存在。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Those complex enough to reveal the genetics behind a trait 说"复杂到能揭示性状 背后基因"，原文却是"取决于单基因的简单情况更可靠"，方向相反。 B) 偷换概念 Those looking for traits responsible for certain diseases 抓住的是 a disease- causing trait——但原文里 "致病性状" 只是"为什么单基因检测可靠"的解释，不是"哪 一类检测可靠"。 C) 偷换概念 Those focusing on the specific questions being asked 把 the specific question you ask 直接搬来，但原文那一句讲的是"准确度取决于问题"，不是"针对特定问题的检 测更可靠"。 D) ✓ 正确 tests for traits that depend on a single gene ↔ Those looking for traits determined by a single gene 全篇只有 single gene 这一处出现"单基因"，且就配着 more reliable，预判和 D 完全 对齐，锁定 D。 从文章中我们了解到关于基因健康检测的什么信息？ A) 它们本身无法识别某些遗传性疾病。 B) 它们通常无法区分遗传因素和非遗传因素。 C) 它们无法独立识别大多数潜在疾病。 D) 它们无法区分生活方式的影响和环境的影响。

questions.q: What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage?
options: They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves.
They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors.
They cannot independently identify the majority of potential diseases.
They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage 问的是文章"告诉我们 什么"，属于事实查询，不是推断。

【拆句】What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage 句式为 "learn about X from Y"——从 Y 中了解到关于 X 的什么；about 后是话题，from 后是来源。结构平铺直 叙，无陷阱。 53. What do we learn about genetic health tests from the passage? A) They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves. B) They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors. C) They cannot independently identify the majority of potential diseases. D) They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment.

【定位】While certain rare diseases can be easily identified, most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone. 虽然某些罕见疾病能轻松识别出来，但大多数潜在的健康问题靠基因检测一项是查不出 来的。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 They are unable to identify certain hereditary diseases by themselves 用 certain （某些）替换原文的 most（多数）——原文恰恰说 certain rare diseases can be easily identified，让步从句中的 certain rare 反而是"能识别的"，A 把它颠倒了。 B) 无中生有 They are generally unable to separate genetic and non-genetic factors 凭空加 了"区分基因与非基因因素"这件事——原文只说健康状况受非基因因素影响，从未要求 基因检测"区分"两者。 C) ✓ 正确 most potential health conditions cannot be identified by genetic testing alone ↔ They cannot independently identify the majority of potential diseases predict 关键的"多数""靠它单独"两个限定词，C 选项用 the majority of 和 independently 一一对应，且主语"基因健康检测"一致，无任何过度信息。 D) 偷换概念 They cannot tell apart the impact of lifestyle and that of the environment 把 lifestyle 和 environment 单挑出来谈区分，但原文这两词只是 non-genetic factors, such as lifestyle, the environment, and many others 的举例，且 also 之后从未谈"区 分两者影响"。 是什么使得针对多因素特征的基因检测难以解读？ A) 确定每个单独基因作用的挑战。 B) 预测各种基因如何相互作用的难度。 C) 区分遗传因素和环境因素的难度。 D) 识别所涉及的数百个基因的巨大工作量。

questions.q: What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret?
options: The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene.
The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact.
The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones.
The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved.
questions.explain:
【判型】What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret 是 What makes X Y 的句式，问的是事实层面的原因，原文里有现成原因句。

【拆句】What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret 结构是 "make + 宾语 + 形容词"——"使...变得难以解读"。What 作主语，问的是导致这件难事的原因；to interpret 是后置不定式作形容词补足语。 54. What makes genetic tests for multi-factorial traits tricky to interpret? A) The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene. B) The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact. C) The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones. D) The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved.

【定位】A test can look at many genes at once, but it's difficult to predict how they will play together. 一次基因检测可以同时查看许多基因，但很难预测这些基因放在一起会怎么"协作"。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 The challenge in determining the role of each individual gene 把"每个单基因的作 用"塞进答案，但 each contributing a little to the outcome 只是顺带一提"每个贡献 一点"，原文并没有说"难以确定每个基因的作用"。 B) ✓ 正确 it's difficult to predict how they will play together ↔ The difficulty of foretelling how the various genes will interact 整篇文章只有 P6 这一句用了 difficult to predict 的结构，预判"基因互动难以预测"严 丝合缝地对应 B 选项的"预测基因如何相互作用的难度"，直接锁定。 C) 无中生有 The difficulty of telling genetic factors from environmental ones 编出"区分基因 因素与环境因素"这件事——原文只说"还要把非基因因素也考虑进去"，从未要求"区分 两者"。 D) 无中生有 The enormous work to identify the hundreds of genes involved 把焦点放到"识别 这几百个基因的庞大工作量"——原文 hundreds of genes 只是说数量大，没说"识别它 们工作量巨大"，也根本没说"工作量"才是"难解读"的原因。 文章关于预测性格或天赋的DNA检测说了什么？ A) 它们具有可供应用的坚实科学基础。 B) 它们有助于寻找浪漫伴侣。 C) 它们目前看起来并不乐观。 D) 它们目前没有任何意义。

questions.q: What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents?
options: They are solid scientific bases for application.
They are helpful in finding a romantic match.
They do not look promising at the moment.
They do not make any sense at present.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents——配 合选项里 do not look promising、do not make any sense 这种全是态度评价的格局，本 质是问作者对这件事的态度。
