【拆句】What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents 中 "DNA tests to predict ..." 的不定式 to predict 作 DNA tests 的后置定语，等于 "DNA tests that predict ..."——"用来预测人格或才能的 DNA 测试"。 55. What does the passage say about DNA tests to predict personality or talents? A) They are solid scientific bases for application. B) They are helpful in finding a romantic match. C) They do not look promising at the moment. D) They do not make any sense at present.

【定位】Tests that offer to find your perfect romantic match and those claiming to predict personality or talents based on your DNA are pure nonsense. At the moment, the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak. 那些声称能帮你找到完美恋爱对象的检测、以及那些号称能根据 DNA 预测性格或才能的检 测，都是纯粹的胡说八道。眼下，这些应用的科学依据要么压根不存在，要么薄弱得离谱。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 They are solid scientific bases for application 说"是坚实的科学依据"，原文恰好说 the scientific bases for these applications are non-existent or incredibly weak ——科学依据要么不存在要么极弱，方向完全相反。 B) 与原文相反 They are helpful in finding a romantic match 抓了原文里的另一个例子 find your perfect romantic match——但原文是把它当作"也是胡说"的反面例子，B 却说它"有帮 助"，立场反了。 C) 偷换概念 They do not look promising at the moment 译过来是"目前看起来不太有前景"—— 但原文是 pure nonsense（纯属胡扯），属于强烈否定，C 把它弱化成"前景不佳"这种 中性偏负的客气说法。 D) ✓ 正确 are pure nonsense ↔They do not make any sense at present At the moment ↔at present 预判"作者强烈否定"对应 do not make any sense；at present 又把 at the moment 这个时间限定带上了——D 一字不漏地把作者的核心态度搬过来了。

items.title: 2026年6月四级真题 第1套 阅读1
items.paperTitle: 2026年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 Is organic food worth the higher price? It's the classic grocery store dilemma. On the one hand, your family dinner table deserves only the best. On the other hand, your wallet can only stretch so far.

P2 Whether or not to buy organic is a personal decision, said Mike von Massow, professor of Food Agriculture.

P3 Science won't give a clear-cut answer to the question of whether organic food is "better". There are often trade-offs( 权衡) and answers become less definitive depending on the product under consideration.

P4 One thing is definitive: Organic and conventionally grown food are equally nutritious. From a nutrition point of view, there is no difference between organic and traditionally grown products.

P5 Organic products don't necessarily have fewer pesticides(杀虫剂)—in fact, they may have more. There is also no big difference between organic and non-organic products from a food-safety perspective. Even organic growers use pesticides. Testing shows little if any pesticide remains on conventionally grown products.

P6 In fact, organic farmers often use larger quantities of pesticide because they can only use the natural variety of insect-killers. Chemical pesticides generally kill a much wider range of pests(害虫) than any single natural pesticide.

P7 The use of animal waste in organic agriculture can also be a factor in the spread of bacteria like E. coli and salmonella. Over the past 10 years, Canada has seen more food-safety recalls for organic products, proportionally, than for conventional products.

P8 On the whole, organic agriculture may have a smaller environmental footprint. That's mostly because the risk of groundwater contamination from organic farming is lower. Organic farmers never use neonics, the controversial pesticides that have been linked to shrinking bee populations worldwide.

P9 Traditional agriculture has been making "dramatic improvements" to reduce its impact on the environment.

P10 It isn't a black-and-white picture, though.

P11 Organic farming is much less efficient when it comes to land use, although yields vary considerably depending on the crop.

P12 On the other hand, advocates of organic farming argue yields and efficiency could be significantly improved if the food industry devoted as much research and money to organic farming as it does conventional agriculture.

questions.q: What is the classic grocery store dilemma?
options: Whether or not one should eat organic food.
Whether or not one can stretch their wallet far.
Organic food costs more but it certainly tastes better.
One wants the best food but their budget is limited.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the classic grocery store dilemma? 没有 infer/suggest/imply 等推断标记，而 是直接询问文中某一表述指什么。

【拆句】What is the classic grocery store dilemma? 是一个简单的主系表疑问句，主干为 What is the dilemma，无否定、比较或从句陷阱。

【定位】On the one hand, your family dinner table deserves only the best. On the other hand, your wallet can only stretch so far. 一方面，你家餐桌上的人只配吃最好的；另一方面，你的钱包只能撑到这么多。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 A 项说'是否应该吃有机食品'，这是文章讨论的大话题，而非 the classic grocery store dilemma 所指的具体两难处境。 B) 以偏概全 B 项只提到'钱包能撑多远'，把原文预算受限的一面单独拿出来，却丢掉了'想要最好的食 物'这一面，不能完整解释 dilemma。 C) 无中生有 C 项说有机食品'当然更好吃'，但原文 P1 只提到' deserves only the best'，并未说明 best 指味道，更无 certainly tastes better 的依据。 D) ✓ 正确 your family dinner table deserves only the best ↔One wants the best food your wallet can only stretch so far ↔their budget is limited D 项把 On the one hand ... On the other hand ... 的两侧都概括进去，既提到'想要最 好的食物'，也提到'预算有限'。 46. What is the classic grocery store dilemma? A) Whether or not one should eat organic food. B) Whether or not one can stretch their wallet far. C) Organic food costs more but it certainly tastes better. D) One wants the best food but their budget is limited. 科学研究让我们了解到有机食品的哪些情况？ A) 它是否更好仍不确定。 B) 它是否更健康仍在研究之中。 C) 它是否比常规食品更有营养尚有争议。 D) 它是否会取代常规食品仍不清楚。

questions.q: What do we learn about organic food from science?
options: Whether it is any better remains uncertain.
Whether it is healthier is under consideration.
Whether it is more nutritious than conventional food is arguable.
Whether it is going to replace conventional food is still unclear.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn about organic food from science? 用 learn 提问，表面像细节，实则 要求把科学观点概括后推出。

【拆句】What do we learn about organic food from science? 主干为 What do we learn about A from B，about 引出对象，from 引出信息来源，无复杂从句。

【定位】Science won't give a clear-cut answer to the question of whether organic food is 'better'. 科学不会对'有机食品是否更好'这个问题给出一个明确的答案。

items.paperTitle: 2026年6月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
items.passage:
P1 It is still controversial whether we are fundamentally generous or selfish and whether these tendencies are shaped by our genes or environment.

P2 Some evidence points to humans being born cooperative. At later stages in life we routinely work together to reach goals and help out in times of need.

P3 Yet instances of selfish behavior are also plenty. One recent study tested people's willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good. It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating. The benefit may be short-lived, however. Another study showed that players who cooperated did better in the long run.

P4 It seems that human nature supports both pro-social and selfish traits(特征). Genetic studies have made some progress toward identifying their biological roots. By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors. In these twin studies, identical and non-identical twins are asked, for example, to split a sum of money with a peer. Such studies often also rely on careful psychological assessments and DNA analysis.

P5 Other work highlights specific genes as key players. My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic(利他的) behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers.

P6 According to evolutionary scientists, cooperative behavior may have evolved first among relatives to promote the continuation of their genetic line. As communities diversified, mutual support could have broadened to include individuals not linked by blood. Another possibility is that humans cooperate to gain some advantage, such as boosting reputation. Finally, evolutionary processes take place at the group level. Groups of highly cooperative individuals have higher chances of survival because they can work together to reach goals that are unattainable to less cooperative groups.

P7 Yet almost no behavior is entirely genetic, even among identical twins. Culture, schooling and parenting are important determinants of cooperation. Thus, the degree to which we act cooperatively or selfishly is unique to each individual and depends on a variety of genetic and environmental influences.

questions.q: What is the finding of one recent study about being selfish?
options: It may bring certain benefits in the short term.
It usually yields more disadvantages than advantages.
It serves individual interest rather than a collective's.
It may give way to cooperating in the long run.
questions.explain:
【判型】题干What is the finding of ...?直接询问某研究的客观结论，属于对文中具体信息的查找。

【拆句】题干What is the finding of one recent study about being selfish?是主系表特殊疑问 句：What（表语）+ is（系动词）+ the finding of one recent study about being selfish（主语），整体询问关于 being selfish 的研究发现。

【定位】One recent study tested people's willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good. It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating. The benefit may be short-lived, however. 一项近期研究测试了人们是否愿意搁置自私利益以实现更大的善。研究发现，自私比合作更 有利。然而，这种好处可能是短暂的。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating ↔bring certain benefits The benefit may be short-lived, however. ↔in the short term It may bring certain benefits in the short term.把原文的'more advantageous'和'short-lived'分别同义替换为'bring certain benefits'和'in the short term'，且保留了may的委婉语气。 B) 与原文相反 It usually yields more disadvantages than advantages.与原文'being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating'直接矛盾。 C) 偷换概念 It serves individual interest rather than a collective's.把实验设计中的'selfish interests'和'greater good'篡改为研究结论，但原文并未说研究发现自私服务于个人而 非集体。 D) 张冠李戴 It may give way to cooperating in the long run.借用了原文'in the long run'，但 把'players who cooperated did better in the long run'说成'selfish may give way to cooperating'，改变了主语与语义。 研究人员通过研究同卵和异卵双胞胎发现了什么？ A) 两者在基因数量上存在极大差异。 B) 一个人的行为在很大程度上由其遗传特征决定。 C) 一个人的生物学根源可以通过其基因确定。 D) 他们在行为模式上彼此不同。

【定位】By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors. 通过比较基因几乎100%相同的同卵双胞胎和约一半基因相同的异卵双胞胎，研究人员发现 了行为受基因影响的压倒性证据。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 They are overwhelmingly different in the amounts of genes.将原文对双胞胎基因共 享比例的客观描述改写成研究结论，且改变了比较对象。 B) ✓ 正确 genetic effects on behaviors ↔behavior is largely determined by their genetic traits overwhelming evidence ↔largely determined One's behavior is largely determined by their genetic traits.是'overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors'的同义概 括，'largely'与'overwhelming'在程度上对应。 C) 偷换概念 One's biological roots can be identified by their genes.中的'biological roots'来自 本段背景句，而'can be identified'夸大了研究进展，不是双胞胎研究的直接发现。 D) 无中生有 They differ from each other in their behavior patterns.在原文没有对应信息，原文关 注的是基因对行为的影响，而非双胞胎行为模式之间的差异。 作者及其同事在最近的研究中发现了什么？ A) 学龄前儿童一种与基因相关的自私行为。 B) 决定一个人利他行为的关键因素。 C) 一种与利他行为相关的特定基因。 D) 基因在塑造一个人的性格方面所发挥的作用。

【拆句】题干What did the author and colleagues identify in their recent research?是what引导 的特殊疑问句，主语the author and colleagues，谓语did...identify，in their recent research为范围状语，询问近期研究中识别出的对象。 53. C) A specific gene associated with altruistic behavior. D) Roles played by genes in shaping one's character.

【定位】My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic(利他的) behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers. 我和我的同事最近识别出一种与利他行为相关的基因，并发现它的某种变体与学龄前儿童的 自私行为有关。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 A gene-related selfish behavior in preschool children.只截取了定位句后半句，忽略 了作者首先'identified a gene linked to altruistic behavior'这一核心对象。 B) 过度推断 Key factors that determine one's altruistic behavior.用复数'Key factors'和'determine'，把原文仅识别的一个基因及其关联上升为决定利他行为的多个 关键因素，过度推断。 C) ✓ 正确 identified a gene linked to altruistic(利他的) behavior ↔ A specific gene associated with altruistic behavior. a gene ↔A specific gene A specific gene associated with altruistic behavior.将'identified'转换 为'associated'，'a gene'具体化为'a specific gene'，其余成分一致。 D) 过度推断 Roles played by genes in shaping one's character.用'shaping one's character'替换 了原文'altruistic behavior'，并把范围扩大到'genes in shaping character'，属于上位 的过度泛化。 关于合作行为，进化科学家告诉了我们什么？ A) 它最初可能起源于有血缘关系的个体之间。 B) 它可能导致了群体的多样化。 C) 它有助于在有血缘关系的人之间建立关系。 D) 它保证实现原本无法实现的目标。

items.paperTitle: 2026年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed.

P2 It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings.

P3 Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. They were then asked why they think they did so well.

P4 The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender.

P5 A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

options: They systematically underestimate their chances of success.
They tend to attribute their achievements to good fortune.

They generally rely on luck and chance for success.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do we learn from the passage about people who suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon? 是问'关于某类人我们能了解到什么'，答案应在文中找对该类人的 直接描述。 46. B) They tend to attribute their achievements to good fortune. C) They seem to live in constant fear of being deceived. D) They generally rely on luck and chance for success.

【拆句】What do we learn from the passage about people who suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon? 是主谓宾结构的特殊疑问句；主干为 What do we learn， about 短语限定讨论对象，who 定语从句修饰 people，整体无否定、比较等陷阱。

【定位】They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. 他们认为任何成功都归因于外部环境，或者仅仅是运气和机遇。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 选项说 systematically underestimate their chances of success，但原文是 systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance，低估的对 象从'自己和自身表现'被偷换为'成功几率'，语义不一致。 B) ✓ 正确 any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance ↔ tend to attribute their achievements to good fortune tend to attribute their achievements to good fortune 准确对应 any success is due to... luck and chance，只是把'成功归因于运气'换了说法。 C) 偷换概念 选项 live in constant fear of being deceived 利用了原文 live in constant fear 和 deception 两个词，但原文是害怕'自己的欺骗被揭穿'，不是害怕'被别人欺骗'。 D) 过度推断 选项 generally rely on luck and chance for success 说患者'依靠'运气获得成功，但原 文 any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance 只是说他 们'认为'成功归因于运气，并非真的去依靠运气。 拥有适度反思和自我怀疑的人往往会做什么？ A) 把所有的成功都归功于努力工作。 B) 努力使自己的技能臻于完善。 C) 避免凭冲动行事。 D) 表现得更好。

questions.q: What do people with a healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt tend to do?
options: Credit all their successes to hard work.
Strive hard to perfect their skills.
Refrain from acting on impulse.
Deliver a better performance.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do people with a healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt tend to do? 询问 具备某特征的人群 tend to do 什么，属于对文中具体行为信息的提取。

【拆句】What do people with a healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt tend to do? 中 with 短语作后置定语修饰 people，tend to do 询问习惯性结果，句子平直，无复杂从句。

【定位】A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. 适度的反思和自我怀疑能够防止一个人冲动行事。 47. What do people with a healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt tend to do? A) Credit all their successes to hard work. B) Strive hard to perfect their skills. C) Refrain from acting on impulse. D) Deliver a better performance.

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 选项 Credit all their successes to hard work 说健康反思者把所有成功归功于努力，但 原文 there are people who are permanently plagued by... self-doubt 之后说的是 IP 患者不把成功归因于自身 skill or hard work，并未说健康反思者就会归因于努力。 B) 无中生有 选项 Strive hard to perfect their skills 在原文关于健康反思者的描述中没有对应信息， 属于凭空添加。 C) ✓ 正确 protect a person from acting impulsively ↔Refrain from acting on impulse Refrain from acting on impulse 与 protect a person from acting impulsively 语义 等值，只是从'被保护不冲动'转换为'主动克制不冲动'。 D) 答非所问 选项 Deliver a better performance 暗示健康反思者会表现更好，但原文 despite delivering a good performance 是修饰 IP 患者的，与健康反思者无比较关系。 根据哈雷-维滕贝格马丁·路德大学心理学家的说法，遭受冒名顶替现象困扰的人常常会怎么做？ A) 把自己的成就归功于他人。 B) 否认自己经测量得出的实际智力水平。 C) 声称自己对自身能力充满信心。 D) 给客观评定的表现打低分。

questions.q: What do Impostor Phenomenon sufferers often do according to psychologists from Martin Luther
options: Attribute their accomplishments to others.
Deny their actual measured intelligence.
Claim to have confidence in their own abilities.
Mark down their objectively rated performance.
questions.explain:
【判型】What do Impostor Phenomenon sufferers often do according to psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg? 问的是某研究发现中患者'经常做什么'，答 案应出自研究结论句。

【拆句】What do Impostor Phenomenon sufferers often do according to psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg? 主干为 What do sufferers do，according to 引出信息来源，句子结构简单，无否定比较。

【定位】people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. 有表现出冒名顶替现象倾向的人会贬低他们客观测得的表现，并把积极结果归因于运气等外 部原因，而非他们自己的能力。 48. What do Impostor Phenomenon sufferers often do according to psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg? A) Attribute their accomplishments to others. B) Deny their actual measured intelligence. C) Claim to have confidence in their own abilities. D) Mark down their objectively rated performance.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 选项 Attribute their accomplishments to others 说患者把成就归因于'他人'，但原文 attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance 说的是'运气等 外部原因'，external causes 不等于 others。 B) 偷换概念 选项 Deny their actual measured intelligence 说患者否认实际测得的智力，但原文 the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance 只是说两者无关，并未说患者否认智力。 C) 与原文相反 选项 Claim to have confidence in their own abilities 说患者声称对自己能力有信心， 但原文明确说患者把成功归因于外部原因 'but not to their own abilities'，说明他们并 不信任自己的能力。 D) ✓ 正确 devalue their objectively measured performance ↔ Mark down their objectively rated performance Mark down their objectively rated performance 几乎是 devalue their objectively measured performance 的同义改写，只是换了动词和形容词。 当一个人长期低估自己的能力时，会发生什么？ A) 他们会把注意力集中在外部因素上。 B) 他们会害怕可能产生的后果。 C) 他们会依靠好运取得成功。 D) 他们会不断提高自己的技能。

questions.q: What happens when a person permanently underestimates their own abilities?
options: They will focus their attention on external factors.
They will be fearful of potential consequences.
They will count on good fortune for success.
They will keep improving their own skills.
questions.explain:
【判型】What happens when a person permanently underestimates their own abilities? 询问 某种情况下会发生什么，答案在原文的条件-结果句中。

【拆句】What happens when a person permanently underestimates their own abilities? 中 when 引导时间/条件状语从句，主句省略了 happen 的实体主语，整体为简单因果结构。

【定位】A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. 长期低估自己的能力常常伴随着一种恐惧：这种所谓的智力欺骗迟早会被揭穿，并且他们会 为此付出代价。 49. What happens when a person permanently underestimates their own abilities? A) They will focus their attention on external factors. B) They will be fearful of potential consequences. C) They will count on good fortune for success. D) They will keep improving their own skills.

【选项】A) 答非所问 选项 focus their attention on external factors 描述的是患者对成功的外部归因，属于 第 46、48 题的内容，不是长期低估能力带来的结果。 B) ✓ 正确 the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this ↔be fearful of potential consequences be fearful of potential consequences 把原文 '害怕欺骗被揭穿、害怕付出代价' 概括 为'害怕潜在后果'，符合同义概括的替换方式。 C) 过度推断 选项 count on good fortune for success 说患者'指望'好运获得成功，但原文只是说他 们认为成功归因于好运，并非真的把成功寄托于好运。 D) 无中生有 选项 keep improving their own skills 在文中没有对应信息，属于用常识捏造的积极 结果。 美国心理学家 Pauline Clance 和 Suzanne Imes 对遭受冒名顶替现象困扰的人作何评价？ A) 他们更容易患抑郁症。 B) 他们很少能够充分发挥自己的潜力。 C) 他们会患上精神疾病。 D) 他们有一天会付出更高的代价。

questions.q: What did US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes say about Impostor Phenomenon
options: They are more liable to have depression.
They seldom realise their potential fully.
They will develop mental illnesses.
They will pay higher prices one day.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes say about Impostor Phenomenon sufferers? 问特定人物对患者的说法，属于对文中观点句的提取。

【拆句】What did US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes say about Impostor Phenomenon sufferers? 是过去时特殊疑问句，say about 后接对象，结构简单；注意 did 提示事件发生在过去。

【定位】However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression. 然而，患有冒名顶替现象的人表现出更高的抑郁易感性。 50. What did US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes say about Impostor Phenomenon sufferers? A) They are more liable to have depression. B) They seldom realise their potential fully. C) They will develop mental illnesses. D) They will pay higher prices one day.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression ↔ They are more liable to have depression They are more liable to have depression 准确对应 people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression，把'易感性高'换成'更容易患上'。 B) 过度推断 选项 They seldom realise their potential fully 说患者很少充分发挥潜力，原文只提到 他们低估自己和害怕被揭穿，没有明确说他们潜力发挥不足。 C) 与原文相反 选项 They will develop mental illnesses 说患者会发展成精神疾病，但原文 The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness 明确说它不是精神疾病。 D) 偷换概念 选项 They will pay higher prices one day 把原文 they will pay the price for this 中 的 the price 改成了 higher prices，添加了比较含义，改变了原意。

items.title: 2026年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读2
items.paperTitle: 2026年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
items.passage:
P1 Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language.

P2 One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other.

P3 Music is tied to specific perceptual(感知的), mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics(美感) (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos).

P4 There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.

questions.q: In what way is music important?
options: It is able to create novel and extraordinary emotions.
It has the power to unite people throughout the world.
It allows different cultural groups to sing in harmony.
It is the only language favored by all peoples of the world.
questions.explain:
【判型】In what way is music important? 用 In what way 询问音乐重要性的具体表现，属于对文 中具体信息的考查。

【拆句】In what way is music important? 为简单疑问句，主干是 music is important，In what way 询问方式或方面，无否定、比较等陷阱。 51. In what way is music important? A) It is able to create novel and extraordinary emotions. B) It has the power to unite people throughout the world. C) It allows different cultural groups to sing in harmony. D) It is the only language favored by all peoples of the world.

【定位】It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. 音乐在全球范围内都极为重要，并且有可能将人们凝聚在一起，实现和平与和谐。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 选项 It is able to create novel and extraordinary emotions 把原文 This can create extraordinary results 中的 extraordinary results 偷换为 extraordinary emotions， 并新增 novel，改变了原文对象。 B) ✓ 正确 has the potential to bring people together ↔has the power to unite people across the globe ↔throughout the world 原文说音乐有潜力将全球人民凝聚在和平与和谐中，It has the power to unite people throughout the world 用 power 替换 potential，unite 替换 bring together， throughout the world 替换 across the globe，整体语义完全一致。 C) 过度推断 原文 bring people together in peace and harmony 中的 harmony 是比喻性的和平 和谐，选项 It allows different cultural groups to sing in harmony 把它具体化为 '唱 歌和谐'，并添加 sing，属于过度具体化。 D) 过度推断 原文 Music is a universal language 只说音乐是通用语言，并未说它是 the only language favored by all peoples of the world，only 与 favored 均无出处。 作者为什么喜欢观看来自不同文化背景的音乐家一起表演？ A) 他们的音乐经历可以进行比较。 B) 可以创造出一种新的语言。 C) 他们独特的技能可以得到展示。 D) 可以取得奇妙的成果。

questions.q: Why does the author like to see musicians from different cultures perform together?
options: Their musical experience can be compared.
A novel language can be created.
Their unique skills can be displayed.
Fantastic results can be achieved.
questions.explain:
【判型】Why does the author like to see musicians from different cultures perform together? 用 Why 询问作者喜欢某现象的原因，属于因果类细节题。

【拆句】Why does the author like to see musicians from different cultures perform together? 为 why 引导的特殊疑问句，主干是 the author likes to see musicians perform together，无复杂从句。 52. Why does the author like to see musicians from different cultures perform together? A) Their musical experience can be compared. B) A novel language can be created. C) Their unique skills can be displayed. D) Fantastic results can be achieved.

【定位】One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. 我在音乐中最喜欢的经历之一，就是看到来自不同文化的音乐家聚到一起、作为一个团体表 演。当每种文化都为这个团体带来自己独特的特质时，一种全新的声音就产生了。这能创造 出非凡的成果。

【选项】A) 无中生有 选项 Their musical experience can be compared 提出 '比较经历'，但原文 P1 只描述 作者喜欢观看这种表演，未涉及比较。 B) 偷换概念 原文 an entirely new sound is achieved 说的是产生全新声音，选项 A novel language can be created 把 sound 偷换为 language。 C) 偷换概念 原文 each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group 强调文化特质被带入 团体以创造新声音，选项 Their unique skills can be displayed 把 qualities 窄化为 skills，并把 brings 改为 displayed，重心从 '共同创造' 偏移为 '展示个人技能'。 D) ✓ 正确 This can create extraordinary results. ↔Fantastic results can be achieved. an entirely new sound is achieved ↔Fantastic results can be achieved. 作者喜欢跨文化合作的原因在 This can create extraordinary results，Fantastic results can be achieved 用被动语态和 fantastic 同义改写 create extraordinary results，准确回答原因。 文章对五声音阶作了怎样的说明？ A) 它存在于世界各地的音乐中。 B) 它有助于理解音乐。 C) 它是音乐家创作的基础。 D) 它是普通人与之建立联系的一种媒介。

questions.q: What does the passage say about the pentatonic scale?
options: It is present in music all around the world.
It is helpful to understanding music.
It is the basis for musicians' creation.
It is a medium for ordinary people to relate.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about the pentatonic scale? 直接问文中关于某对象的具体 说法，属于典型细节题。

【拆句】What does the passage say about the pentatonic scale? 为 what 引导的特殊疑问句， about 的宾语 pentatonic scale 是定位核心，结构简单。 53. What does the passage say about the pentatonic scale? A) It is present in music all around the world. B) It is helpful to understanding music. C) It is the basis for musicians' creation. D) It is a medium for ordinary people to relate.

【定位】This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. 这种音阶可以在世界各地的音乐中找到，包括美洲原住民、非洲人和亚洲人的音乐。它也存 在于流行音乐、蓝调、爵士乐和摇滚乐中。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 This scale can be found in music everywhere ↔It is present in music all around the world. including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians ↔ It is present in music all around the world. 原文 This scale can be found in music everywhere 与 It is present in music all around the world 语义完全等值，仅表达方式不同。 B) 过度推断 原文 musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other 说的是音乐 家相互理解，选项 It is helpful to understanding music 把对象扩大为 '理解音乐'，范 围过宽。 C) 过度推断 原文 a medium through which they can relate 说五声音阶是交流的媒介，选项 It is the basis for musicians' creation 把 medium 提升为 basis for creation，夸大了其 地位。 D) 偷换概念 原文 musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate 的主体是 musicians，选项 It is a medium for ordinary people to relate 把主 体换成 ordinary people。 音乐在人们生活中的根本作用是什么？ A) 将人们团结在一起。 B) 展示他们的身份。 C) 表达他们的情感。 D) 使他们保持愉悦。

questions.q: What is the fundamental role of music in people's life?
options: To bring them together.
To show their identity.
To express their emotions.
To keep them entertained.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the fundamental role of music in people's life? 用 What is the ... role 询问音 乐的根本作用，属于细节题。

【拆句】What is the fundamental role of music in people's life? 为 what 引导的特殊疑问句，of music in people's life 是后置定语，修饰 role，结构平铺直叙。 54. What is the fundamental role of music in people's life? A) To bring them together. B) To show their identity. C) To express their emotions. D) To keep them entertained.

【定位】Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. 音乐本质上用于表达或改变情绪。

【选项】A) 答非所问 原文 has the potential to bring people together 与 it has the power to unite us 确 实是音乐的作用，但题干问的是 fundamental role，答案应是 essentially serves to express or change emotions，A 项答非所问。 B) 无中生有 选项 To show their identity 提出 '展示身份'，但原文从未提到 identity 或相关概念。 C) ✓ 正确 Music essentially serves to express or change emotions ↔To express their emotions. 原文 Music essentially serves to express or change emotions 中，express or change emotions 是音乐的本质功能，To express their emotions 提取了其中 express emotions 这一核心，对应 fundamental role。 D) 以偏概全 原文 Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun 提到娱乐是音乐 的用途之一，但选项 To keep them entertained 把它提升为根本作用，忽略了 express or change emotions 的核心地位。 世界各地的音乐在哪一方面相似？ A) 人们对它作出反应的方式。 B) 它在社会中所发挥的作用。 C) 它带给人们的快乐。 D) 人们利用它的方式。

questions.q: In what aspect is music similar throughout the world?
options: The way people respond to it.
The role it plays in society.
The joy it brings to people.
The way it is made use of.
questions.explain:
【判型】In what aspect is music similar throughout the world? 用 In what aspect 询问全球音 乐相似的具体方面，属于细节题。

【拆句】In what aspect is music similar throughout the world? 为 in what aspect 引导的特殊 疑问句，主干是 music is similar，throughout the world 限定范围，无复杂结构。

【定位】Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. 尽管每种文化都有自己独特的音乐风格和处理方式，但你会发现音乐背后的目的总体上是 十分相似的。你使用音乐的任何方式，几乎可以肯定其他文化也以完全相同的方式使用过 音乐。 55. In what aspect is music similar throughout the world? A) The way people respond to it. B) The role it plays in society. C) The joy it brings to people. D) The way it is made use of.

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文 every other culture has used music in the very same way 说的是 '使用' 音乐的 方式相同，选项 The way people respond to it 把它改为 '回应' 音乐的方式，动作性质 改变。 B) 以偏概全 原文 the purposes behind music are very similar across the board 强调使用目的/ 方式相似，选项 The role it plays in society 把它扩大为 '社会角色'，范围过宽且未突出 '方式'。 C) 以偏概全 原文 Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun 提到 joy 是娱 乐用途的一部分，选项 The joy it brings to people 把它提升为音乐全球相似性的方 面，范围过窄。 D) ✓ 正确 the purposes behind music are very similar across the board ↔The way it is made use of. every other culture has used music in the very same way ↔The way it is made use of. 原文指出不同文化音乐的目的和使用方式非常相似，The way it is made use of 准确概 括了 purposes behind music 与 used music in the same way 两者。

items.passage:
P1 Disgust is a universal human emotion. One type of disgust is called physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us, such as raw meat or insects. Children experience physical disgust from a very early age, but do not achieve an understanding of the concept until they are around four years old.

P2 Some researchers maintain that there is another type of disgust, called moral disgust, that protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong. Examples of moral disgust are stealing, lying or cheating.

P3 However, not all academics think that moral disgust really exists. Some say that when we refer to disgust in relation to moral issues, we are using disgust as a metaphor(隐喻), and what we are feeling is in reality anger.

P4 If moral disgust appears quite late in development, it makes sense to think that there is actually a social component to it. Children learn about emotions in many different ways. Of special relevance are parents-children conversations about emotions. Indeed, children whose parents talk about emotions often have a better emotional understanding than children whose parents do not discuss emotions often.

P5 However, there are no studies that have examined how parents and children talk about disgust. This is what we set up to examine in our study.

P6 We asked 68 English-speaking mothers and their four-, six- or eight-year-old children to discuss some stories about moral and physical disgust. Our preliminary findings show mothers and children do talk about disgust, but mainly about physical disgust and not so much about moral disgust.

P7 When we asked mothers and children to discuss moral issues, such as whether it is OK to play with a child who has stolen someone else's snack, they linked this type of moral wrongdoing with the emotion of anger and not disgust.

P8 Does this mean that moral disgust does not exist? Some researchers suggest moral disgust exists in adults. Our findings suggest that moral disgust is either understood at a later age or is only used metaphorically, if at all, in children as old as eight years.

questions.q: What does the passage tell us about physical disgust?
options: It is an emotion as contrasted with thoughts.
It is a concept beyond children's understanding.
It is a mechanism to keep us from being harmed.
It is an experience gained from any form of danger.
questions.explain:

【定位】One type of disgust is called physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us, such as raw meat or insects. 厌恶感的一种类型被称为生理厌恶，它保护我们不去吃或触碰可能对我们有危险的东西，比 如生肉或昆虫。

【选项】A) 以偏概全 It tends to appear in various forms of wrongdoing.把Examples of moral disgust are stealing, lying or cheating.中的举例包装成"moral disgust本身以多种形式出现"， 混淆了"触发它的行为"与"它本身"。 B) 无中生有 It is just as annoying to people as physical disgust.使用just as...as结构，但原文从 未比较两种厌恶的annoying程度，也未评价其是否annoying。 C) 张冠李戴 It is a term used by common folk to describe anger.源于Some say that when we refer to disgust in relation to moral issues, we are using disgust as a metaphor(隐 喻), and what we are feeling is in reality anger.，但该观点是some academics而非 some researchers，且common folk缩小了原句we的范围。 D) ✓ 正确 protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong ↔ It stops people from doing anything morally wrong. It stops people from doing anything morally wrong.与protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong.在语义场和语法结构上均对应， 是正确项。 为什么道德厌恶在儿童的发展过程中出现得相当晚？ A) 它需要通过社会互动来学习。 B) 他们对其学习过程几乎没有控制力。 C) 它对他们来说过于复杂，难以掌握。 D) 他们的父母很少谈论情绪。

【拆句】Why does moral disgust appear quite late in children's development?是why引导的特 殊疑问句，主语moral disgust，谓语appear，状语quite late in children's development；询问原因，需在定位句附近找因果解释。

【定位】If moral disgust appears quite late in development, it makes sense to think that there is actually a social component to it. Children learn about emotions in many different ways. 如果道德厌恶在成长过程中出现得相当晚，那么认为它实际上具有社会成分是合理的。儿童 以多种方式学习情绪。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 social component to it. Children learn about emotions in many different ways ↔ It needs to be learnt through social interactions. It needs to be learnt through social interactions.是原文因果链的一步推理，既未跳 跃也未添加新信息。 B) 无中生有 They have little control over its learning process.引入control概念，但原文Children learn about emotions in many different ways只说学习方式多，未涉及控制程度。 C) 过度推断 It is too complex for them to acquire.用too...to结构把原文的"late"和"social component"臆断为复杂度问题，原文未出现complex或acquire difficulty。 D) 与原文相反 Their parents seldom talk about emotions.与children whose parents talk about emotions often have a better emotional understanding than children whose parents do not discuss emotions often.直接相反，原文强调父母经常谈情绪。 作者和他的同事想在实验中考察什么？ A) 父母会告诉孩子哪些反对道德不当行为的话。 B) 父母和孩子会把道德不当行为与什么联系起来。 C) 4岁、6岁和8岁的儿童如何看待道德厌恶。 D) 父母和孩子之间如何谈论厌恶。

【定位】However, there are no studies that have examined how parents and children talk about disgust. This is what we set up to examine in our study. 然而，还没有研究考察过父母和孩子如何谈论厌恶。这正是我们研究要考察的问题。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 What parents tell children against moral wrongdoing.把how parents and children talk about disgust中的talk about disgust替换为tell children against moral wrongdoing，范围收窄且改变了话题。 B) 答非所问 What parents and children link moral wrongdoing to.对应的是they linked this type of moral wrongdoing with the emotion of anger and not disgust.，这是实验 结果，不是作者想考察的问题。 C) 偷换概念 How moral disgust is seen by children aged 4, 6 and 8.把four-, six- or eight-year- old children中的年龄信息放大为研究核心，但原文研究的是父母与孩子如何谈 disgust，而非儿童如何看待moral disgust。 D) ✓ 正确 how parents and children talk about disgust ↔ How disgust is discussed between parents and children. How disgust is discussed between parents and children.与how parents and children talk about disgust. This is what we set up to examine in our study.逐成分 对应，完全等值。 从作者和他的同事的研究结果中，我们可以推断出关于道德厌恶的什么信息？ A) 这是一个儿童几乎无法理解的概念。 B) 八岁以下的儿童很少有道德厌恶。 C) 这是大多数父母与孩子交谈时使用的一个术语。 D) 它存在于具有强烈正义感的成年人身上。

items.passage:
P1 After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. As a result, we act more honestly around them, according to a recent study in Nature.

P2 Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal(相互的). Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn't know you at all. Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social ties are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us.

P3 In a series of lab-based studies, this is exactly what the researchers found. When we know about strangers, we erroneously think they also know about us. But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. The team developed leaflets(传单) containing fairly ordinary information about local community police officers, such as their favourite food, hobbies, or reasons for joining the police force. They then sent out these leaflets to every apartment in a number of housing developments in disadvantaged areas. The officers themselves also dropped off cards to local residents containing similar information.

P4 Two months later, the researchers surveyed residents at these housing developments as well as control areas that did not receive leaflets or outreach cards. Residents were asked to imagine that they had committed a crime and how likely it would be that local officers would find out about it. They also rated how well the officers in the area knew them.

P5 The team found that residents of the developments that had received the leaflets believed it more likely that local officers would find out about illegal activity than residents of the control areas. Even more strikingly, the team found that immediately after the leaflet distribution, there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments.

questions.q: What is the finding of a recent study in Nature?
options: People are more honest with those who know them than with total strangers.
People we want to have detailed information about are keen to know about us.
People who get to know about a person wrongly assume the person knows them too.
People who are familiar with each other tend to behave honestly in their everyday dealings.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the finding of a recent study in Nature? 直接要求提取 recent study in Nature 的具体结论，不涉及全文主旨或作者态度。

【拆句】What is the finding of a recent study in Nature? 是主系表结构的特殊疑问句，主语为 the finding of a recent study in Nature，结构平铺直叙，无隐藏否定或比较陷阱。 51. What is the finding of a recent study in Nature? A) People are more honest with those who know them than with total strangers. B) People we want to have detailed information about are keen to know about us. C) People who get to know about a person wrongly assume the person knows them too. D) People who are familiar with each other tend to behave honestly in their everyday dealings.

【定位】After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. 在了解到一个陌生人的一些细节后，我们错误地认为他们也了解我们。

【选项】A) 比较结构警惕对象与方向 People are more honest with those who know them than with total strangers. 把 原文的诚实对象从陌生人偷换成熟人，并将比较对象反向设置。 B) 无中生有 People we want to have detailed information about are keen to know about us. 中的 want 与 keen 是原文没有的主观意愿，属于无中生有。 C) ✓ 正确 After finding out details about a stranger ↔People who get to know about a person we mistakenly think that they also know about us ↔ wrongly assume the person knows them too People who get to know about a person wrongly assume the person knows them too. 与 After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. 在语义上完全等价，仅做了代词和词汇替换。 D) 偷换概念 People who are familiar with each other tend to behave honestly in their everyday dealings. 将原文的 stranger 替换为 familiar with each other，把研究对象 从陌生人之间的错觉改为熟人之间的日常行为。 关于社会关系是相互的这一假设，文章是怎么说的？ A) 它是特例，而不是惯例。 B) 它并非在每种情况下都成立。 C) 它不适用于复杂的关系。 D) 在单向社会关系中，这一假设更加准确。

What does the passage say about the assumption that social relationships are reciprocal? A) It is more the exception than the rule. B) It does not hold true in every situation. C) It does not apply to complex relationships. D) It is more accurate in one-sided social ties.

【定位】Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal. Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn't know you at all. 过去的研究发现，我们倾向于认为社会关系是相互的。大多数时候这一假设是准确的：你视 为朋友的人通常也视你为朋友。但有时社会关系更单向：例如，你可能了解到一个根本不认 识你的陌生人的某些事情。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 It is more the exception than the rule. 表示互惠假设多为例外，但原文说 Most of the time 是准确的，因此该选项与原文相反。 B) ✓ 正确 Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided ↔It does not hold true in every situation. It does not hold true in every situation. 没有绝对化，也没有扩大范围，恰好对应 Most of the time... But sometimes... 的语义。 C) 无中生有 It does not apply to complex relationships. 提到复杂关系，但原文只讨论 one- sided ties，并未对关系复杂程度分类。 D) 与原文相反 It is more accurate in one-sided social ties. 与原文相反，原文指出 one-sided ties 正是假设不准确的例外情况。 Anuj Shah 和 Michael LaForest 想 выяс清关于社会关系是相互的这一看法的什么问题？ A) 它是否可以消除对社会关系的误解。 B) 它是否有助于发展自己与陌生人的关系。 C) 它是否有助于加强人际关系。 D) 它是否可能导致对陌生人的错误假设。

【拆句】What did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest want to find out about the belief that social relationships are reciprocal? 中 that social relationships are reciprocal 为同位语 从句，修饰 belief，整体询问过去的研究目的。 53. 【定位】Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social relationships are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us. 研究者 Anuj Shah 和 Michael LaForest 想知道，我们相信社会关系是互惠的这种倾向，是 否会让我们误以为一个陌生人确实认识我们。

options: During lab-based studies.

【拆句】When did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest find something really interesting in their research? 为 when 引导的特殊疑问句，主语为研究者，谓语为 find something really interesting，结构清晰。 54. When did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest find something really interesting in their research? A) During lab-based studies. B) During a field experiment. C) While investigating local residents' crime. D) While talking to police officers nearby.

【定位】But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. 但真正有趣的发现出现在研究者走出实验室、开展实地实验的时候。

【选项】A) 转折后的内容权重高于转折前 During lab-based studies. 对应的是前文提到的实验室研究，而原文用 But 转折指出真 正有趣的发现来自 field experiment。 B) ✓ 正确 when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment ↔ During a field experiment. During a field experiment. 与 when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. 在时间上完全对应，是对原文的精确概括。 C) 张冠李戴 While investigating local residents' crime. 对应的是第4段中居民被问及犯罪的调查环 节，而非第3段中 really interesting finding 发生的时机。 D) 偷换概念 While talking to police officers nearby. 中的 talking 是原文未描述的行为，警察只是 发放传单和卡片，并未与居民交谈。 在研究所涉及的住宅开发项目周边地区发生了什么？ A) 这些地区的犯罪案件少于对照住宅项目周边地区。 B) 这些地区见证了非法活动更快地被遏制。 C) 当地警方比以前更快地回应了犯罪投诉。 D) 当地警方与那里的居民相处得比与其他地区的居民更好。

items.title: Meetings on the Move
items.passage:
Ask a group of office workers to describe their most {{1}} meetings and few will mention a conference room. The ones they remember tend to be conversations that happened while moving: on a walk to a nearby cafe or around a city block. That observation has led some managers to {{2}} the traditional seated discussion with a walking meeting, in which colleagues talk side by side rather than facing each other across a table.

Supporters insist the change is more than a fashion. Walking gives the body a steady rhythm, and that rhythm appears to {{3}} the grip of the usual workplace routine. Ideas that might have been ignored are more likely to be voiced. Because nobody is typing, the exchange becomes more {{4}}: people listen, pause, and answer in full sentences instead of firing off quick replies.

The arrangement also shifts the balance of power. In a conference room whoever sits at the head of the table tends to dominate, but outdoors that hierarchy {{5}}. Quieter members find it easier to {{6}} to the discussion, and a junior employee may speak as freely as a director. Difficult news, some say, is delivered more honestly on a footpath.

The method is not suitable for everything. A {{7}} budget needs a spreadsheet, and a complex plan needs diagrams that nobody can {{8}} while crossing a street. Weather is another {{9}} consideration, and long routes may leave out colleagues with {{10}} mobility. Experienced organisers therefore keep walks short, choose flat paths, and reserve the format for informal thinking. Used with care, a walk can turn a dull update into a conversation.

blanks.explain: 空格修饰 meetings，后文“the ones they remember”提示是“令人难忘的”，故填 memorable；hostile、fragile 与语境不符。

主语 hierarchy 为第三人称单数，dissolve 表示“（等级差别）消失”，语法与语义都成立；其余动词不合。

items.title: Reading Aloud, Again
items.passage:
Most reading is silent and {{1}}: one person alone with a page. Reading aloud reverses that arrangement. It turns a private act into a performance with an {{2}}, and it slows the eye down to the speed of the voice. Teachers have long used the practice in classrooms, but adults rarely return to it once school ends. That is a pity, because reading to another person exercises skills that silent reading never touches.

The first is how words sound. A reader who has only met a word on the page may {{3}} before it, unsure how to {{4}} it; saying it out loud exposes the gap and, with practice, closes it. The second is attention to {{5}} and pace. A sentence read aloud has to be breathed, and punctuation becomes a set of instructions: stop here, lift there, slow down. The result is often more {{6}} than the same sentence read in silence, because the ear catches effects the eye skips.

There is also a social benefit. Listening to a story is one of the oldest forms of {{7}} entertainment, and it builds {{8}} between people in a way that scrolling alone does not. Libraries and community groups have begun to host reading evenings for exactly this reason, and participants report that they {{9}} far more of a text they have heard than of one they have merely scanned.

None of this requires talent. Reading aloud is a skill, not a {{10}}, and a short pause or a stumbled name matters far less than the willingness to try.

blanks.explain: 冒号后 one person alone with a page 说明阅读通常是“独自的”，solitary 符合；spacious、bitter 与语境不符。

items.title: The Repair Habit
items.passage:
Not long ago, a broken toaster usually meant a trip to the bin. Today a growing number of people are choosing to {{1}} that habit and fix things instead. Repair cafes, where neighbours bring broken objects and fix them together, have appeared in many towns, and online forums offer step-by-step advice for almost any item.

The appeal is partly financial. A new appliance costs far more than a spare part, and mending is usually more {{2}} than buying another. But money is not the whole story. Many visitors say they come to learn a {{3}} their grandparents took for granted, or to spend time with people who enjoy taking things apart.

The social side matters as much as the technical one. Experienced {{4}} sit at long tables with toolboxes open, and a nervous owner can find {{5}} from someone who has fixed the same fault. Beginners often arrive convinced that they are useless with their hands; a few hours later they leave more {{6}} and eager to try another job.

Repair culture also changes how people shop. Once you have opened a machine and seen how it is built, you look for products that are {{7}} rather than sealed shut, and you become less willing to {{8}} a device that still has years of use. Manufacturers notice this: some now publish manuals and sell parts directly to customers, a policy that would have seemed odd a generation ago.

None of this will {{9}} the problem of electronic waste alone. But every object kept in use is one that does not reach the bin, and the habit of mending is {{10}} in a world of limited resources.

blanks.explain: discard that habit 意为“抛弃那个习惯”，与后文 fix things instead 形成对比；nod、edit 语义不合。
more affordable than buying another 指“比再买一个更负担得起”，与整段关于金钱的讨论一致。

items.title: Museums Beyond the Glass Case
items.passage:
For generations the museum visit followed a simple rule: look, but do not touch. Objects sat behind glass, labels supplied dates, and visitors moved through rooms in silence. That model still suits many collections, yet it excludes anyone who cannot see well and leaves most people with only a faint impression of the past.

Designers have begun to {{1}} the experience. Some galleries now provide {{2}} copies of sculptures that visitors may handle, with labels in larger print and plain language. Others use sound: a recording of a workshop or the murmur of a market can {{3}} a scene more vividly than text.

The change is not only about disability. Curators have found that a multi-sensory room holds school groups far longer than a case of objects, and that families stay until closing. When a visitor can lift a replica sword or smell the resin used in a boat, the past becomes something like a memory.

Critics warn that replicas may {{4}} real objects in the minds of visitors, and that a museum should not {{5}} scholarship for novelty. Curators answer that the two goals are not in {{6}}. A careful reconstruction, they argue, draws attention to the original rather than {{7}} its importance. Many institutions now label replicas clearly and invite visitors to compare the copy with the genuine item.

The biggest {{8}} is training. Front-of-house staff need time to {{9}} new formats, and small museums often lack the money to build them. Still, the principle is hard to {{10}}: a collection that few people can fully experience serves the public less well than one that welcomes everybody.

blanks.explain: begun to rethink the experience 指开始“重新思考”参观体验，后文列举的新做法与之一致；wander、publish 不合。
tactile copies 指可供触摸的“触觉”复制品，与 may handle 直接呼应；sudden、ceiling 不合。

items.title: Birdsong in the City
items.passage:
Early in the morning, before the streets fill, a city can sound almost like a forest. Blackbirds, sparrows, and gulls sing from rooftops and plane trees, and for a few minutes the {{1}} of traffic is drowned out. City dwellers who notice this are often surprised, because the common view is that wildlife belongs to the countryside.

The truth is more interesting. Cities support fewer species than forests, but the birds that do live there are often remarkably {{2}}. Some have learned to sing at a higher pitch so that their songs can be heard above low engine {{3}}. Others have shifted the hours of their dawn chorus, starting earlier when the background is quieter. Such adjustments happen over decades rather than overnight, yet they show how quickly animals can {{4}} to an artificial environment.

For humans the benefits run the other way. Many office workers and hospital patients say that a view of greenery, or even a recording of birdsong, can {{5}} recovery and calm the nerves. This may explain why urban planners now {{6}} parks and green roofs not as decoration but as public health measures.

None of this happens by accident. A city that {{7}} nature needs space for insects, water for drinking, and trees old enough to shelter nests. It also needs residents who will {{8}} the racket their own machinery makes. Several councils have placed a {{9}} on building work during the breeding season, and some have dimmed street lights to help birds rest.

Such measures are cheap compared with the cost of a city that has {{10}} its birds, where the only sound is the traffic that drove them away.

blanks.explain: the {{1}} of traffic 需要名词，指车流的“轰鸣声”，与 drowned out 搭配；lecture 不合语义。

主语 A city 为单数，故用第三人称单数 welcomes，意为“接纳自然”；punish 与 needs space... 的语境相反。

items.title: Gardens Above the Street
items.passage:
Look down on a modern city from a high window and you will see a grey landscape of roofs. Look again in a few years and some of those roofs may have turned green. Rooftop gardens, once a novelty on expensive apartment blocks, are spreading to schools, offices, and public housing, and they are changing the way cities {{1}} heat, water, and food.

The environmental case is easy to {{2}}. A layer of soil and plants absorbs sunlight that would otherwise be {{3}} by concrete, so the building below stays cooler in summer. The plants also slow rainwater, which {{4}} the pressure on drains during storms. In dense neighbourhoods where ground space is scarce, a roof may be the only {{5}} place to grow vegetables.

The social case is less obvious but just as {{6}}. A shared garden gives neighbours a reason to talk, and a school roof can become an outdoor classroom where children learn where food comes from. Tenants who have never met may find themselves {{7}} tomatoes together on a Saturday morning.

Rooftop gardens are not {{8}}, however. The structure must carry the weight of wet soil, the waterproofing must be perfect, and someone must water the plants in dry spells. Costs can {{9}} quickly, and a poorly planned garden may be abandoned within a season.

Cities that have made the gardens work usually started small. A single pilot roof allowed engineers to test the load, gardeners to learn which plants {{10}} the wind, and residents to see the benefit for themselves. Success then spread by example rather than by rule.

blanks.explain: the way cities manage heat, water, and food 指城市“管理”热、水和食物的方式；publish、punish 语义不合。

items.title: Letters in the Drawer
items.passage:
A handwritten letter arrives slowly. It may take days to reach its reader, and its paper carries the marks of a particular day: a smudge, a crossed-out word, a change of pen. In an age of {{1}} messages, that slowness looks like a fault. Yet people who write letters by hand describe the practice as a form of {{2}} that no screen can imitate.

The difference begins with time. Typing a message encourages a quick reply, while writing by hand forces the writer to {{3}} each sentence before it is committed to paper. The hand moves more slowly than the mind, and that gap gives the writer room to {{4}} what is worth saying. Many letter writers say their real thoughts appear only after the second page.

A letter also lasts. Emails pile up in an inbox and are rarely read twice, whereas a letter can be kept in a drawer for years. Grandchildren may one day {{5}} a bundle of envelopes and learn what their grandparents were like as young people. In this sense, a letter is less a message than a small {{6}} of a life.

Handwriting itself carries meaning. A hasty scrawl suggests impatience; a careful loop suggests care. None of this can be conveyed by a standard font, however {{7}} the design. The reader hears a voice even though nothing is spoken.

None of this means that digital messages are {{8}}. They are simply different tools, suited to different tasks. The {{9}} is to keep both: a quick note to confirm a meeting, and, now and then, a letter that shows someone you were willing to spend an {{10}} on them.

blanks.explain: an age of instant messages 指“即时消息”的时代，与 slowness 形成对比；sudden、elegant 不合。
a form of patience 指写信是一种“耐心”的体现，呼应慢、需等待的特点；lecture、furniture 不合。
forces the writer to weigh each sentence 指被迫“权衡”每个句子，与手写速度慢的语境一致。
room to discover what is worth saying 指有空间“发现自己”真正想说的话；descend、punish 不合。
grandchildren may inherit a bundle of envelopes 指孙辈可能“继承”一捆信件，符合代际传递的语境。
a small record of a life 指信是人生的“记录”，与上句 kept in a drawer for years 呼应。
however elegant the design 指无论字体设计多么“优雅”，都无法传达手写的意味；sudden 不合。
否定句意为数字消息并非“毫无价值”，后文 They are simply different tools 正是解释。
The answer is to keep both 指应对办法是两者兼用；lecture、furniture 不能表达“办法”。
